title: Engineered design trigger
applies_to: Bearing wall removed or altered; new opening in bearing or exterior wall; any structural element outside the prescriptive limits
check: Structural elements that fall outside the prescriptive limits of the code must be designed by accepted engineering practice (signed and sealed). Show beam, header, posts and load path on the permit set.
note: Structure is not in the model; show whenever a wall flagged as bearing is demolished or cut. See also FBC-EB 807.4.

title: Wind design pressure, replaced openings
applies_to: New or replaced exterior window, exterior door, sliding glass door, skylight, garage door
check: Each exterior window, door, skylight and garage door must be rated for the component-and-cladding design pressures for the site (ultimate wind speed from Fig. R301.2(4), Table R301.2(2) adjusted by Table R301.2(3) for height and exposure; garage doors Table R301.2(4)). Product rating (+/- psf) must meet or exceed the required pressure.
needs: Site ultimate design wind speed (Vult), exposure category, mean roof height, wall zone (4 or 5), and the product's rated design pressure / Florida Product Approval or Miami-Dade NOA number
note: FBC-EB 707.4 makes this apply to replacements in existing dwellings. Where Vult is 115 mph or more (all of South Florida) wind design must follow one of the listed methods (R301.2.1.1); windows and doors per R609.

title: Wind-borne debris opening protection
applies_to: New or replaced exterior glazed opening (window, glazed door, sliding glass door, skylight) in a wind-borne debris region
check: Every exterior glazed opening must be protected from wind-borne debris: impact-rated product or a shutter/panel system tested to the Large Missile Test of ASTM E1996 and E1886, or TAS 201/202/203, or AAMA 506. Flag any new or replaced exterior glazed opening that is neither impact rated nor shown with an approved shutter.
edition_difference: 9th Edition deletes subsection R301.2.1.2.1 (the Florida substitution text for ASTM E1996 wind zones); the requirement itself is unchanged.
needs: Project field: in wind-borne debris region (yes/no) and HVHZ (Miami-Dade/Broward) yes/no; per opening: impact rated or shutter type
note: Replacement-only relief (25 percent in 12 months for pre-FBC houses) is in FBC-EB 707.4, see EB rules. In the HVHZ the Chapter 44 / FBC-B HVHZ provisions (TAS protocols, NOA) apply.

title: Garage door glazing protection
applies_to: New or replaced garage door with glazing in a wind-borne debris region
check: Glazing in a garage door must have opening protection meeting an approved impact standard or ANSI/DASMA 115.
needs: Garage door has glazing (yes/no); impact rating / product approval

title: Plywood panel shutters (exception)
applies_to: Openings protected by wood structural panels instead of rated shutters
check: Wood structural panels may serve as opening protection only if: at least 7/16 in. thick, span between fastener lines 44 in. max, building mean roof height 33 ft or less, Vult 180 mph or less, panels precut and predrilled, overlapping the wall at least 2 in. beyond the fastener lines, with corrosion-resistant attachment hardware permanently installed on the building (fasteners 16 in. o.c. on the long sides as the prescriptive alternative).
note: Not accepted in the HVHZ. Anchors: 300 lb ASD withdrawal; masonry also 525 lb shear at 1.5 in. edge distance.

title: Enclosed porch / sunroom openings
applies_to: Porch, balcony or sunroom enclosed under an existing roof
check: Openings of a sunroom, balcony or porch enclosed under an existing roof or deck need not be protected if the space is separated from the house interior by a wall and every opening in that separating wall is protected.
note: Same allowance repeated in FBC-EB 707.5.

title: Flood hazard area trigger
applies_to: Any project in a flood hazard area (A, AE, AH, AO, Coastal A, V/VE zone)
check: If the work is a substantial improvement or repair of substantial damage, the whole building must be brought into compliance with Section R322 (or ASCE 24). Buildings in a floodway follow ASCE 24. Where a building lies in more than one flood zone the most restrictive applies.
edition_difference: 9th Edition rewords only (lists A Zones, Coastal A Zones and V Zones); no change in requirement.
needs: Flood zone, base flood elevation, cost of work, market value of the structure (to compute the 50 percent test)
note: Substantial improvement = cost equals or exceeds 50 percent of market value of the structure before the work (FBC-EB definition). Many communities count cumulative work over a look-back period by local ordinance.

title: Coastal construction control line
applies_to: Dwelling seaward of the CCCL
check: Structures seaward of the coastal construction control line must be designed for the forces of a 100-year storm event per FBC-B Section 3109 (and need a DEP permit).
needs: Project field: seaward of CCCL (yes/no)
note: Also FBC-EB 601.3 and R322.1.11.

title: Live loads when use changes
applies_to: Attic, garage, porch or storage space converted to living space; new loft or mezzanine; new stair, guard or handrail
check: Floors must carry: 40 psf rooms other than sleeping rooms, 30 psf sleeping rooms, 30 psf habitable attics and attics served by fixed stairs, 20 psf attics with limited storage, 10 psf attics without storage, 40 psf stairs (300 lb concentrated on a tread), 50 psf garages. Guards and handrails: 200 lb concentrated load at the top; guard infill 50 lb on 1 sq ft.
note: Structure is not modeled. Attic trusses designed for 10 or 20 psf cannot be converted to habitable space without engineering.

title: Deflection limits, new members
applies_to: New beam, header, floor or ceiling framing, new interior wall
check: Deflection limits: floors L/360; ceilings with gypsum board L/240; ceilings with plaster or stucco L/360; interior walls and partitions H/180; other members L/240.
edition_difference: 9th Edition excludes guards and handrails from the 'all other structural members' L/240 line.

title: Exterior wall near lot line
applies_to: New or enlarged window or door opening, or new projection, in an exterior wall close to a property line
check: Table R302.1: no openings in an exterior wall less than 3 ft from the lot line; walls less than 3 ft from the line need a 1-hour rating (exposure from outside); projections not allowed within 2 ft, and need 1-hour underside (or heavy timber / fire-retardant-treated wood) between 2 and 3 ft; penetrations within 3 ft per R302.4.
edition_difference: 9th Edition adds noncombustible fiber-cement as an acceptable projection underside material.
needs: Fire separation distance from the wall to the lot line
note: Florida exceptions: walls perpendicular to the lot line, zero-lot-line developments with 6 ft between buildings, screen enclosures, exempt sheds.

title: Townhouse separation wall
applies_to: Townhouse: any work on or in the wall shared with the neighbor
check: Each townhouse is separated by its own 1-hour exterior-type wall, or by a common 2-hour wall that contains no plumbing or mechanical equipment, ducts or vents in its cavity. The wall must be continuous from foundation to the underside of the roof sheathing (R302.2.1). Do not open, notch or run plumbing/ducts in the common wall; electrical boxes per R302.4.
needs: Wall flagged as townhouse separation (rated) wall
note: Parapet / roof-deck alternatives (R302.2.2, R302.2.3) and structural independence (R302.2.4) are new-building items. See FBC-EB 903.2.1 for Level 3 alterations.

title: Two-family dwelling unit separation
applies_to: Duplex: wall or floor/ceiling between the two units
check: Units in a two-family dwelling must be separated by wall and floor assemblies rated 1 hour (ASTM E119 / UL 263), tight to the exterior wall and extending from foundation to the underside of roof sheathing. Exceptions: 1/2 hour if sprinklered throughout; wall need not go through the attic if the ceiling is 5/8 in. Type X gypsum, an attic draftstop is provided above the wall, and the framing supporting the ceiling is protected by 1/2 in. gypsum. Supporting construction must have equal rating (R302.3.1).
edition_difference: 9th Edition: the 1/2-hour sprinkler exception accepts NFPA 13, 13R, 13D or P2904 systems (8th: NFPA 13 only); test reference changes to FBC-B 703.2.2.
needs: Wall/ceiling flagged as dwelling-unit separation; assembly rating

title: Shared accessory rooms (duplex)
applies_to: Two-family dwelling with a shared laundry, storage or similar accessory room
check: 9th Edition only: a shared accessory room must be separated from each dwelling unit by 1/2 in. gypsum board on the accessory-room side (5/8 in. Type X where habitable rooms are above or below). No opening from the shared room directly into a sleeping room; other doors must be 1-3/8 in. solid wood, 1-3/8 in. steel, or 20-minute doors, and self-closing or automatic-closing. Ducts through the separation: minimum 26 gage steel with no openings into the room.
edition_difference: New section in the 9th Edition; no equivalent in the 8th.
needs: Room flagged as shared accessory room
note: 9th Edition only.

title: Through penetrations of rated walls/floors
applies_to: Pipes, conduits, ducts passing through a townhouse or duplex separation assembly
check: Through penetrations of a rated separation must be installed as tested in the rated assembly or protected by a listed firestop system (ASTM E814 / UL 1479) with an F rating not less than the assembly rating. Steel, ferrous or copper pipe up to 6 in. in concrete/masonry may be grouted solid (opening 144 sq in. max).
note: Applies only to assemblies rated under R302.2 or R302.3 (townhouse and duplex separations), not ordinary interior walls.

title: Electrical boxes in rated walls
applies_to: Receptacles, switches, low-voltage boxes or recessed fixtures in a townhouse or duplex separation wall or ceiling
check: Steel boxes up to 16 sq in. are allowed if total openings do not exceed 100 sq in. per 100 sq ft of wall and the gap around the box is 1/8 in. max. Boxes on opposite sides of the wall must be separated horizontally by at least 24 in. (or by the cavity depth if the cavity is filled with loose-fill/mineral wool, or by solid fireblocking, or both boxes wrapped with listed putty pads). Non-steel boxes must be listed for rated assemblies. Recessed luminaires in a rated ceiling must be listed for it or protected with listed materials.
needs: Wall flagged as rated separation wall (then the 24 in. back-to-back box spacing can be checked automatically)

title: No garage door into a bedroom
applies_to: Door or other opening between a garage and a room used for sleeping
check: No opening is permitted from a private garage directly into a room used for sleeping.
note: Replaces part of B-21. Bites when a room next to the garage is renamed a bedroom.

title: Garage-to-house door construction
applies_to: Door between garage and residence
check: Door must be solid wood at least 1-3/8 in. thick, solid- or honeycomb-core steel at least 1-3/8 in. thick, or a 20-minute fire-rated door.
needs: Door construction/rating attribute
note: Replaces part of B-21. Florida's text (8th and 9th) does NOT include the self-closing device required by the model IRC; do not flag missing closers.

title: No duct openings into garage
applies_to: HVAC supply register, return grille or transfer opening placed in a garage
check: Ducts in the garage or passing through the garage/house separation must not have openings into the garage.
note: Flag any register or return drawn in a room typed as garage (a garage converted to conditioned living space is no longer a garage, but then must meet habitable-room rules).

title: Garage duct material
applies_to: Ducts in the garage or penetrating the garage/house wall or ceiling
check: Such ducts must be minimum No. 26 gage sheet steel, 1 in. minimum rigid nonmetallic Class 0 or Class 1 duct board, or other approved material.
note: Flex duct through the separation is not permitted.

title: Other penetrations of garage separation
applies_to: Pipes, cables, vents passing through the garage/house wall or garage ceiling
check: Seal the annular space around every penetration of the garage separation with an approved material that resists passage of flame and products of combustion (R302.11 item 4).

title: Garage/house wall and attic separation
applies_to: Wall between attached garage and residence; garage ceiling below attic
check: Garage must be separated from the residence and its attic by not less than 1/2 in. gypsum board (or equivalent) applied on the garage side. Check that the garage-side layer of every garage/house wall, and the garage ceiling where the attic is common, is at least 1/2 in. gypsum.
note: Replaces part of B-21. Does not apply to garage walls perpendicular to the adjacent dwelling wall. An attic hatch in the garage ceiling is part of this membrane and must maintain it (gypsum-faced panel); reviewer interpretation, not explicit text.

title: Garage ceiling under rooms above
applies_to: Garage with habitable rooms above
check: Ceiling must be not less than 5/8 in. Type X gypsum board, and the structure supporting that floor/ceiling (walls, beams, columns) must be protected with not less than 1/2 in. gypsum board.
edition_difference: 9th Edition applies the 5/8 in. Type X requirement under any 'portion of the dwelling unit' above the garage, not only habitable rooms.
needs: Garage ceiling board type and thickness; flag that there is a room above the garage

title: Detached garage within 3 ft
applies_to: Detached garage less than 3 ft from the dwelling on the same lot
check: Interior side of the garage exterior walls within that area must have not less than 1/2 in. gypsum board.

title: Under-stair protection
applies_to: Enclosed, accessible space under a stair (closet, storage with door or access panel)
check: Walls, the under-stair surface and any soffits on the enclosed side must be covered with 1/2 in. gypsum board.
needs: Under-stair space is enclosed and has a door/access panel (yes/no); finish on enclosed side

title: Wall and ceiling finish flammability
applies_to: New wall or ceiling finish other than gypsum board (wood paneling, planks, acoustic panels, decorative panels, HDPE/PP)
check: Wall and ceiling finishes: flame spread index 200 max and smoke-developed index 450 max (ASTM E84 / UL 723), or pass NFPA 286. Trim (baseboard, chair rail, picture mold, handrails), doors, windows and thin wallcoverings under 1/28 in. are exempt. HDPE and polypropylene finishes must pass NFPA 286.
needs: Finish material and its flame-spread / smoke class (product data)
note: FBC-EB 702.1-702.3 points to FBC-B Chapter 8 for newly installed finishes in alterations; same Class C threshold for dwellings.

title: Insulation flammability
applies_to: New insulation in walls, floors, ceilings, attic
check: Insulation including facings: flame spread 25 max and smoke-developed 450 max. Facings may be exempt only when installed in substantial contact with the back of the wall/ceiling finish (kraft-faced batts must not be left exposed). Exposed attic-floor insulation: critical radiant flux at least 0.12 W/sq cm. Cellulose must carry the CPSC 16 CFR 1209/1404 label.
edition_difference: 9th Edition folds the ASTM E970 test reference into R302.10.4 and deletes R302.10.5.

title: Fireblocking in new walls
applies_to: New framed wall, furred wall, double or staggered stud wall (wood framing)
check: Fireblock concealed stud spaces vertically at the ceiling and floor levels and horizontally at intervals not exceeding 10 ft.
note: Applies to combustible (wood) construction. Add to notes whenever new wood-framed or furred walls are drawn.

title: Fireblocking at soffits and dropped ceilings
applies_to: New soffit, dropped ceiling, tray, coffer or cove ceiling built against framed walls
check: Fireblock the connection between concealed vertical spaces (stud bays) and horizontal spaces (soffit, drop ceiling, cove) so the wall cavity does not open into the soffit/ceiling space.
note: Typical kitchen-soffit and tray-ceiling correction item.

title: Fireblocking at stairs
applies_to: New or rebuilt stair
check: Fireblock concealed spaces between stair stringers at the top and bottom of the run.

title: Fireblocking at penetrations
applies_to: New pipes, vents, ducts, cables and wires passing through top plates, bottom plates, floors and ceilings
check: Seal openings around vents, pipes, ducts, cables and wires at ceiling and floor level with an approved material that resists passage of flame and products of combustion.

title: Fireblocking materials
applies_to: Any required fireblock
check: Acceptable: 2 in. nominal lumber; two layers of 1 in. lumber with staggered joints; 23/32 in. wood structural panel or 3/4 in. particleboard with backed joints; 1/2 in. gypsum board; 1/4 in. cement millboard; mineral wool or glass fiber batts securely retained (unfaced fiberglass must fill the cavity for at least 16 in. of height); listed cellulose. Loose-fill is not a fireblock unless tested. Keep existing fireblocks intact when cutting in.

title: Draftstopping above dropped ceilings
applies_to: Suspended/dropped ceiling under a framed floor, or open-web floor trusses, in a multi-story house
check: Where there is usable space above and below a floor/ceiling assembly and the ceiling is suspended below the framing (or the framing is open-web), draftstop the concealed space so no area exceeds 1,000 sq ft, in roughly equal areas. Materials: 1/2 in. gypsum board or 3/8 in. wood structural panel, parallel to framing.
needs: Story has a floor above (yes/no); area of the concealed space above the dropped ceiling

title: Floor underside membrane
applies_to: Ceiling removed or new floor framing below an upper floor (I-joists, trusses, lumber smaller than 2x10)
check: The underside of floor framing must be covered with 1/2 in. gypsum board or 5/8 in. wood structural panel. Exceptions: sprinklered space below, crawl space, up to 80 sq ft unprotected per story with perimeter fireblocking, or solid sawn/structural composite lumber 2x10 or larger.
note: Bites when a first-floor ceiling is left open or replaced with a non-gypsum finish under engineered joists.

title: Insulation clearance at recessed lights
applies_to: Recessed luminaires, fan motors and other heat-producing devices in an insulated ceiling
check: Keep combustible insulation at least 3 in. away unless the device is listed for lesser clearance (IC-rated). Recessed luminaires in the thermal envelope must also meet FBC-Energy (IC-rated, sealed/airtight).
needs: Luminaire is IC-rated / airtight (yes/no); ceiling is insulated (yes/no)

title: Fire-retardant-treated wood
applies_to: FRT wood specified (e.g., townhouse roof deck repair, blocking in rated assemblies)
check: 9th Edition adds FRTW requirements to the Residential code: flame spread 25 or less with the extended 20-minute test, labeled, 'Exterior' type where exposed to weather or damp locations, moisture content 19 percent max for lumber and 15 percent for panels.
edition_difference: New section in the 9th Edition.
note: 9th Edition only.

title: Natural light 8 percent
applies_to: Every habitable room (bedroom, living, dining, den, family room, kitchen); new or re-purposed rooms; windows removed or reduced
check: Total glazing area of the room's windows, glazed doors and skylights must be at least 8 percent of the room floor area. Exception: glazing may be omitted if artificial light gives an average 6 footcandles over the room at 30 in. above the floor (in the 8th Edition this also requires mechanical ventilation per exception 1).
edition_difference: 9th Edition renumbers to R303.1.1, moves the 'glazing must face a street, yard or court' rule here, and makes the artificial-light exception stand alone (no longer tied to mechanical ventilation).
note: Replaces B-04 (light). FBC-EB 801.3 exc. 1 lets windows be ADDED in a Level 2 alteration without meeting the light/ventilation minimums; a room newly created or converted to habitable use must comply.

title: Natural ventilation 4 percent
applies_to: Every habitable room; windows removed, fixed, or reduced
check: Openable area to the outdoors (windows, doors, skylights, louvers) must be at least 4 percent of the room floor area and readily operable. Exceptions: rooms other than kitchens may use whole-house mechanical ventilation or a system giving 0.35 air changes per hour (M1507); kitchens may use a local exhaust system instead of an openable window.
edition_difference: 9th Edition renumbers to R303.1.2 and adds allowances to ventilate through a roofed porch/patio with 40 percent of its perimeter open or through a thermally isolated sunroom.
note: Replaces B-04 (ventilation). In 8th Edition exceptions 1 and 2 apply only where the opening is not also the required emergency escape opening.

title: Borrowed light from adjoining room
applies_to: Interior room with no exterior window relying on an adjacent room
check: A room counts as part of the adjoining room only if the common wall is at least one-half open and unobstructed, and the opening is at least one-tenth of the interior room's floor area and at least 25 sq ft. Then apply the 8 percent / 4 percent tests to the combined floor area.
edition_difference: 9th Edition moves the sunroom / patio-cover exception (20 sq ft opening) into R303.1.2.

title: Bathroom light and ventilation
applies_to: Bathrooms, toilet rooms and similar rooms
check: Provide a window with at least 3 sq ft of glazing, half of it openable; OR artificial light plus a local exhaust fan (rates per Section M1507) ducted directly to the outdoors.
note: Replaces B-05. Fan rate (50 cfm intermittent / 20 cfm continuous in Table M1507.4) and duct termination are covered in the mechanical rule set. Exhaust may not discharge into an attic, soffit cavity or crawl space.

title: Whole-house mechanical ventilation
applies_to: Dwelling tested tighter than 3 ACH50
check: Where blower-door leakage is less than 3.00 air changes per hour at 50 Pa, whole-house mechanical ventilation per M1507.3 is required.
note: New-construction test trigger; relevant to a gut remodel only if a blower-door test is run.

title: Outdoor air intake location
applies_to: New outdoor-air intake (fresh-air duct, ERV, makeup air)
check: Intake openings must be at least 10 ft from hazardous or noxious sources (plumbing vents, chimneys, appliance vents, streets, alleys, parking), or at least 3 ft below the source. Bathroom, toilet and kitchen exhaust from the dwelling is not treated as noxious for this rule.

title: Exhaust not onto walkways
applies_to: New exhaust termination (bath fan, range hood, dryer)
check: Exhaust air must not be directed onto walkways.

title: Screens on exterior air openings
applies_to: New exhaust or intake terminations
check: Protect with corrosion-resistant screens, louvers or grilles with openings between 1/4 in. and 1/2 in., and against weather. (Dryer terminations are governed separately: no screen.)

title: Interior stair lighting and switches
applies_to: Interior stairway (new, relocated, or within the work area)
check: Provide a light source that illuminates treads and landings to at least 1 footcandle at their centers. Where the stair has six or more risers, a wall switch is required at each floor level (unless lighting is automatic or remotely controlled).
note: Check: stair object has a luminaire serving it and, with 6 or more risers, a switch at top and bottom (3-way). Complements NEC 210.70(A)(2).

title: Exterior stair lighting
applies_to: Exterior stairway serving the dwelling
check: Provide a light at the top landing of an exterior stairway (and at the bottom landing of a stair down to a basement).

title: Required windows must face open air
applies_to: Window counted toward required light/ventilation that faces a porch, enclosed patio or sunroom
check: Required glazed openings must open directly onto a street, public alley, yard or court on the same lot. Allowed: facing a roofed porch whose longer side is at least 65 percent open with a ceiling at least 7 ft; under a deck/balcony with at least 36 in. clear height; into a sunroom or patio cover with more than 40 percent of its walls open or screened and a 7 ft ceiling (R303.9.1).
edition_difference: 9th Edition moves this into R303.1.1 (light) and R303.1.2 (ventilation); R303.9 becomes Required heating. 9th also allows required glazing to face any sunroom adjacent to a yard.
needs: What the window faces (open yard / roofed porch / enclosed porch / sunroom) and how open that space is
note: Bites when a porch or lanai is enclosed and bedrooms/living rooms lose their direct exterior exposure.

title: Required heating
applies_to: Space converted to habitable use (garage, porch, attic) or heating equipment removed
check: Where the winter design temperature is below 60 F, each dwelling unit needs permanent heating able to hold 68 F at 3 ft above the floor and 2 ft from exterior walls in every habitable room. Portable heaters do not count.
edition_difference: 9th Edition renumbers to R303.9; text unchanged.
note: Winter design temperatures across Florida are below 60 F, so this applies statewide.

title: Minimum room area
applies_to: Habitable rooms except kitchens
check: Floor area at least 70 sq ft.
note: Replaces B-03.

title: Minimum room dimension
applies_to: Habitable rooms except kitchens
check: No horizontal dimension less than 7 ft.
note: Replaces B-03.

title: Low-ceiling area not counted
applies_to: Rooms with sloped or furred-down ceilings
check: Floor area under a sloped ceiling lower than 5 ft, or under a furred ceiling lower than 7 ft, does not count toward the required 70 sq ft.

title: Ceiling height, habitable rooms and halls
applies_to: Habitable space and hallways; new soffits, dropped or furred ceilings
check: Ceiling height at least 7 ft.
note: Replaces B-01. Dropped soffits, ducts and furred areas must also keep 7 ft; the only projections allowed lower are beams/girders (see next rules). FBC-EB 801.3 exc. 4 sets the same 7 ft minimum for newly created habitable spaces and corridors in alterations.

title: Ceiling height, baths and laundry
applies_to: Bathrooms, toilet rooms, laundry rooms
check: Ceiling height at least 6 ft 8 in.
note: Replaces B-01.

title: Sloped ceiling rooms
applies_to: Rooms with sloped or vaulted ceilings
check: The required floor area must have at least 5 ft ceiling height everywhere, and at least 50 percent of the required floor area must be 7 ft or higher.
note: Exception 1.

title: Ceiling height over fixtures and showers
applies_to: Bathroom fixtures; tub or shower with a showerhead
check: Height over each fixture must allow its intended use. A shower or tub with showerhead needs at least 6 ft 8 in. ceiling height over a 30 in. x 30 in. area at the showerhead.
note: Replaces B-02. Exception 2.

title: Beams below ceiling
applies_to: Exposed or dropped beams and girders in habitable space
check: Beams and girders spaced at least 36 in. apart (clear) may project down to not less than 6 ft 6 in. (78 in.) above the finished floor.
note: Exception 4. The 6 ft 4 in. allowance for beams, ducts and obstructions (exception 3 and R305.1.1) applies only in basements.

title: Minimum bathroom fixtures
applies_to: Whole dwelling after remodel; bathroom removed or converted
check: Every dwelling unit must have a water closet, a lavatory, and a bathtub or shower.

title: Kitchen and sink
applies_to: Whole dwelling after remodel; kitchen relocated
check: Every dwelling unit must have a kitchen area with a sink.

title: Sewer or septic connection
applies_to: New or relocated plumbing fixtures; added bedroom or bathroom on a septic system
check: All fixtures must drain to a sanitary sewer or an approved onsite system under the Florida onsite sewage rule (Chapter 64E-6, F.A.C.).
edition_difference: 9th Edition cites Chapter 62-6, F.A.C. (rule renumbered after the program moved to DEP).
needs: Project field: sewer or septic
note: On septic, adding a bedroom or increasing floor area normally requires an existing-system evaluation/modification approval before the building permit.

title: Hot and cold water to fixtures
applies_to: Kitchen sink, lavatory, bathtub, shower, bidet, laundry tub, washing machine outlet
check: Each of these fixtures must be supplied with both hot and cold water from an approved supply.
note: Check that each such fixture's utility points include both hot and cold supply.

title: Fixture clearances
applies_to: Water closet, bidet, lavatory, tub, shower
check: Space fixtures per Figure R307.1 and P2705.1: water closet or bidet centerline at least 15 in. from any side wall, partition or vanity and 30 in. center-to-center from an adjacent fixture; at least 21 in. clear in front of a water closet, bidet or lavatory; at least 24 in. clear in front of a shower opening.
note: Replaces B-07 and B-08. The section text was read (it points to Figure R307.1 and P2705.1) but the figure is an image that could not be read as text; the dimensions given are the long-standing figure / P2705.1 values and should be confirmed against the plumbing rule set (P2705.1).

title: Nonabsorbent shower and tub walls
applies_to: Bathtub with a showerhead; shower compartment
check: Floors and walls must be finished with a nonabsorbent surface, and the wall surface must extend at least 6 ft above the floor.
needs: Wall finish material and finished height in the tub/shower
note: Replaces B-10. Backing board and waterproofing are in Chapter 7 (R702.4) and the plumbing code.

title: Safety glazing label
applies_to: Every pane in a hazardous location
check: Each pane must carry a permanent manufacturer's designation (etched, sandblasted, ceramic-fired, laser etched or embossed) naming the standard; a label is allowed. Multipane assemblies with lites of 1 sq ft or less need at least one lite fully marked and the others marked CPSC 16 CFR 1201 or ANSI Z97.1.
note: Inspector looks for the bug in the corner of the glass; note on the window/door schedule.

title: Jalousie and louvered windows
applies_to: Existing or replacement jalousie/louvered windows
check: Glass slats must be at least 3/16 in. nominal thickness, not longer than 48 in., with smooth exposed edges; wired glass with exposed wire edges is not allowed.
needs: Window type = jalousie; slat thickness and length
note: Jalousies cannot provide wind-borne debris protection by themselves.

title: Safety glazing standard and category
applies_to: Glazing (including mirrors) in any hazardous location
check: Must pass CPSC 16 CFR 1201 Category II; Category I is allowed only for lites of 9 sq ft or less in doors and next-to-door panels. Tub/shower enclosures and sliding patio doors are Category II at any size. ANSI Z97.1 Class A is an alternative only for glazing that is not in doors or wet-area enclosures. Mirrors or glass panels fully backed on a wall are exempt.
needs: Glazing type (tempered / laminated) and category per lite
note: Mirrored closet doors and glass shower enclosures are the common misses.

title: Glazing in doors
applies_to: Any swinging, sliding or bifold door with glass (fixed or operable panels)
check: All glazing in doors must be safety glazing. Exceptions: openings too small to pass a 3 in. sphere; decorative glazing.
note: Replaces B-11. Check: door has glazing and safety-glazing flag is off.

title: Glazing next to doors
applies_to: Window, sidelight or fixed panel near a door
check: Safety glazing required where the bottom edge of the glass is less than 60 in. above the floor AND either (1) the glass is within 24 in. of either side of the door in the plane of the closed door, or (2) the glass is on a wall at an angle less than 180 degrees to the door plane and within 24 in. of the hinge side of an in-swinging door. Exceptions: decorative glass; an intervening wall or permanent barrier; door to a closet/storage 3 ft or less deep; glass next to the fixed panel of a patio door.
note: Replaces B-12.

title: Large low windows
applies_to: Window or fixed glass panel
check: Safety glazing required where ALL apply: pane larger than 9 sq ft; bottom edge less than 18 in. above the floor; top edge more than 36 in. above the floor; a walking surface within 36 in. horizontally. Exceptions: decorative glass; a horizontal rail 34 to 38 in. high able to take 50 lb/ft with at least 1-1/2 in. cross-section height; outboard panes 25 ft or more above grade.
note: Replaces B-13.

title: Glass in guards and railings
applies_to: Glass balusters, glass guard panels, glass railing infill
check: All glazing in guards and railings is a hazardous location regardless of size or height: safety glazing required (and designed with a load factor of 4 per Table R301.5 note h).
needs: Guard/railing infill material = glass

title: Glazing at tubs, showers and wet areas
applies_to: Windows, glass walls and enclosures at bathtubs, showers, hot tubs, spas, whirlpools, saunas, steam rooms, pools
check: Safety glazing required where the bottom exposed edge is less than 60 in. above any standing or walking surface (tub floor, shower floor, bench, deck). Exception: glass more than 60 in. horizontally from the water's edge of a tub/spa/pool or from the edge of a shower, sauna or steam room. Applies to every pane of multiple glazing.
note: Replaces B-14. Covers the shower door/enclosure itself and any window in or beside the tub or shower.

title: Glazing beside stairs and ramps
applies_to: Window or glass panel next to a stair, stair landing or ramp
check: Safety glazing required where the bottom edge is less than 36 in. above the adjacent walking surface. Exceptions: protective rail 34 to 38 in. high (50 lb/ft, 1-1/2 in. section); glass 36 in. or more horizontally from the walking surface.
edition_difference: 9th Edition says 'flights of stairs' instead of 'stairways'; no dimensional change.
note: Checkable only when the stair is drawn.

title: Glazing at bottom stair landing
applies_to: Window or glass panel near the bottom of a stair
check: Safety glazing required where the glass is less than 36 in. above the landing and within a 60 in. horizontal arc (less than 180 degrees) of the bottom tread nosing. Exception: glass protected by a guard with the glass more than 18 in. from the guard.

title: Site-built windows
applies_to: Field-glazed or site-built window/storefront units
check: Must comply with FBC-Building Section 2404 (engineered glass design).

title: Skylights and sloped glazing
applies_to: New or replaced skylight, tubular daylighting device, sloped glazing
check: Glazing must be laminated (0.015 in. interlayer up to 16 sq ft and 12 ft above the floor, otherwise 0.030 in.), fully tempered, heat-strengthened, wired glass or approved plastic; tempered/heat-strengthened units need a retention screen below unless they meet the size/height exceptions. Unit skylights on roofs flatter than 3:12 need a curb at least 4 in. high unless the manufacturer allows otherwise. Units must be labeled to AAMA/WDMA/CSA 101/I.S.2/A440 and meet the wind/impact requirements.
edition_difference: 9th Edition drops the 'greater than 16 sq ft' condition from screen exception 2 (R308.6.5).
needs: Skylight product approval, glazing type, roof slope
note: Roof work itself is outside the model; show as a note when a skylight is drawn.

title: Garage floor
applies_to: Garage floor (new, re-poured, or partially converted garage)
check: Floor must be an approved noncombustible material, and the parking area must slope to a drain or toward the vehicle door.

title: Carport enclosure becomes a garage
applies_to: Carport being enclosed or partly enclosed
check: A carport must be open on at least two sides; if not, it is a garage and must meet all garage rules (separation R302.5/R302.6, floor R309.1).
needs: Number of open sides of the carport

title: Garage in flood hazard area
applies_to: Garage or carport in a flood zone; garage conversion to living space
check: Garages and carports in flood hazard areas must comply with R322: a garage floor below the required elevation may be used only for parking, access and storage and must have flood openings. Converting such a garage to living space is not permitted unless the floor meets the elevation requirement.
needs: Flood zone, base flood elevation, garage floor elevation

title: Garage door opener
applies_to: New or replaced automatic garage door opener
check: Opener must be listed and labeled to UL 325.
edition_difference: 9th Edition adds: install per the manufacturer's instructions.

title: Automotive lifts and EV chargers
applies_to: Vehicle lift or EV charging equipment in a garage
check: 9th Edition only: automotive lifts must be listed to ANSI/ALI ALCTV, installed per listing, and not located in habitable space (R309.6). EV charging systems must follow NFPA 70 with equipment listed to UL 2202 / UL 2594 (R309.7).
edition_difference: New in the 9th Edition.
note: 9th Edition only.

title: Emergency escape opening required
applies_to: Every sleeping room (and basement, habitable attic); room renamed or converted to a bedroom
check: Each sleeping room needs at least one operable emergency escape and rescue opening (window or door) that opens directly to a public way or to a yard or court leading to a public way. Florida allows it to open into a screen enclosure that is open to the atmosphere and has a screen door leading away from the house.
edition_difference: 9th Edition also requires one in the room to which a sleeping loft is open.
note: Replaces B-15. A bedroom whose only window now faces an enclosed (glassed-in) porch, sunroom or garage does not comply.

title: Escape opening operation
applies_to: Escape window or door
check: Must open from inside the room without keys, tools or special knowledge. Window opening control devices and fall-prevention devices complying with ASTM F2090 are allowed.

title: Escape opening net clear area
applies_to: Escape window in a sleeping room
check: Net clear opening at least 5.7 sq ft; 5.0 sq ft for grade-floor openings.
note: Replaces B-15. Net clear opening is the actual free opening with the sash fully open in normal operation (use the manufacturer's egress data; it is smaller than the frame size). See R310.2.6 / FBC-EB 702.5 for replacement windows.

title: Escape opening clear height and width
applies_to: Escape window in a sleeping room
check: Net clear height at least 24 in. and net clear width at least 20 in., obtained by normal operation.
note: Replaces B-15. Both minimums together give less than 5.7 sq ft, so the area test also applies.

title: Escape opening sill height
applies_to: Escape window in a sleeping room
check: Bottom of the clear opening not more than 44 in. above the floor.
note: Replaces B-15.

title: Escape opening under a deck or porch
applies_to: Escape window below a deck, porch or balcony
check: Allowed if the window can fully open and there is a path at least 36 in. high to a yard or court.

title: Replacement window exemption
applies_to: Existing bedroom window being replaced in the same opening
check: A replacement window is exempt from the 5.7 sq ft, 24 in., 20 in. and 44 in. requirements if it is the manufacturer's largest standard size that fits the existing frame or rough opening, is the same operating style or one giving equal or greater opening area, and is not part of a change of occupancy.
needs: Window flagged as replacement in existing opening (not a new or resized opening); operating style of old and new
note: Same rule in FBC-EB 702.5. Do not flag an undersized existing bedroom window that is replaced like-for-like; do flag if the opening area is reduced by a change of style (e.g., single-hung replacing a casement).

title: Door as the escape opening
applies_to: Sleeping room using a door as its escape opening
check: A side-hinged door or a sliding door may serve; it must provide the net clear opening of R310.2.1.
edition_difference: 9th Edition also accepts pivoted and balanced doors.

title: Bars, grilles, shutters on escape openings
applies_to: Security bars, grilles, screens or storm shutters over a bedroom escape opening or egress door
check: Bars/grilles must be releasable from inside without key, tool or special knowledge and must not reduce the required opening. Storm shutters/panels may be closed temporarily during a storm threat, but at least one means of escape must remain on the first floor, not through a garage unless the garage has a side-hinged exterior door, and reachable without passing through a door locked from the other side.
note: Florida-specific shutter language.

title: Egress path not through garage
applies_to: Whole floor plan after remodel
check: A continuous, unobstructed path must lead from every part of the dwelling to the required egress door without passing through a garage, and that door must open directly to a public way or to a yard/court leading to one.
note: Path-finding check: every room must reach the egress door without crossing a room typed as garage.

title: Egress door size and type
applies_to: The one required egress door of each dwelling unit (usually the front door)
check: At least one door must be side-hinged with clear width at least 32 in. (measured between door face and stop with the door open 90 degrees) and clear height at least 78 in. (threshold to stop), and openable from inside without a key or special knowledge. Other doors have no minimum size in the Residential code.
edition_difference: 9th Edition also allows pivoted and balanced doors as the egress door.
note: Replaces B-16. A 3-0 x 6-8 door satisfies it; a 2-8 door gives roughly 30 in. clear and does not. Double-keyed deadbolts are not allowed on this door.

title: Landings at exterior doors
applies_to: Every exterior door (new, relocated or widened)
check: A floor or landing is required on each side of each exterior door: at least as wide as the door, at least 36 in. in the direction of travel, exterior slope not more than 1/4 in. per ft (2 percent). Exception: balcony under 60 sq ft reached only from that door.
edition_difference: 9th Edition adds exceptions for doors from Category I and II sunrooms and from screen enclosures that open onto grass or soil at slab level.
needs: Exterior landing/slab dimensions at the door

title: Threshold height at egress door
applies_to: Required egress door
check: Interior floor or landing not more than 1-1/2 in. below the top of the threshold; the exterior landing may be up to 7-3/4 in. below the top of the threshold. If the exterior landing is not at grade, provide a ramp (R311.8) or stair (R311.7) to grade.
needs: Threshold height above interior floor and above exterior landing

title: Step-down at other exterior doors
applies_to: Exterior doors other than the required egress door
check: Landing or floor not more than 7-3/4 in. below the top of the threshold. No top landing needed where an exterior stair of two risers or fewer is at the door.
needs: Threshold height above exterior landing

title: Vertical egress from upper levels
applies_to: Second floor, habitable attic, loft or other habitable level without its own egress door
check: Each habitable level without an egress door must be served by a stairway (R311.7) or ramp (R311.8).
edition_difference: 9th Edition rewording (basements and habitable levels); same requirement.

title: Hallway width
applies_to: Hallways
check: Clear width at least 36 in.
note: Replaces B-17. Measure finished wall to finished wall.

title: Stair width
applies_to: Stairs (new or rebuilt)
check: Clear width at least 36 in. above handrail height; at and below the handrail at least 31-1/2 in. with one handrail or 27 in. with two. Handrails may project up to 4-1/2 in. from each side (R311.7.8.5).
note: Replaces B-24. Existing stairs not being altered may remain (FBC-EB).

title: Stair headroom
applies_to: Stairs; new soffit, beam or floor framing over a stair
check: Headroom at least 6 ft 8 in. measured vertically from the sloped line along the tread nosings and from landing surfaces. Spiral stairs 6 ft 6 in.
note: Replaces B-24. Needs the ceiling/soffit height over the stair run.

title: Maximum rise of a flight
applies_to: Stairs
check: A flight may not rise more than 12 ft 7 in. (151 in.) between floors or landings.

title: Riser height
applies_to: Stairs
check: Riser not more than 7-3/4 in.; tallest and shortest riser in a flight within 3/8 in. Open risers allowed only if a 4 in. sphere cannot pass where the tread is more than 30 in. above the floor below.
note: Replaces B-24. Dimensions are measured without carpet. New flooring that changes the top or bottom riser can break the 3/8 in. uniformity.

title: Tread depth
applies_to: Stairs
check: Tread depth at least 10 in. (nosing to nosing, horizontally); deepest and shallowest within 3/8 in.
note: Replaces B-24.

title: Winder treads
applies_to: Stairs with winders
check: At least 10 in. deep at the walkline (12 in. in from the narrow side) and at least 6 in. at any point; winder depths at the walkline within 3/8 in. of each other.

title: Nosings
applies_to: Stairs with solid risers
check: Nosing projection 3/4 in. to 1-1/4 in., uniform within 3/8 in.; nosing radius 9/16 in. max (or bevel 1/2 in. max). No nosing needed where treads are 11 in. or deeper.
edition_difference: 9th Edition: uniformity applies within a flight and its top landing; adds exception letting the projection exceed 1-1/4 in. where risers are open.
needs: Nosing projection

title: Stair landings
applies_to: Top and bottom of every stair; door at the top of a stair
check: Floor or landing at top and bottom of each stair, at least as wide as the stair and at least 36 in. deep in the direction of travel. Exception: no landing needed at the top of an interior flight (including in a garage) provided a door does not swing over the stairs.
edition_difference: 9th Edition rewords the interior exception (the top landing may be on the far side of a door at the top that does not swing over the stairs) and adds a 36 in. bottom-landing-width exception for small exterior deck/porch stairs.

title: Tread and landing slope
applies_to: Stairs
check: Walking surfaces of treads and landings sloped not more than 1:48 (2 percent).

title: Handrail required
applies_to: Each flight with four or more risers
check: Handrail on at least one side.
note: Replaces B-24. FBC-EB 805.9 (Level 3) requires adding one to an existing work-area stair with three or more risers that has none.

title: Handrail height
applies_to: Stair handrails
check: 34 to 38 in. measured vertically above the sloped plane of the tread nosings.
needs: Handrail height
note: Replaces B-24. Volutes/turnouts at the lowest tread and transition fittings may exceed the range.

title: Handrail continuity and wall clearance
applies_to: Stair handrails
check: Continuous for the full flight from above the top riser to above the bottom riser; ends returned to the wall or terminated in a newel/safety terminal; at least 1-1/2 in. clear between handrail and wall. May be interrupted by a newel at a turn.

title: Handrail grip size
applies_to: Stair and ramp handrails
check: Type I: round 1-1/4 to 2 in. diameter, or non-round with perimeter 4 to 6-1/4 in. and max cross-section 2-1/4 in. Type II: larger perimeter allowed only with finger recesses on both sides (rail width above recess 1-1/4 to 2-3/4 in.).
needs: Handrail profile
note: A flat 2x6 cap is not a graspable handrail.

title: Spiral stairs
applies_to: Spiral stair
check: Clear width at and below handrail at least 26 in.; walkline radius 24-1/2 in. max; tread at least 6-3/4 in. at the walkline; all treads identical; rise 9-1/2 in. max; headroom 6 ft 6 in. min.

title: Alternating tread devices and ship's ladders
applies_to: Ladder-type access to a loft or mezzanine
check: Not allowed as a means of egress, except to lofts/mezzanines of 200 sq ft or less that do not give the only access to a kitchen or bathroom. Min 20 in. clear width between handrails, handrails both sides 30 to 34 in. high, riser 9-1/2 in. max, tread depth 5 in. min (projected 8-1/2 in.).
note: Covers R311.7.11 and R311.7.12. 9th Edition R331 gives separate stair/ladder allowances for sleeping lofts.

title: Ramps
applies_to: Interior or exterior ramp (e.g., at a floor level change or the egress door)
check: Ramp serving the required egress door: slope 1:12 max (1:8 only where site constraints make 1:12 technically infeasible); other ramps 1:8 max. Landings at top, bottom, at doors and at changes of direction, at least 36 in. wide. Handrail on at least one side where steeper than 1:12, 34 to 38 in. high, graspable, continuous, 1-1/2 in. from the wall.
needs: Ramp rise and run
note: Ramps are not a model object; show as a note where floor levels differ.

title: Guard required
applies_to: Open side of a stair, landing, loft, balcony, mezzanine, raised floor or ramp
check: Guard required where the walking surface is more than 30 in. above the floor or grade below, measured at any point within 24 in. horizontally of the open edge. Insect screening is not a guard.
needs: Height of the walking surface above the floor/grade below at each open edge
note: FBC-EB 803.5 requires adding guards in the work area where they are missing or failing.

title: Guard height
applies_to: Required guards
check: At least 36 in. above the walking surface; on the open side of stairs at least 34 in. above the nosing line; where the guard top is also the handrail, 34 to 38 in.
needs: Guard height

title: Guard openings
applies_to: Required guards
check: No opening that passes a 4 in. sphere; 4-3/8 in. on the open side of stairs; 6 in. at the triangle formed by riser, tread and bottom rail.
needs: Baluster / cable / infill spacing

title: Window fall protection
applies_to: Operable window on an upper story
check: Where the bottom of the clear opening is less than 24 in. above the finished floor AND more than 72 in. above the grade or surface below outside, the window must limit its opening so a 4 in. sphere cannot pass, or have an ASTM F2090 fall-prevention device, or an ASTM F2090 window opening control device.
needs: Height of the window sill above exterior grade (or story level)
note: FBC-EB 702.4 applies the same trigger to replacement windows. Sill height above floor is already in the model.

title: Opening control devices on escape windows
applies_to: Bedroom escape window fitted with an opening control device
check: Device must comply with ASTM F2090 and, once released, must not reduce the net clear opening below R310.2.1 / R310.2.2.

title: Smoke alarm upgrade trigger
applies_to: Any interior alteration, repair or addition that requires a permit; any bedroom added or created
check: The whole dwelling unit must be provided with smoke alarms located as required for a new dwelling. Not triggered by: exterior-surface work only (roofing, siding, window/door replacement, porch or deck) or by plumbing/mechanical work only.
note: Replaces B-19. This is the main 'bring up to code' item for remodels: flag missing alarms throughout the house, not only in the work area. Under the 9th Edition the 'as for new' locations include the attached garage.

title: Smoke alarm in each bedroom
applies_to: Every sleeping room in the dwelling
check: A smoke alarm inside each sleeping room.
note: Replaces B-19.

title: Smoke alarm outside sleeping areas
applies_to: Hall or room immediately outside each separate sleeping area
check: A smoke alarm outside each separate sleeping area in the immediate vicinity of the bedrooms.
note: Replaces B-19.

title: Smoke alarm on each story
applies_to: Each story incl. basement and habitable attic
check: At least one smoke alarm on every additional story. On split levels without a door between, the alarm on the upper level covers a lower level less than one full story below.
note: Replaces B-19.

title: Smoke alarm distance from bathroom
applies_to: Smoke alarm near a bathroom with tub or shower
check: At least 3 ft horizontally from the bathroom door or opening, unless that would prevent placing a required alarm.

title: Smoke alarm distance from cooking
applies_to: Smoke alarm near a range, cooktop or oven
check: 8th Edition: ionization alarm at least 20 ft from a permanently installed cooking appliance (10 ft if it has a silencing switch); photoelectric alarm, or one marked for reduced cooking nuisance, at least 6 ft. Does not apply if it would prevent a required location.
edition_difference: 9th Edition: every smoke alarm at least 10 ft from a cooking appliance; 6 ft allowed where needed to satisfy a required location. No sensor-type distinction.
needs: Alarm sensing type (ionization / photoelectric / listed for cooking nuisance)
note: Without the sensor type, check 6 ft as the absolute minimum and warn under 10 ft / 20 ft.

title: Smoke/heat detection in attached garage
applies_to: Attached garage; room open to a sleeping loft
check: 9th Edition only: a smoke alarm is required in an attached garage; where a smoke alarm cannot be used there because of its listing, install a listed heat detector interconnected with the smoke alarms. Also required in the room to which a sleeping loft is open, near the loft.
edition_difference: New in the 9th Edition; not required under the 8th.
note: 9th Edition only. Because R314.2.2 requires alarms 'located as required for new dwellings', this reaches existing houses with attached garages on permit-requiring interior alterations applied for after December 31, 2026.

title: Smoke alarm interconnection
applies_to: All required smoke alarms in the dwelling
check: Alarms must be interconnected so one sounding triggers all (hard-wired or listed wireless). In existing areas interconnection is not required where the work does not remove wall or ceiling finishes, unless an attic, crawl space or basement gives access without removing finishes.
needs: Interconnected (wired / listed wireless / none)
note: In single-story Florida houses with attic access the exception rarely applies; plan on interconnection (wireless is accepted).

title: Smoke alarm power source
applies_to: All required smoke alarms
check: Primary power from building wiring (no switch other than the breaker) with battery backup. Florida exception: for a repair or a Level 1 alteration, alarms powered by sealed 10-year nonremovable batteries may be used instead of hard-wiring; any battery-only alarm installed or replaced in that work must be the 10-year sealed type.
needs: Alarm power type (hard-wired with backup / 10-year sealed battery) and the project's alteration level
note: Level 2 and Level 3 alterations do not get the battery exception: new alarms are hard-wired with battery backup. Same text in FBC-EB 403.2 and 703.2 (from s. 553.883, F.S.).

title: Smoke alarm listing
applies_to: Smoke alarms and combination smoke/CO alarms
check: Smoke alarms listed to UL 217 and installed per NFPA 72; combination smoke/CO alarms listed to UL 217 and UL 2034 and permitted in place of smoke alarms (R314.5). A household fire alarm system with UL 268 detectors in the same locations is an accepted alternative (R314.7).
edition_difference: 9th Edition adds 'listed and labeled' and installation per listing and manufacturer's instructions (R314.1.2).

title: Carbon monoxide alarms
applies_to: NEW building or ADDITION that has a fossil-fuel appliance, fireplace, attached garage or other CO source
check: An operational CO alarm must be installed within 10 ft of each room used for sleeping. Hard-wired or battery, or a combination smoke/CO alarm listed by an NRTL. Florida exception: does NOT apply to existing buildings undergoing alteration or repair unless the work is an addition (increase in floor area, stories or height).
edition_difference: 9th Edition: battery-only CO alarms must have a nonreplaceable, nonremovable battery good for at least 10 years (R315.1.1).
note: Replaces B-20, which should be corrected: an interior remodel alone does not trigger CO alarms in Florida. Treat as required only when the project includes an addition; otherwise show as a recommendation when gas appliances or an attached garage exist.

title: Foam plastic thermal barrier
applies_to: Spray foam or rigid foam insulation installed in walls, ceilings, roof deck underside, garage
check: Foam plastic must be separated from the interior by a thermal barrier: 1/2 in. gypsum board, 23/32 in. wood structural panel, or material passing NFPA 275. Foam itself: flame spread 75 max, smoke 450 max (R316.3); packages labeled (R316.2). Not needed behind 1 in. of masonry or concrete (R316.5.1).
edition_difference: 9th Edition adds R316.1.1 (spray foam must comply with ICC 1100) and R316.1.2 (material standards for foam sheathing).

title: Foam in attics: ignition barrier
applies_to: Spray foam on the underside of the roof deck or in an attic entered only for service
check: In an attic entered only for repairs/maintenance, the thermal barrier may be replaced by an ignition barrier (e.g., 1-1/2 in. mineral fiber, 1/4 in. wood structural panel, 3/8 in. gypsum board, 3/8 in. particleboard, 1/4 in. hardboard, 0.016 in. steel, 1-1/2 in. cellulose, 1/4 in. fiber-cement) or by a foam tested for exposed use per R316.6.
note: Product evaluation report must show the tested assembly for exposed attic use.

title: Foam plastic trim
applies_to: Polyurethane/polystyrene crown, beams, medallions, decorative trim
check: Exposed foam trim allowed without a thermal barrier only if: density at least 20 pcf, thickness 1/2 in. max, width 8 in. max, covering not more than 10 percent of the wall and ceiling area of the room, flame spread 75 max. Foam used as interior finish otherwise needs specific approval (R316.5.10, R316.6).
note: Faux foam beams larger than these limits need a tested/approved product.

title: Treated wood at slab and masonry
applies_to: New wall plates on a slab on grade; furring on exterior masonry walls; framing near grade
check: Use preservative-treated (AWPA U1) or naturally durable wood for: sills and sleepers on a concrete slab in direct contact with the ground (unless separated by an impervious moisture barrier); furring or framing attached directly to the interior of exterior masonry/concrete walls below grade (unless a vapor retarder is between); wood within the listed clearances of exposed ground. Field-treat cut ends per AWPA M4.
note: Typical note: bottom plates of all new partitions on the slab to be pressure treated.

title: Fasteners in treated wood
applies_to: Fasteners and connectors into preservative-treated wood
check: Hot-dipped galvanized, stainless steel, silicon bronze or copper; staples stainless. Connectors per manufacturer or minimum G185. Exceptions: steel bolts 1/2 in. or larger; plain steel allowed in borate (SBX/DOT, zinc borate) treated wood in dry interior locations.

title: Termite re-treatment at slab cuts
applies_to: Slab trenched or cut for new plumbing, or soil disturbed inside the foundation
check: Where soil treatment is the termite protection, any soil disturbed after the initial treatment must be re-treated, including boxed or formed areas such as tub traps.
note: R318.1 is written for new construction (certificate of compliance); for remodels building departments commonly require re-treatment where the slab is opened. Confirm with the local department.

title: Pipe sleeves through slab
applies_to: New piping penetrating a slab on grade
check: Protective sleeves must not be cellulose-containing material; with soil treatment the sleeve wall is 0.010 in. max and sealed in the slab with a noncorrosive clamp; no termiticide inside the sleeve.

title: Remove wood debris and forms
applies_to: Work at or under slab level
check: Remove all loose wood, grade stakes, forms, tub-trap boxes, plumbing supports and other cellulose material from under and within 1 ft of the building; do not store wood in contact with the ground under the building.

title: Condensate discharge away from wall
applies_to: New or relocated A/C condensate line; irrigation risers; downspouts
check: Condensate lines (and irrigation risers and roof downspouts) must discharge at least 1 ft away from the structure sidewall.

title: Florida 29 in. bathroom door
applies_to: NEW single-family houses, duplexes, triplexes, condominiums and townhouses with a bathroom on a habitable grade level
check: At least one bathroom on a habitable grade level (or the toilet room, if only a toilet room is at grade) must have a door with a 29 in. clear opening.
note: Replaces B-18. Written for new dwellings (from s. 553.504(2), F.S.); in a remodel treat it as: do not narrow the one compliant grade-level bathroom door, and recommend 2-8 (32 in.) doors, rather than flagging existing narrower doors. A 2-6 door gives about 28 in. clear and fails; a 2-8 door passes.

title: Residential elevators and lifts
applies_to: Private residence elevator or platform lift added
check: Elevators per ASME A17.1/CSA B44; platform lifts per ASME A18.1. Florida door-gap limits (R321.4): hoistway door to landing sill edge 3/4 in. max for swinging doors, 2-1/4 in. for sliding doors; space between hoistway door and car door/gate must reject a 4 in. sphere (or 4 in. max for powered sliding doors), or install a permanent hoistway door space guard; car doors must resist 75 lb. Controller must monitor hoistway door locks (R321.4.2).

title: Flood: substantial improvement test
applies_to: Any remodel in a flood hazard area
check: If the cost of the improvement equals or exceeds 50 percent of the market value of the structure before the work (or the building is substantially damaged), the entire building must meet R322, including lowest-floor elevation. Show the cost breakdown and market value (appraisal or adjusted assessed value) for the floodplain administrator.
needs: Flood zone, BFE, lowest floor elevation, total cost of work (labor and materials at market rate), market value of the structure
note: Exclusions and cumulative look-back periods are set by the local floodplain ordinance (many Palm Beach, Broward and Miami-Dade municipalities are stricter than the state minimum).

title: Flood: equipment elevation
applies_to: Electrical, HVAC, plumbing appliances and fixtures, ducts, water heater, panel in a flood hazard area
check: When replaced as part of a substantial improvement, electrical systems and equipment, HVAC, plumbing appliances and fixtures, and ducts must be at or above the required elevation (BFE + 1 ft or DFE), or be designed to keep water out and resist flood loads per ASCE 24. Nothing may be mounted on or pass through breakaway walls. Replacement of flood-damaged exterior equipment must meet this section.
edition_difference: 9th Edition: flood-damaged exterior equipment replaced outside a substantial improvement need only be raised to the height of the first floor or 4 ft above grade, whichever is higher; pool equipment wording changed.
needs: Elevation of each piece of equipment relative to BFE + 1 ft

title: Flood-damage-resistant materials
applies_to: Finishes (flooring, wall board, insulation, cabinets) below the required flood elevation in a substantially improved building
check: Flooring, walls and wall coverings below the required elevation must be flood-damage-resistant materials per FEMA Technical Bulletin 2.
needs: Floor elevation of the room relative to BFE + 1 ft

title: Flood: lowest floor elevation (A zones)
applies_to: Substantially improved dwelling in an A/AE/AH/AO zone
check: Lowest floor at or above BFE + 1 ft or the design flood elevation, whichever is higher (AO zones: depth number + 1 ft above highest adjacent grade, or 3 ft if no depth given). Attached garages may be below only if used solely for parking, access or storage with flood openings.
needs: BFE / DFE and lowest floor elevation

title: Flood: enclosed areas below elevation
applies_to: Garage, storage or enclosure with floor below the required flood elevation
check: Use limited to parking, building access or storage (no bedrooms, baths, kitchens, living space). Flood openings: at least two, on different sides, total net area 1 sq in. per sq ft of enclosed area (or engineered), each at least 3 in. in any direction, bottom not more than 1 ft above the higher of interior floor or exterior grade.
needs: Floor elevation of the enclosure vs. required elevation; flood vent count and net area
note: Garage or ground-level enclosure conversions to living space in a flood zone are the classic violation.

title: Flood: coastal high hazard (V and Coastal A)
applies_to: Dwelling in a V/VE zone or Coastal A zone
check: Lowest horizontal structural member at or above BFE + 1 ft or DFE; space below free of obstruction or enclosed only by lattice, screening or breakaway walls (10 to 20 psf); enclosed areas below used only for parking, access, storage; no fill for structural support; no MEP on or through breakaway walls; an exterior door is required at the top of stairs enclosed by breakaway walls (R322.3.6.1); design sealed by a registered design professional (R322.3.9).
edition_difference: 9th Edition adds an ultimate-load equivalent for breakaway walls (17 to 33 psf).
needs: Flood zone = V or Coastal A; elevation of lowest horizontal structural member

title: Flood: as-built elevation documents
applies_to: Substantial improvement in a flood hazard area
check: A licensed surveyor or registered design professional must prepare and seal documentation of the as-built elevations.
edition_difference: 9th Edition specifies the FEMA Elevation Certificate (or equivalent).

title: Mezzanines and lofts
applies_to: New loft or mezzanine open to a room
check: Clear height above and below the mezzanine floor at least 7 ft; total mezzanine area not more than one-third of the floor area of the room it is in; open to that room except for walls 36 to 42 in. high (enclosed part 10 percent max, unless sprinklered); egress per R311; guards per R312.
edition_difference: 9th Edition adds R331 Sleeping Lofts as an alternative: loft under 70 sq ft, at least 3 ft headroom in the loft, 7 ft clear below, with reduced stair (17 in. wide, risers 7 to 12 in.) or ladder (12 in. rungs, 70 to 80 degrees) access.
note: Needs loft as a room with its own floor level; otherwise show as reminder.

title: Battery storage (ESS) location
applies_to: Home battery energy storage system
check: Allowed only in: detached garages/accessory structures; attached garages separated per R302.6; outdoors at least 3 ft from doors and windows; enclosed utility closets or storage/utility spaces with finished or noncombustible walls and ceilings (unfinished wood framing needs 5/8 in. Type X). Never in sleeping rooms or in closets/spaces opening directly into sleeping rooms. Units 3 ft apart unless tested for less (R328.3.1).
edition_difference: 9th Edition retitles the section and revises R328.4 and impact-protection details (R328.8.1 to R328.8.3); recheck when the 9th is in force.
needs: ESS present; room it is located in
note: ESS listed to UL 9540 and marked for use in residential dwelling units, installed per instructions and NEC, are exempt from R328 (R328.1 exc. 1).

title: Battery storage (ESS) size and protection
applies_to: Home battery energy storage system
check: Each unit 20 kWh max. Aggregate: 40 kWh in utility closets/storage spaces; 80 kWh in garages, on exterior walls or outdoors on grade. Listed to UL 9540 (R328.2). Room must have a smoke alarm, or an interconnected heat detector where a smoke alarm cannot be used (R328.7). Protect from vehicle impact where exposed (R328.8).
needs: ESS kWh rating and count

title: Standby generators
applies_to: Permanently installed generator
check: Listed and labeled to UL 2200, connected through a listed transfer switch, installed per listing, manufacturer's instructions and the electrical chapter, in an approved location.
note: Clearances to openings come from the manufacturer's instructions and NFPA 37; fuel gas sizing from the fuel gas code.

title: Corrosion-resistant fasteners near salt water
applies_to: Exposed or unconditioned-space fasteners and connectors within 3,000 ft of a saltwater coastline
check: 9th Edition only: fasteners and connectors (not embedded in concrete/mortar) must meet Table R332.1: stainless steel for exterior exposures within 300 ft of the coast; galvanized / enhanced galvanized elsewhere within 3,000 ft and in vented unconditioned spaces.
edition_difference: New section in the 9th Edition.
needs: Project field: distance to saltwater coastline
note: 9th Edition only. Affects exterior door/window anchors, attic straps and exterior framing hardware.

title: Which code governs a remodel
applies_to: Every remodel of an existing one- or two-family dwelling or townhouse (3 stories or less)
check: New houses follow the Florida Building Code, Residential. Existing buildings undergoing repair, alteration, addition or change of occupancy must comply with the Florida Building Code, Existing Building (R101.2 exception 3), which in turn sends new work back to the Residential, Energy, Mechanical, Plumbing, Fuel Gas codes and the NEC. Administration is under Chapter 1 of FBC-Building.
note: Cover sheet should cite both: FBC Existing Building (alteration level) and FBC Residential, with the edition.

title: Existing legal conditions may remain
applies_to: Parts of the house not being altered
check: The legal occupancy and existing construction of a previously occupied building may continue without change except where this code or the Florida Fire Prevention Code specifically requires an upgrade, or the code official finds it necessary for safety.
note: Basis for not flagging existing non-conforming items outside the work (existing stairs, hall widths, ceiling heights, windows).

title: Substantial improvement definition
applies_to: Any work on a building in a flood hazard area
check: Substantial improvement = any repair, alteration, addition or improvement whose cost equals or exceeds 50 percent of the market value of the structure before the work starts. Repairs of substantial damage (restoration cost 50 percent or more of pre-damage market value) always count. Excluded: minimum work to correct cited health/sanitary/safety violations; alterations of historic structures that keep the designation.
needs: Cost of work, market value of structure, flood zone

title: Work area definition
applies_to: Every alteration permit
check: Work area = all reconfigured spaces shown on the construction documents. It excludes areas where only incidental work is done and areas where work is required only because the code demands it.
note: The app can total the floor area of rooms with new/moved/removed walls, doors or reconfigured layouts and divide by building area to suggest Level 2 vs Level 3.

title: Compliance method
applies_to: Every alteration permit
check: Pick one method and do not mix: prescriptive (Chapter 5), work area (Chapters 6 to 13, the usual choice), or performance (Chapter 14). With the code official's approval, an alteration may instead comply with the code in effect when the building was built, except for new structural members, flood substantial improvement, and the structural provisions (707, 807, 907).
note: State the method on the cover sheet (e.g., 'FBC-EB Work Area Method, Alteration Level 2').

title: Other codes apply to new work
applies_to: All new work in an alteration
check: New work must also meet the Energy Conservation, Fuel Gas, Mechanical, Plumbing and Residential volumes, the Florida Fire Prevention Code and NFPA 70 as they apply to alterations; where they conflict with the Existing Building code, the Existing Building code governs.

title: Existing materials may stay
applies_to: Existing materials and assemblies not being replaced
check: Materials already in use that complied when installed may remain unless the building official finds them unsafe.

title: New and replacement materials
applies_to: All new or replacement materials
check: Use materials permitted for new construction. Like-for-like materials are allowed for repairs and alterations if no unsafe condition results.

title: Repair classification
applies_to: Patching, restoring or replacing damaged materials, elements, equipment or fixtures
check: Repair work follows Chapter 4 (not the alteration chapters): it must not make the building less conforming than before (401.3); work on undamaged components needed to make the repair is part of the repair (401.4).

title: Repairs in flood hazard areas
applies_to: Repair in a flood zone, incl. storm/flood damage repair
check: Repairs that amount to substantial improvement, and buildings with substantial damage (406.2.4), must be brought into compliance with R322.
needs: Flood zone; cost of repair vs. market value

title: Replacement glass in hazardous locations
applies_to: Any glass replaced in a hazardous location (doors, sidelights, tub/shower, low large windows, stairs)
check: Replacement glazing in hazardous locations must be safety glazing per R308, even in a repair. Exception: glass block, louvered windows and jalousies repaired with like materials.
note: Use the R308.4 location tests on any window or door flagged as re-glazed or replaced.

title: Smoke alarms in repairs / Level 1
applies_to: Repair or Level 1 alteration of a one- or two-family dwelling or townhouse
check: May use smoke alarms with sealed 10-year nonremovable batteries instead of hard-wiring. Any battery alarm newly installed or replaced in that work must be the 10-year sealed type (not required for monitored systems, RF-wireless interconnected alarms, or multi-sensor/combination units).
needs: Alarm power type
note: Identical text in 703.2 and FBC-R R314.6 exc. 2.

title: Structural repairs
applies_to: Repair of damaged structural members (rot, termite, water damage found during the remodel)
check: Dangerous conditions must be eliminated. Less-than-substantial structural damage may be restored to its pre-damage condition; new members and connections must meet current detailing requirements.
note: Use for the existing-condition 'damage' pins.

title: Electrical repairs
applies_to: Repair or like-for-like replacement of existing wiring, devices, equipment
check: 8th Edition: existing wiring and equipment may be repaired or replaced with like material; replacement receptacles must follow NEC 406.4(D) (GFCI, AFCI, tamper-resistant and grounding-type replacement rules); Edison-base plug fuses only where no evidence of overfusing.
edition_difference: 9th Edition replaces this with: electrical repairs shall be in accordance with NFPA 70; adds a rule on reconditioned equipment; deletes the separate receptacle, plug-fuse, nongrounding-receptacle and appliance-grounding subsections (NEC governs directly).

title: Replacing two-prong receptacles
applies_to: Nongrounding receptacles replaced on circuits without an equipment ground
check: 8th Edition: a grounding-type replacement may be grounded to any accessible point on the grounding electrode system or grounding electrode conductor per NEC 250.130(C). Existing range, oven, cooktop and dryer frames on existing circuits may remain grounded to the neutral per NEC 250.140 (407.1.5).
edition_difference: Deleted in the 9th Edition (NEC 406.4(D), 250.130(C) and 250.140 still apply through 407.1).

title: Replacement water closets
applies_to: Water closet replaced
check: Replaced water closets: 1.6 gallons per flush maximum.
needs: Fixture flush volume
note: New fixtures in an alteration must also meet the current plumbing/energy water-efficiency limits, which may be lower; see the plumbing rule set.

title: Show the work area on the drawings
applies_to: Every alteration permit set
check: The work area must be identified on the construction documents.
note: Generate a work-area key plan (hatched reconfigured spaces) with work-area sq ft, building sq ft and the percentage.

title: Level 1 alteration
applies_to: Removal and replacement or covering of existing materials, elements, equipment or fixtures with new ones serving the same purpose
check: Classify as Level 1 when nothing is reconfigured: same-location cabinet, fixture, finish, flooring, drywall, window/door (same opening) and equipment replacement. Comply with Chapter 7.
note: Project-level classifier: no walls added/removed, no door or window added or eliminated, no system reconfigured or extended.

title: Level 2 alteration
applies_to: Reconfiguration of space; adding or eliminating any door or window; reconfiguring or extending any system; installing additional equipment
check: Classify as Level 2 when any of those occur and the work area is 50 percent or less of the building area. Comply with Chapter 7 and Chapter 8.
note: Moving a wall, relocating a sink or adding a circuit/extension of plumbing makes it Level 2.

title: Level 3 alteration
applies_to: Work area exceeds 50 percent of the building area
check: Classify as Level 3 when the work area is more than 50 percent of the building area. Comply with Chapters 7, 8 and 9; under 901.2 the Chapter 8 building-element, fire-protection and egress sections (803, 804, 805) then apply to all work areas.
note: Whole-house interior gut = Level 3.

title: Change of occupancy
applies_to: Use of the building or part of it changes so that the code requires more (e.g., house to office, assisted living, short-term lodging, adding a dwelling unit)
check: Classify as change of occupancy and apply Chapter 10. Changing room names inside a single-family house (den to bedroom, garage to family room) is not a change of occupancy classification, but the re-purposed room is a new space that must meet current code for its new use.
note: The second sentence is an application note, not code text.

title: Do not reduce safety or efficiency
applies_to: All alterations
check: The building or the altered portion may not be made less safe or less energy efficient than it was. If any current level of safety or sanitation is reduced, the altered portion must meet the code for new construction.
note: Examples: removing the only tub/shower, deleting a bedroom window, narrowing the egress door, removing smoke alarms, removing a rated garage door.

title: Flood: alterations
applies_to: Alteration in a flood hazard area
check: An alteration that is a substantial improvement requires the building to comply with R322. Replacement of flood-damaged exterior equipment and appliances must meet R322.1.6.
edition_difference: 9th Edition: outside a substantial improvement, flood-damaged exterior equipment being replaced must be raised to the height of the first floor or 4 ft above grade, whichever is higher.
needs: Flood zone; cost vs. market value

title: New interior finishes
applies_to: Newly installed wall, ceiling and floor finishes and trim
check: New wall and ceiling finishes must meet the interior-finish flammability chapter (FBC-B Chapter 8; for dwellings the same limits as R302.9: flame spread 200, smoke 450); new floor finish incl. carpet per FBC-B 804; new trim per FBC-B 806.
note: Sections 702.1 to 702.3.

title: Fall protection on replacement windows
applies_to: Existing operable window being replaced (sash and frame, or sash only)
check: Install an ASTM F2090 window opening control device or fall-prevention device when ALL apply: the bottom of the clear opening is less than 24 in. above the finished floor (one- and two-family dwellings and townhouses); the window can open enough to pass a 4 in. sphere; and the opening is more than 72 in. above the grade or surface below.
needs: Height of the opening above exterior grade; window flagged as replacement

title: Replacement bedroom windows (escape)
applies_to: Replacement of a window that serves as the required emergency escape opening
