check: Exempt from the R310.2.1, R310.2.2 and R310.2.3 size and sill limits if the replacement is the manufacturer's largest standard size that fits the existing frame or rough opening and is the same operating style or one giving equal or greater opening area. Opening control devices must release to the full opening without keys or tools (702.5.1).
needs: Window flagged as replacement in existing opening; old and new operating style

title: Materials and methods for new work
applies_to: All new work in any alteration level
check: New work must meet the materials-and-methods requirements of the Building, Energy, Mechanical and Plumbing codes: material standards, installation and connection details, joints, penetrations and continuity. For fuel gas (702.6.1): FBC-Fuel Gas Chapters 3 to 6 apply; existing gas piping need not be resized unless the load or length of the system is increased.
note: Tie to the existing-condition gas pin: adding a gas range, tankless heater or generator increases load and triggers pipe sizing.

title: Maintain fire protection
applies_to: All alterations
check: Work must maintain the level of fire protection that exists (do not remove garage separation, rated walls, fireblocking, smoke alarms).

title: Maintain egress
applies_to: All alterations
check: Work must maintain the existing level of protection for the means of egress (do not block or narrow the egress path, required door, stairs, escape windows).

title: Added dead load from equipment
applies_to: Replacement equipment supported by the structure that is heavier than what it replaces (attic air handler, water heater platform, stone tops on framed floors, heavy tile)
check: Supporting structure must meet gravity-load requirements unless the added dead load increases force in the member by 5 percent or less (or, for conventionally framed houses, the dead load is not increased more than 5 percent).

title: Replacement windows and doors: wind loads
applies_to: Replacement of garage doors, exterior doors, skylights, operable and fixed windows
check: Replacements must be designed and installed for current wind loads (FBC-B Chapter 16 / R301.2.1): rated design pressure at least the required pressure, anchored per the product approval.
edition_difference: 9th Edition also requires compliance with FBC-B Chapter 14 and FBC-R Chapter 7 (exterior wall / flashing and water-resistance at the opening).
needs: Required design pressures and each product's rating / approval number

title: Opening protection: 25 percent exception
applies_to: One- or two-family dwelling built under a pre-FBC code, in a wind-borne debris region (not HVHZ), replacing windows/glazed doors
check: Replacement glazed products installed within any 12-month period need not have impact/shutter protection if the aggregate glazed area replaced is 25 percent or less of the total glazed opening area of the dwelling; they must still meet wind pressures for an enclosed building. Above 25 percent, all replaced openings need protection.
needs: Year built / permitted under a pre-FBC code; wind-borne debris region; glazed area of each exterior opening; which are replaced; replacements in the prior 12 months
note: The app can compute replaced glazing area / total glazing area. The first statewide FBC took effect March 1, 2002 (date from general knowledge, not from the section text). Houses built under the FBC get no exception.

title: Opening protection: HVHZ 25 percent exception
applies_to: One- or two-family dwelling in the HVHZ (Miami-Dade, Broward) built under codes before September 1, 1994
check: Replacement exterior glazed doors, sliding glass doors, skylights and windows within any 12-month period need not have opening protection if the aggregate glazed area replaced is 25 percent or less of the dwelling's total glazed opening area.
needs: County; year built; glazed areas as above
note: Products still need a Miami-Dade NOA or Florida HVHZ approval and must meet HVHZ wind pressures.

title: Enclosed porch/balcony openings
applies_to: Sunroom, balcony or porch enclosed under an existing roof
check: Its openings need not be protected if a wall separates it from the interior and all openings in that wall are protected. Screen or removable vinyl/acrylic panel enclosures do not trigger protection of the wall behind. HVHZ follows FBC-B Chapter 16 instead.

title: Energy code applies
applies_to: All alteration levels (also 811.1, 908.1)
check: Alterations must comply with the Florida Building Code, Energy Conservation, alteration provisions (new/replaced windows, insulation in opened cavities, HVAC and water-heater replacement, lighting).
note: Details are in the energy rule set.

title: New elements meet current code
applies_to: Level 2 and 3: every new wall, room, space, component and system
check: All new construction elements, components, systems and spaces must comply with the code for new construction (for dwellings, the Residential code).
note: This is the hook that applies the FBC-R Chapter 3 rules to new and reconfigured rooms, while existing untouched rooms may remain.

title: Added windows: light/ventilation relief
applies_to: Level 2: window added to an existing room
check: Windows may be added without having to bring the room up to the natural light and ventilation minimums.
note: Exception 1.

title: Ceiling height of newly created spaces
applies_to: Level 2 and 3: newly created habitable or occupiable rooms and corridors
check: Minimum ceiling height 7 ft.
note: Exception 4. Consistent with R305.1.

title: Guards in the work area
applies_to: Level 2 and 3: floor edge, balcony, loft or landing within the work area more than 30 in. above the floor/grade below
check: Where there is no guard, or the existing guard is in danger of collapse, a guard meeting current code must be provided.
needs: Existing guard present and sound (yes/no); drop height

title: Smoke alarms in the work area
applies_to: Level 2 and 3: dwelling units within the work area
check: Dwelling units in the work area must have smoke alarms per the Florida Fire Prevention Code; interconnection outside the work area is not required by this section.
note: For one- and two-family dwellings FBC-R R314.2.2 is the more demanding rule (whole dwelling); apply that.

title: Handrails on existing stairs
applies_to: Level 3 (and Level 2 with shared exits): existing stair serving the work area with three or more risers
check: If the stair has no handrail, or the handrail is in danger of collapse, provide a code-complying handrail full length on at least one side.
edition_difference: 9th Edition adds: handrail extensions may be omitted where hazardous due to plan configuration; and 805.13, an existing stair need not be rebuilt to current rise/run where space does not allow a reduction in pitch.
needs: Existing stair has a sound handrail (yes/no)
note: In a single-family dwelling Section 805 applies through 901.2 (Level 3). Level 2 applies it only to exits/corridors shared by more than one tenant.

title: Guards on existing stairs and landings
applies_to: Level 3: open sides of stairs, landings, balconies on the egress path more than 30 in. above the floor below
check: Where guards are missing or failing, provide guards meeting current code.
needs: Existing guard present and sound (yes/no)

title: New structural elements
applies_to: New beams, headers, posts, framing, connections
check: New structural elements and their connections must comply with the current code.

title: Existing gravity structure
applies_to: Bearing wall removed or opened; added load on existing framing (second-floor bath, stone, tile, tub, equipment)
check: Do not reduce the capacity of existing gravity-load elements unless shown adequate for current design loads; existing elements that receive added load must meet current code unless stress rises 5 percent or less. One- and two-family dwellings may be checked with the Residential code's conventional framing provisions.
note: Minimum design loads for unaffected existing elements are those in effect when built (807.3).

title: Existing lateral (wind) structure
applies_to: Removing or cutting exterior or shear walls; adding wind area
check: If the alteration increases lateral design loads or reduces the capacity of a lateral-load element, show the structure meets current wind provisions, unless the demand-capacity ratio of each affected element rises 10 percent or less (cumulative since original construction).

title: New electrical work to NEC
applies_to: Level 2 and 3: all newly installed wiring and equipment in the work area
check: Must comply with NFPA 70 (the adopted NEC edition).
note: Detailed NEC checks are in the electrical rule set.

title: Minimum outlets in altered rooms
applies_to: Level 2 and 3: enclosed rooms in the work area other than closets, kitchens, basements, garages, hallways, laundry, utility, storage and bathrooms
check: Each such room must end up with at least two duplex receptacles, or one duplex receptacle plus one ceiling or wall lighting outlet.
note: This is a floor for existing rooms in the work area; rooms with new wiring must meet full NEC 210.52 spacing.

title: Minimum kitchen receptacles
applies_to: Level 2 and 3: kitchen in the work area
check: At least two duplex receptacle outlets.
note: A remodeled kitchen with new wiring must meet NEC 210.52(B) and (C) in full.

title: Laundry receptacle
applies_to: Level 2 and 3: laundry area in the work area
check: At least one duplex receptacle near the laundry equipment on an independent circuit.

title: GFCI for new receptacles
applies_to: Level 2 and 3: newly installed receptacles
check: New receptacle outlets must have GFCI protection wherever the NEC requires it.
note: See electrical rule E-05 (NEC 210.8).

title: Minimum lighting outlets
applies_to: Level 2 and 3: work area within a dwelling unit
check: At least one lighting outlet in every bathroom, hallway, stairway, attached garage and detached garage with power, and at outdoor entrances and exits.

title: Lighting in utility rooms
applies_to: Level 2 and 3: utility rooms and basements used for storage or containing equipment needing service
check: At least one lighting outlet.

title: Service equipment clearance
applies_to: Level 2 and 3: electrical service equipment in the work area
check: Working clearance per NFPA 70 must be provided.
note: See electrical rule E-16 (NEC 110.26). Bites when cabinets, laundry or walls are built in front of an existing panel.

title: Ventilation of reconfigured or converted spaces
applies_to: Level 2 and 3: reconfigured rooms and spaces converted to habitable use (garage, porch, attic)
check: Provide natural or mechanical ventilation per the Mechanical code (for dwellings: R303 / M1505-M1507).

title: Local exhaust for new sources
applies_to: Level 2 and 3: newly introduced equipment that produces odors, fumes, vapor or combustion products
check: Provide local exhaust for the new source.

title: Level 3 scope expansion
applies_to: Level 3 alteration
check: Comply with all of Chapters 7 and 8; Sections 803 (building elements), 804 (fire protection) and 805 (means of egress) apply in all work areas regardless of shared exits or occupant load.

title: Townhouse/attached unit separation wall
applies_to: Level 3 in a townhouse or attached dwelling unit where finishes are removed
check: Unit separation walls that do not run continuously from foundation to the underside of roof sheathing must be completed as a continuous fire separation (matching existing construction or new-construction requirements), working from the side being altered. Not required where wall/ceiling finishes are not removed.

title: Level 3 lateral system
applies_to: Level 3 alteration with structural work
check: One- and two-family dwellings altered using Residential-code conventional framing are exempt from the full lateral evaluation; otherwise an engineer's evaluation is required, and a substantial structural alteration (gravity elements altered within 5 years supporting more than 30 percent of floor and roof area) must meet current wind loads.

title: Change of use within the same group
applies_to: Part of the dwelling changes use so that different code requirements apply
check: Work must meet the alteration-level requirements for the work plus Sections 1002 to 1011: light and ventilation for the new use per current code (1011.1), unsafe electrical conditions corrected and outlets/service adequate for the new use (1008), mechanical ventilation (1009), plumbing fixtures for the new use (1010).

title: Existing escape windows at change of occupancy
applies_to: Change of occupancy that newly requires emergency escape openings
check: An existing operable window may serve if it gives at least 4 sq ft net clear opening, 22 in. clear height and 20 in. clear width; a replacement must meet those and be the largest standard size that fits the existing opening.
needs: Net clear opening of the existing window
note: Applies only to a true change of occupancy classification, not to converting a den to a bedroom inside a single-family house (there the new sleeping room must meet R310).

title: HVHZ uses Chapter 44
applies_to: Any project in Miami-Dade or Broward County (High-Velocity Hurricane Zone)
check: In the HVHZ, floors, walls, wall coverings and roof-ceiling work follow FBC-R Chapter 44 instead of Chapters 5 through 8. Flag the project so the HVHZ rule set is used for framing, sheathing, windows and doors.
needs: Project county (HVHZ yes/no)
note: Same exception is repeated at R601.1, R701.1 and R801.1. Palm Beach County is not HVHZ. Chapter 44 was not walked in this area.

title: Floor carries added loads
applies_to: New heavy items on a framed floor: cast-iron or stone tub, mortar-bed shower, stone island, water heater, masonry
check: Floor framing must carry the loads of Section R301 and pass them to the supports. Where the remodel adds concentrated or heavy dead load on a wood-framed floor, show that the existing framing is adequate or show the reinforcement.
note: Slab-on-grade houses are not affected. Structural members are not in the model.

title: Floor framing design basis
applies_to: New or altered wood floor framing (second floors, raised floors, new floor openings, stair openings)
check: Florida has no prescriptive joist span tables or floor-opening framing rules in the Residential code. New or altered floor framing, including headers and trimmers around a new floor opening, must follow the AWC Wood Frame Construction Manual (WFCM) or the NDS (engineered).
note: IRC R502.3 through R502.10 (spans, bearing, lateral restraint, notching, openings, attachment) are Reserved in Florida. Do not cite those IRC numbers on a Florida permit set.

title: Joist notching and boring
applies_to: Plumbing, electrical or duct runs through sawn-lumber floor joists
check: Sawn joists: notch depth at most 1/6 of joist depth and never in the middle third of the span; notch at the bearing end at most 1/4 of depth; holes at most 1/3 of joist depth, at least 2 in. from the top and bottom edges and from any other hole or notch.
note: Florida reserved (deleted) the model-code prescriptive text for this item; the numbers shown are the base IRC limits, which match the AWC WFCM limits as best known. Not read from an opened source: confirm against the WFCM or the engineer's detail. Florida 8th and 9th Editions both point R502.2 to R301.2.1.1 (WFCM, ASCE 7, FBC-Building) or the NDS.

title: No cutting floor trusses
applies_to: Floor trusses or engineered floor members where plumbing, ducts or openings are added
check: Do not cut, notch, splice or otherwise alter floor truss members without written approval of a registered design professional. Added load beyond the truss design load (large tub, stone, equipment) needs verification that the truss can carry it.

title: Truss drawings for new trusses
applies_to: New floor trusses added in the remodel
check: Submit truss design drawings to the building official before installation and keep them on site. Drawings prepared by a registered design professional where Florida Statutes require.

title: Draftstopping in floor-ceilings
applies_to: New suspended or furred ceiling below a framed floor; opened floor-ceiling cavities
check: Provide draftstopping in floor-ceiling assemblies as required by R302.12 when the remodel creates or opens a concealed floor-ceiling space.
note: The numeric limit is in R302.12 (Chapter 3 area).

title: Fireblocking in floor framing
applies_to: Any new framing, soffit, chase or penetration at floor or ceiling level
check: Provide fireblocking per R302.11 in floor framing work. See the fireblocking rules listed under R302.11.

title: Subfloor replacement
applies_to: Replaced subfloor or sheathing in a bathroom, kitchen or laundry on a framed floor
check: Replacement floor sheathing must follow the WFCM or the NDS (panel grade, thickness for the joist spacing, fastening). There is no Florida prescriptive subfloor table.
note: The code has no separate rule for underlayment under floor tile; tile work follows the ANSI A108 series (see R702.4.1) and the tile backer manufacturer's instructions.

title: Slab patch thickness
applies_to: Concrete slab trenched or cut for relocated drains, island plumbing, floor outlets or a curbless shower recess
check: Restore slab-on-ground to at least 3-1/2 in. thick concrete. A recessed shower pan area cut into the slab must still leave or rebuild a 3-1/2 in. slab.
note: Soil disturbed under a slab also triggers termite re-treatment under R318 (Chapter 3 area).

title: Trench backfill under slab
applies_to: Slab trench backfilled after under-slab plumbing
check: Fill must be free of vegetation and debris and compacted for uniform slab support. Fill depth limit unless approved: 24 in. clean sand or gravel, 8 in. earth.

title: Vapor retarder at slab patch
applies_to: Slab trench or patch in conditioned living space
check: Place a 6-mil polyethylene (or approved) vapor retarder under the new concrete, lapped at least 6 in. with the existing retarder. Not required in garages, unheated accessory buildings or exterior flatwork.

title: No carpet under walls
applies_to: New wall or partition set on an existing finished floor
check: A wall, partition or column fastened to the floor may not sit on compressible floor covering (compresses more than 1/32 in. under 50 lb on 1 sq in. and is over 1/8 in. thick). Remove carpet and pad under new plates.

title: Stud grade
applies_to: New wood stud walls
check: Studs at least No. 3, Standard or Stud grade. Utility grade is allowed only for nonbearing studs and for bearing studs that do not support floors.

title: Bearing wall work needs design
applies_to: Wall flagged bearing that is new, demolished, shortened or given a new or wider opening; any new header or beam
check: Florida deleted the IRC prescriptive wall-framing rules (stud tables, top plates, interior bearing walls, header span tables, header supports). Flag every bearing wall that is removed or opened: the header or beam, jack and king studs, and the load path to the foundation must be sized from the WFCM or by an engineer and shown on the permit set.
note: Test: wall.bearing is true AND (status is demo OR a new or widened opening exists in it). IRC R602.3.1 through R602.7.5 and Tables R602.7(1),(2) are Reserved in Florida in both the 8th and 9th Editions.

title: Nonbearing partition framing
applies_to: New interior nonbearing wood partitions
check: Typical compliant partition: 2x4 studs at 16 in. or 24 in. on center with a single bottom plate and a top plate, fastened to floor and ceiling framing. Base IRC allowed 2x3 at 24 in. or 2x4 flat at 16 in. for nonbearing walls and a single top plate.
needs: Stud size and spacing of each new wall type
note: Florida reserved (deleted) the model-code prescriptive text for this item; the numbers shown are the base IRC limits, which match the AWC WFCM limits as best known. Not read from an opened source: confirm against the WFCM or the engineer's detail. IRC R602.5 is Reserved in Florida.

title: Stud notching and boring
applies_to: Pipes and cables through studs of new or existing walls; plumbing walls behind toilets, tubs and showers
check: Bearing or exterior wall studs: notch at most 25 percent of stud width, bored hole at most 40 percent (60 percent if the stud is doubled and no more than two successive studs are bored). Nonbearing studs: notch at most 40 percent, hole at most 60 percent. Hole edge at least 5/8 in. from the stud edge and not in the same section as a notch.
note: Florida reserved (deleted) the model-code prescriptive text for this item; the numbers shown are the base IRC limits, which match the AWC WFCM limits as best known. Not read from an opened source: confirm against the WFCM or the engineer's detail. IRC R602.6 is Reserved in Florida. Derived drawing check: a 3 in. drain or vent (3-1/2 in. outside diameter) cannot pass through a 2x4 wall within these limits, so flag a wall thinner than 2x6 that carries a toilet drain or 3 in. stack.

title: Top plate cut for piping
applies_to: Top plate of a bearing or exterior wall cut or notched more than half its width for a pipe or duct
check: Tie the plate across the cut with a galvanized metal strap at least 16 gage and 1-1/2 in. wide, fastened each side with eight 10d nails (or equivalent), extending at least 6 in. past the opening.
note: Florida reserved (deleted) the model-code prescriptive text for this item; the numbers shown are the base IRC limits, which match the AWC WFCM limits as best known. Not read from an opened source: confirm against the WFCM or the engineer's detail. IRC R602.6.1 is Reserved in Florida.

title: Headers in nonbearing walls
applies_to: Door or cased opening in a new nonbearing partition
check: Nonbearing walls do not need a load-bearing header. Base IRC allowed a single flat 2x4 header for openings up to 8 ft wide where the height above to the top plate is 24 in. or less; cripples or blocking above as needed for finish attachment.
note: Florida reserved (deleted) the model-code prescriptive text for this item; the numbers shown are the base IRC limits, which match the AWC WFCM limits as best known. Not read from an opened source: confirm against the WFCM or the engineer's detail. IRC R602.7.4 is Reserved in Florida.

title: Fireblocking in walls
applies_to: New stud walls, furred walls, double or staggered stud walls, walls taller than 10 ft
check: Fireblock concealed stud spaces vertically at ceiling and floor levels and horizontally at intervals of 10 ft or less. Flag any new framed or furred wall taller than 10 ft for mid-height fireblocking.
note: Test: new framed wall height greater than 120 in. Florida Reserved R602.8, but R302.11 itself is in force. This item sits in Chapter 3; keep one copy if the Chapter 3 list also has it.

title: Fireblocking at soffits
applies_to: New soffit, dropped ceiling, cove ceiling, tray ceiling, bulkhead over cabinets, framed chase
check: Fireblock where a concealed vertical space (stud bay) meets a concealed horizontal space (soffit, drop or cove ceiling). Show a note at every new soffit and dropped ceiling.
note: Trigger from the model: any soffit, tray, coffered or dropped ceiling object touching a framed wall.

title: Fireblock penetrations
applies_to: New pipes, vents, ducts, cables through top or bottom plates
check: Seal the opening around vents, pipes, ducts, cables and wires at ceiling and floor level with an approved material that resists passage of flame and smoke.

title: Fireblocking materials
applies_to: Any fireblocking location
check: Acceptable fireblocking: 2 in. nominal lumber; two layers of 1 in. lumber with staggered joints; 23/32 in. structural panel or 3/4 in. particleboard with backed joints; 1/2 in. gypsum board; 1/4 in. cement millboard; mineral wool or glass fiber batts held securely in place. Unfaced fiberglass batts must fill the full cavity section for at least 16 in. of height.

title: Load-bearing steel studs
applies_to: New load-bearing cold-formed steel stud walls
check: Load-bearing cold-formed steel wall framing must be designed under AISI S230 (or engineered). Florida has no prescriptive steel stud tables in the Residential code.

title: Nonbearing steel studs
applies_to: New interior partitions framed with light-gauge steel studs
check: Steel framing that supports gypsum board must have a face at least 1-1/4 in. wide. Nonbearing steel studs comply with AISI S220; load-bearing with AISI S240.
needs: Wall framing material and stud gauge/standard

title: Chases in masonry walls
applies_to: Recess, niche, panel box recess or pipe chase cut into a concrete block or brick wall
check: A chase or recess may be no deeper than 1/3 of the wall thickness; a horizontal chase no longer than 4 ft; keep at least 8 in. of masonry behind it and between chases and opening jambs; none within a pier. Masonry above a chase wider than 12 in. needs a noncombustible lintel. The chase may not reduce required strength or fire resistance.
needs: Wall is masonry; recess depth and width
note: In a standard 8 in. block wall these limits leave little or no room for a recess; treat any niche or recessed panel in a block wall as needing an engineer's detail.

title: Lintel at new masonry opening
applies_to: New or widened door, window or pass-through opening in a masonry (CBS) wall
check: Masonry over every opening must be carried by a steel, reinforced concrete or reinforced masonry lintel (or arch) designed for the load. Flag each new or enlarged opening in a masonry wall for a lintel detail.
note: Test: opening is new or wider than existing AND host wall layers include masonry. Masonry design follows R606, R301.2.1.1 (ICC 600, ASCE 7) or TMS 402/403/404 (R606.1).

title: Masonry opening tolerance
applies_to: Window or door rough opening in a masonry wall
check: Built masonry rough opening may differ from the plan dimension by no more than minus 1/4 in. to plus 1/2 in.

title: Beam bearing on masonry
applies_to: New beam, girder or header bearing on a masonry wall
check: A beam or other concentrated load needs at least 3 in. of bearing length on solid masonry at least 4 in. thick, or a designed metal bearing plate. Joists need at least 1-1/2 in. of bearing.

title: Glass block unit thickness
applies_to: Glass block wall or panel (shower wall, partition, window infill)
check: Standard glass block units at least 3-7/8 in. thick; thin units at least 3-1/8 in. (hollow) or 3 in. (solid). Reclaimed units are not allowed.
needs: Glass block unit thickness

title: Interior glass block panel size
applies_to: Interior glass block panel
check: Each interior panel at most 250 sq ft with standard units or 150 sq ft with thin units; at most 25 ft wide and 20 ft high between structural supports.
note: Test on panel width, height and area once the wall type is glass block.

title: Exterior glass block panels
applies_to: Glass block infill in an exterior wall opening
check: Exterior thin-unit panels at most 85 sq ft, 15 ft wide, 10 ft high, and not allowed where design wind pressure exceeds 20 psf. Standard-unit panels 144 sq ft at 20 psf, less at higher pressure per the code figure.
needs: Design wind pressure at the opening
note: Florida design pressures normally exceed 20 psf, so thin units are effectively excluded on exterior walls and a product approval is needed.

title: Glass block lateral support
applies_to: Glass block panel
check: Support the panel along the top and both sides with panel anchors at 16 in. on center or less (embedded 12 in., two fasteners) or channel restraints with at least 1 in. of recess. Supports resist 200 lb per linear ft. The supporting member may not deflect more than L/600.

title: Glass block joints and mortar
applies_to: Glass block panel
check: Expansion joints at least 3/8 in. at the top and sides, free of mortar and filled with resilient material; Type S or N mortar; horizontal joint reinforcement at 16 in. on center or less and directly above and below openings; asphalt emulsion coating on the sill before bedding.

title: Window and door installation
applies_to: Replaced or new exterior window or door
check: Install and flash each exterior window and door per the manufacturer's written instructions, which must be provided for each unit, and flash the opening per R703.4.

title: Design pressure rating
applies_to: Replaced or new exterior window, exterior door or sliding glass door
check: The unit's rated design pressure (positive and negative) must equal or exceed the required wind design pressure for that opening from Table R301.2(2) adjusted by Table R301.2(3), or from ASCE 7. Show required and rated pressures on the window and door schedule.
needs: Project wind speed, exposure and mean roof height; wall zone (4 or 5) of each opening; product rated design pressure
note: Once the project wind fields exist this becomes an automatic comparison per opening.

title: Product approval and label
applies_to: Replaced or new exterior window, sliding door or side-hinged exterior door
check: Each unit must be tested and labeled (AAMA/WDMA/CSA 101/I.S.2/A440 or TAS 202; side-hinged doors also ANSI/WMA 100) and carry a Florida product approval or Miami-Dade NOA number. The temporary label stays on until final inspection. List the approval number for every exterior opening on the schedule.
edition_difference: 9th Edition rewrites water-test Exception 2: door assemblies with a Limited Water (LW) rating may be used where the overhang ratio is 1 or more.
needs: Florida product approval or NOA number per opening

title: Unit size within tested size
applies_to: Replaced or new exterior window or door
check: The installed unit may not be larger than the maximum size covered by the product approval unless justified by comparative analysis; frame or panel area may not exceed the tested unit.
needs: Maximum approved size from the product approval

title: Custom exterior doors
applies_to: One-of-a-kind exterior door assembly
check: A custom exterior door must be laboratory tested or engineered by a Florida registered design professional, with signed and sealed calculations submitted at permit application.

title: Garage door rating
applies_to: Replaced garage door
check: Garage doors must be tested (ANSI/DASMA 108, ASTM E330 or TAS 202) for the required design pressure and carry a permanent label with model, design pressures, impact rating if any and the product approval number. Installation drawing on site.
needs: Garage door design pressure rating and product approval number

title: Other exterior assemblies
applies_to: Exterior window or door assembly not covered by the standard labeling rules
check: Assemblies outside R609.3 and R609.4 must be tested per ASTM E330, with glass meeting R308.5.

title: Windborne debris protection
applies_to: New or replaced exterior glazed opening (window, glazed door, sliding glass door, skylight) in a windborne debris region
check: Glazed openings in windborne debris regions must be impact rated (ASTM E1886 and E1996 large missile, TAS 201/202/203, or AAMA 506) or protected by an approved impact-resistant covering. Flag any new or replaced exterior glazed opening whose impact flag is off and that has no shutter assigned.
needs: Project field: windborne debris region yes/no
note: Test: project is in a windborne debris region AND opening is exterior, glazed, new or replaced AND not impact rated AND no approved covering. Palm Beach, Broward and Miami-Dade are treated as windborne debris regions. The Existing Building code has its own trigger for how much replacement glazing forces protection; see that area's rules. Requirement text is R301.2.1.2.

title: Window anchorage
applies_to: Replaced or new exterior window or glass door
check: Anchor per the manufacturer's published instructions for the design pressure and substrate. A substitute anchor for a substrate not covered by the instructions must be shown equal or better by engineering.

title: Bucks at masonry openings
applies_to: Window or glass door installed in a masonry or concrete opening
check: Wood buck thinner than 1-1/2 in.: anchor through the jamb or with clips directly into the masonry. Buck 1-1/2 in. or thicker and securely fastened to the masonry: anchors may stop in the buck. Unless tested otherwise the buck must extend past the interior face of the frame so the frame is fully supported.

title: Anchorage in frame walls
applies_to: Window or glass door installed in a wood-framed opening
check: Anchor through the frame, by frame clip, or through the flange into the framing so the load transfers to the structure.

title: Mullions
applies_to: Two or more window or door units joined side by side or stacked in one opening
check: Mullions must be tested (AAMA 450) or engineered, transfer the unit loads to the rough opening, deflect no more than L/175 for spans up to 13 ft 6 in. (L/240 plus 1/4 in. above that), and resist 1.5 times design pressure. List the mullion product approval.
note: Trigger from the model: adjacent exterior units sharing a jamb in one rough opening.

title: Perimeter sealant joint
applies_to: Window in a masonry rough opening
check: Size the masonry rough opening so the perimeter sealant joint around the window is no wider than 1/4 in.
note: Test: (rough opening minus unit frame size) / 2 is 1/4 in. or less per side when both sizes are entered; otherwise show as a reminder.

title: Door component substitution
applies_to: Exterior door assembled with substituted components (slab, frame, hardware, glazing kit)
check: Substituted door components must comply with ANSI/WMA 100 or be evaluated as equal or better by an approved entity or engineer.

title: Shutters and impact coverings
applies_to: Impact-resistant coverings used to protect glazed openings
check: Coverings must be tested at 1.5 times design pressure, carry a permanent label with the approval number, and be installed per the manufacturer's instructions and product approval, with instructions on site.
note: Covers R609.11.1 through R609.11.4.

title: Interior finish flame spread
applies_to: New interior wall and ceiling finishes (paneling, wood ceilings, wall coverings)
check: Interior wall and ceiling finishes must meet the flame-spread and smoke-developed limits of R302.9.
note: R302.9 limits (flame spread 200, smoke developed 450) were not opened in this pass; take them from the Chapter 3 list.

title: Interior masonry veneer
applies_to: Interior stone or brick veneer (fireplace surround, accent wall)
check: Interior masonry veneer must be supported and anchored the same as exterior veneer, except no airspace is required. Check floor support for full-thickness veneer.

title: Interior plaster
applies_to: New or patched interior plaster or stucco
check: At least three coats over metal lath and two coats over other bases; veneer plaster one coat up to 3/16 in. Minimum thickness per Table R702.1(1), e.g. 5/8 in. gypsum plaster on metal lath, 1/2 in. on masonry. Lath supports at most 16 in. on center for 3/8 in. gypsum lath, 24 in. for 1/2 in.

title: Framing behind gypsum board
applies_to: New walls and ceilings finished with gypsum board on wood framing
check: Wood framing supporting gypsum board at least 2 in. nominal in its least dimension. 1x2 furring strips allowed over solid backing or over framing at 24 in. on center or less.

title: Gypsum thickness vs spacing
applies_to: New gypsum board on walls and ceilings
check: 3/8 in. board: framing at most 16 in. on center. 1/2 in. board: walls up to 24 in. on center; ceilings 16 in. either direction or 24 in. only with board perpendicular to framing. 5/8 in. board: up to 24 in. on center.
needs: Framing spacing for each wall and ceiling type (board thickness comes from the wall layers)

title: Gypsum fastener spacing
applies_to: New gypsum board
check: Without adhesive: nails at 7 in. on ceilings and 8 in. on walls; screws at 12 in. on ceilings, 16 in. on walls with studs at 16 in., 12 in. on walls with studs at 24 in. With adhesive the spacings increase per the table.

title: Ceilings with texture
applies_to: Gypsum ceiling that will get a water-based texture or carry insulation
check: For water-based texture use 1/2 in. board on framing at 16 in., and 5/8 in. board (or 1/2 in. sag-resistant ceiling board) at 24 in., applied perpendicular to framing. 3/8 in. board may not carry ceiling insulation or texture.
needs: Ceiling finish (textured or smooth) and ceiling framing spacing

title: Garage ceiling under rooms
applies_to: Garage ceiling with habitable room above that is new or replaced
check: 5/8 in. Type X gypsum board applied perpendicular to framing at 24 in. on center or less, fastened at 6 in. on center with 1-7/8 in. nails or equivalent screws.
needs: Habitable room above the garage yes/no
note: The separation requirement itself is R302.6 (existing rule B-21).

title: Gypsum board application
applies_to: New gypsum board
check: Apply board perpendicular or parallel to framing with all ends and edges landing on framing, except edges perpendicular to the framing. Do not use interior gypsum board where it is directly exposed to weather or water.

title: Gypsum board screws
applies_to: New gypsum board
check: Type W or S screws penetrating wood at least 5/8 in.; on steel studs at least No. 6 screws penetrating at least 3/8 in. (Type S or bugle head for steel under 0.033 in.).

title: Gypsum ceiling diaphragm
applies_to: Ceiling gypsum board removed and replaced where the ceiling acts as a horizontal diaphragm
check: A gypsum ceiling diaphragm needs 1/2 in. board perpendicular to joists, staggered end joints, fasteners at 7 in. on center at all supports, and 2x6 flat perimeter blocking. Capacity 90 plf at 16 in. framing, 70 plf at 24 in. Not allowed to brace masonry or concrete walls.
note: Only matters where the original design relied on the ceiling as a diaphragm; ask the engineer when whole ceilings are replaced.

title: Water-resistant gypsum backer
applies_to: Gypsum board used as a base for adhered tile or other required nonabsorbent finish outside the wet zone
check: Use board meeting ASTM C1396, C1178 or C1278. Allowed on ceilings. Not over a Class I or II vapor retarder in a tub or shower compartment. Seal cut and exposed edges per the manufacturer.

title: No green board in wet areas
applies_to: Wall and ceiling layers inside a tub or shower enclosure, steam shower or other continuously humid space
check: Water-resistant gypsum backing board (green board) and regular gypsum board may not be used where directly exposed to water or to continuous high humidity. Flag any tub or shower wall whose backer layer is paper-faced gypsum.
note: Test: wall segment bounds a tub or shower fixture AND its backer layer is regular or water-resistant paper-faced gypsum.

title: Tile installation standards
applies_to: Ceramic or porcelain tile on walls and floors
check: Install tile per the ANSI A108 series (A108.1, .4, .5, .6, .11) with setting materials meeting A118.1, A118.3 or A136.1 and tile meeting A137.1.

title: Tile backer in tubs and showers
applies_to: Walls with tile in tub and shower areas; wall panels in shower areas
check: Backer must be one of: glass-mat gypsum backing panel (ASTM C1178), fiber-reinforced gypsum panel (C1278), fiber-cement backer board (C1288 or ISO 8336 Category C), or fiber-mat reinforced cementitious backer unit (C1325), installed per the manufacturer.
edition_difference: 9th Edition drops the word nonasbestos from the two cement board names; same standards.
note: Test: backer layer type on every wall bounding a tub or shower is one of the four listed. Works with existing rule B-10 (R307.2 nonabsorbent surface height), which stays in the Chapter 3 list. Foam-core and sheet or liquid membrane systems are accepted through product approvals or evaluation reports, not this table.

title: Wood and hardboard paneling
applies_to: Interior wood veneer or hardboard paneling
check: Framing at 16 in. on center or less. Paneling thinner than 1/4 in. needs a gypsum board backer at least 3/8 in. thick.
needs: Paneling thickness and framing spacing

title: Vapor retarders in Florida walls
applies_to: Exterior frame walls opened, re-insulated or newly built
check: No interior vapor retarder is required in Climate Zones 1, 2 and 3 (all of Florida). In Zones 1 and 2 a Class I (polyethylene, foil) or Class II retarder is not permitted on the interior side of frame walls unless its permeance is above 1 perm by the ASTM E96 water method. Do not add poly sheeting behind drywall on exterior walls.
edition_difference: 9th Edition adds an installation subsection (R702.7.2) and a new Exception 5 for Zones 4 through 8; the Florida result is the same.
note: Florida climate zones: 1A for Broward, Collier, Hendry, Lee, Miami-Dade, Monroe, Palm Beach; 2A for all other counties (FBC-EC Table R301.1).

title: Flashing at replaced openings
applies_to: Replaced or new exterior window or door
check: Flash exterior window and door openings per the manufacturer, a design professional's detail, or FMA/AAMA 100, 200, FMA/WDMA 250, FMA/AAMA/WDMA 300 or 400. Where no instructions exist, install a sill pan and protect head and jambs. Seal the unit to the wall with sealant meeting AAMA 800 or ASTM C920 Class 25.

title: Ceiling and roof framing design
applies_to: Ceiling raised, vaulted or re-framed; ceiling joists, rafter ties or collar ties removed; new ceiling beams
check: Florida has no prescriptive rafter or ceiling joist tables in the Residential code. Any change to ceiling or roof framing, including converting a flat ceiling to vaulted or tray, must follow the WFCM or be engineered.
note: Trigger from the model: a room whose ceiling type changes from flat to vaulted, sloped or tray in an existing house.

title: Notching ceiling joists and rafters
applies_to: Holes and notches in sawn ceiling joists and rafters for wiring, ducts, recessed lights
check: Cuts, notches and holes in sawn joists, rafters and beams follow the same limits as floor joists (R502.2, by the WFCM). A taper cut at the end of a ceiling joist may not exceed 1/4 of the member depth.
note: See the joist notching rule for the numeric limits.

title: No cutting engineered wood
applies_to: Trusses, LVL or PSL beams, glulam, I-joists near new ducts, lights, skylights or attic hatches
check: No cuts, notches or bored holes in trusses, structural composite lumber, glulam, cross-laminated timber or I-joists unless the manufacturer allows it or a registered design professional has designed for it.

title: No altering roof trusses
applies_to: Roof trusses where an attic hatch, pull-down stair, skylight, vaulted ceiling or attic equipment is added
check: Do not cut, notch, drill, splice or alter truss members without approval of a registered design professional. New attic loads (air handler, water heater, storage platform) need verification that the trusses can carry them.
note: Derived test: flag an attic hatch, pull-down stair or skylight whose rough opening is wider than about 22-1/2 in. (clear space between trusses at 24 in. on center), and flag any equipment placed in the attic. Truss layout is not in the model, so treat the result as a warning.

title: Truss drawings for new trusses
applies_to: New roof trusses or truss repairs
check: Truss design drawings must be submitted and approved before installation and delivered with the trusses; prepared by a registered design professional where Florida Statutes require.

title: Ceiling finishes
applies_to: New or replaced ceilings
check: Install ceiling finishes under the same rules as interior wall finishes in R702 (board thickness, spacing, fasteners).

title: Attic cross ventilation
applies_to: Remodel that vaults a ceiling, closes soffit vents, or adds enclosed rafter spaces
check: Each enclosed attic and enclosed rafter space needs cross ventilation to outside air through openings protected from rain; openings 1/16 in. to 1/4 in. or screened to that size.
note: Only when the remodel changes the attic or creates a new enclosed rafter cavity.

title: Attic vent area
applies_to: Remodel that changes attic area or vents
check: Net free vent area at least 1/150 of the vented space. 1/300 is allowed when 40 to 50 percent of the area is in the upper part (within 3 ft of the ridge) and the rest is in the bottom third.
needs: Attic area and net free area of existing and new vents

title: Insulation clear of eave vents
applies_to: Attic insulation added or disturbed
check: Insulation, blocking and bridging may not block eave or soffit vents; keep at least 1 in. of air space between insulation and roof sheathing at the vent.

title: Unvented attic conditions
applies_to: Attic converted to unvented (spray foam at roof deck) or a vaulted ceiling insulated without vents
check: Allowed only if the unvented space is entirely inside the thermal envelope, no Class I vapor retarder is on the ceiling side, and air-impermeable insulation is in direct contact with the underside of the roof sheathing (or rigid insulation above the deck). Where air-permeable insulation is combined with it in Zones 1 and 2, the air-impermeable layer or above-deck board must be at least R-5.

title: Vapor diffusion port option
applies_to: Unvented attic in Zones 1 to 3 with air-permeable insulation on the attic floor
check: Provide an approved vapor diffusion port within 12 in. of the highest point of the roof, with a membrane of 20 perms or more that also acts as an air barrier. Port area at least 1/600 of the ceiling area.
edition_difference: 9th Edition requires port area of at least 1/150 of the ceiling area (8th Edition: 1/600).

title: Attic access required
applies_to: Dwelling with an attic at least 30 in. high over at least 30 sq ft, when ceilings or halls are remodeled or the existing access is removed
check: Provide an attic access opening to each such attic area. Flag a remodel that removes or covers the only access without drawing a new one.
edition_difference: 8th Edition applies to buildings with combustible ceiling or roof construction; 9th Edition applies to all buildings with attics.
needs: Attic present with 30 in. height over 30 sq ft yes/no

title: Attic access size
applies_to: Attic hatch or access panel
check: Rough-framed opening at least 22 in. by 30 in. In a wall, at least 22 in. wide by 30 in. high.
note: Test: hatch rough opening width is 22 in. or more and length is 30 in. or more. Where equipment is in the attic, M1305.1.3 also requires an opening large enough to remove the largest appliance (mechanical area).

title: Attic access location
applies_to: Attic hatch or access panel
check: Locate the access in a hallway or another location with ready access. Above a ceiling hatch there must be at least 30 in. of unobstructed attic headroom.
edition_difference: 8th Edition: 30 in. headroom at some point above the access. 9th Edition: 30 in. headroom along at least one side of the access.
note: Test: hatch is in a hall or other room not blocked by cabinets, shelving or fixtures below it. Attic headroom needs a roof slope or attic height entry.

title: Flashing at new roof penetrations
applies_to: New roof penetration from interior work: bath fan, range hood or dryer exhaust, plumbing vent, skylight or sun tunnel
check: Flash every new roof penetration so water cannot enter; roofing work must follow Chapter 9 and usually needs a roofing permit or licensed roofer.
note: Chapter 9 was not opened; section number given from memory. The rest of Chapter 9 is outside an interior remodel.

title: Firebox wall thickness
applies_to: Masonry firebox rebuilt or relined
check: Firebox walls at least 8 in. of solid masonry including a firebrick lining at least 2 in. thick, or 10 in. without a lining. Firebrick joints 1/4 in. or less, laid in refractory mortar.

title: Firebox dimensions
applies_to: Masonry firebox rebuilt or opening resized
check: Firebox depth at least 20 in.; throat at least 8 in. above the opening and at least 4 in. deep. Rumford fireplaces: depth at least 12 in. and at least 1/3 of the opening width.
needs: Firebox depth and opening size

title: Fireplace lintel and damper
applies_to: Masonry fireplace opening altered or refaced
check: Masonry over the opening sits on a noncombustible lintel with at least 4 in. of bearing each end. A ferrous metal damper at least 8 in. above the top of the opening, operable from the room.

title: Hearth construction
applies_to: Masonry fireplace hearth or hearth extension built or rebuilt
check: Hearth and hearth extension of concrete or masonry, supported on noncombustible material, reinforced to carry their load. No combustible material (forms, framing, subfloor) left under them.

title: Hearth thickness
applies_to: Masonry fireplace hearth
check: Hearth (floor of the firebox) at least 4 in. thick.
needs: Hearth thickness

title: Hearth extension thickness
applies_to: Masonry fireplace hearth extension
check: Hearth extension at least 2 in. thick. Where the bottom of the firebox opening is at least 8 in. above the top of the extension, 3/8 in. of brick, concrete, stone, tile or other noncombustible material is enough.
needs: Hearth extension thickness and height of firebox floor above it

title: Hearth extension size
applies_to: Masonry fireplace with new flooring, new surround or a rebuilt hearth
check: Extension at least 16 in. in front of and 8 in. beyond each side of the opening. Opening of 6 sq ft or more: at least 20 in. in front and 12 in. beyond each side. Combustible flooring may not run into this zone.
needs: Fireplace object with opening width and height, hearth extension depth and width
note: Test: opening area = width x height; compare extension depth and side overrun. Needs a fireplace object in the model; until then treat as DATA.

title: Framing clearance to fireplace
applies_to: Wood framing near a masonry fireplace (new walls, built-ins, TV niche framing)
check: Combustible framing at least 2 in. clear of the front faces and sides and 4 in. clear of the back of a masonry fireplace. Leave the air space open except for fireblocking.
edition_difference: 9th Edition also allows the air space to be filled with noncombustible material.

title: Fireplace in masonry wall
applies_to: Masonry fireplace built into a masonry or concrete wall
check: Combustible material may not touch the masonry or concrete wall within 12 in. of the inside surface of the nearest firebox lining.

title: Trim abutting fireplace
applies_to: Drywall, wood flooring, paneling or trim that butts against a masonry fireplace or its hearth extension
check: Combustible trim and the edges of sheathing, flooring and gypsum board may abut the fireplace sidewalls and hearth extension only where at least 12 in. from the inside surface of the nearest firebox lining.
edition_difference: 9th Edition: 8 in. minimum for openings under 6 sq ft; 12 in. where the opening is 6 sq ft or larger.
needs: Distance from firebox lining to the nearest combustible finish

title: Mantel and surround clearance
applies_to: Combustible mantel, shelf, wood surround or trim on a masonry fireplace face
check: No combustible material within 6 in. of the fireplace opening. Within 12 in. of the opening, combustible material may project no more than 1/8 in. for each 1 in. of distance from the opening (a 6 in. deep mantel must be 12 in. or more above the opening).
needs: Mantel or trim: distance from opening and projection
note: Test: distance is 6 in. or more AND (distance is 12 in. or more OR projection is at most distance / 8). Needs mantel geometry; until then treat as DATA.

title: Fireblocking at fireplaces
applies_to: Framing around a fireplace or chimney
check: Fireblock the spaces around fireplaces per R302.11, and fireblock between chimneys and floors or ceilings with noncombustible material fixed in place (R1003.19).

title: Fireplace doors and accessories
applies_to: Glass doors, grates, heat exchangers or other accessories added to a masonry fireplace
check: Accessories must be listed and labeled (UL 907) and installed per the listing and the manufacturer's instructions.

title: Masonry heater clearance
applies_to: Masonry heater
check: Keep combustibles 36 in. from the heater surface, or 4 in. where the heater walls are at least 8 in. of solid masonry and channel walls 5 in.; 8 in. from the capping slab to a combustible ceiling. Listed heaters per their listing.
note: Rare in Florida; kept for completeness.

title: Chimney termination height
applies_to: Chimney extended, rebuilt or with a roof change beside it
check: Chimney top at least 3 ft above where it passes through the roof and at least 2 ft higher than any part of the building within 10 ft.
note: Outside pure interior work; applies only if the chimney is touched.

title: Flue lining for new appliance
applies_to: Existing masonry chimney reused for a new fireplace insert, stove or gas appliance
check: The flue lining must suit the connected appliance per its listing: clay liner (ASTM C315), listed liner system (UL 1777) or listed factory-built chimney inside the masonry. Gas appliance liners follow Chapter 24. A flue relined for one appliance type needs a permanent label near the connection.

title: Chimney clearance to framing
applies_to: New framing, cabinets or finishes beside a masonry chimney
check: Keep a 2 in. air space between combustibles and a chimney inside the building or in an exterior wall (1 in. for a chimney wholly outside). Do not fill the space except for fireblocking. Trim and sheathing edges may abut the chimney only where 8 in. or more from the flue lining.
edition_difference: For chimneys built into masonry or concrete walls the no-contact distance is 12 in. from the flue lining in the 8th Edition and 8 in. in the 9th Edition.

title: Factory-built fireplace listing
applies_to: New or replaced factory-built (prefab) wood or gas fireplace
check: Unit must be listed and labeled (tested to UL 127) and installed exactly per its listing: framing clearances, mantel and surround clearances, facing materials and chase construction come from the manufacturer's instructions.
needs: Manufacturer and model; clearances from the installation manual
note: Gas fireplaces, logs and inserts also fall under Chapter 24 (fuel gas area).

title: Prefab fireplace hearth extension
applies_to: Factory-built fireplace
check: Hearth extension per the fireplace listing, and readily distinguishable from the surrounding floor. Listed hearth extensions comply with UL 1618.

title: Gas logs in prefab fireplaces
applies_to: Unvented gas log heater placed in a factory-built fireplace
check: Not allowed unless the fireplace system is specifically tested, listed and labeled for that use.
edition_difference: 9th Edition adds fireplace inserts to the same restriction.

title: Gasketed doors on prefab fireplaces
applies_to: Gasketed fireplace door added to a factory-built fireplace
check: Not allowed unless the fireplace system is specifically tested, listed and labeled for it.

title: Factory-built chimney installation
applies_to: Factory-built chimney new, rerouted or boxed in by new framing
check: Listed and labeled, installed and terminated per the manufacturer. Solid-fuel appliances need Type HT chimney (UL 103). Framing that supports the chimney must be designed for the load.

title: Chimney offsets
applies_to: Factory-built chimney offset to clear new framing or a new ceiling
check: No part of the chimney more than 30 degrees from vertical, and no more than four elbows in the assembly.

title: Chimney insulation shield
applies_to: Factory-built chimney passing through an insulated ceiling or attic
check: Provide a steel insulation shield (26 gage minimum) that keeps insulation at the listed clearance and extends at least 2 in. above the attic insulation, fixed in place.

title: Fireplace exterior air supply
applies_to: New factory-built or masonry fireplace
check: Provide an exterior combustion air supply unless the room is mechanically ventilated to neutral or positive pressure. For factory-built units the air duct must be a listed part of the fireplace.
note: FBC-EC R402.4.2 separately requires outdoor combustion air and tight dampers or doors for new wood-burning fireplaces.

title: Combustion air intake and duct
applies_to: Fireplace exterior air duct
check: Intake not in a garage or basement, not higher than the firebox (except listed units), with 1/4 in. corrosion-resistant mesh. Passageway 6 to 55 sq in. Unlisted ducts keep 1 in. clearance to combustibles within 5 ft of the outlet. Outlet in the firebox back or side, or within 24 in. of the opening at hearth level, and closable.
note: Combines R1006.2 through R1006.5.

title: Existing buildings exempt unless renovated
applies_to: Every remodel of an existing dwelling
check: An existing building is exempt from the Energy code unless it is a renovated building, changes occupancy type, or was unconditioned and has comfort conditioning added. Decide at project setup which case applies; replaced equipment and windows are still covered by R501.7.
needs: Renovation cost, assessed value of the structure, and whether conditioning is being added to unconditioned space

title: 30 percent renovation threshold
applies_to: Remodel that changes insulation, HVAC, water heating or the exterior envelope
check: The project is a renovated building when the alteration changes insulation, HVAC systems, water heating systems or exterior envelope conditions AND the estimated renovation cost exceeds 30 percent of the assessed value of the structure. Test: cost / assessed structure value greater than 0.30.
needs: Project fields: estimated renovation cost; assessed value of the structure (property appraiser, building only)
note: This is Florida's 30 percent rule. The definitions chapter has no visible section number for each term; R202 is the chapter section.

title: Energy data on permit drawings
applies_to: Permit set for a renovation or for replaced windows, HVAC, water heater
check: Show as applicable: compliance path, insulation types and R-values, window and door U-factors and SHGC with area-weighted calculation, mechanical and water heating equipment type, size and efficiency, controls, duct sealing and insulation, air sealing details, and the thermal envelope.

title: Energy compliance form
applies_to: Renovated building, addition, or space newly conditioned
check: Submit Form R402 (prescriptive, or a Florida REScheck printout) or Form R405 from Commission-approved software, with the owner's or agent's compliance certification before permit.
note: No license is required to prepare the form for single-family houses, duplexes and townhouses (R103.1.1.1.1).

title: Insulation certification
applies_to: New insulation installed in walls, ceilings or attic
check: Insulation 12 in. or wider must carry the manufacturer's R-value mark, or the installer posts a signed certification of type, manufacturer and R-value. Blown attic insulation needs thickness markers at least one per 300 sq ft facing the attic access.

title: NFRC labels on windows
applies_to: Replacement or new windows, glazed doors and skylights
check: U-factor per NFRC 100 and SHGC per NFRC 200, labeled and certified. A product without a label gets the code default values (for example metal-frame double pane U 0.80), which will fail in Climate Zone 2.
needs: NFRC U-factor and SHGC for each replaced unit

title: Insulation for altered envelope
applies_to: Exterior wall, ceiling or floor assemblies newly built or opened as part of the alteration (infilled openings, garage conversion, new exterior wall sections)
check: Zone 1 (Palm Beach, Broward, Miami-Dade, Monroe, Collier, Lee, Hendry): ceiling R-30, wood-frame wall R-13, mass wall R-3 (R-4 if insulation is mostly inside), floor R-13. Zone 2 (rest of Florida): ceiling R-38, wood-frame wall R-13, mass wall R-4 (R-6 inside), floor R-13. No slab edge insulation.
edition_difference: 9th Edition adds alternatives: wood-frame wall R-13 cavity or R-10 continuous; floor R-13 or R-7 plus R-5 continuous or R-10 continuous. Ceiling values unchanged.
needs: Project climate zone (from county) and R-value of each new or opened envelope assembly
note: R-30 over the full ceiling is accepted in place of R-38 where uncompressed insulation extends over the wall top plate (R402.2.1).

title: Ceilings without attic space
applies_to: Vaulted or flat-roof ceiling too shallow for the required insulation
check: Where more than R-30 is required and the roof-ceiling cavity cannot fit it, R-30 is accepted for up to 500 sq ft or 20 percent of the insulated ceiling area, whichever is less.
needs: Area of reduced-insulation ceiling

title: Eave baffles
applies_to: Air-permeable attic insulation added in a vented attic
check: Install a baffle next to each soffit or eave vent that keeps an opening at least the size of the vent and extends above the top of the insulation.

title: Attic hatch insulated and sealed
applies_to: Attic hatch, pull-down stair or knee-wall door between conditioned and unconditioned space
check: Weatherstrip the access and insulate it to the level of the surrounding surface. With loose-fill insulation, build a dam or retainer around the opening so insulation stays in place.
note: Trigger from the model: any attic hatch or access panel object.

title: Air barrier behind tubs and showers
applies_to: Tub or shower placed against an exterior wall
check: Install the air barrier on the exterior wall behind the tub or shower and insulate that wall before the unit or backer goes in.
note: Test: a tub or shower fixture touches a wall flagged exterior. R503.1.1 does not list R402.4.1 for alterations by number; R503.1 applies new-construction rules to the altered portion, so reviewers commonly ask for it.

title: Air sealing at altered envelope
applies_to: Altered exterior walls and ceilings: dropped ceilings and soffits, electrical boxes, register boots, garage wall
check: Align the air barrier with the insulation at dropped ceilings and soffits; seal electrical and low-voltage boxes that penetrate the air barrier; seal HVAC register boots to the ceiling, wall or subfloor; seal the gap between window or door jambs and framing; air-seal the wall between garage and conditioned space.

title: Blower door test not required
applies_to: Alteration or addition where new construction is under 85 percent of the thermal envelope
check: Envelope air-leakage testing (7 ACH50 limit in Zones 1 and 2) is not required for additions, alterations, renovations or repairs where the new construction is less than 85 percent of the building thermal envelope.

title: Wood-burning fireplace air sealing
applies_to: New wood-burning fireplace
check: Provide a tight-fitting flue damper or doors and outdoor combustion air. Doors must be listed for the fireplace (UL 127 units) or labeled to UL 907 (masonry).

title: Window and door air leakage
applies_to: Replacement or new windows, skylights, sliding and swinging exterior doors
check: Labeled air infiltration no more than 0.3 cfm per sq ft for windows, skylights and sliding glass doors, and 0.5 cfm per sq ft for swinging doors. Site-built units are exempt.
needs: Labeled air infiltration rate (normally on the NFRC or AAMA label)

title: Recessed lights in insulated ceilings
applies_to: Recessed luminaires in a ceiling or wall that is part of the thermal envelope (ceiling below attic or roof)
check: Every such recessed luminaire must be IC-rated, labeled for air leakage of 2.0 cfm or less (ASTM E283 at 75 Pa), and sealed to the ceiling finish with a gasket or caulk.
needs: Luminaire flags: IC-rated, airtight (2.0 cfm label)
note: Test: light type is recessed AND host ceiling has attic or roof above AND (IC flag is off OR airtight flag is off).

title: Air-sealed electrical boxes
applies_to: Electrical and low-voltage boxes in exterior walls and insulated ceilings
check: Where air-sealed boxes are used they must be marked per NEMA OS 4, sealed to the air barrier and surrounded by insulation; otherwise seal ordinary boxes to the air barrier.

title: Thermostat per system
applies_to: New or replaced heating and cooling system
check: At least one thermostat for each separate heating and cooling system.
note: Test: count of thermostats is at least the count of HVAC systems once systems are entered; otherwise a reminder.

title: Programmable thermostat
applies_to: Thermostat for the primary heating or cooling system when the system is new or replaced
check: Thermostat must run a daily schedule with different set points, allow setback to 55 F heating and 85 F cooling, and ship programmed at no higher than 70 F heating and no lower than 78 F cooling.
edition_difference: 9th Edition retitles it programmable or smart thermostat; requirements otherwise the same.

title: Heat pump auxiliary heat control
applies_to: New or replaced heat pump with electric strip heat
check: Controls must lock out supplementary electric heat except when the compressor cannot meet the load, during defrost, or on malfunction.

title: Duct insulation
applies_to: New or replaced supply and return ducts outside the thermal envelope
check: In attics: R-8 for ducts 3 in. diameter and larger, R-6 for smaller. Elsewhere outside the envelope: R-6 and R-4.2. Ducts entirely inside the thermal envelope are exempt.
needs: Duct location and insulation R-value
note: For replacement ducts where space does not allow, the same or higher R-value as the old ducts is accepted and R-6 is deemed sufficient (R501.7 Exception 5).

title: Duct and air handler sealing
applies_to: New or replaced ducts, plenums, filter boxes and air handlers
check: Seal all duct joints, air handlers and filter boxes per the commercial duct construction section (C403.2.9.2). New air handlers need the manufacturer's designation of 2 percent or less cabinet leakage (ASHRAE 193).

title: Duct leakage test
applies_to: New duct system installed as part of the alteration
check: Test total duct leakage at 25 Pa: 4 cfm or less per 100 sq ft of conditioned floor area (3 cfm at rough-in without the air handler), with a signed report to the building official. Not required when ducts and air handler are entirely inside the thermal envelope.
edition_difference: 8th Edition also exempts buildings complying by the R405 performance method unless leakage credit is claimed; the 9th Edition deletes that exception.
needs: Whether new ducts are outside the thermal envelope; test result
note: Limits are in R403.3.4. Existing systems need not be tested (R501.7.1).

title: Short duct extensions not tested
applies_to: Existing duct system extended to serve remodeled rooms
check: Extending existing ducts with less than 40 linear ft of new duct in unconditioned space does not trigger the duct leakage test. Flag when the new duct length in unconditioned space reaches 40 ft.
needs: Linear feet of new duct in unconditioned space

title: No framing cavities as ducts
applies_to: New returns or supplies: panned joists, stud-bay returns, soffit plenums
check: Building framing cavities may not be used as ducts or plenums. Every new return and supply needs a real duct or lined plenum.
note: Trigger from the model: new return grille drawn on a wall or soffit without an attached duct.

title: Air handler in attic
applies_to: New or relocated air handler placed in the attic
check: Not allowed under the prescriptive (R402) path. Under the performance (R405) path only if the service panel is within 6 ft of an attic access, a condensate overflow alarm or shutoff is installed, the access is large enough to replace the unit, and the required homeowner notice is posted on the electrical panel.
needs: Air handler location and distance to attic access; compliance path

title: Refrigerant and hydronic pipe insulation
applies_to: New or replaced refrigerant suction lines and other mechanical piping above 105 F or below 55 F
check: Insulate to at least R-3. Outdoors, protect the insulation from sunlight, moisture and damage; adhesive tape is not acceptable protection.

title: Hot water recirculation controls
applies_to: New hot water recirculation or heat-trace system
check: Recirculation needs a pump with demand-based controls that shut off at set temperature and when there is no demand; gravity and thermosyphon loops are prohibited. Demand systems limit water entering the cold line to 104 F. Heat trace per IEEE 515.1 or UL 515 with automatic control.

title: Hot water pipe insulation
applies_to: New or replaced hot water piping
check: Insulate to R-3: pipe 3/4 in. and larger, pipe outside conditioned space, pipe from the water heater to a manifold, pipe under a slab or buried, and recirculation supply and return piping.
note: Under-slab hot water lines to a relocated island sink or bath are the usual remodel case.

title: Heat traps
applies_to: New or replaced storage water heater with vertical pipe risers
check: If the heater has no integral heat traps, install heat traps on both inlet and outlet (a listed trap or a 3-1/2 in. down-and-up loop) as close to the tank as possible.

title: Water heater controls and shutoff
applies_to: New or replaced water heater
check: Automatic temperature control adjustable across at least 100 F to 140 F. Electric units need a separate switch or a clearly marked breaker; fuel-fired units need a separate fuel shutoff valve.

title: Water heater efficiency
applies_to: New or replaced water heater
check: Equipment must meet the minimum efficiency in Table C404.2 of the commercial provisions for its type (federal minimums). Record type, size and rated efficiency on the plans.
needs: Water heater type, capacity and rated efficiency (UEF)

title: Dampers on intakes and exhausts
applies_to: New bath fan, range hood, dryer or other exhaust to outdoors; new outdoor air intake
check: Outdoor air intakes and exhausts need automatic or gravity dampers that close when the system is off. Ventilation itself must meet the Residential or Mechanical code.

title: Ventilation fan efficacy
applies_to: Fan that serves as the whole-house mechanical ventilation system
check: Minimum efficacy: bathroom or utility fan 10 to under 90 cfm 2.8 cfm/W; 90 cfm and over 3.5 cfm/W; range hood 2.8; in-line fan 3.8; HRV or ERV 1.2. An air handler used for ventilation needs an ECM motor.
needs: Fan cfm (already in the model) and watts; flag that the fan is the whole-house ventilation fan
note: Does not apply to ordinary intermittent bath fans or hoods.

title: Ventilation air source
applies_to: Mechanical ventilation or makeup air intake
check: Do not draw ventilation or makeup air from an attic, crawl space, attached garage or pool or spa enclosure. Ventilation rates may not exceed the ASHRAE 62.2 design minimums.

title: Ventilation flow testing
applies_to: New mechanical ventilation system under a 9th Edition permit
check: Test and document that the ventilation system delivers its required flow (ANSI/RESNET/ICC 380). Kitchen range hoods ducted outside with 6 in. or larger duct, 10 ft or less long and no more than two elbows are exempt.
edition_difference: New in the 9th Edition; no equivalent in the 8th Edition.
note: Read on the 9th Edition page: https://codes.iccsafe.org/content/FLEC2026V1.0/chapter-4-re-residential-energy-efficiency

title: HVAC sizing calculation
applies_to: New heating and cooling system; complete system added for remodeled or newly conditioned space
check: Size equipment by ACCA Manual S from a Manual J load calculation (or approved equal) with no safety factors. Submit manufacturer and model of indoor and outdoor units with sensible and total capacities at design conditions. New and replacement equipment must meet the federal minimum efficiency for the region.
needs: Manual J load, equipment model numbers and capacities
note: R503.1.2 lists R403.1, R403.2, R403.3 and R403.6 for alterations and does not list R403.7, and R501.7.1 exempts existing equipment from sizing. Many Florida building departments still ask for a sizing calculation on change-outs; confirm locally.

title: Cooling capacity limit
applies_to: New cooling-only equipment
check: Total capacity not less than the calculated total load and not more than 1.15 times it, or the next available size. Latent capacity at least the latent load. Use expanded performance data, not the nominal AHRI rating.
needs: Calculated total and latent cooling load; selected equipment capacity

title: Heating capacity limits
applies_to: New heat pump or electric furnace
check: Size a heat pump on the cooling load (cooling capacity not over 1.15 times the design cooling load). Size an electric resistance furnace within 4 kW of the design heating load.
needs: Design heating and cooling loads; equipment capacity

title: Dehumidifier requirements
applies_to: Whole-house or ducted dehumidifier added
check: Efficiency above 1.7 L/kWh (under 75 pints/day total) or 2.38 L/kWh (75 pints/day or more); humidity sensor in mixed house air; R-2 on a unit in unconditioned space; condensate per M1411.3.1. Ducted units: backdraft damper, never ducted to the return side upstream of the cooling coil, R-6 on ducts in unconditioned space.

title: Lighting efficacy
applies_to: Every new permanently installed luminaire (not those inside kitchen appliances)
check: Each permanently installed luminaire must have an efficacy of at least 45 lumens per watt, or use lamps of at least 65 lumens per watt. Integrated LED fixtures and LED lamps normally pass; incandescent and halogen do not.
needs: Luminaire efficacy (lm/W) or lamp type per light
note: Replaces B-25. Section and numbers confirmed identical in the 8th and 9th Editions. This is a Florida-specific wording (the model code uses a percentage of high-efficacy lamps).

title: No pilot lights on gas lighting
applies_to: Fuel gas lighting fixture
check: Gas lighting may not have a continuously burning pilot light.

title: Unaltered parts not upgraded
applies_to: Every alteration
check: Only the altered portion must comply. The unaltered parts of the building and its systems are not required to be brought up to the Energy code.

title: Materials for alterations
applies_to: New materials used in an alteration or repair
check: Use materials allowed for new construction; like-for-like materials are allowed for repairs if no hazard is created.

title: Historic building relief
applies_to: Dwelling that is listed, designated or contributing historic
check: Energy provisions are not mandatory where a report signed by the owner, a design professional or the preservation authority shows compliance would harm the historic form, fabric or function.
needs: Historic designation yes/no

title: Replaced systems must meet efficiency
applies_to: Permitted replacement of HVAC equipment, water heater, pool heater, lighting system or windows and glazed doors
check: New and replacement products in an existing building that need a permit must meet the code's minimum efficiency: HVAC, service water and pool heating, lighting, and replacement fenestration. This applies even when the project is under the 30 percent renovation threshold.

title: Matched HVAC components
applies_to: Condenser or air handler replaced alone
check: Replacing a part (for example a compressor) is a repair and does not force a full system replacement. Replacing a whole functional unit such as a condenser is not a repair: indoor and outdoor units must be a matched system, verified by AHRI data, an accredited lab, a manufacturer's letter or a Florida P.E. letter.
needs: AHRI certificate number for the indoor and outdoor unit combination

title: Existing ducts and wiring reused
applies_to: Replacement HVAC or lighting using existing ducts, wiring or controls
check: Existing components reused with a replacement system (ducts, wiring, controls) need not meet current code where that would require replacing them.

title: Replacement duct R-value
applies_to: Ducts replaced in a space too tight for the prescriptive insulation
check: Replacement ducts must be at least the R-value of the ducts removed; R-6 is deemed sufficient.
needs: R-value of replaced and new ducts

title: Existing equipment exempt
applies_to: Existing heating and cooling equipment that stays
check: Equipment that remains need not meet current minimum efficiency, sizing or duct sealing rules.

title: No electric resistance primary heat
applies_to: Complete central system replacement in Climate Zone 2
check: In Climate Zone 2 a complete central equipment replacement may not use electric resistance (strip heat furnace) as the primary heating system; use a heat pump or fuel-fired heat. Zone 1 counties are not covered by this limit.
needs: Project county (climate zone) and primary heating type of the replacement system
note: Test: climate zone is 2 AND full system replacement AND primary heat is electric resistance. New systems have the same prescriptive limit in R403.7.2. Zone 1: Broward, Collier, Hendry, Lee, Miami-Dade, Monroe, Palm Beach.

title: Alterations: general rule
applies_to: Every alteration covered by the Energy code
check: Altered portions comply as new construction. The alteration may not make the building less conforming, create a hazard, overload existing systems, or make the building use more energy than before.

title: Altered envelope assemblies
applies_to: Exterior walls, ceilings, floors, windows, doors and skylights that are part of the alteration
check: Altered envelope assemblies must meet Table R402.1.2 (or the U-factor alternative), the specific insulation rules R402.2.1 through R402.2.13, fenestration averaging R402.3.1 and R402.3.2, fenestration air leakage R402.4.3 and recessed lighting R402.4.5.

title: Insulate exposed cavities
applies_to: Existing exterior wall, ceiling or floor cavity opened during the remodel
check: An existing cavity exposed during construction need not reach the new-construction R-value if the cavity is filled with insulation. Flag every exterior wall or top-floor ceiling whose finish is removed and note fill cavity with insulation.
note: Test: wall is exterior (or ceiling is under attic or roof) AND its interior finish layer is demo or new. Frame cavities only; furred block walls have a shallow cavity that still must be filled.

title: Unopened cavities exempt
applies_to: Existing roof, wall or floor cavities not exposed by the work
check: No insulation upgrade is required where the existing cavity is not exposed. Storm windows over existing windows and window film on existing single-pane glass are also exempt.

title: Replacement window U-factor
applies_to: Existing window, glazed door or sliding door replaced with a new unit (frame, sash and glazing)
check: Maximum U-factor by climate zone: Zone 1 no requirement; Zone 2 0.40, or 0.65 for impact-rated units. An area-weighted average across all replacement units may be used.
needs: NFRC U-factor per replaced unit; project climate zone
note: Test: Zone 2 and area-weighted U of replaced units exceeds 0.40 (0.65 if impact rated). Values from Table R402.1.2 and its impact-glazing footnote; same in the 9th Edition.

title: Replacement window SHGC
applies_to: Existing window, glazed door or sliding door replaced with a new unit
check: Maximum solar heat gain coefficient 0.25 in Climate Zones 1 and 2 (all of Florida). Area-weighted average across the replacement units (those more than 50 percent glazed) may be used.
needs: NFRC SHGC per replaced unit
note: Test: area-weighted SHGC of replaced units exceeds 0.25. R503.1.1 does not carry over the 15 sq ft glazing exemption of R402.3.3 for alterations; ask the building department before relying on it.

title: Replacement skylight ratings
applies_to: Skylight or tubular daylight device replaced or added
