check: Skylight U-factor at most 0.75 in Zone 1 and 0.65 in Zone 2. Skylights are excused from the 0.25 SHGC limit if their SHGC is 0.30 or less.
edition_difference: 9th Edition: skylight U-factor at most 0.60 in Zones 1 and 2, and a separate skylight SHGC limit of 0.28.
needs: Skylight U-factor and SHGC

title: New HVAC in an alteration
applies_to: New heating, cooling or duct system installed as part of the alteration
check: The new system must meet the controls rules (R403.1), duct insulation, sealing and testing (R403.3) and ventilation rules (R403.6).

title: New water heating in an alteration
applies_to: New service hot water system installed as part of the alteration
check: The new system must comply with the section the code cites (R403.4, piping insulation); also apply the service hot water rules of R403.5 (pipe insulation, heat traps, controls, efficiency).
note: The cross-reference R403.4 comes from model-code numbering; in the Florida code service hot water is R403.5. R501.7 separately requires replaced water heaters to meet minimum efficiency.

title: Lighting alteration threshold
applies_to: Rooms where luminaires are added or replaced
check: New lighting in the alteration must meet R404.1. Exempt: replacing fewer than 10 percent of the luminaires in a space without increasing installed lighting power. Test per room: replaced or new luminaires / total luminaires.
note: Test: per room, count of new or replaced lights divided by total lights is 10 percent or more, then every new light needs the R404.1 efficacy.

title: Space newly conditioned
applies_to: Garage, porch, lanai, attic or other unconditioned space converted to conditioned living space
check: A nonconditioned or low-energy space altered to become conditioned must be brought into full compliance with the Energy code (envelope insulation, windows, air sealing, ducts, lighting). With the R405 performance method the proposed loads may be up to 110 percent of the reference design.
note: Test: room existing type is garage, porch, lanai, storage or attic AND proposed type is a conditioned room, or a register is added to a previously unconditioned room. Also triggers the R101.4.2 loss of exemption.

title: Repairs exempt
applies_to: Glass-only replacement in an existing sash and frame; lamp or ballast replacement; roof repairs
check: These are repairs, not alterations: glass-only replacement in an existing sash and frame, and replacing only lamps or ballasts in existing fixtures without increasing lighting power. Window energy ratings do not apply to glass-only replacement.

title: Change of occupancy
applies_to: Space changing occupancy so that energy demand increases
check: A space whose change of occupancy increases demand for fossil fuel or electricity must comply with the Energy code.

title: Conversion to dwelling unit
applies_to: Non-dwelling space converted to a dwelling unit or part of one (accessory apartment in a garage or outbuilding)
check: Any space converted to a dwelling unit or part of one must comply with the Energy code; R405 performance path allows 110 percent of reference loads.
note: Test: same trigger as the newly conditioned space rule, plus a kitchen added in a converted space.

title: Mechanical equipment in flood zone
applies_to: New or replaced mechanical appliances, equipment, ducts (also M1401.5, M1601.4.10, M1701.2, M2001.4, M1905.2.2) when the project is in a flood hazard area
check: Locate or install mechanical appliances, equipment, duct systems, combustion air openings, boilers and water heaters as required by R322.1.6 (at or above the required flood elevation, or designed to resist flood water).
needs: Project flood zone and required flood elevation; equipment mounting elevation
note: One rule covers the flood cross-references repeated in M1401.5, M1601.4.10, M1701.2, M2001.4 and M1905.2.2.

title: Appliances listed and labeled
applies_to: Any new or replaced mechanical appliance
check: Use only appliances listed and labeled for the application in which they are installed.

title: Fuel type and conversion
applies_to: Fuel-fired appliance connected to a fuel supply (natural gas vs LP)
check: Appliance must be made for the fuel it is connected to; convert to another fuel only where approved and done per the manufacturer instructions.

title: Appliance access and working space
applies_to: Air handler, furnace, water heater or other mechanical appliance
check: Appliance must be reachable for inspection, service, repair and replacement without removing permanent construction, other appliances, or piping/ducts not connected to it. Provide a level working space at least 30 in. deep by 30 in. wide in front of the control side.
note: Check clear floor rectangle 30 x 30 in. in front of the service side; cabinets, walls or other fixtures inside that rectangle are a conflict.

title: Furnace/air handler closet clearances
applies_to: Furnace or air handler in a compartment, closet or alcove
check: Working clearance at least 3 in. along sides, back and top, and the enclosure at least 12 in. wider in total than the unit. Furnace with a firebox open to the atmosphere needs at least 6 in. along the front combustion chamber side.
note: Exception: replacement appliance in an existing compartment may use the clearances in the manufacturer installation instructions.

title: Appliance room access
applies_to: Appliance in a compartment, alcove, closet or similar space
check: Access by an opening or door and an unobstructed passageway at least 24 in. wide and large enough to remove the largest appliance. Level service space at least 30 in. deep and as high as the appliance (not less than 30 in.) at the front or service side with the door open.
note: Door width to an air handler or water heater closet: at least 24 in. clear and not narrower than the appliance.

title: Attic appliance access opening
applies_to: Attic containing an appliance (air handler, water heater) and the attic hatch
check: Clear access opening at least 20 in. by 30 in. and large enough to remove the largest appliance.
note: Compare attic hatch clear size with 20 x 30 in. and with the appliance dimensions when the attic contains an appliance.

title: Attic passageway and service platform
applies_to: Attic containing an appliance
check: Clear passageway from the opening to the appliance at least 30 in. high and 22 in. wide, not more than 20 ft long, with continuous solid flooring at least 24 in. wide. Level service space at least 30 in. by 30 in. on every side of the appliance where access is required.
needs: Appliance location in attic and passage length from hatch
note: Exceptions: passageway and service space not needed where the appliance can be serviced and removed through the opening; passageway may be up to 50 ft long where it is at least 6 ft high and 22 in. wide for its whole length.

title: Attic appliance light and receptacle
applies_to: Attic containing an appliance
check: Provide a luminaire controlled by a switch at the passageway opening and a receptacle outlet at or near the appliance. Protect exposed lamps by location or guards.
needs: Appliance is in the attic (then check for switch at hatch, light and receptacle)

title: Under-floor appliance access
applies_to: Appliance in a crawl space or under-floor space
check: Rough-framed access opening at least 22 in. by 30 in.; passageway at least 30 in. high and 22 in. wide, not more than 20 ft long; level service space 30 in. by 30 in. at the service side. Switch-controlled light at the opening and receptacle near the appliance (M1305.1.4.3).
note: Exceptions for appliances serviceable through the opening and for 6 ft high passageways. Rare in slab-on-grade houses.

title: Equipment support above ground
applies_to: Equipment supported from the ground (condensing unit, outdoor appliance) or suspended under a floor
check: Set on a level concrete slab or other approved base at least 3 in. above adjoining ground; suspended appliances at least 6 in. above ground.
note: Also referenced for outdoor equipment by M1401.4.

title: Clearance to combustibles
applies_to: Any heat-producing appliance
check: Keep the clearances from unprotected combustible material shown on the appliance label and in the manufacturer installation instructions.

title: Reduced clearance protection
applies_to: Appliance installed closer to combustibles than its listed clearance
check: Reduce clearances only with a listed UL 1618 assembly or the protection methods of Table M1306.2 and the manufacturer instructions; ventilated protection needs a 1 in. air space with edges open at least 1 in. Solid-fuel appliances: never below 12 in. by table (M1306.2.3).

title: Install per listing
applies_to: Any appliance
check: Install per the listing, label and manufacturer instructions; leave the operating and installation instructions attached to the appliance.

title: Appliance anchorage
applies_to: Appliances designed to be fixed in position (water heater, air handler, condensing unit)
check: Fasten or anchor in an approved manner.

title: Ignition source height in garage
applies_to: Appliance with an ignition source (water heater, dryer, furnace) in a garage or in a non-living room that opens to the garage
check: Ignition source at least 18 in. above the garage floor.
needs: Height of ignition source above floor, or appliance is listed flammable-vapor-ignition resistant (FVIR)
note: Exception: FVIR-listed appliances. Rooms that are not living space and open to the garage count as garage.

title: Vehicle impact protection
applies_to: Appliance in a garage or carport where a vehicle can reach it
check: Do not install where subject to vehicle damage unless protected by approved barriers (bollard, curb, wheel stop, raised platform).
needs: Impact barrier provided, or appliance is outside the vehicle path

title: No gypsum board support
applies_to: Appliance platform or base
check: Do not use gypsum board as the support base under an appliance.

title: Drilling and notching for mechanical
applies_to: Mechanical piping, refrigerant lines or ducts passing through framing
check: Drill and notch wood framing only within R502.2, R602.3 and R802.7 limits; do not cut flanges or lips of load-bearing cold-formed steel members.

title: Shield plates for mechanical piping
applies_to: Piping (other than cast iron or galvanized steel) concealed in framed walls, floors or ceilings
check: Where piping passes through or lies in framing less than 1-1/2 in. from the face that receives the finish, protect with steel shield plates at least 0.0575 in. (16 gage) covering the pipe and extending 2 in. each side of the member and 2 in. above bottom plates and below top plates.
edition_difference: 9th Edition: trigger distance for piping through bored holes or notches and within a framing member is 1-1/4 in. (M1308.2.1, M1308.2.2); piping outside a member stays 1-1/2 in.
note: Applies to refrigerant and condensate lines.

title: Air handler in attic
applies_to: Air handler located in an attic
check: Install heating/cooling equipment per manufacturer instructions; attic air-handling units must also meet Florida Energy Conservation R403.3.6.
note: Energy code conditions for attic air handlers are in the energy rule list.

title: HVAC service access
applies_to: Heating and cooling equipment
check: Place equipment so filters, blowers, motors, controls and coils can be cleaned, serviced and replaced.

title: Equipment sizing
applies_to: New or replaced heating/cooling equipment; added conditioned area (garage conversion, enclosed porch)
check: Size equipment per ACCA Manual S from loads calculated per ACCA Manual J (or other approved methods).
note: Exceptions for multistage/variable equipment and next-larger standard size.

title: Outdoor equipment
applies_to: Equipment installed outdoors
check: Must be listed and labeled for outdoor installation, on supports that prevent vibration, settlement and movement, per M1305.1.4.1.

title: Furnace combustion air openings
applies_to: Central furnace (oil or other non-gas fuel)
check: Supply combustion air per Chapter 17; keep combustion air openings unobstructed for at least 6 in. in front of them.

title: Electric baseboard heaters
applies_to: Electric baseboard convector
check: Install per manufacturer instructions and the electrical chapters; must be listed to UL 1042.

title: Electric radiant floor/ceiling heat
applies_to: Electric radiant heating (e.g. heated bathroom floor)
check: System must be listed for the application and installed per manufacturer instructions; panels on wood framing installed as complete units unless listed for field cutting, fastened only through unheated portions and not closer than 1/4 in. to an element; do not bridge expansion joints; finish fasteners must not pierce elements (M1406.3 to M1406.5).

title: Electric duct heaters
applies_to: Electric duct heater or heat strip in ductwork
check: Listed to UL 1996 and installed per instructions; heater within 4 ft of a heat pump or air conditioner must be listed for that use (both units); keep service access; fan interlock must stop the heater when the fan is off (M1407.1 to M1407.5).

title: Vented wall furnace location
applies_to: Oil-fired vented wall furnace
check: No door may swing within 12 in. of the furnace air inlet or outlet (door stops or closers do not count); must not circulate air from a bathroom to other rooms; no ducts attached; manual shutoff ahead of controls (M1409.3).
note: Gas wall furnaces: see G2436.

title: Room heater floor protection
applies_to: Vented room heater (pellet, oil or solid fuel stove)
check: Set on a noncombustible floor or approved noncombustible assembly extending at least 18 in. beyond the appliance on all sides, unless listed otherwise (UL 1618 floor protector per manufacturer).

title: Condensate disposal
applies_to: Air handler / cooling coil
check: Pipe condensate from the drain pan to an approved place of disposal with at least 1/8 in. per foot slope; not onto a street, alley or where it causes a nuisance.
edition_difference: 9th Edition renumbers to M1411.9 (text unchanged).

title: Secondary condensate protection
applies_to: Cooling coil located where overflow would damage the building (attic, closet above finished space, upper floor)
check: Provide one of: (1) auxiliary pan with separate drain to a conspicuous point, pan at least 1.5 in. deep and 3 in. larger than the unit each way, 24 gage galvanized or 0.0625 in. nonmetallic; (2) separate overflow drain line to a conspicuous point; (3) auxiliary pan with a UL 508 water-level shutoff; (4) UL 508 water-level shutoff device in the primary line, overflow line or unit pan. Drain piping at least 3/4 in. with 1/8 in. per foot slope.
edition_difference: 9th Edition renumbers to M1411.9.1.

title: Down-flow unit overflow switch
applies_to: Down-flow air handler or coil with no secondary drain provision
check: Install a water-level monitoring device inside the primary drain pan that shuts the equipment off; not in the drain line.
edition_difference: 9th Edition renumbers to M1411.9.1.1.

title: Condensate drain size and material
applies_to: Condensate drain piping
check: Minimum 3/4 in. nominal from pan to disposal; ABS, cast iron, copper, PEX, CPVC, galvanized steel, PE-RT, PE, PP or PVC.
edition_difference: 9th Edition (M1411.9.2) adds: condensate drains from cooling coils must be insulated to at least R-3 where inside the unconditioned space of the building.

title: Condensate drain cleanout
applies_to: Condensate drain piping
check: Arrange the drain so blockages can be cleared without cutting the line.
edition_difference: 9th Edition renumbers to M1411.9.3.

title: Equipment above auxiliary pan rim
applies_to: Appliance or insulation sitting in an auxiliary drain pan
check: Keep water-sensitive parts and insulation above the flood rim of the pan; supports in the pan must be water resistant.
edition_difference: 9th Edition renumbers to M1411.9.4.
note: Same requirement repeated at M1411.3.1.2.

title: Condensate pump interlock
applies_to: Condensate pump in an attic, crawl space or other uninhabitable space
check: Wire the pump so the equipment cannot run when the pump fails.
edition_difference: 9th Edition renumbers to M1411.10.

title: Suction line insulation
applies_to: Refrigerant vapor (suction) piping
check: Insulate with at least R-3 insulation having surface permeance not over 0.05 perm.
edition_difference: 9th Edition renumbers to M1411.12.

title: Refrigerant piping near roof deck
applies_to: Refrigerant piping within 1-1/2 in. of the underside of the roof deck
check: Protect from nails and other fasteners.
edition_difference: 9th Edition renumbers to M1411.13.

title: Locking refrigerant caps
applies_to: Outdoor refrigerant access ports (new or replaced condensing unit)
check: Fit locking tamper-resistant caps unless the ports are inside the unit cabinet.
edition_difference: 9th Edition renumbers to M1411.14.

title: Refrigerant piping support
applies_to: Refrigerant piping at the condensing unit
check: Fasten to a permanent support within 6 ft of the condensing unit.
edition_difference: 9th Edition renumbers to M1411.15.

title: A2L refrigerant systems
applies_to: New or replaced air conditioner or heat pump (9th Edition permits)
check: 9th Edition only: A2L systems listed to UL 60335-2-40; install per instructions and leave manuals with the unit or owner; duct-mounted accessories on A2L systems may not have electric heating elements, open flame or switch loads over 2.5 kVA; permanent label with installer contact, charge and refrigerant number; charge not over 34.5 lb per system; test A2L piping per the listing.
edition_difference: New in 9th Edition; 8th Edition M1411.1 only requires refrigerants to conform to ASHRAE 34.
note: Section numbers are 9th Edition.

title: Fireplace stoves
applies_to: Wood-burning fireplace stove
check: Listed (UL 737) and installed per the listing; hearth extension per the listing, at the same level as the stove support and distinguishable from the floor (M1414.2).

title: Exhaust discharges outdoors
applies_to: Every exhaust fan, range hood and dryer exhaust
check: Discharge all mechanical exhaust to the outdoors per M1506.3; never into an attic, soffit, ridge vent or crawl space.
needs: Termination point of each exhaust duct (roof cap, wall cap)
note: Exception: whole-house attic fans discharging into a private attic.

title: Dryer exhaust independent
applies_to: Clothes dryer
check: Dryer exhaust must be a system of its own, carry moisture to the outdoors, and follow the dryer manufacturer instructions (M1502.1).
needs: Dryer type: vented or listed condensing (ductless)
note: Exception: listed and labeled condensing (ductless) dryers.

title: Dryer exhaust termination
applies_to: Dryer exhaust outlet on the exterior
check: Terminate outside the building per the dryer instructions; if they are silent, at least 3 ft in any direction from openings into the building, including ventilated soffit openings. Backdraft damper required; no screen.
needs: Dryer vent termination location on the exterior wall or roof
note: Once the termination is placed, the 3 ft distance to windows, doors and soffit vents can be measured automatically.

title: Dryer terminal open area
applies_to: Dryer exhaust wall or roof terminal
check: Terminal passageway undiminished in size with at least 12.5 sq in. of open area.

title: Dryer duct material and size
applies_to: Dryer exhaust duct
check: Smooth-interior metal at least 0.0157 in. thick (28 gage), 4 in. nominal diameter.
note: Florida exception: 4 in. Schedule 40 PVC permitted where run horizontally beneath the slab.

title: Dryer duct installation
applies_to: Dryer exhaust duct
check: Support at intervals not over 12 ft and secure; male (insert) end points in the direction of airflow; seal joints per M1601.4.1; no screws or similar fasteners in joints.
note: Gas dryers: G2439.7.2 calls for supports every 4 ft and allows fasteners that protrude no more than 1/8 in.

title: Wall cavity fits dryer duct
applies_to: Wall or ceiling cavity enclosing the 4 in. dryer duct
check: Cavity must accept the duct without deforming it.
needs: Which wall the dryer duct rises in (then compare stud depth to the 4 in. round duct)
note: A 2x4 stud cavity (3.5 in.) cannot hold a 4 in. round duct undeformed; flag dryer walls thinner than 2x6 unless the duct runs elsewhere.

title: Dryer transition duct
applies_to: Flexible connector between dryer and exhaust duct
check: Single length, listed and labeled to UL 2158A, not over 8 ft long, never concealed in construction.

title: Dryer booster fans
applies_to: Dryer exhaust duct
check: Florida: domestic booster fans are not allowed in dryer exhaust systems. Dryer exhaust duct power ventilators listed to UL 705 for dryer ducts are addressed separately (M1502.4.4, M1502.4.5.3) and set the allowable length by their instructions.
note: The Florida prohibition (M1502.4.8) sits beside the model-code allowance for listed power ventilators (M1502.4.4); confirm with the local building department before relying on a power ventilator.

title: Dryer duct maximum length
applies_to: Dryer exhaust duct from the transition duct connection to the outlet terminal
check: Maximum 35 ft, reduced for each fitting: 4 in. radius mitered 45 deg 2 ft 6 in., mitered 90 deg 5 ft; 6 in. radius smooth 45 deg 1 ft, 90 deg 1 ft 9 in.; 8 in. radius smooth 45 deg 1 ft, 90 deg 1 ft 7 in.; 10 in. radius smooth 45 deg 9 in., 90 deg 1 ft 6 in. Transition duct not counted.
needs: Dryer duct developed length and number/type of elbows
note: Replaces B-23. Alternative: length per the dryer manufacturer instructions (M1502.4.5.2).

title: Dryer duct length per manufacturer
applies_to: Dryer exhaust duct longer than the 35 ft method allows
check: Size and length may follow the dryer manufacturer instructions; give the inspector a copy of the instructions for that make and model at the concealment inspection. Use the code fitting table if the manufacturer gives no fitting equivalents.

title: Dryer duct length label
applies_to: Dryer exhaust duct with equivalent length over 35 ft
check: Post a permanent label or tag stating the equivalent length within 6 ft of the exhaust duct connection.

title: Dryer exhaust duct required
applies_to: Any space provided for a clothes dryer (laundry room, closet, garage laundry)
check: Install an exhaust duct system wherever a dryer space is provided; if no dryer is installed, cap the duct in that space and mark it for future use.
note: Check that every dryer location has an exhaust point. Exception: listed condensing dryer installed before occupancy.

title: Dryer duct nail plates
applies_to: Dryer duct in framed walls or ceilings
check: Steel shield plates at least 0.062 in. thick on the finished face of framing wherever the duct is less than 1-1/4 in. from that face, extending at least 2 in. above sole plates and below top plates.

section_now: (none in 8th Edition; gas dryers see G2439.5)
title: Dryer makeup air
applies_to: Clothes dryer, especially in a closet
check: 9th Edition: provide makeup air where the installation exhausts more than 200 cfm. Dryer closet: makeup air per the dryer instructions, or permanent opening(s) totaling at least 100 sq in. in the closet enclosure, or other approved means.
edition_difference: New Chapter 15 section in the 9th Edition; in the 8th Edition the same 200 cfm / 100 sq in. rule appears only for gas dryers (G2439.5, G2439.5.1).
needs: Free area of louver, undercut or grille serving the dryer closet
note: Section numbers are 9th Edition.

title: Range hood ducted to outdoors
applies_to: Range hood or downdraft exhaust
check: Discharge to the outdoors through a duct with smooth interior, airtight, with a backdraft damper, independent of all other exhaust systems; never terminate in an attic, crawl space or inside the building.
needs: Hood is ducted or listed ductless (recirculating); duct termination point
note: Exception: listed ductless (recirculating) hoods installed per instructions where mechanical or natural ventilation is otherwise provided.

title: Range hood duct material
applies_to: Range hood exhaust duct
check: Galvanized steel, stainless steel or copper only.
note: Exception: downdraft systems may use solvent-cemented Schedule 40 PVC under a slab on grade, trench backfilled with sand or gravel, extending not more than 1 in. above the indoor floor and 8 in. above outside grade.

title: Kitchen exhaust rate
applies_to: Ducted range hood or downdraft exhaust
check: Fan capacity at least 100 cfm intermittent or 25 cfm continuous (Table M1507.4).
edition_difference: 9th Edition wording: exhaust rate must meet Table M1507.4 at one or more speed settings.
needs: Range hood cfm rating
note: Use AUTO where the hood object carries a cfm value.

title: Range hood makeup air
applies_to: Range hood or downdraft exhaust
check: Hoods able to exhaust more than 400 cfm need makeup air at about the exhaust rate, through a system with at least one gravity or automatic damper that opens when the hood runs, damper accessible for service. Florida exception for single-family dwellings: no makeup air at 400 cfm or less, and none from over 400 up to 800 cfm if there are no gravity-vent appliances inside the conditioned living space.
edition_difference: 9th Edition: makeup air system must have at least one outdoor air duct and damper.
needs: Range hood cfm; whether any gravity-vent (natural draft) fuel appliance is inside the conditioned space
note: Replaces B-06. Above 800 cfm makeup air is always required. The Florida exception is worded for a single-family dwelling.

title: Makeup air discharge location
applies_to: Kitchen exhaust makeup air
check: Discharge makeup air into the room with the hood, or into rooms or ducts that communicate with it through permanent openings at least as large as the required makeup air opening.
edition_difference: 9th Edition limits this sentence to makeup air ducted from the outdoors.

title: Microwave over range
applies_to: Microwave or other cooking appliance mounted over a range or cooktop
check: Install per the upper appliance listing, label and manufacturer instructions (mounting height above the cooktop comes from those instructions); microwave must conform to UL 923.
note: The app can prompt for the manufacturer minimum height when a microwave is placed above a cooktop.

title: Open-top broiler hood
applies_to: Domestic open-top broiler unit (indoor grill)
check: Metal exhaust hood at least 28 gage with 1/4 in. clearance to combustibles or cabinets above it; at least 24 in. between cooking surface and combustibles or cabinets; hood at least as wide as the unit, over the whole unit, ducted outdoors with a backdraft damper.
note: Units with integral exhaust listed for use without a hood are exempt.

title: Exhaust fan duct length
applies_to: Bath fan, kitchen or other ventilating fan duct
check: Duct length limited by Table M1506.2 for fan cfm and duct diameter, less 15 ft per elbow. Examples: 50 cfm with 4 in. duct: flex 56 ft, smooth 114 ft; 80 cfm with 4 in.: flex 4 ft, smooth 31 ft; 100 cfm with 4 in.: flex not allowed, smooth 10 ft; 100 cfm with 5 in.: flex 42 ft, smooth 91 ft; 100 cfm with 6 in.: flex 158 ft, smooth no limit; 3 in. duct only for 50 cfm smooth, 5 ft.
needs: Fan cfm, duct diameter, duct type (flex or smooth), length and elbows
note: Exception: no limit where the duct follows the fan manufacturer design criteria or the installed flow is measured.

title: Exhaust outlet location
applies_to: Exterior termination of any exhaust (bath fan, hood, dryer)
check: At least 3 ft from property lines, 3 ft from operable and nonoperable openings into the building, and 10 ft from mechanical air intakes unless the outlet is 3 ft above the intake. Outlet protection per R303.5.2 and R303.6.
needs: Exhaust termination locations; distance to property line
note: Measurable automatically once terminations are drawn on exterior walls.

title: Bathroom exhaust not recirculated
applies_to: Bathroom or toilet room exhaust fan
check: Exhaust directly to the outdoors; never recirculate within the dwelling and never discharge into an attic, crawl space or other indoor area.
needs: Bath fan duct termination point
note: Covers the bathroom fan termination part of B-05.

title: Whole-house ventilation system
applies_to: Whole-house mechanical ventilation system, where one is provided or required
check: One or more supply or exhaust fans with ducts and controls; controls must allow manual override and be labeled with their function (M1507.3.1, M1507.3.2).
note: Whether a system is required comes from the building-planning and energy provisions (see those lists).

title: Whole-house ventilation rate
applies_to: Whole-house mechanical ventilation system
check: Continuous outdoor air rate from Table M1507.3.3(1) or cfm = 0.01 x floor area (sq ft) + 7.5 x (bedrooms + 1). Table examples: under 1,500 sq ft: 30/45/60 cfm for 0-1/2-3/4-5 bedrooms; 1,501-3,000: 45/60/75; 3,001-4,500: 60/75/90. Intermittent operation allowed with at least 25 percent run time in each 4 hours and the rate multiplied (x4 at 25 percent, x2 at 50 percent). 30 percent reduction for balanced systems ducted to each bedroom and a living, dining or kitchen space.
needs: Ventilation system airflow (cfm) and run-time control; conditioned floor area and bedroom count come from the model

title: Local exhaust rates
applies_to: Exhaust fans in bathrooms, toilet rooms and kitchens
check: Bathroom/toilet room fan: at least 50 cfm intermittent or 20 cfm continuous. Kitchen: at least 100 cfm intermittent or 25 cfm continuous. Bath fan rating taken at 0.25 in. w.c. static pressure.
edition_difference: 9th Edition: rate must be met at one or more speed settings; the 0.25 in. w.c. rating condition moves from a table footnote into the section text.
note: Replaces the cfm part of B-05. Uses the exhaust fan cfm attribute.

title: Duct design
applies_to: New or altered duct system
check: Design and install per ACCA Manual D, the appliance manufacturer instructions or other approved methods.

title: Duct materials
applies_to: New ductwork
check: Factory-made ducts listed and labeled to UL 181; duct materials with flame spread index not over 200; discharge air temperature limited to 250 F; gypsum board allowed only for return ducts or plenums where air stays at or below 125 F and surfaces are not subject to condensation.

title: Framing cavities as return plenums
applies_to: Stud wall cavity or joist space used to carry air (panned return, return air chase)
check: Never for supply air; not part of a required fire-resistance-rated assembly; a stud cavity may not carry air from more than one floor; isolate from adjacent concealed spaces with tight fireblocking (R302.11); exterior-wall stud cavities may not be used.
note: Item 7 of M1601.1.1. The energy code separately restricts building cavities used as ducts; see the energy rule list.

title: Vibration isolators
applies_to: Flexible connector between air handler and metal duct
check: Approved material, not over 10 in. long.

title: Duct insulation materials
applies_to: Duct coverings, linings and insulation
check: Flame spread index not over 25 and smoke-developed index not over 50; listed and labeled; external insulation and insulated flex duct marked at least every 36 in. with manufacturer, R-value and indices.
note: Exception for spray foam on ducts in attics and crawl spaces with ignition barrier.

title: Duct joints sealed
applies_to: Duct joints, seams and connections
check: Fasten and seal every joint, seam and connection with welds, gaskets, mastic, mastic-plus-fabric or tape; UL 181A products (181A-P, 181A-M, 181A-H) on fibrous glass duct, UL 181B (181B-FX tape, 181B-M mastic) on metal and flex duct; flex duct fasteners marked 181B-C; round metal crimp joints lap at least 1 in. with at least three screws or rivets; connections to equipment flanges sealed and mechanically fastened.

title: Duct support
applies_to: Ductwork
check: Support factory-made ducts per manufacturer instructions; other ducts per SMACNA or NAIMA standards.

title: Fireblocking at ducts
applies_to: Duct penetrations and chases through framing (new soffits, chases, dropped ceilings)
check: Fireblock duct installations per R302.11.

title: Duct insulation vapor retarder
applies_to: Cooling supply ducts in unconditioned space (attic, garage)
check: Vapor retarder not over 0.05 perm, or aluminum foil at least 2 mils, on the outside of the insulation; exterior ducts protected from weather; duct coverings must not pass through a fireblocked wall or floor.
note: Duct R-values are set by the energy code.

title: Factory ducts and earth contact
applies_to: Flex duct or duct board near or in the ground, slab or masonry
check: Factory-made air ducts may not be installed in or on the ground, in tile or metal pipe, or within masonry or concrete; keep ducts at least 4 in. from earth unless built as an underground duct (M1601.4.8, M1601.1.2).

title: Ducts in garages
applies_to: Ducts in a garage or passing through the garage-to-house wall or ceiling
check: Comply with R302.5.2 (garage duct penetrations and duct material; no openings into the garage).
note: See the garage separation rule (replaces part of B-21 in the building list).

title: Under-floor plenums
applies_to: Existing under-floor plenum being modified or repaired
check: Prohibited in new structures; repairs to existing ones must keep the space clean and tightly enclosed, ground covered with a 4 mil moisture barrier, no plumbing cleanouts inside, materials with flame spread not over 200, 18 x 24 in. floor access (M1601.5.1 to M1601.5.5).

title: No shared HVAC with garage
applies_to: Supply register or return grille in a garage
check: A furnace or air-handling system that serves living space may not supply air to or return air from a garage.
note: Flag any register or return placed in a room of type garage unless it is on a dedicated garage-only system. Matters for garage conversions: the converted room is no longer a garage, the remaining garage is.

title: Outdoor air intake location
applies_to: Outdoor air intake for HVAC or ventilation
check: Locate per R303.5.1 and protect the opening per R303.6.

title: Return near open-combustion appliance
applies_to: Return air grille in the same room as a fuel-burning appliance with an open combustion chamber or draft hood
check: Return opening at least 10 ft in any direction from the open combustion chamber or draft hood.
needs: Appliance has an open combustion chamber or draft hood (natural draft)
note: Item 1 of M1602.2.

title: Return air quantity and sizing
applies_to: Return and transfer openings
check: Return air taken from a room may not exceed the supply air delivered to it; size return and transfer openings per equipment instructions, Manual D or the design professional.
note: Items 2 and 3 of M1602.2.

title: Prohibited return air locations
applies_to: Return air grille and the room it is in
check: No return air from a closet, bathroom, toilet room, kitchen, garage, mechanical room, boiler room, furnace room or unconditioned attic. Exceptions: kitchen return serving only the kitchen and at least 10 ft from cooking appliances; dedicated garage-only system; dedicated dehumidifier recirculating to the same closet or bathroom; Florida closet exception: return serving only the closet, and for closets under 30 sq ft not more than 30 cfm with the door undercut at least 1.5 in. or a louvered door or transfer grille of at least 30 sq in. net free area.
edition_difference: 9th Edition list omits bathroom (toilet room remains): closet, toilet room, kitchen, garage, mechanical room, boiler room, furnace room, unconditioned attic.
note: Item 4 of M1602.2. For gas furnaces G2442.3 still lists bathroom in both editions.

title: Balanced return air (Florida)
applies_to: Habitable rooms with a supply register and a door but no return (bedrooms, offices, master suite)
check: Pressure difference across a closed interior door not over 0.01 in. w.c. (2.5 Pa). Prescriptive options: transfer duct with 1.5 times the cross-sectional area of the supply duct to the room plus an unrestricted 1 in. door undercut; or through-wall transfer grille of 50 sq in. per 100 cfm of supply plus a 1 in. door undercut. Applies to habitable rooms only (not bathrooms, closets, storage or laundry rooms), but all supply air into the master suite counts.
note: Florida-specific section. Flag each closed-door habitable room that has supply but neither a return nor a transfer grille/jump duct; sizing needs the supply cfm or duct size for the room.

title: Combustion air, non-gas fuels
applies_to: Solid-fuel or oil-fired appliance
check: Solid-fuel appliances: combustion air per manufacturer instructions; oil-fired: per NFPA 31. Gas appliances follow G2407. Does not apply to fireplaces, fireplace stoves and direct-vent appliances.

title: Venting required
applies_to: Fuel-burning appliance (non-gas; gas per Chapter 24)
check: Vent to the outdoors per the listing and manufacturer instructions unless listed for unvented use; venting system must provide the draft the appliance needs (M1801.2).

title: Existing chimney or vent reuse
applies_to: Appliance replaced, removed from, or newly connected to an existing chimney or vent
check: Resize the chimney or vent as needed for draft and to control condensation; flue passage clear, clean and with a continuous undamaged liner; masonry chimney cleanout per R1003.17; clearances to combustibles per code and manufacturer (M1801.3.1 to M1801.3.4).
note: Triggered by appliance replacement or removal even where the chimney itself is not being altered.

title: Vents and ducts kept apart
applies_to: Chimney, vent or vent connector near ductwork
check: Vents and connectors may not extend into or through supply or return ducts or plenums; fireblock vent and chimney installations per R302.11 (M1801.9); close or cap unused openings in a venting system (M1801.10).

title: Common venting
applies_to: Two or more appliances on one natural-draft vent
check: Appliances on the same floor; inlets offset so none is opposite another; no natural-draft connector into a positive-pressure mechanical draft system. A solid-fuel appliance or fireplace may not share a flue with another appliance (M1801.12).

title: Vent connector installation
applies_to: Chimney or vent connector (oil or solid fuel appliance)
check: Within the space where the appliance is located, as short and straight as possible, sloped up at least 1/4 in. per foot, supported and fastened; may not pass through a floor or ceiling, and through a wall only with a listed pass-through (M1803.3.1); whole length accessible (M1803.3.5).

title: Connector clearance to combustibles
applies_to: Unlisted single-wall or Type L connector on oil or solid-fuel appliance
check: Single-wall metal connector: 18 in. (9 in. for oil appliances listed for Type L vent). Type L connector: 9 in. (3 in. or per listing for oil appliances listed for Type L). Reductions only per Table M1306.2.

title: Mechanical draft vent terminal
applies_to: Side-wall mechanical draft vent terminal (non-direct-vent, oil or pellet appliance)
check: At least 3 ft above any forced air inlet within 10 ft; 4 ft below, 4 ft horizontally from, or 1 ft above any door, window or gravity air inlet; 3 ft from an inside corner; bottom at least 12 in. above grade; not above or within 3 ft horizontally of an oil tank vent or gas meter; power exhauster outlets 10 ft from lot lines and adjacent buildings.

title: Door swing at vent terminal
applies_to: Exterior door near an appliance vent terminal
check: Doors may not swing within 12 in. horizontally of a vent terminal; door stops or closers do not satisfy this.
needs: Location of appliance vent terminals on exterior walls
note: Same rule for gas at G2426.7.1.

title: Masonry chimney connection
applies_to: Connector entering a masonry chimney
check: Enter at least 6 in. above the bottom of the chimney (or provide a capped tee cleanout), flush with the inner face of the liner, cemented in; flue area at least the connector area, and for solid fuel not more than three times the flue collar area (M1805.3, M1805.3.1).

title: Clearance above cooktop
applies_to: Range or cooktop and the cabinet, shelf or other combustible material above it
check: At least 30 in. vertically from the cooking top to unprotected combustible material above. Less only as allowed by the listing and labeling of the range hood or appliance; a listed microwave or cooking appliance above follows M1504.1.
note: Replaces B-22 (electric and general case). Gas ranges: G2447.5 also counts metal cabinets and sets a 24 in. floor with protection.

title: Household cooking appliances
applies_to: Range, cooktop, wall oven
check: Must be listed and labeled for household use and installed per manufacturer instructions without blocking combustion air or service access; electric cooking appliances to UL 1026 or UL 858.
needs: Appliance is listed for household (residential) use
note: Commercial-style ranges must carry a household listing.

title: Sauna heaters
applies_to: Electric sauna heater
check: Guard of low-conductivity material (such as wood) against accidental contact; listed to UL 875 and installed per instructions; thermostat limiting room temperature to 194 F, with a remote sensing element within 6 in. of the ceiling (M1902.2, M1902.4).

title: Standby generator exhaust
applies_to: Permanently installed standby generator
check: Listed and installed per instructions (M1905.1, M1905.2); exhaust at least 10 ft from doors, operable windows, eave vents and air intakes. May be 5 ft (or the manufacturer distance if greater) where CO alarms are installed within 10 ft of each sleeping room and another as close as possible to the opening nearest the exhaust. Must resist design wind pressures (M1905.2.4).
note: Florida-specific section. Exterior item; listed because generators are often added with a remodel or service upgrade.

title: Boilers
applies_to: Hydronic boiler (rare in Florida)
check: Install per manufacturer instructions with rating data and instructions attached; shutoff valves on supply and return; pressure and temperature gauges; pressure-relief valve; low-water cutoff; expansion tank sized per Table M2003.2 (M2001 to M2003).
edition_difference: 9th Edition adds M2002.4.1 relief discharge pipe rules: air break in the boiler room, full size, single device, no valves or tees, not trapped, gravity flow, end not threaded, ending not more than 6 in. above the floor or receptor. 8th Edition: discharge piped by gravity to within 18 in. of the floor or to an open receptor.

title: Water heater installation
applies_to: Water heater (new, replaced or relocated)
check: Install per Chapter 28, the manufacturer instructions and this code; attic installations must meet M1305.1.3 access; gas units per Chapter 24; electric units per the electrical chapters (M2005.3).
note: Relief valve, discharge pipe and drain pan requirements are in Chapter 28 (plumbing list).

title: Water heater prohibited locations
applies_to: Fuel-fired water heater and the room it is in
check: No fuel-fired water heater in a room used as a storage closet. In a bedroom or bathroom it must be in a sealed enclosure so combustion air is not taken from the living space.
needs: Water heater fuel (electric, gas, other) and whether it is direct-vent
note: Direct-vent water heaters need no enclosure. Electric water heaters are not restricted by this section. Check again when a room is renamed bedroom or bathroom.

title: Water heater access through closet
applies_to: Water heater in an attic or crawl space reached through a bedroom or bathroom closet
check: Access through a closet in a sleeping room or bathroom is allowed where those spaces are ventilated per code.
note: Permission, not a restriction.

title: Combination water/space heating
applies_to: Water heater also used for space heating
check: Install per Chapter 20, Chapter 24, Chapter 28 and the manufacturer instructions.

title: Gas appliances listed
applies_to: Any gas appliance
check: Listed and labeled for the application.

title: Wind resistance of gas appliances
applies_to: Gas appliance and supports exposed to wind (exterior tankless water heater, generator, pool heater)
check: Design and install to resist the code wind pressures.

title: Gas appliances in flood zone
applies_to: Gas appliance, equipment or piping in a flood hazard area
check: Locate at or above the R322 elevation for utilities and equipment, or design and install to keep water out and resist flood loads.
needs: Project flood zone and required elevation; appliance elevation

title: Condensing appliance drain pan
applies_to: Category IV condensing gas appliance (condensing furnace or water heater) where a blocked drain would damage the building
check: Provide an auxiliary drain pan per M1411 unless the appliance shuts down automatically on a blocked condensate drain; condensate pumps in attics or crawl spaces must be interlocked with the appliance (G2404.11).

title: Trusses and added appliance loads
applies_to: Gas piping or an appliance (water heater, air handler) supported by roof or floor trusses
check: Do not cut, notch, drill or alter truss members or engineered wood without the approval of a registered design professional or the manufacturer; do not add appliance loads to a truss without verifying its capacity (G2405.2, G2405.3). Gas piping work must leave the building structurally sound (G2405.1).

title: Gas appliance prohibited rooms
applies_to: Gas appliance and the room it is in or opens into
check: No gas appliance in a sleeping room, bathroom, toilet room or storage closet, or in a space that opens only into such a room, unless one of the listed exceptions applies: direct-vent appliance; vented room heater, wall furnace, vented decorative appliance, vented gas fireplace or fireplace heater, or decorative appliance in a vented fireplace, in a room meeting the G2407.5 volume; the limited unvented heater, dedicated-enclosure and bathroom dryer cases in the next three rules.
needs: Appliance type (direct-vent, vented room heater/fireplace, unvented heater, other) and input rating
note: Re-check when a room is renamed bedroom, bathroom or closet (for example a den with a gas water heater closet becoming a bedroom).

title: Unvented heater in bath or bedroom
applies_to: Wall-mounted unvented gas room heater in a bathroom or bedroom
check: One heater only, with oxygen-depletion shutoff (G2445.6): not over 6,000 Btu/h in a bathroom, not over 10,000 Btu/h in a bedroom; the room must meet the G2407.5 volume.
needs: Heater input rating (Btu/h); room volume comes from the model
note: Exceptions 3 and 4 of G2406.2.

title: Gas appliance closet off bedroom/bath
applies_to: Gas appliance in a room or closet that opens only into a bedroom or bathroom
check: Allowed where the space is used for nothing else, has a solid weather-stripped door with an approved self-closing device, and all combustion air comes directly from outdoors per G2407.6.
needs: Door is solid, weather-stripped and self-closing; combustion air openings to outdoors provided
note: Exception 5 of G2406.2.

title: Gas dryer in bathroom
applies_to: Gas clothes dryer in a residential bathroom or toilet room
check: Allowed where the room has a permanent opening of at least 100 sq in. to a space that is not a sleeping room, bathroom, toilet room or storage closet.
needs: Permanent opening (louver/grille) free area and the room it opens to
note: Exception 6 of G2406.2.

title: Outdoor gas appliances
applies_to: Gas appliance installed outdoors
check: Listed for outdoor installation or protected from the weather.

title: Combustion air required
applies_to: Gas appliance that draws combustion air from the room (natural draft, Category I)
check: Provide combustion, ventilation and dilution air by indoor volume (G2407.5), outdoor openings (G2407.6), a combination (G2407.7), engineering (G2407.8) or mechanical supply (G2407.9). Direct-vent, power-burner and non-Category I vented appliances follow the manufacturer instructions.
note: New walls or doors that enclose an existing gas water heater or furnace change its combustion air supply.

title: Makeup air for exhaust appliances
applies_to: Dwelling with gas appliances plus exhaust fans, dryer or kitchen hood
check: Provide makeup air where exhaust fans, clothes dryers or kitchen ventilation interfere with appliance operation.
note: Related to the range hood makeup air rule M1503.4.

title: Indoor combustion air volume
applies_to: Room or space containing gas appliances using indoor air
check: Standard method: at least 50 cu ft of room volume per 1,000 Btu/h of total appliance input. Rooms joined by doorless openings or by G2407.5.3 openings count together. Where infiltration is known to be under 0.40 ACH use the G2407.5.2 equations instead.
needs: Input rating (Btu/h) of each gas appliance in the space; room volume comes from area and ceiling height
note: Also the volume test used by G2406.2 exceptions 2 to 4.

title: Openings combining indoor spaces
applies_to: Louvered doors or grilles linking an appliance closet to adjoining rooms
check: Same story: two permanent openings, one starting within 12 in. of the top and one within 12 in. of the bottom of the enclosure, each at least 1 sq in. per 1,000 Btu/h and not less than 100 sq in., minimum dimension 3 in. Different stories: openings totaling 2 sq in. per 1,000 Btu/h.
needs: Appliance input rating; opening sizes and heights

title: Outdoor combustion air, two openings
applies_to: Appliance enclosure taking combustion air from outdoors
check: Two permanent openings, one starting within 12 in. of the top and one within 12 in. of the bottom. Each at least 1 sq in. per 4,000 Btu/h where direct to outdoors or through vertical ducts; 1 sq in. per 2,000 Btu/h through horizontal ducts. Minimum dimension 3 in.
needs: Appliance input rating; opening sizes and whether ducts are vertical or horizontal

title: Outdoor combustion air, one opening
applies_to: Appliance enclosure taking combustion air from outdoors through a single opening
check: One permanent opening starting within 12 in. of the top, at least 1 sq in. per 3,000 Btu/h and not less than the sum of the vent connector areas; appliance clearances at least 1 in. at sides and back and 6 in. at front.
needs: Appliance input rating; opening size

title: Mechanical combustion air
applies_to: Combustion air supplied by a fan
check: At least 0.35 cfm per 1,000 Btu/h from outdoors; each appliance interlocked so the burner cannot fire when the air supply is off; makeup air where exhaust fans are installed.

title: Louver free area
applies_to: Louvers, grilles and screens on combustion air openings
check: Size by net free area; if unknown assume 25 percent for wood louvers and 75 percent for metal; screen mesh not smaller than 1/4 in.; fixed open or interlocked with the appliance.

title: Combustion air ducts
applies_to: Combustion air duct
check: Galvanized steel or equivalent; serves one enclosure; ends in unobstructed space; separate ducts for upper and lower openings; not screened where ending in an attic; upper horizontal duct not sloped down toward the source; exterior intake at least 12 in. above grade.

title: Install per listing and instructions
applies_to: Any gas appliance
check: Install per the listing, manufacturer instructions and code; have the installation instructions on site at inspection. Where the listing or instructions are stricter than the code, they govern.

title: Gas ignition source in garage
applies_to: Gas appliance with an ignition source in a garage or a non-living room opening to the garage
check: Ignition source at least 18 in. above the floor.
needs: Ignition source height above floor, or appliance is listed flammable-vapor-ignition resistant (FVIR)
note: Exceptions: FVIR-listed appliances; appliances in a separate enclosed space reached only from outside the garage with combustion air from outside the garage may sit at floor level (G2408.2.1).

title: Gas appliances in private garages
applies_to: Gas appliance in a private garage
check: Mount with at least 6 ft clearance above the floor unless protected from vehicle impact and installed per G2408.2.
needs: Vehicle impact protection provided, or mounting height above floor

title: Clearance from grade
applies_to: Gas equipment at grade (outdoor tankless heater, pool heater, generator)
check: On a level concrete slab or approved base at least 3 in. above adjoining grade, or suspended at least 6 in. above grade.

title: Gas appliance clearances to combustibles
applies_to: Heat-producing gas appliance near walls, cabinets, shelving, doors
check: Keep the listed clearances; account for door swing, drawer pull, overhead projections, shelving and window swing; door stops, limiters or closers may not be used to obtain clearance. Reduce only per G2409.
needs: Listed clearances from the appliance label (sides, back, front, top)
note: With the listed clearances entered, door swings and cabinets inside the clearance zone can be flagged automatically.

title: Clearance reduction methods
applies_to: Gas appliance, vent connector or single-wall pipe closer to combustibles (including gypsum board) than listed
check: Use a UL 1618 listed assembly or the protection methods of Table G2409.2 (for example 24 gage sheet metal with ventilated air space reduces 36 in. to 18 in. above and 12 in. at sides and rear); 1 in. ventilated air space; no reduction where the appliance listing prohibits it.

title: Furnace and boiler clearances
applies_to: Gas central furnace, boiler or gas air-conditioning appliance
check: Clearances per manufacturer instructions; front clearance sufficient for servicing; supply ducts keep the plenum clearance for the first 3 ft from the supply plenum (G2409.3, G2409.4).

title: Gas pipe not a grounding electrode
applies_to: Gas piping and electrical grounding
check: Never use gas piping as a grounding electrode; appliance electrical connections and grounding per the electrical chapters (G2410.2).

title: Gas piping bonding
applies_to: Metallic gas piping other than CSST
check: Above-ground piping likely to become energized must be electrically continuous and bonded; considered bonded when connected to an appliance that is connected to its circuit equipment grounding conductor.
edition_difference: 9th Edition wording: connected to one or more appliances.

title: CSST bonding
applies_to: Gas piping system containing any CSST without an arc-resistant jacket
check: Bond to the electrical service grounding electrode system with a jumper not smaller than 6 AWG copper, not longer than 75 ft, attached to a metallic pipe, pipe fitting or CSST fitting with a UL 467 listed clamp, connections per NFPA 70.
needs: Gas piping material includes CSST (and whether it is arc-resistant listed)
note: Arc-resistant CSST listed to ANSI LC1/CSA 6.26 is treated like other piping (G2411.3), but any non-arc-resistant segment triggers G2411.2.

title: Capacity check for added appliance
applies_to: Adding a gas appliance or increasing input (tankless water heater, range, generator) on existing piping
check: Check that the existing piping has capacity for all appliances served; if not, enlarge it or run separate piping. Additions and modifications must keep sizes per the chapter (G2412.3, G2412.8).
note: A tankless water heater replacing a tank unit commonly exceeds the existing branch and meter capacity.

title: Gas piping identification
applies_to: Exposed gas piping other than steel pipe and CSST (copper or other tubing)
check: Yellow label marked Gas in black letters at intervals not over 5 ft; not required in the same room as the appliance served.

title: LP-gas storage
applies_to: LP-gas tank or cylinders
check: Design and install the storage system per the Florida Fire Prevention Code and NFPA 58.

title: Gas pipe sizing
applies_to: New or extended gas piping
check: Size piping to deliver the total connected input of all appliances at not less than each appliance minimum supply pressure, using the code tables or equations, a listed system manufacturer tables, or approved engineering (G2413.2, G2413.3).
note: Permit sets usually carry a gas piping diagram with lengths, sizes and Btu/h loads. Sizing tables themselves were not transcribed.

title: Gas piping prohibited locations
applies_to: Gas piping route
check: Not in or through a supply, return or exhaust duct, clothes chute, chimney, gas vent, dumbwaiter or elevator shaft; not through a townhouse unit other than the one served.

title: Gas piping in solid walls
applies_to: Concealed gas piping in solid partitions or solid (masonry/concrete) walls
check: Only inside a chase or casing.
note: Relevant to concrete block walls.

title: Concealed gas fittings
applies_to: Fittings in concealed gas piping
check: Only threaded elbows, tees, couplings, plugs and caps; brazed fittings; welded fittings; or fittings listed to ANSI LC1/CSA 6.26 or LC4/CSA 6.32. No unions or other fittings in concealed spaces.

title: Gas entry above grade
applies_to: Gas piping entering or leaving the building
check: Enter and exit above grade with the annular space sealed; no penetration of foundation walls below grade.

title: Shield plates for gas piping
applies_to: Gas piping other than black or galvanized steel (CSST, copper) concealed in framing
check: Where less than 1-1/2 in. from the framing face that receives the finish, protect with steel shield plates at least 0.0575 in. (16 gage) covering the pipe and extending at least 4 in. each side of the member, 4 in. above bottom plates and 4 in. below top plates.
note: Gas plates extend 4 in.; plumbing and mechanical piping plates extend 2 in.

title: Gas piping in slab floors
applies_to: Gas piping run in a solid (concrete) floor, e.g. to an island cooktop
check: Lay in a covered channel that allows access, or in Schedule 40 steel, wrought iron, PVC or ABS conduit. Conduit ending outdoors: sealed at the indoor end, extends 2 in. past where the pipe leaves the floor and 4 in. outside the building, vented above grade. Conduit with both ends indoors: both ends in accessible locations, not sealed, 2 in. past the floor.

title: Gas piping under the building
applies_to: Gas piping underground beneath the slab or building
check: Prohibited unless encased in approved conduit (wrought iron, plastic, steel or a listed system) designed for the loads and protected from corrosion; conduit terminations as for G2415.8 (sealed and vented outdoors, or open at both accessible indoor ends).

title: Outdoor above-ground gas piping
applies_to: Gas piping outdoors or passing through an exterior wall
check: At least 3-1/2 in. above ground or roof surface, supported and protected from damage; coat or wrap where passing through an outside wall; seal the annular space of any sleeve.

title: Gas piping burial depth
applies_to: Underground gas piping outdoors
check: At least 12 in. below grade; individual lines to outdoor lights, grills and similar appliances at least 8 in. where approved and not subject to damage. Plastic pipe only outdoors underground, with yellow insulated tracer wire at least 18 AWG (G2415.17). Steel underground piping needs corrosion protection; galvanizing alone is not enough (G2415.11).
note: Site item kept as a reminder for outdoor kitchens and generators.

title: Cap unused gas outlets
applies_to: Gas outlet with no appliance connected (appliance removed or converted to electric)
check: Cap gastight.
note: Exception: listed quick-disconnect devices and gas convenience outlets.

title: Gas outlet location
applies_to: Gas stub-out / outlet for an appliance
check: Outlet in the same room or space as the appliance; not behind a door; unthreaded pipe extends at least 1 in. through finished walls and ceilings and at least 2 in. above floors, patios or slabs; securely supported.
note: Check that each gas utility point is in the same room as its appliance and not within a door swing.

title: Gas piping pressure test
applies_to: New or altered gas piping
check: Test before use or concealment: not less than 1.5 times the maximum working pressure and never less than 3 psig, measured with a suitable gauge or manometer (G2417.4, G2417.4.1). New branches: only the new branch needs testing (G2417.1.3). Minor repairs or additions may be inspected and leak-checked with noncorrosive leak-detection fluid instead (G2417.1.2). Leak-check before turning gas on (G2417.6).
edition_difference: 9th Edition adds G2417.7.3.1 (purge piping removed from service indefinitely) and calls for a listed combustible gas detector in G2417.5.1.
note: Test duration not transcribed; see G2417.4.2.

title: Gas piping support
applies_to: Gas piping
check: Support with metal hangers, straps or structure, not from other piping. Maximum spacing (Table G2424.1): steel pipe 1/2 in. 6 ft, 3/4 or 1 in. 8 ft, 1-1/4 in. and larger 10 ft horizontal and every floor vertical; smooth-wall tubing 1/2 in. 4 ft, 5/8 or 3/4 in. 6 ft, 7/8 or 1 in. 8 ft; CSST per manufacturer.

title: Sediment trap
applies_to: Gas water heater, furnace, boiler, pool heater and other appliances not exempted
check: Install a sediment trap (tee with capped vertical nipple at the bottom, or approved device) downstream of the appliance shutoff valve as close to the appliance inlet as practical, unless built into the appliance.
note: Not required for ranges, clothes dryers, illuminating appliances, decorative vented appliances in fireplaces, gas fireplaces and outdoor grills.

title: Shutoff valves not concealed
applies_to: Gas shutoff valves
check: No shutoff valve in a concealed location or furnace plenum; place for access and protect from damage (G2420.1.3).

title: Appliance shutoff valve
applies_to: Each gas appliance
check: Shutoff valve in the same room as the appliance, within 6 ft of it, upstream of the union, connector or quick-disconnect, with access. A valve behind a movable appliance (range, dryer) counts as accessible. Valve in a fireplace firebox per the appliance instructions.
note: Measure from each gas appliance to its gas shutoff/outlet point: same room and not more than 6 ft. Becomes DATA if the valve is not drawn.

title: Remote valve for fireplaces and heaters
applies_to: Vented decorative appliance, room heater or gas logs in a vented fireplace
check: Shutoff may be remote from the appliance where it has ready access, is permanently identified and serves no other appliance.

title: Shutoff at manifold
applies_to: Appliance shutoff valve located at a gas manifold
check: Within 50 ft of the appliance served, readily accessible and permanently identified.

title: Gas pressure regulators
applies_to: Line or MP regulator (2 psi systems)
check: Listed regulator where the appliance needs lower pressure than the supply; accessible and protected; vented directly outdoors or fitted with a listed vent-limiting device; MP regulators need an upstream listed shutoff valve (G2420.4), test tees and a union within 1 ft where on rigid pipe (G2421.2, G2421.3).

title: Appliance connection method
applies_to: Connection of each gas appliance to the piping
check: Rigid metallic pipe, CSST per manufacturer, or a listed and labeled appliance connector (ANSI Z21.24/CSA 6.10) located entirely in the same room as the appliance; listed quick-disconnects or convenience outlets with listed connectors; listed outdoor connectors or hoses for outdoor appliances. Protect connectors from damage; no strain on piping (G2422.1.1, G2408.6).

title: Connector length
applies_to: Flexible appliance connector
check: Not over 6 ft along its centerline, one connector per appliance, sized for the appliance demand (G2422.1.2.2).
note: Distance from gas outlet to appliance connection point must not exceed 6 ft. Exception: rigid metallic pipe sized as part of the piping system.

title: Connector not through construction
applies_to: Flexible appliance connector
check: May not be concealed in or pass through walls, floors, partitions, ceilings or appliance housings (limited exceptions for rigid pipe, protected openings in appliance housings and fireplace inserts with factory protection).
note: Same test as outlet location: outlet and appliance in the same room with no wall or cabinet partition between unless the appliance housing exception applies.

title: Union at rigid-piped appliance
applies_to: Appliance connected with rigid metallic pipe
check: Provide an accessible union within 6 ft of the appliance.

title: Appliances needing no vent
applies_to: Gas appliances
check: Every gas appliance must be vented outdoors except: ranges; built-in domestic cooking units; hot plates and laundry stoves; Type 1 clothes dryers (exhausted per G2439); refrigerators; counter appliances; room heaters listed for unvented use. Unvented refrigerators, counter appliances and room heaters together may not exceed 20 Btu/h per cu ft of room volume.

title: Existing vent or chimney reuse
applies_to: Gas appliance replaced on, added to, or permanently removed from an existing chimney or vent
check: Resize the vent or chimney as needed for draft and to control condensation; flue clear, clean, liner continuous and undamaged; masonry flue cleanout at least 6 in. high; clearances to combustibles kept (or relined with a UL 1777 listed liner).
note: Typical trigger: furnace removed or changed to electric, leaving a gas water heater alone on an oversized common vent.

title: Gas appliance into fireplace flue
applies_to: Gas appliance connected to a chimney flue serving a fireplace
check: Noncombustible seal below the connection, access for inspection and cleaning; no connection to a factory-built fireplace flue unless the appliance is listed for it; connector must run into the masonry flue itself.

title: Gas vent sizing
applies_to: Chimney or vent serving gas appliances
check: Size per G2427 and the G2428 tables (Category I), or the appliance manufacturer instructions.
note: Sizing tables not transcribed.

title: Vent insulation shield
applies_to: Gas vent passing through an insulated ceiling or attic
check: Steel insulation shield (26 gage minimum) keeping insulation at the vent clearance, ending at least 2 in. above the insulation in an attic and secured.

title: Vent shield plates
applies_to: Gas vent through studs, joists or rafters less than 1-1/2 in. from the member edge
check: 16 gage steel shield plates covering the vent at the member and extending at least 4 in. above sole plates, below top plates and each side of the member.

title: Door swing at gas vent terminal
applies_to: Exterior door near an appliance vent terminal
check: Doors may not swing within 12 in. horizontally of a vent terminal; door stops or closers do not satisfy this.
needs: Location of gas appliance vent terminals on exterior walls

title: Vents not through ducts
applies_to: Gas vent route
check: Venting may not extend into or pass through a fabricated air duct or furnace plenum.

title: Vent type for appliance
applies_to: Gas appliance vent material
check: Category I and draft-hood appliances: Type B vent, lined chimney, listed liner or single-wall pipe where allowed; wall furnaces: Type B-W; Category II, III, IV: as specified by the appliance manufacturer; plastic vent only where the appliance is listed for it and the instructions name the material (G2427.4.1).

title: Gas vent roof termination
applies_to: Type B gas vent through the roof
check: Vents 12 in. or smaller at least 8 ft from a vertical wall: cap height above the roof by slope (1 ft up to 6/12, 1.25 ft to 7/12, 1.5 ft to 8/12, 2 ft to 9/12, 2.5 ft to 10/12, 3.25 ft to 11/12, 4 ft to 12/12). Larger vents or within 8 ft of a wall: 2 ft above the roof penetration and 2 ft above any part of the building within 10 ft. At least 5 ft above the highest draft hood or flue collar (12 ft above the bottom of a wall furnace for B-W) (G2427.6.5). Listed cap (G2427.6.6). At least 3 ft above any forced air inlet within 10 ft (G2427.6.7).

title: Side-wall vent terminal clearances
applies_to: Through-the-wall vent terminal (tankless water heater, direct-vent fireplace, condensing furnace)
check: At least 12 in. above grade, porch or deck. Direct-vent terminal to an openable window or door: 6 in. for input up to 10,000 Btu/h, 9 in. up to 50,000, 12 in. up to 150,000, larger per manufacturer. Non-direct-vent terminal: 4 ft below or to the side of an opening or 1 ft above. Mechanical air inlet: 10 ft horizontally or 3 ft above. 7 ft above a public sidewalk or driveway. Under a porch or deck: 12 in. below it and only where open on at least two sides. 3 ft from a gas service regulator vent (10 ft above 2 psi).
needs: Vent terminal location, appliance input rating and whether it is direct-vent
note: Once the terminal is placed on an exterior wall the distances to windows and doors can be checked automatically. Other clearances per the manufacturer.

title: Vent condensate
applies_to: Category II or IV or other condensing appliance
check: Collect and dispose of vent condensate per the appliance and vent manufacturer instructions.

title: Gas vent connector rules
applies_to: Vent connector for a Category I gas appliance
check: Clearance to combustibles: listed Type B connector as listed; single-wall connector 6 in. for listed draft-hood appliances (9 in. for conversion-burner furnaces). Slope up at least 1/4 in. per foot with no dips (G2427.10.8); joints fastened (G2427.10.6); ready access for the whole length (G2427.10.12); single-wall connectors may not pass through walls, floors or ceilings (G2427.10.14); no connection to a fireplace flue unless the fireplace opening is permanently sealed (G2427.10.13).
note: Other subsections of G2427.10 (size, length, materials) not transcribed.

title: Gas logs in fireplaces
applies_to: Decorative gas appliance (gas logs) in a solid-fuel fireplace
check: Listed (ANSI Z21.60, or Z21.84 for manually lighted natural gas sets) and installed per instructions; flame safeguard shutoff required except Z21.84 sets (G2432.2); not in rooms prohibited by G2406.2 (G2432.3).

title: Log lighters
applies_to: Gas log lighter
check: Listed to CSA 8 and installed per manufacturer instructions.

title: Vented gas fireplaces
applies_to: Vented gas fireplace or fireplace heater
check: Listed (ANSI Z21.50/CSA 2.22 fireplaces; Z21.88/CSA 2.33 fireplace heaters), installed per instructions with flame safeguard; service panels and grilles may not be attached to the building (G2434.2, G2435.1).
note: Framing and mantel clearances come from the manufacturer instructions.

title: Gas wall furnace location
applies_to: Vented gas wall furnace
check: No door may swing within 12 in. of an air inlet or outlet (door stops and closers do not count); must not circulate air from a bathroom to other rooms; no ducts attached; service access kept (G2436.3 to G2436.6).

title: Gas dryer listing
applies_to: Gas clothes dryer
check: Listed to ANSI Z21.5.1/CSA 7.1 and installed per manufacturer instructions.

title: Gas dryer exhaust to outdoors
applies_to: Gas clothes dryer
check: Exhaust system independent of all others, carrying moisture and combustion products outside the building, per manufacturer instructions.
note: A gas dryer can never be ductless; check for an exhaust point.

title: Dryer duct through fireblocking or rated assemblies
applies_to: Dryer exhaust duct crossing fireblocking, draftstopping or a fire-resistance-rated wall or floor/ceiling (garage separation, townhouse wall)
check: Only galvanized steel or aluminum duct of the required thickness with the rating maintained; no fire dampers in dryer exhaust.

title: Gas dryer exhaust termination
applies_to: Gas dryer exhaust duct
check: Terminate outside with a backdraft damper and no screen; no fasteners that obstruct flow; never connected to a vent connector, vent or chimney; not through ducts or plenums; joints sealed per M1601.4.1; terminal open area at least 12.5 sq in. (G2439.3.1).

title: Gas dryer makeup air
applies_to: Gas dryer, especially in a closet
check: Makeup air where the installation exhausts more than 200 cfm. Dryer closet: opening of at least 100 sq in. in the closet enclosure, or other approved makeup air.
needs: Free area of louver, undercut or grille serving the dryer closet
note: 9th Edition adds the same rule for all dryers at M1502.6.

title: Gas dryer duct nail plates
applies_to: Gas dryer duct in framed walls or ceilings
check: Steel shield plates at least 0.062 in. thick where the duct is less than 1-1/4 in. from the finished face of framing, extending at least 2 in. above sole plates and below top plates.

title: Gas dryer duct material and support
applies_to: Gas dryer exhaust duct
check: Smooth-interior metal at least 0.016 in. thick, 4 in. nominal; supported every 4 ft and secured; insert end in the direction of airflow; fasteners may not protrude more than 1/8 in. into the duct; cavities must fit the duct undeformed (G2439.7.2).
note: Stricter support spacing than M1502.4.2 (12 ft); M1502.4.2 bans screws outright. Use the stricter of each.

title: Gas dryer duct length
applies_to: Gas dryer exhaust duct
check: Maximum 35 ft from the transition duct connection to the terminal, reduced by the fitting table (same values as Table M1502.4.5.1), or per the dryer manufacturer instructions with a copy given to the inspector before concealment (G2439.7.4.2). Transition duct: single length, UL 2158A, not over 8 ft, not concealed (G2439.7.3). Label within 6 ft of the connection where equivalent length exceeds 35 ft (G2439.7.5). Exhaust duct required wherever a dryer space is provided (G2439.7.6).
needs: Dryer duct developed length and number/type of elbows
note: Gas counterpart of B-23.

title: Gas sauna heaters
applies_to: Gas-fired sauna heater
check: Guarded against contact; draft hood and combustion air intake outside the sauna room; thermostat limit 194 F with sensor within 6 in. of the ceiling; timer maximum 1 hour with control outside the room; ventilation opening at least 4 in. by 8 in. near the top of the sauna door (G2440.2 to G2440.7).

title: Furnace return air prohibited sources
applies_to: Return or outdoor air intake for a gas forced-air furnace system
check: Not within 10 ft of an appliance vent outlet, plumbing vent or exhaust fan discharge unless the outlet is 3 ft above the intake; not from a room smaller than 25 percent of the volume served (unless return does not exceed supply to that room); not solely from a room containing a fuel-burning appliance (exceptions for direct-vent appliances and for rooms with over 1 cu ft per 10 Btu/h and returns 10 ft from draft hoods); not from a closet, bathroom, toilet room, kitchen, garage, boiler room, furnace room or unconditioned attic (kitchen-only returns 10 ft from cooking appliances and garage-only systems excepted).
note: Room-type test is automatic; distance tests need the appliance and vent locations. Bathroom stays on this list in the 9th Edition even though M1602.2 drops it.

title: Return duct sealed to furnace
applies_to: Gas furnace in a closet or room with supply ducts serving other spaces
check: Return air must be carried by a duct sealed to the furnace casing and ending outside the furnace space. Required outdoor air inlets screened with 1/4 in. mesh (G2442.4).

title: Gas unit heaters
applies_to: Gas unit heater (garage or workshop)
check: Listed (ANSI Z83.8/CSA 2.6). Suspended type: at least 18 in. at sides, 12 in. below and 6 in. above to combustibles (1 in. above a sloping vertical draft hood), unless listed for less; supports noncombustible and designed for the load; no ducts unless listed (G2444.1 to G2444.3).

title: Unvented room heaters, general
applies_to: Unvented gas room heater or unvented gas log set
check: Listed to ANSI Z21.11.2; not the sole source of heat for the dwelling; not over 40,000 Btu/h each; oxygen-depletion safety shutoff; location limits of G2406.2; not in a factory-built fireplace unless the fireplace is listed for it (UL 127); ventless firebox enclosures listed to ANSI Z21.91 (G2445.1 to G2445.7.1).

title: Unvented heater room volume
applies_to: Room containing unvented gas appliances
check: Total input of all unvented appliances in the room not over 20 Btu/h per cu ft of room volume; adjoining rooms joined by an opening that cannot be closed may be counted.
needs: Input rating (Btu/h) of each unvented appliance; room volume comes from the model

title: Gas cooking appliance listing
applies_to: Gas range, cooktop, oven, built-in grill
check: Listed to ANSI Z21.1 or Z21.58/CSA 1.6 and installed per instructions; must be listed and labeled as household-type for domestic use. Appliances listed only for commercial use are prohibited in dwellings (G2447.2, G2447.3).
needs: Appliance is listed for household (domestic) use

title: Range on combustible floor
applies_to: Gas range on a combustible floor
check: Set on its own base or legs with clearances not less than shown on the label.

title: Clearance above gas cooktop
applies_to: Gas range or cooktop and the combustible material or metal cabinet above it
check: At least 30 in. vertically from the cooking top to combustible material and metal cabinets. May be 24 in. where: (1) the underside is protected with at least 1/4 in. insulating millboard covered with sheet metal at least 0.0122 in. thick; or (2) a metal ventilating hood at least 0.0122 in. thick is installed with at least 1/4 in. clearance to the material above, at least as wide as the appliance and centered over it; or (3) a listed cooking appliance or microwave is installed above per its instructions.
note: Replaces B-22 for gas. Unlike M1901.1, metal cabinets count and 24 in. is the floor for options 1 and 2. Hood width and centering are also checkable.

title: Gas water heaters
applies_to: Gas water heater
check: Listed (ANSI Z21.10.1/CSA 4.1 or Z21.10.3/CSA 4.3) and installed per instructions; sizing, relief valves, drain pans and scald protection per the plumbing provisions (G2448.1.1); combination space-heating units listed for that use (G2448.2).
note: Location limits: G2406.2 and M2005.2. Garage elevation: G2408.2.

title: Gas lights
applies_to: Gas illuminating appliance (gas lantern)
check: Listed to ANSI Z21.42; mounted to structure, not hung from the gas piping; post mounts rigid; regulator where needed (G2450.2 to G2450.4).

title: Infrared radiant heaters
applies_to: Gas infrared (patio or garage) heater
check: Listed to ANSI Z83.19 or Z83.20; fixed in position independent of gas and electric lines; noncombustible hangers.

title: Outdoor decorative gas appliances
applies_to: Permanent outdoor fire pit or fire feature
check: Listed to ANSI Z21.97 and installed per manufacturer instructions. Pool and spa heaters: listed to ANSI Z21.56/CSA 4.7 (G2441.1).

title: Examine existing drains
applies_to: Remodel that replaces the entire sanitary drainage system
check: When the whole drainage system is replaced, internally examine (camera) existing under-slab building drains and the building sewer that will stay in service: correct slope, not broken, not obstructed, sized for the new load.

title: Alterations to existing plumbing
applies_to: Any new, moved or replaced plumbing fixture or piping
check: New and altered plumbing must meet the code for new work; the untouched existing system need not be upgraded, but the work must not leave it unsafe, insanitary or overloaded. Minor repairs and like-for-like replacements may match the existing arrangement if not hazardous and approved.
note: Governs how far plumbing upgrades reach in a remodel. Show added fixture load on the permit set where fixtures are added.
