title: Plumbing inspections
applies_to: Any plumbing work
check: New plumbing and the parts of the existing system affected by the work must be inspected by the building official.

title: No concealment before inspection
applies_to: Walls, floors or ceilings that will cover new piping
check: Do not cover, conceal or use new plumbing until it is tested, inspected and approved.

title: DWV rough-in test
applies_to: New or altered drain, waste or vent piping
check: Test rough DWV: water to at least 5 ft above the highest fitting (or to the highest point) held 15 min; or air at 5 psi held 15 min (not for plastic pipe); or vacuum of -5 psi held 15 min for plastic pipe. No leaks.

title: DWV final test
applies_to: New plumbing fixtures set
check: Fill and drain each fixture; traps and fixture connections must be watertight by visual check.
edition_difference: 9th Edition renames this the drainage and vent final test and drops the optional smoke and peppermint gas-tightness tests; the fill-and-drain visual test remains.

title: Shower liner flood test
applies_to: Site-built (tile) shower with a pan liner or membrane
check: Plug the drain and flood the completed liner to at least 2 in. deep measured at the threshold (build a temporary 2 in. dam for curbless showers); hold 15 minutes with no leakage.
note: 9th Edition P2709.3 adds an explicit cross-reference requiring this test.

title: Water piping pressure test
applies_to: New or altered water supply piping
check: Test new water piping at not less than working pressure with potable water, or 50 psi air for non-plastic pipe, held 15 minutes. Air/gas testing of PEX only where every pipe and fitting manufacturer's instructions allow it.

title: Backflow assembly testing
applies_to: Testable backflow assembly installed or relocated (RPZ, double check, PVB)
check: Test the assembly at installation and right after any repair or relocation.

title: Fixtures connect to drainage
applies_to: Any fixture or appliance that discharges waste
check: Every fixture, drain and appliance that discharges waste must connect to the sanitary drainage system (directly, or indirectly where the code calls for it). Flag a drawn fixture with no drain connection point.
note: Exception for approved gray-water systems (P2910, P2911).

title: Fixtures in flood hazard areas
applies_to: New or relocated fixtures, drains and plumbing appliances in a flood zone project
check: In a flood hazard area, locate or install fixtures, drains and appliances per R322.1.6 (at or above the required elevation, or designed to stay watertight and functional).
needs: Project flood zone and required elevation; floor elevation of the room
note: Also P2705.1 item 7 and P2602.2 (keep floodwater out of water and sewer piping).

title: Restore structure after plumbing work
applies_to: Cutting floors, walls or slabs for piping
check: Any finished floor, wall, ceiling or tile cut for plumbing must be left structurally safe and restored to code.

title: Notching and boring framing
applies_to: Pipes run through new or existing studs, joists, plates, rafters or trusses
check: Do not cut, notch or bore wood structural members beyond the limits the building portion of the code allows; never cut or notch flanges or lips of load-bearing cold-formed steel members; never cut trusses or engineered lumber without the manufacturer's or engineer's detail.
note: FLORIDA: this section points to R502, R602.3 and R802.7, but Florida has RESERVED R602.6 (the IRC stud notching and boring limits) and most of R602; Florida wood framing limits come from the AWC WFCM/NDS or FBC-Building 2308.9.10 and 2308.9.11 (typical limits: bearing stud notch 25 percent, bored hole 40 percent of stud depth; nonbearing notch 40 percent, hole 60 percent). Verify the typical figures against the building-code rule set before showing them as code text.

title: Nail (shield) plates
applies_to: Pipes other than cast iron or galvanized steel passing through studs, joists or plates in concealed spaces
check: Where the pipe is less than 1-1/4 in. from the nearest edge of the framing member, cover it with a steel shield plate at least 0.0575 in. thick (16 gage) that covers the pipe at the notch or hole and extends at least 2 in. above sole plates and below top plates.
edition_difference: 9th Edition moves the 16 gage thickness into new P2603.2.1.1; requirement unchanged.

title: Pipe corrosion protection
applies_to: Copper or other metallic pipe in contact with steel studs, concrete or masonry
check: Do not place metallic pipe (other than cast iron, ductile iron or galvanized steel) in direct contact with steel framing, concrete or masonry; sleeve or wrap it with plastic at least 0.010 in. thick that lets the pipe move. CPVC needs no sleeve in concrete.

title: Slab penetration sleeves
applies_to: New pipe penetrations through a slab on grade
check: Sleeves around pipes through a slab on grade must not contain cellulose; where soil is termite-treated the sleeve wall is at most 0.010 in. thick and clamped tight to the pipe in the slab with a noncorrosive clamp, with no termiticide inside the sleeve.
note: Florida-specific termite provision.

title: Pipe support spacing
applies_to: New water, drain or vent piping
check: Support piping at no more than the Table P2605.1 spacing, e.g. horizontal: PVC and ABS 4 ft; CPVC 1 in. and smaller 3 ft; PEX 1 in. and smaller 32 in.; copper tube 1-1/4 in. and smaller 6 ft; cast iron 5 ft. Vertical: 10 ft for most materials, with a mid-story guide for sizes 2 in. and smaller. Hangers must not cause galvanic action.

title: Seal pipe penetrations
applies_to: Pipes passing through the building envelope or a rated wall or ceiling
check: Seal the annular space around pipes through exterior walls, floors and ceilings with compatible caulk, foam or gaskets; penetrations of fire-resistance-rated assemblies (garage separation, townhouse and two-family walls) need firestopping per the building provisions (R302.4).

title: Exterior wall pipe penetrations
applies_to: New hose bibb, drain or relief line through an exterior wall
check: Seal each pipe through an exterior wall on the outside with waterproof sealant or elastomeric flashing. Roof penetrations (P2607.1) need flashing.

title: Listed plumbing products
applies_to: All fixtures, valves, pipe and fittings specified
check: Products must carry manufacturer identification and third-party listing to the referenced standard; plastic pipe to NSF 14; anything carrying drinking water to NSF 61.
note: Includes P2609.1, P2609.3, P2609.5. Product listing detail is otherwise outside the drawing check.

title: Fixture strainers
applies_to: Lavatories, sinks, tubs, showers, laundry tubs
check: Every fixture other than a water closet needs an approved strainer (not required for standpipes or clear-water hub drains).

title: Tailpiece size
applies_to: Sinks, dishwashers, laundry tubs, bathtubs, lavatories, bidets
check: Tailpieces at least 1-1/2 in. for sinks, dishwashers, laundry tubs and bathtubs; at least 1-1/4 in. for lavatories and bidets.

title: Access to slip joints
applies_to: Tub, shower, sink or lavatory with slip-joint (tubular) trap connections that will be enclosed
check: Slip joints are allowed only on tubular waste between the fixture and the drainage piping connection and must stay accessible through an opening at least 12 in. in its smallest dimension. Flag a tub or enclosed fixture with a slip-joint trap and no access panel.
edition_difference: 9th Edition words the allowed zone as from the fixture waste outlet (not trap outlet) to the drainage connection; 12 in. access unchanged.
needs: Trap connection type (slip joint or solvent-welded/solid) and whether an access panel is drawn

title: Fixture securing and sealing
applies_to: All new fixtures
check: Secure floor-mounted fixtures to the drain and floor with corrosion-resistant fasteners; support wall-hung fixtures so no strain goes to the piping; seal fixtures watertight where they meet walls and floors; fixtures must be usable.

title: Toilet and bidet side clearance
applies_to: Water closet or bidet
check: Centerline at least 15 in. from any side wall, partition, vanity or tub, and at least 30 in. center to center from an adjacent fixture.
note: Replaces B-07 (side clearance part). Same numbers as R307.1 figure.

title: Lavatory side clearance
applies_to: Lavatory
check: Lavatory centerline at least 15 in. from a side wall or partition and 30 in. center to center between adjacent fixtures.
note: Replaces B-08. The text applies the same 15 in. and 30 in. to lavatories; two bowls in one vanity top are commonly accepted closer by local officials, so show as a warning for double-bowl vanities.

title: Front clearance
applies_to: Water closet, bidet or lavatory
check: At least 21 in. clear in front of the fixture to any wall, fixture or door (check the door swing arc too).
note: Replaces B-07/B-08 (front clearance part).

title: Fixtures clear of doors and windows
applies_to: Any fixture, piping or equipment near a door or operable window
check: Fixtures, piping and equipment must not block the operation of doors or windows: flag a door swing or window sash that collides with a fixture.

title: Waste receptor location
applies_to: Standpipe, hub drain, floor sink or other waste receptor
check: Receptors must be readily accessible and not in concealed spaces, plenums, attics, crawl spaces or above-ceiling/below-floor spaces; a removable strainer is required except on standpipes and clear-water hub drains.

title: Hub drain height
applies_to: Hub drain
check: Hub or pipe extends at least 1 in. above a water-impervious floor.

title: Washer standpipe height
applies_to: Clothes washer standpipe
check: Standpipe extends at least 18 in. and at most 42 in. above the trap weir.
needs: Standpipe top height and trap weir height
note: Trap must be 2 in. (Table P3201.7).

title: Laundry tray into standpipe
applies_to: Laundry tub draining into the washer standpipe
check: Standpipe extends at least 30 in. above its trap weir and above the laundry tray flood rim; tray outlet no more than 30 in. horizontally from the standpipe trap.
needs: Standpipe height; distance from tray outlet to standpipe trap

title: Prohibited waste receptors
applies_to: Indirect waste (condensate, T&P, RO, washer) discharging into a fixture
check: Do not discharge indirect waste into a fixture used for washing or bathing. Exceptions: dishwasher into the kitchen sink trap/tailpiece; clothes washer into a laundry tray.

title: Directional fitting at disposer/dishwasher
applies_to: Kitchen sink with disposer or dishwasher
check: Use a directional (wye-type) branch fitting on the sink tailpiece that receives disposer or dishwasher discharge.

title: Shower minimum size
applies_to: Shower compartment (prefab or tile)
check: Finished interior at least 900 sq in. and at least 30 in. in the least dimension, measured at the top of the threshold and held clear up to at least 70 in. above the drain (valves, heads, soap dishes and grab bars may project). Alternative: least dimension 25 in. if the area is at least 1,300 sq in.
note: Replaces B-09 (size). Fold-down seats allowed if 900 sq in. remains with the seat up. Built-in benches reduce the clear area: measure the area net of a fixed bench.

title: Shower door swing
applies_to: Shower with a hinged door
check: Hinged shower doors must open outward (in-and-out swing is acceptable; inward-only is not).
note: Check the 21 in. front clearance and nearby fixtures against the open door.

title: Shower and tub wall backing
applies_to: Walls of a shower or of a tub with a shower head
check: Wall area in the shower and above the tub must be built per R702.4 (cement, fiber-cement or glass-mat backer behind tile; no paper-faced or water-resistant gypsum board as tile backer in wet areas) with watertight joints to each other and to the tub, receptor or shower floor.
needs: Wall backer material at shower/tub walls
note: The backer-material detail comes from R702.4 (building rule set) and was not re-read in this pass: verify there.

title: Shower access opening
applies_to: Shower entry (door, glass opening or walk-in)
check: Clear finished opening at least 22 in. wide.
note: Replaces B-09 (access).

title: Shower drain size
applies_to: Shower drain
check: Drain outlet at least 1-1/2 in.; trap size by total shower flow per Table P3201.7 (2 in. over 5.7 gpm).
needs: Shower drain size; total gpm of shower heads and body sprays

title: Shower riser secured
applies_to: Shower valve and head rough-in
check: Fasten the riser from valve to shower head to the structure with supports made for the pipe (e.g. drop-ear elbow screwed to blocking).

title: Shower valve type
applies_to: Every shower and tub/shower valve, new or replaced
check: Valve must be pressure-balanced, thermostatic or combination (ASSE 1016/ASME A112.1016/CSA B125.16 or ASME A112.18.1/CSA B125.1), installed at the point of use and rated for the flow of the installed shower head.
needs: Shower valve type/listing and shower head gpm
note: An in-line thermostatic valve, an ASSE 1066 in-line balancer (P2722.4) or an ASSE 1062 flow-reduction device (P2724.2) cannot substitute.

title: Shower 120 F limit
applies_to: Every shower and tub/shower valve
check: Set the valve's high-limit stop in the field so delivered water does not exceed 120 F.

title: Hand shower backflow
applies_to: Hand-held shower
check: Hand showers must comply with ASME A112.18.1/CSA B125.1 and have backflow protection (integral or an ASME A112.18.3 device).

title: Shower curb height
applies_to: Shower receptor with a curb
check: Top of curb at least 1 in. below the sides and back of the receptor; curb at least 2 in. and at most 9 in. above the top of the drain.
note: Curbless showers: see liner exceptions under P2709.2 and the flood test in P2503.6.

title: Shower floor slope
applies_to: Shower floor
check: Finished floor slopes uniformly to the drain at not less than 1/4 in. per ft and not more than 1/2 in. per ft; drain flanged for a watertight joint.
note: Compute from drawn floor heights at the perimeter and drain. Florida text states 1/4 to 1/2 unit in 12 (2 to 4 percent).

title: Shower pan liner required
applies_to: Site-built shower receptor
check: Line the floor and adjoining wall framing with sheet lead, sheet copper, PVC (ASTM D4551) or CPE (ASTM D4068) liner, hot mopping, or an ANSI A118.10 bonded sheet membrane (liquid/trowel-applied A118.10 products per P2709.2.4).
needs: Shower waterproofing/liner type
note: Exceptions: bonded sheet membrane need not be recessed; first-floor showers whose drain is depressed at least 2 in. below the surrounding floor and poured integrally with the slab need no liner.

title: Liner turn-up height
applies_to: Site-built shower receptor liner
check: Liner extends at least 2 in. beyond or around the rough jambs and at least 2 in. above the finished threshold.
note: Hot-mop liners: at least three layers of Type 15 felt, corners reinforced with webbing lapped 4 in. (P2709.2.3).

title: Pre-sloped liner
applies_to: Site-built shower receptor liner
check: Slope the liner itself 1/4 in. per ft to the drain weep holes on a smooth solid subbase (pre-slope), recess and fasten it to backing, and do not nail or puncture it lower than 1 in. above the finished threshold.
edition_difference: 9th Edition adds that the assembly must be tested per P2503.6 (flood test).

title: Shower clamping drain
applies_to: Site-built shower receptor
check: Use a flanged drain with clamping ring and weep holes (ASME A112.18.2/CSA B125.2), flange flush with the subbase and sealed to the liner.

title: Shower wall finish
applies_to: Shower walls and walls above a tub with a wall shower head
check: Nonabsorbent wall surface per R307.2 to at least 6 ft above the floor.
note: Replaces B-10. The 6 ft height is from R307.2 (building rule set), not re-read in this pass; this section only points to it.

title: Lavatory waste outlet
applies_to: Lavatory
check: Waste outlet at least 1-1/4 in. with a strainer, pop-up, crossbar or similar.

title: Water closet flush volume
applies_to: Water closet
check: Maximum 1.6 gallons per flush (Table P2903.2); listed to ASME A112.19.2/CSA B45.1; dual-flush to ASME A112.19.14.
needs: Toilet gallons per flush

title: Flush tank access
applies_to: Water closet, including concealed in-wall tanks
check: Flush tank parts must be accessible for repair and replacement (in-wall tanks need the actuator-plate access).

title: Water closet seat
applies_to: Water closet
check: Seat of smooth nonabsorbent material sized for the bowl.

title: Wall-hung toilet carrier
applies_to: Wall-hung water closet
check: Install on a carrier complying with ASME A112.6.2; show wall thickness adequate for the carrier.
needs: Toilet mounting type (floor or wall-hung) and wall depth

title: Bathtub waste and overflow
applies_to: Bathtub
check: Waste outlet at least 1-1/2 in. with a watertight stopper; overflow, where provided, at least 1-1/2 in.

title: Tub enclosure doors
applies_to: Bathtub with pressure-sealed door (walk-in tub)
check: Doors within a bathtub enclosure comply with ASME A112.19.15.
note: Glass tub/shower enclosures need safety glazing under R308 (building rule set).

title: Tub filler 120 F limit
applies_to: Bathtub or whirlpool tub with a tub-only filler valve
check: Provide an ASSE 1070 temperature-limiting device (or a valve with integral limiter) set to 120 F maximum; combination tub/shower valves comply through P2708.4. Provide access to the device unless it is nonadjustable and integral with a fitting that can itself be reached.
needs: Tub filler has ASSE 1070 limiter or is a P2708.4 tub/shower valve

title: Sink waste outlet
applies_to: Kitchen or bar sink
check: Waste outlet at least 1-1/2 in. with strainer or crossbar.

title: Laundry tub outlet
applies_to: Laundry tub
check: Each compartment has a waste outlet at least 1-1/2 in. with strainer or crossbar.

title: Disposer drain
applies_to: Food-waste disposer
check: Connect to a drain at least 1-1/2 in.

title: Disposer needs a faucet
applies_to: Sink with a food-waste disposer
check: The sink with a disposer must have a faucet (water supply).

title: Dishwasher backflow
applies_to: Dishwasher
check: Water supply protected by the machine's integral air gap (ASME A112.1.2 or A112.1.3) or a backflow preventer per P2902.

title: Dishwasher drain high loop
applies_to: Dishwasher
check: Discharge hose rises to the underside of the counter and is fastened there (high loop) before connecting to the disposer inlet or a wye on the sink tailpiece; shared trap at least 1-1/2 in. A deck air-gap fitting is not required by this code.
edition_difference: 9th Edition rewrites the section as Dishwasher waste connection: connect to a wye on the kitchen sink tailpiece, to the disposer's dishwasher inlet, or through an air break to a standpipe; hose rises and is secured to the underside of the sink rim or countertop; if draining to a standpipe, secure the hose to the top of the standpipe.
note: App can check that the dishwasher is adjacent to (or has a route to) a sink.

title: Washer discharge air break
applies_to: Clothes washer
check: Washer discharges through an air break (hose into standpipe or laundry tray, not a sealed connection).

title: Floor drains
applies_to: Floor drain (laundry, water heater closet)
check: Outlet at least 2 in. with removable strainer; drain inlet accessible; not located under or blocked by a permanently installed appliance.
note: Trap seal protection where subject to evaporation: P3201.2.1.

title: Whirlpool pump access
applies_to: Whirlpool/jetted bathtub
check: Provide pump access per the manufacturer; if not specified, an opening at least 12 x 12 in.; at least 18 x 18 in. where the pump is more than 2 ft from the opening. Opening must be unobstructed (a door or panel may close it) and large enough to remove the pump.
needs: Access panel size and distance from panel to pump
note: Electrical side (GFCI, dedicated circuit, bonding) is in the NEC 680.71 to 680.74 rules.

title: Whirlpool pump location
applies_to: Whirlpool/jetted bathtub
check: Pump located above the trap crown weir; pump and circulation piping self-draining.

title: Whirlpool leak test
applies_to: Whirlpool/jetted bathtub
check: Leak-test and run the pump per the manufacturer before enclosing; install per manufacturer's instructions (P2720.4).

title: Bidet backflow
applies_to: Bidet
check: Supply fitting must be air-gap or vacuum-breaker type.

title: Bidet 110 F limit
applies_to: Bidet
check: Limit discharge temperature to 110 F with an ASSE 1070 device.
needs: Bidet has ASSE 1070 temperature limiter

title: Faucets and supply fittings
applies_to: All faucets and fixture supply valves
check: Faucets and supply valves to ASME A112.18.1/CSA B125.1; drinking-water fittings to NSF 61 Section 9; flexible connectors to ASME A112.18.6 (P2906.7).

title: Hot on the left
applies_to: Any faucet or valve with hot and cold
check: Hot water control on the left when facing the outlet (shower valves may follow their own markings).

title: Bidet seats
applies_to: Toilet with integral bidet or bidet seat
check: Personal hygiene devices integral to a water closet or seat comply with ASME A112.4.2.
note: Needs a receptacle near the toilet (see electrical rules).

title: Macerating toilets
applies_to: Macerating (upflush) toilet system
check: Install per manufacturer (ASME A112.3.4/CSA B45.9); discharge pipe at least 3/4 in.
needs: Toilet is macerating type; discharge size
note: Includes P2723.2 (3/4 in. discharge). See also P3007.5.

title: Master mixing valves
applies_to: Thermostatic mixing valve at the water heater
check: Temperature-actuated mixing valves comply with ASSE 1017 and are installed at the hot water source; they do not replace the fixture-level limits (P2708.4, P2713.3, P2721.2).

title: Hot water required
applies_to: Dwelling fixtures for bathing, washing or cooking
check: Supply hot water to fixtures and appliances used for bathing, washing or culinary purposes: flag a tub, shower, lavatory or kitchen sink with no hot supply point.
edition_difference: 9th Edition marks P2801.1 Reserved (the requirement is not stated in this section).

title: Water heater drain valve
applies_to: Tank water heater or storage tank
check: Drain valve at the bottom of the tank, inlet at least 3/4 in., with male hose thread outlet.

title: Water heater access
applies_to: Water heater (new, relocated or enclosed by new walls/cabinets)
check: Locate and connect so the heater can be observed, maintained, serviced and replaced; appliance access per M1305 (30 in. deep x 30 in. wide level service space in front of the control side; attic or crawl installations need a 22 x 30 in. opening and a passage as M1305.1.2 and M1305.1.3 require).
needs: Clear service space in front of the water heater; door or opening width to its closet
note: M1305 dimensions belong to the mechanical rule set; quoted here from general knowledge of M1305.1, not re-read in this pass.

title: Water heater prohibited locations
applies_to: Fuel-fired water heater; any water heater in a bedroom, bathroom or closet
check: Fuel-fired water heaters may not be in a storage closet. A fuel-fired heater in a bedroom or bathroom must be in a sealed enclosure that takes no combustion air from the living space, unless it is direct-vent.
note: Reached through P2801.5 (locations per Chapter 20). Check room type against water heater fuel type. Gas units also G2406.2.

title: Water heater pan
applies_to: Tank water heater or storage tank where a leak would cause damage (interior closet, attic, upper floor, above finished space)
check: Install in a pan of galvanized steel or aluminum at least 0.0236 in. thick, plastic at least 0.036 in. thick, or other approved material. Plastic pans under gas heaters need flame spread 25 or less and smoke-developed 450 or less.
needs: Water heater location type and whether a pan is shown

title: Pan size and drain
applies_to: Water heater pan
check: Pan at least 1-1/2 in. deep, sized to catch drips; drained by an indirect waste pipe at least 3/4 in. of water-distribution pipe material (Table P2906.5).
note: Replacement heater where no pan drain existed before: a pan drain is not required.

title: Pan drain termination
applies_to: Water heater pan drain
check: Run full size to a suitable indirect waste receptor, or to the exterior ending 6 to 24 in. above the adjacent ground.

title: Water heater in garage
applies_to: Water heater with an ignition source located in a garage
check: Elevate so the ignition source is at least 18 in. above the garage floor, unless the unit is listed flammable-vapor-ignition-resistant (FVIR).
needs: Water heater fuel/type, FVIR listing, and platform height
note: Vehicle impact protection is under M1307.3.1 (mechanical rule set).

title: Water heater shutoff
applies_to: Water heater
check: Readily accessible full-open valve on the cold supply at or near each water heater.

title: T&P relief valve required
applies_to: Water heater or hot water storage tank
check: Protect with a combination temperature-and-pressure relief valve (or separate valves) listed to ANSI Z21.22 and rated for the heater input.
note: Includes P2804.2.

title: Relief valve settings
applies_to: Water heater relief valve
check: Pressure relief set at least 25 psi above system pressure, at most 150 psi and not above the tank's rated working pressure; temperature relief opens at 210 F or less with its sensor in the top 6 in. of the tank (P2804.4).

title: No valves on relief line
applies_to: Water heater relief valve
check: No check or shutoff valve between the relief valve and the tank or heater, or anywhere in the discharge pipe.

title: T&P discharge pipe
applies_to: Water heater relief valve discharge
check: Discharge pipe: not directly connected to the drainage system; discharges through an air gap in the same room as the heater; full size of the valve outlet to the air gap; serves one relief device only; ends at the floor, the heater pan, a waste receptor or outdoors; termination readily observable and safe; not trapped; drains by gravity; ends no more than 6 in. and no less than two pipe diameters above the floor or receptor flood rim; no threads on the end; no valves or tees; approved material (P2906.5 or ASME A112.4.1); one size larger if insert (PEX) fittings are used, with the end fastened.
note: Fourteen listed conditions; show as a checklist whenever a water heater is drawn.

title: Vacuum relief valve
applies_to: Bottom-fed tank water heater
check: Bottom-fed tank heaters and connected bottom-fed tanks need a vacuum relief valve (ANSI Z21.22).

title: Solar water heating tempering
applies_to: Solar thermal water heating system
check: ASSE 1017 mixing valve limiting delivered water to 140 F with a temperature indicator; isolation valve on the cold feed (P2802.2).

title: Water heater lead content
applies_to: Water heater
check: Water heater complies with NSF 372 (0.25 percent weighted average lead or less).
edition_difference: New section in the 9th Edition; not in the 8th Edition.
note: 9th Edition only. 9th Edition only; no 8th Edition section (number is in section_other).

title: No cross-connections
applies_to: All water supply connections
check: No connection that could contaminate potable water; cross-connection between a private well and public water is prohibited.

title: Faucet air gap
applies_to: Faucets and spouts at lavatories, sinks, tubs
check: Spout outlet above the fixture flood rim by at least twice the outlet diameter and not less than: lavatory 1 in.; sink or laundry tray 1-1/2 in.; over-rim tub filler 2 in. (1-1/2, 2-1/2 and 3 in. respectively when close to a wall).
note: Table P2902.3.1. Applies to roman tub fillers and vessel sink faucets.

title: Toilet fill valve
applies_to: Water closet flush tank
check: Antisiphon fill valve (ASSE 1002 or CSA B125.3) with its critical level at least 1 in. above the top of the overflow pipe.

title: Pull-out faucet vacuum breaker
applies_to: Faucets with pull-out spray or deck-mounted vacuum breaker
check: Integral or deck-mounted vacuum breaker critical level at least 1 in. above the flood rim; install per listing.

title: Hose bibb backflow
applies_to: Hose bibb, sillcock, wall hydrant, laundry sink threaded faucet
check: Every hose-threaded outlet needs a vacuum breaker (atmospheric or pressure type, or a permanently attached hose-connection vacuum breaker).
note: Exceptions: water heater drain valves; clothes washer supply valves where the machine has backflow protection.

title: Irrigation backflow
applies_to: Lawn irrigation connected to potable water
check: Protect with an atmospheric vacuum breaker, pressure vacuum breaker or reduced-pressure assembly; reduced-pressure assembly where chemicals are injected.
note: Only relevant when the remodel touches the irrigation tie-in.

title: Backflow preventer access
applies_to: Any backflow preventer
check: Provide access per manufacturer; relief port discharges through an air gap to an approved receptor or outdoors (P2902.6.3).

title: Fixture flow and pressure
applies_to: Water supply to fixtures
check: Design supply for Table P2903.1 minimums at the fixture: 20 psi at tub, shower, bidet and water closet valves; 8 psi at lavatory, sink, dishwasher, laundry tray and hose bibb.

title: Lavatory faucet flow
applies_to: Lavatory faucet
check: Maximum 2.2 gpm at 60 psi.
needs: Lavatory faucet gpm
note: Florida Table P2903.2 keeps 2.2 gpm in both editions. FBC-Energy and local water-conservation ordinances (e.g. Miami-Dade, Broward WaterSense requirements) can be stricter: verify locally.

title: Shower head flow
applies_to: Shower head or hand shower
check: Maximum 2.5 gpm at 80 psi; a hand-held spray counts as a shower head.
needs: Shower head gpm
note: Local ordinances may require 2.0 gpm WaterSense heads (Miami-Dade, Broward): verify locally.

title: Sink faucet flow
applies_to: Kitchen or bar sink faucet
check: Maximum 2.2 gpm at 60 psi.
needs: Sink faucet gpm

title: Water closet consumption
applies_to: Water closet
check: Maximum 1.6 gallons per flushing cycle.
needs: Toilet gallons per flush
note: Local ordinances may require 1.28 gpf: verify locally.

title: Maximum water pressure
applies_to: Dwelling water service
check: Static pressure not over 80 psi; above that install a pressure-reducing valve (ASSE 1003 or CSA B356) at the service entrance.
needs: Measured static water pressure (psi)

title: Thermal expansion control
applies_to: Storage water heater on a system with a PRV, check valve or backflow preventer
check: Where a pressure-reducing valve, check valve or backflow device makes the system closed, install an expansion tank or other pressure-control device.
needs: System has PRV/check valve/backflow preventer (closed system)
note: P2903.4.1 and P2903.4.2. Most metered public supplies in South Florida have a check or dual-check at the meter.

title: Water hammer arrestors
applies_to: Quick-closing valves: clothes washer, dishwasher, ice maker
check: Install ASSE 1010 water hammer arrestors where quick-closing valves are used, per manufacturer.

title: Water pipe sizing
applies_to: Added fixtures on existing water piping
check: Size mains, branches and risers from fixture-unit demand (Table P2903.6), available pressure and developed length (Appendix P or engineering method); water service at least 3/4 in.
note: Pipe sizes are not in the model; show the added water supply fixture units as a note (e.g. full bath group 3.6, half bath 2.6, kitchen group 2.5, laundry group 2.5, lavatory 0.7, shower 1.4, tub 1.4, water closet 2.2, hose bibb 2.5).

title: Manifold (home-run) line size
applies_to: PEX manifold distribution system
check: Individual lines at least 3/8 in. where the run is 60 ft or less and meter pressure is at least 40 psi; larger where the fixture maker requires. Manifold valves labeled with the fixture served (P2903.8.4). No gridded hot water systems (P2903.8).

title: Main shutoff valve
applies_to: Dwelling water service
check: Accessible full-open main shutoff near where the service enters, with a means of drainage.

title: Fixture shutoff valves
applies_to: Every plumbing fixture and plumbing appliance except tubs and showers
check: Shutoff (stop) valve on each fixture supply pipe: toilets, lavatories, sinks, bidets, dishwashers, ice makers, clothes washers, water heaters. Valves must be accessible.
note: Check that each supply utility point except tub and shower has a stop valve; flag valves buried behind fixed cabinetry or tile without access.

title: No below-grade outlets
applies_to: Potable water outlets and stop-and-waste valves
check: Do not install potable outlets or stop-and-waste valves underground or below grade.

title: Metal water service used for grounding
applies_to: Replacing a metallic water service that serves as the electrical grounding electrode
check: Do not replace metallic water service pipe used for electrical grounding with nonmetallic pipe until another approved grounding means is installed.
edition_difference: New section in the 9th Edition; not in the 8th Edition (NEC 250.50 and 250.53 still govern under either edition).
note: 9th Edition only. 9th Edition only; no 8th Edition section (number is in section_other).

title: Hot water run length
applies_to: Hot water piping to a new or relocated fixture
check: Developed length from the hot water source (heater or recirculation loop) to each hot water fixture not over 100 ft.
needs: Hot water pipe run length to the fixture
note: Florida text is 100 ft (the model IRC uses different language). Recirculation and heat trace controls per FBC-Energy R403.5.1 and R403.5.2 (P2905.1, P2905.2).

title: Lead-free drinking water parts
applies_to: Pipe, fittings, valves and faucets for drinking or cooking water
check: Weighted average lead content 0.25 percent or less (NSF 372); other water supply pipe and fittings 8 percent or less; solder and flux 0.2 percent or less (P2906.15).

title: Water distribution pipe materials
applies_to: New water piping inside the dwelling
check: Use listed NSF 61 materials from Table P2906.5 (copper K/L/M, CPVC, PEX, PEX-AL-PEX, PE-RT, PP, stainless, galvanized steel) rated at least 100 psi at 180 F. PVC and PE are service-only materials, not allowed for distribution inside the dwelling.
needs: Water pipe material

title: No saddle taps
applies_to: Ice maker, humidifier or filter connections
check: Saddle tap fittings and saddle valves are prohibited; use a tee and stop valve.

title: Flexible connector access
applies_to: Braided supply connectors at fixtures and appliances
check: Flexible connectors under continuous pressure comply with ASME A112.18.6/CSA B125.6 and must be accessible (not buried in walls).

title: Solvent cement joints
applies_to: CPVC or PVC water piping
check: CPVC: primer plus orange cement, or one-step yellow/red cement where the manufacturer allows (ASTM F493). PVC: purple primer (ASTM F656) and ASTM D2564 cement.
edition_difference: 9th Edition adds green as a permitted one-step CPVC cement color and changes joint-making references to ASTM D2855 and ASTM F3328.

title: Joints between different materials
applies_to: Tying new pipe to existing pipe of another material
check: Use an approved adapter or transition fitting; copper to galvanized steel needs a copper-alloy or dielectric fitting; push-fit fittings (ASSE 1061) only on copper-tube-size CPVC, PEX, PE-RT and copper (P2906.21).

title: Reverse osmosis drain
applies_to: Under-sink RO or water treatment unit
check: RO units to NSF 58; waste discharges to the drain through an air gap or NSF 58 air gap device.

title: Fire sprinkler piping
applies_to: Dwelling with an existing residential sprinkler system
check: If the dwelling is sprinklered, moved walls, ceilings and soffits require sprinkler coverage to be re-laid out per NFPA 13D or P2904.
needs: Dwelling has fire sprinklers (yes/no)
note: Florida does not mandate sprinklers in one- and two-family dwellings; applies only where a system exists. P2904 details not walked.

title: DWV pipe materials
applies_to: New drain, waste and vent piping
check: Use listed materials from Tables P3002.1(1) and (2) (PVC or ABS DWV, cast iron, copper DWV). No galvanized steel underground or within 6 in. of the ground. Allow for thermal movement of plastic pipe.

title: Drainage fittings
applies_to: New drain piping
check: Use drainage-pattern fittings with a smooth full-bore interior; no ledges or reductions that obstruct flow.

title: PVC DWV joints
applies_to: PVC drain and vent joints
check: Purple (or other approved ASTM F656) primer and ASTM D2564 cement. Primer may be omitted only with third-party-certified cement on non-pressure DWV 4 in. and smaller.
edition_difference: 9th Edition adds a third condition for primerless joints: the joint must be made per ASTM F3328.
note: Other P3003 joint sections (ABS, cast iron, copper, transitions with listed couplings) were not itemised; one reminder covers them: join dissimilar DWV pipe with listed transition couplings (P3003.13).

title: Drainage fixture units
applies_to: Fixtures added to an existing drain
check: Count added load in d.f.u.: lavatory 1, bidet 1, bar sink 1, bathtub 2, shower 2, kitchen sink 2, dishwasher 2, laundry tub 2, washer standpipe 2, water closet (1.6 gpf) 3; full bath group 5, half bath 4, kitchen group 2, laundry group 3.
note: App can total d.f.u. for new fixtures and print it on the plumbing sheet; pipe sizes themselves are not modeled.

title: Drainage fitting patterns
applies_to: Changes of direction in new drain piping
check: Use fittings per Table P3005.1: sanitary tee only for horizontal-to-vertical; wye, combo or long sweep for vertical-to-horizontal and horizontal-to-horizontal; quarter bend and short sweep limited to 2 in. and smaller fixture drains in those positions (short sweep 3 in. and larger allowed vertical-to-horizontal).

title: Back-to-back fixtures
applies_to: Back-to-back fixtures on a common wall, especially two toilets
check: Double sanitary tees may not serve back-to-back water closets or pumped discharges (washer, dishwasher) unless the toilet outlet is at least 18 in. of developed length from the fitting; use a double fixture fitting or double wye.
note: Trigger when two toilets are drawn back to back on one wall.

title: Closet bend and flange
applies_to: Water closet
check: 3 in. closet bend acceptable with a 4 x 3 flange; flange secured to the floor.

title: Future fixture rough-ins
applies_to: Capped rough-in for a future fixture
check: Include future fixture d.f.u. in sizing and end the rough-in with an accessible permanent cap or plug; rough in a vent at least half the drain diameter (P3104.6).

title: No reduction in flow direction
applies_to: New drain piping
check: Drain size never reduces in the direction of flow (4 x 3 closet flange and offset flanges excepted).

title: Cleanout spacing
applies_to: Horizontal drains
check: Cleanouts at intervals of 100 ft or less on horizontal drains and building drains.

title: Building drain cleanout
applies_to: Junction of building drain and building sewer
check: Cleanout at the junction or within 10 ft upstream; removing a toilet does not count as this cleanout.
note: Often requested by inspectors when the drain system is substantially reworked.

title: Cleanout at direction change
applies_to: Horizontal drain with a bend over 45 degrees
check: Cleanout at each horizontal change of direction greater than 45 degrees; one cleanout may serve all such changes within 40 ft of developed length.

title: Cleanout size
applies_to: Cleanouts
check: Same size as the pipe up to 4 in. A removable P-trap with slip or ground joints can serve as the cleanout for a drain one size larger than the trap.

title: Cleanout clearance
applies_to: Cleanouts
check: At least 18 in. clear in front of cleanouts on pipes 6 in. and smaller.
needs: Cleanout locations

title: Cleanout access
applies_to: Cleanouts in remodeled walls, floors and cabinets
check: Cleanouts may not be concealed inside walls, floor/ceiling assemblies or below grade without being extended; wall cleanout openings within 1-1/2 in. of the finished wall surface; never cover a plug with tile, mortar or plaster. A removable fixture trap or toilet counts as a cleanout equivalent (P3005.2.10.1).
note: Trigger when new walls, cabinets or tile cover an existing cleanout pin.

title: No fixtures on cleanouts
applies_to: Tying a new fixture into an existing cleanout
check: Do not use a threaded cleanout opening to add a fixture or extend piping unless another equal cleanout with access is installed.

title: Drain slope
applies_to: Horizontal drain piping to new or relocated fixtures
check: At least 1/4 in. per ft for pipe 2-1/2 in. and smaller; at least 1/8 in. per ft for 3 in. and larger.
needs: Drain run length and available fall (e.g. slab depth or joist depth) for a relocated fixture
note: App can warn when a fixture is moved far from the stack: required fall = run x slope.

title: Branch and stack capacity
applies_to: Fixtures added to an existing branch or stack
check: Maximum d.f.u.: 1-1/2 in. branch 3 (stack 4); 2 in. branch 6 (stack 10); 2-1/2 in. branch 12 (stack 20); 3 in. branch 20 (stack 48); 4 in. branch 160 (stack 240). No water closets on pipes smaller than 3 in. Below-grade drains at least 1-1/2 in.
needs: Existing branch/stack size serving the new fixtures

title: Building drain capacity
applies_to: Whole-dwelling fixture count after the remodel
check: Building drain at 1/4 in. per ft: 2 in. 21 d.f.u.; 2-1/2 in. 24; 3 in. 42; 4 in. 216. At 1/8 in. per ft: 3 in. 36; 4 in. 180. No water closets on drains under 3 in.
needs: Building drain size and slope

title: Sewage ejector for below-sewer fixtures
applies_to: Fixtures that cannot drain by gravity (e.g. added bath below the sewer line)
check: Discharge to a gas-tight vented sump with an automatic pump: pit at least 18 in. diameter x 24 in. deep with gas-tight cover; check valve plus full-open valve on the discharge, accessible; pump passes 2 in. solids where it serves a water closet (grinder pump discharge at least 1-1/4 in.).

title: Backwater valve
applies_to: Fixtures with flood rims below the next upstream sewer manhole cover
check: Protect those fixtures with a backwater valve with access to its working parts (P3008.4); fixtures above that level must not drain through a normally closed valve (existing buildings excepted).

title: Pipe bursting replacement
applies_to: Replacing building drain or sewer by pipe bursting
check: 6 in. and smaller gravity pipe only, same nominal size, HDPE (ASTM F714); video survey before and after; add code-required cleanouts; pressure test.

title: Relining existing drains
applies_to: Lining (CIPP) of existing cast-iron building drains or sewers
check: 8th Edition: 4 in. and larger gravity pipe; clean and video survey before; building official reviews the video before permit; no lining over backslope, collapsed or separated pipe; post-lining video and written certification to the building official.
edition_difference: 9th Edition replaces the whole section with a single requirement: cured-in-place rehabilitation per ASTM F1216 or ASTM F1743 (the survey, permit-review and certification steps are deleted).
note: Common in South Florida cast-iron drain remodels.

title: Every trap vented
applies_to: Every new or relocated fixture
check: Each trap must be protected by a vent using one of the Chapter 31 methods (individual, common, wet, waste stack, circuit, combination, island or air admittance valve).

title: One vent to outdoors
applies_to: Dwelling drainage system
check: At least one dry vent connected to the building drain must extend to the outdoors (cannot be an island vent; AAVs do not satisfy this, P3114.7).

title: Vent through roof height
applies_to: New vent terminal through the roof
check: Terminate at least 6 in. above the roof (7 ft above a roof used as a deck); flash watertight (P3103.3).

title: Side wall vent terminal
applies_to: Vent terminating through a wall
check: At least 10 ft from a lot line and 10 ft above the highest grade within 10 ft; not under a vented soffit overhang; screened against birds and rodents.

title: Vent terminal near openings
applies_to: New vent terminal near a door, operable window or air intake
check: Not within 10 ft horizontally of an opening unless at least 3 ft above its top; never less than 4 ft directly below one.
needs: Vent terminal location relative to openings

title: Dry vent rise
applies_to: Dry vents on new fixtures
check: Vent rises vertically to at least 6 in. above the flood rim of the fixture served before running horizontal; connect dry vents above the centerline of a horizontal drain (P3104.3); slope vents to drain back (P3104.2).
note: Also P3104.5: branch vent connections at least 6 in. above the highest fixture flood rim. This is why relocated sinks under windows and in half walls need planning.

title: Trap arm maximum length
applies_to: Every new or relocated trapped fixture (not water closets)
check: Trap weir to vent: 1-1/4 in. trap 5 ft; 1-1/2 in. 6 ft; 2 in. 8 ft (all at 1/4 in. per ft); 3 in. 12 ft and 4 in. 16 ft (at 1/8 in. per ft). Water closet fixture drains are not length-limited.
needs: Distance from the fixture trap to its vent (or to the vented wall/stack) and trap size
note: App can estimate from fixture position to the nearest plumbing wall/vent pin and warn when a lavatory is over 5 ft, a tub or kitchen sink over 6 ft, or a 2 in. shower or washer over 8 ft.

title: Trap arm fall
applies_to: Trap arms
check: Total fall of the fixture drain not more than one pipe diameter; vent connection not below the trap weir (water closets excepted).

title: No crown vents
applies_to: Vent connection near a trap
check: Vent connection at least two pipe diameters from the trap weir.

title: Common vent
applies_to: Two fixtures sharing one vent (e.g. double lavatory, back-to-back lavatories)
check: One vent may serve two traps on the same floor; if drains connect at different levels the upper fixture may not be a water closet and the shared vertical drain is sized by Table P3107.3 (1-1/2 in. 1 d.f.u., 2 in. 4, 2-1/2 to 3 in. 6).

title: Horizontal wet venting
applies_to: Bathroom group fixtures (toilet, lavatory, tub/shower, bidet) on one floor
check: Up to two bathroom groups on the same floor may be wet vented; each fixture drain connects independently and horizontally to the wet-vented branch (or has its own dry vent); only bathroom-group fixtures on the wet vent, others connect downstream; the dry vent is an individual or common vent of a bathroom fixture, and only one wet-vented fixture may be upstream of the dry-vented fixture connection (P3108.2.1).
note: Kitchen sinks, laundry and washer standpipes can never be on the bathroom wet vent.

title: Wet vent size
applies_to: Wet-vented bathroom group
check: Wet vent pipe: 1-1/2 in. 1 d.f.u.; 2 in. 4; 2-1/2 in. 6; 3 in. 12; 4 in. 32. Trap arms still limited by Table P3105.1 (P3108.5).

title: Vertical wet vent
applies_to: Stacked connections of bathroom fixtures on one floor
check: Each fixture connects independently; all water closets at the same elevation with other fixtures at or above them; dry vent at the most upstream fixture.

title: Waste stack vent
applies_to: Fixtures vented by a waste stack
check: Stack vertical with no offsets between lowest and highest fixture connections; no water closets or urinals; each fixture connects separately; stack vent full size of the stack; size per Table P3109.4.

title: Circuit venting
applies_to: Up to eight fixtures on one horizontal branch
check: Circuit vent connects between the two most upstream fixtures; each fixture drain connects horizontally; vent section slope at most 1 in 12.

title: Combination waste and vent
applies_to: Floor drains, sinks, lavatories on a combination waste and vent
check: Only floor drains, sinks, lavatories and drinking fountains; only vertical pipe is the fixture connection, at most 8 ft; slope at most 1/2 in. per ft; size per Table P3111.3 (2 in. 3 d.f.u. to a branch).

title: Island sink venting
applies_to: Kitchen island or peninsula sink (with or without dishwasher and disposer)
check: Island venting is allowed only for sinks and lavatories. Vent rises above the fixture drain outlet (as high as possible under the counter) before turning down; the foot of the vent connects full size to a vertical drain or the top half of a horizontal drain; vent below the flood rim is built with drainage fittings and slope; cleanouts provided so all vent piping below the flood rim can be rodded.
note: P3112.2, P3112.3. Alternative: air admittance valve under the island (P3114). Trigger whenever a sink is drawn in an island or peninsula.

title: Vent size
applies_to: New vents
check: At least half the required drain diameter and never under 1-1/4 in.; increase one size if the vent is longer than 40 ft developed length.

title: Air admittance valve use
applies_to: Fixture vented with an AAV (island sink, relocated lavatory)
check: AAVs (ASSE 1051 individual/branch, ASSE 1050 stack type) may terminate individual, branch, circuit and stack vents; individual and branch AAVs vent only fixtures on the same floor connected to a horizontal branch. Install after the DWV test (P3114.2); rated for the vent size (P3114.6).
needs: Vent method for the fixture (conventional or AAV)
note: Not usable for sumps unless engineered (P3114.8). Some local officials restrict AAVs: confirm with the building department.

title: AAV height
applies_to: Air admittance valve
check: Individual and branch AAVs at least 4 in. above the horizontal branch or fixture drain; stack type at least 6 in. above the highest flood rim; within the maximum trap-to-vent distance; at least 6 in. above attic insulation.

title: AAV access and air
applies_to: Air admittance valve
check: Accessible and located where air can enter (open cabinet, or louvered access panel if in a wall); never sealed in a wall cavity.

title: AAV system still needs a roof vent
applies_to: Dwelling using AAVs
check: At least one stack vent or vent stack must still extend outdoors to open air.

title: Trap construction
applies_to: Fixture traps
check: Standard smooth self-cleaning traps without interior partitions (lavatory traps of corrosion-resistant material excepted); slip-joint traps need access per P2704.1.

title: Trap seal depth
applies_to: Fixture traps
check: Liquid seal at least 2 in. and at most 4 in.

title: Trap seal protection
applies_to: Floor drains and seldom-used traps
check: Protect trap seals subject to evaporation with a trap primer (ASSE 1018 or 1044) or a barrier-type device (ASSE 1072).

title: Prohibited traps
applies_to: Any trap, including existing ones exposed in the remodel
check: No bell traps, S-traps, drum traps, traps with moving parts or partitioned traps. Building (house) traps are prohibited (P3201.4).
note: Existing S-traps and drum traps are commonly found under old tubs and sinks; replace when the fixture is replaced or relocated.

title: One trap per fixture
applies_to: Every fixture
check: Each fixture separately trapped; no double trapping. Fixture outlet to trap weir at most 24 in. vertical and at most 30 in. horizontal (outlet centerline to trap inlet centerline).

title: Shared trap for like fixtures
applies_to: Double-bowl kitchen sink, double lavatory or laundry tubs on one trap
check: One trap may serve two or three like fixtures (kitchen sinks, laundry tubs, lavatories) that are adjacent in the same room with outlets not more than 30 in. apart; trap at the center fixture when there are three.
note: Check center-to-center distance of two lavatories or sink bowls intended to share one trap.

title: Trap sizes
applies_to: Every fixture trap
check: Minimum trap: lavatory 1-1/4 in.; bidet 1-1/4 in.; bathtub 1-1/2 in.; kitchen sink 1-1/2 in.; dishwasher on its own trap 1-1/2 in.; laundry tub 1-1/2 in.; clothes washer standpipe 2 in.; floor drain 2 in.; shower by total flow: 5.7 gpm or less 1-1/2 in., over 5.7 to 12.3 gpm 2 in., over 12.3 to 25.8 gpm 3 in., over 25.8 to 55.6 gpm 4 in. Trap not larger than the drain it enters.
needs: Trap/drain size at each fixture; total shower flow in gpm (heads plus body sprays)
note: App can auto-fill the minimum trap size on the plumbing schedule from fixture type and shower gpm. Converting a tub (1-1/2 in.) to a multi-head shower over 5.7 gpm requires a 2 in. trap and drain.

group: NEC: general, branch circuits, feeders, services (Art. 100-230)
title: NEC governs dwelling electrical
applies_to: Any electrical work in a one- or two-family dwelling or townhouse
check: Electrical systems, equipment and components must comply with NFPA 70 (NEC). FBC-R Chapters 35 to 43 carry no Florida text of their own; E3402 to E3407 are reserved. FBC 8th Edition references NFPA 70-2020; FBC 9th Edition references NFPA 70-2023.
edition_difference: Same wording in both editions; only the referenced NEC edition changes (2020 to 2023).
note: Read on the ICC viewer for both FLRC2023P1 and FLRC2026V1.0. NEC 2020 is the edition in force with FBC 8th Edition until Dec 31, 2026; NEC 2023 applies with FBC 9th Edition.

group: NEC: general, branch circuits, feeders, services (Art. 100-230)
title: Alterations: FBC-EB plus NEC
applies_to: Any addition or alteration to an existing electrical system
check: Alterations and additions to an existing electrical system must conform to the Florida Building Code, Existing Building and to the NEC. New work is built to the current NEC; what must be upgraded in untouched areas is set by FBC-EB.
note: FBC Building 2701.1 says the same for buildings under FBC-B: FBC-EB and NFPA 70 govern alteration, repair, relocation, replacement and addition.

group: NEC: general, branch circuits, feeders, services (Art. 100-230)
title: Florida GFCI amendment, HVAC
applies_to: Outdoor HVAC equipment outlet (condenser, heat pump) at a dwelling
check: Florida amends NEC 210.8(F): outdoor outlets at dwellings on single-phase circuits of 150 V to ground or less and 50 A or less need GFCI protection, EXCEPT lighting outlets (other than crawl-space lighting) and EXCEPT listed (8th Ed.: listed and labeled) HVAC equipment. Do not flag a missing GFCI on a listed outdoor condenser or heat pump.
edition_difference: 8th Ed. amends NFPA 70-20 210.8(F) and adds Exception No. 2 for listed and labeled HVAC equipment. 9th Ed. amends NFPA 70-23 210.8(F): keeps the garage (floor at or below grade), accessory building and boathouse wording and the replaced-equipment sentence, and gives a permanent HVAC exception (the NEC 2023 exception expires Sept 1, 2026; the Florida one has no expiry date).
needs: Outdoor equipment is listed HVAC equipment (yes/no)
note: This is the only Florida-specific amendment to NEC Chapters 1-2 found in FBC-R Part VIII. 9th Ed. text read at https://codes.iccsafe.org/content/FLRC2026V1.0/chapter-34-general-requirements

group: NEC: general, branch circuits, feeders, services (Art. 100-230)
title: FBC-B Chapter 27 scope
applies_to: Electrical work in buildings under FBC Building (not one- and two-family)
check: FBC Building Chapter 27 adopts NFPA 70 for design and installation and sends alterations to FBC-EB plus NFPA 70. Section 2702 covers emergency and standby power for commercial and high-rise occupancies only; it adds nothing for a house remodel. No Sections 2703 or 2704 appear in the 8th Edition chapter.
edition_difference: 9th Edition Chapter 27 not opened; the Commission's change analysis lists no Chapter 27 change that I could read.
note: UpCodes labels the Florida electrical code as NFPA 70-2020 adopted without amendments; the HVAC GFCI amendment lives in FBC-R E3408.

group: NEC: general, branch circuits, feeders, services (Art. 100-230)
title: Sunroom receptacles (9th Ed.)
applies_to: Sunroom of Category I or II
check: FBC-R 9th Edition adds a section stating receptacles are not required in Category I or II sunrooms, regardless of the NEC wall-spacing rule. Do not flag missing receptacles in a room tagged as a Category I or II sunroom under the 9th Edition.
edition_difference: New in 9th Edition per the Commission's change analysis; not in the 8th Edition list of changes.
needs: Sunroom category (I to V)
note: Taken from the Florida Building Commission analysis of changes, not from the code text itself. Section number as printed in the analysis.

group: NEC: general, branch circuits, feeders, services (Art. 100-230)
title: Bathroom definition test
applies_to: Room typing for GFCI, receptacle and circuit rules
check: Treat a room as a bathroom when it has a sink (basin) plus at least one of: toilet, urinal, tub, shower, bidet or similar fixture. A room with only a toilet, or only a sink, is not a bathroom for NEC purposes.
note: From memory of Article 100; wording not opened. 2023 moved all definitions into Article 100 with no part subdivisions (Leviton Captain Code 2023).

group: NEC: general, branch circuits, feeders, services (Art. 100-230)
title: Kitchen definition test
applies_to: Room typing for GFCI, AFCI and small-appliance rules
check: Treat an area as a kitchen when it has a sink and permanent provisions for food preparation and cooking. A wet bar with a sink but no cooking provisions is not a kitchen, but see the 2023 GFCI item for sinks with food or beverage preparation provisions.
note: From memory of Article 100.

group: NEC: general, branch circuits, feeders, services (Art. 100-230)
title: Habitable room test
applies_to: Room typing for lighting outlet and wall-receptacle rules
check: Habitable rooms are spaces for living, sleeping, eating or cooking. Bathrooms, toilet rooms, closets, hallways, storage and utility spaces are not habitable rooms.
edition_difference: Definition was added to Article 100 in the 2020 NEC; unchanged in substance in 2023.
note: From memory of Article 100. A garage or den converted to a bedroom becomes a habitable room and picks up 210.52(A), 210.70(A)(1) and 210.12.

group: NEC: general, branch circuits, feeders, services (Art. 100-230)
title: Dwelling unit test
applies_to: Project typing
check: A dwelling unit is a single unit with complete, independent living facilities: permanent provisions for living, sleeping, cooking and sanitation. Each side of a duplex and each townhouse is its own dwelling unit and needs its own required circuits and receptacles.
note: From memory of Article 100.

group: NEC: general, branch circuits, feeders, services (Art. 100-230)
title: Laundry area test
applies_to: Room typing for laundry GFCI, AFCI, circuit and lighting rules
check: A laundry area is any area designed to hold a laundry tray, clothes washer or clothes dryer, whether or not the equipment is installed. A washer in a closet, hall or garage makes that spot a laundry area.
edition_difference: Definition added in 2020.
note: Restated in Mike Holt's 2023 text as an Article 100 definition.

group: NEC: general, branch circuits, feeders, services (Art. 100-230)
title: Countertop versus work surface
applies_to: Cabinet runs, islands, desks, built-ins
check: A countertop is a surface meant for food preparation and serving, or one routinely exposed to large water spills. Other fixed surfaces (desk tops, built-in benches) are work surfaces; in kitchens, pantries, breakfast and dining areas both get the countertop receptacle rules when 12 in. or wider.
needs: Surface type: countertop or work surface
note: Restated in Mike Holt's 2023 text as an Article 100 definition; whether the same definition is in the 2020 Article 100 was not confirmed.

group: NEC: general, branch circuits, feeders, services (Art. 100-230)
title: Readily accessible test
applies_to: GFCI devices, disconnects, breakers
check: Readily accessible means reachable quickly without tools (other than keys), without climbing over or removing obstacles, and without a portable ladder. A GFCI receptacle behind a refrigerator, dishwasher or washer, or inside a cabinet blocked by an appliance, does not qualify.
needs: GFCI device location (breaker / exposed receptacle / hidden)

group: NEC: general, branch circuits, feeders, services (Art. 100-230)
title: Follow listing and instructions
applies_to: Every appliance, fan, luminaire, panel and device drawn
check: Install and use listed or labeled equipment exactly as its listing and manufacturer's instructions say (dedicated circuit, breaker size, clearances, GFCI over a tub or shower, max breaker type in a panel).
note: Common review comment: appliance nameplate or installation manual calls for an individual circuit or a specific breaker size.

group: NEC: general, branch circuits, feeders, services (Art. 100-230)
title: Interrupting and fault ratings
applies_to: New or replaced panel, service equipment, breakers
check: Breakers and equipment must have an interrupting rating at least equal to the available fault current at their line terminals. On a service upgrade, get the available fault current from the utility and match the panel and breaker ratings (10 kA is not always enough near a large transformer).
needs: Available fault current at service; panel short-circuit rating

group: NEC: general, branch circuits, feeders, services (Art. 100-230)
title: Workmanship and unused openings
applies_to: Panels, boxes, enclosures touched by the remodel
check: Install equipment neatly. Close every unused opening in boxes, panels and enclosures with a fitting giving protection equal to the wall of the equipment; keep paint, plaster and drywall mud out of panels and devices.

group: NEC: general, branch circuits, feeders, services (Art. 100-230)
title: Termination temperature rating
applies_to: Circuits and feeders sized in the circuit schedule
check: Size conductors from the 60 C ampacity column for equipment rated 100 A or less (or wire 14 to 1 AWG) unless the equipment is listed and marked for 75 C conductors. NM cable is always limited to its 60 C ampacity.
note: Feeds the wire-size check: 14 AWG Cu 15 A, 12 AWG 20 A, 10 AWG 30 A, 8 AWG 40 A (60 C), 6 AWG 55 A (60 C).

group: NEC: general, branch circuits, feeders, services (Art. 100-230)
title: Torque terminations
applies_to: Panel, breaker, lug and device terminations
check: Tighten terminals to the torque value marked on the equipment or in its instructions, using a calibrated torque tool.
edition_difference: 2023 wording clarified; requirement has existed since 2017.

group: NEC: general, branch circuits, feeders, services (Art. 100-230)
title: Label disconnects
applies_to: Panels, subpanels, disconnects
check: Mark every disconnecting means to show what it controls unless that is obvious, with a durable label. Field-applied hazard labels must be permanent, not handwritten (except variable parts), and suited to the environment.
note: Circuit directory itself is in 408.4 (another rule set).

group: NEC: general, branch circuits, feeders, services (Art. 100-230)
title: Working space access, open doors
applies_to: Panel, subpanel, service equipment, disconnects
check: Keep access to and exit from the working space clear. Open equipment doors may not cut the path into or out of the working space to less than 24 in. wide and 6 ft 6 in. high.
edition_difference: 2023 moved this open-door rule up from 110.26(A)(2)(b) into the main paragraph and reworded it.

group: NEC: general, branch circuits, feeders, services (Art. 100-230)
title: Working space depth
applies_to: Panel, subpanel, service equipment, disconnect likely to be worked on live
check: Provide clear depth of at least 36 in. in front of the equipment for systems up to 150 V to ground (all dwelling panels), measured from the enclosure front or opening. Nothing may sit in that depth: no cabinets, shelves, countertop, washer, water heater or door swing parking.
note: Table 110.26(A)(1): 0 to 150 V to ground is 3 ft for Conditions 1, 2 and 3 (table value from memory; article confirms the method). Replaces E-16 (working-space part).

group: NEC: general, branch circuits, feeders, services (Art. 100-230)
title: Working space width
applies_to: Panel, subpanel, service equipment, disconnect
check: Provide clear width of at least 30 in. or the width of the equipment, whichever is greater. The 30 in. need not be centered on the panel. The panel door must be able to open at least 90 degrees.
note: Replaces E-16.

group: NEC: general, branch circuits, feeders, services (Art. 100-230)
title: Working space height
applies_to: Panel, subpanel, service equipment, disconnect
check: Keep the working space clear from the floor to 6 ft 6 in. or the top of the equipment, whichever is higher. Other electrical items above or below may project no more than 6 in. beyond the panel front. Flag soffits, beams, shelves or ducts lower than 78 in. within the 30 x 36 in. zone.
note: Exception: in an EXISTING dwelling unit, service equipment or panelboards of 200 A or less may stay where headroom is under 6 ft 6 in. Meters in meter sockets may project past the 6 in. limit.

group: NEC: general, branch circuits, feeders, services (Art. 100-230)
title: Limited-access equipment
applies_to: Equipment above a lay-in (ACT) ceiling or in a crawl space
check: Equipment needing live servicing above a lay-in ceiling or in a crawl space needs an access opening of at least 22 x 22 in. (ceiling) or 22 x 30 in. (crawl space), 30 in. working width, and the standard working depth.
needs: Equipment located above ceiling or in crawl space (yes/no)

group: NEC: general, branch circuits, feeders, services (Art. 100-230)
title: Level working floor
applies_to: Panel and service equipment locations
check: The floor, grade or platform in the working space must be kept clear and as level and flat as practical for the full required depth and width.
edition_difference: New in 2023; not in the 2020 NEC.
note: Section number and wording from memory; not opened.

group: NEC: general, branch circuits, feeders, services (Art. 100-230)
title: No storage in working space
applies_to: Panel in closet, garage, laundry, pantry
check: The working space may not be used for storage. Flag a panel drawn inside or behind shelving, a pantry run, base cabinets, or a laundry appliance location.
note: Clothes-closet and bathroom panel prohibitions are in 240.24(D),(E) (other rule set).

group: NEC: general, branch circuits, feeders, services (Art. 100-230)
title: Entrance to working space
applies_to: Panel and service equipment locations
check: Provide at least one entrance of sufficient size to reach and leave the working space.
note: The large-equipment two-entrance and panic-hardware rules (1200 A, 800 A) do not apply to house services.

group: NEC: general, branch circuits, feeders, services (Art. 100-230)
title: Light at indoor panels
applies_to: Indoor service equipment, panelboards, subpanels
check: Provide lighting for the working space at indoor service equipment and panelboards. It may not be controlled by automatic means only (occupancy sensor or timer with no manual on). A nearby room light can serve.
note: Check: at least one lighting outlet in the room or area containing the panel, with a manual switch.

group: NEC: general, branch circuits, feeders, services (Art. 100-230)
title: Dedicated space above panel
applies_to: Indoor panelboards and service equipment
check: The zone as wide and deep as the panel, from the floor to 6 ft above the panel or to the structural ceiling if lower, is reserved for electrical work: no plumbing pipes, ducts, or other foreign equipment in it. A dropped or lay-in ceiling is not a structural ceiling. Foreign systems above that zone need drip protection.
note: Flag supply registers, plumbing fixtures or water heaters drawn in the panel footprint, and soffits carrying ducts over a panel.

group: NEC: general, branch circuits, feeders, services (Art. 100-230)
title: Outdoor panel space
applies_to: Outdoor panels, meter-mains, disconnects
check: Outdoor equipment needs an enclosure rated for the location, protection from vehicles and from accidental contact, the same working clearances, and no architectural projections or other equipment in the working zone. The dedicated space extends from grade to 6 ft above the equipment.
note: Typical conflict: A/C condenser, hose bibb, gas meter or generator set in front of the meter-main.

group: NEC: general, branch circuits, feeders, services (Art. 100-230)
title: Guard live parts
applies_to: Open panels, exposed terminals, equipment 50 V or more
check: Live parts at 50 V or more must be guarded against accidental contact by an approved enclosure, a room accessible only to qualified persons, or elevation of 8 ft or more above the floor. Missing panel fillers, covers and dead-fronts must be installed.
edition_difference: 2020 lists 50 to 1000 V; 2023 same intent.

group: NEC: general, branch circuits, feeders, services (Art. 100-230)
title: Protect from physical damage
applies_to: Panels and equipment in garages, carports
check: Where electrical equipment is exposed to physical damage (vehicle impact in a garage or carport), protect it with enclosures or guards strong enough to prevent damage.

group: NEC: general, branch circuits, feeders, services (Art. 100-230)
title: Enclosure type for location
applies_to: Outdoor or wet-location panels and disconnects
check: Use an enclosure type suited to the location (outdoors: Type 3R minimum; corrosive coastal exposure may call for 4X).
needs: Panel location indoor/outdoor and enclosure type

group: NEC: general, branch circuits, feeders, services (Art. 100-230)
title: Group neutrals with their circuit
applies_to: Panels and boxes containing more than one neutral
check: Where an enclosure holds more than one neutral, tie or identify each neutral with its own ungrounded conductors inside the enclosure, unless the grouping is obvious from the cable or raceway entry.

group: NEC: general, branch circuits, feeders, services (Art. 100-230)
title: White wire identification
applies_to: All new circuits; switch loops
check: Neutrals 6 AWG and smaller must be white or gray (or three white or gray stripes). A white conductor in a cable used as a hot (switch loop, 240 V circuit) must be permanently re-marked another color at every termination and may not be the switched return to the light.

group: NEC: general, branch circuits, feeders, services (Art. 100-230)
title: Polarity
applies_to: Receptacles and luminaires
check: Do not reverse polarity: the neutral lands only on the terminal identified for it (silver screw, screw shell).

group: NEC: general, branch circuits, feeders, services (Art. 100-230)
title: Multiwire circuit source
applies_to: Multiwire branch circuits (shared neutral)
check: All conductors of a multiwire branch circuit must start from the same panelboard.
note: Check: circuits flagged as sharing a neutral have the same panel and opposite legs.

group: NEC: general, branch circuits, feeders, services (Art. 100-230)
title: Multiwire circuit handle tie
applies_to: Multiwire branch circuits (shared neutral)
check: Each multiwire branch circuit needs a means to disconnect all its ungrounded conductors at once at the panel: a 2-pole breaker or single-pole breakers with an identified handle tie.
needs: Circuit shares a neutral; breaker is 2-pole or handle-tied

group: NEC: general, branch circuits, feeders, services (Art. 100-230)
title: Multiwire circuit loads
applies_to: Multiwire branch circuits
check: A multiwire circuit may supply only line-to-neutral loads, unless it serves a single piece of equipment or all hots open together through a common-trip breaker.

group: NEC: general, branch circuits, feeders, services (Art. 100-230)
title: Multiwire circuit grouping
applies_to: Panels with multiwire circuits
check: Group the hots and neutral of each multiwire circuit together inside the panel with wire ties or similar at least once, unless the grouping is obvious from a single cable or raceway.

group: NEC: general, branch circuits, feeders, services (Art. 100-230)
title: Identify circuits by system
applies_to: Premises with more than one voltage system
check: Where the building has more than one nominal voltage system, identify each ungrounded conductor by phase and system at terminations and splices and post the method at the panel. A normal 120/240 V house has one system, so this rarely applies.

group: NEC: general, branch circuits, feeders, services (Art. 100-230)
title: Two circuits on one yoke
applies_to: Split-wired duplex receptacle or device fed by two circuits
check: Where two or more branch circuits feed devices on the same yoke, provide a means at the panel to disconnect all of them simultaneously (2-pole breaker or handle tie).
needs: Device fed by two circuits (yes/no)

group: NEC: general, branch circuits, feeders, services (Art. 100-230)
title: GFCI device readily accessible
applies_to: Every GFCI-protected receptacle or outlet
check: The GFCI device (breaker or receptacle) must be in a readily accessible location: not behind an appliance, not requiring a ladder. Where a protected receptacle is hidden (dishwasher, disposal, refrigerator, range), put the GFCI at the breaker or at an upstream exposed device.
edition_difference: 2023 calls for a listed Class A GFCI.
needs: GFCI device location for the circuit

group: NEC: general, branch circuits, feeders, services (Art. 100-230)
title: GFCI distance measurement
applies_to: Receptacles near sinks, tubs and showers
check: Measure the 6 ft GFCI distances as the shortest path a cord would take without going through a floor, wall, ceiling or fixed barrier. Since 2020 a door or doorway no longer breaks the path; in 2023 a window does not either.
edition_difference: 2020 still stops the path at a window; 2023 dropped the window wording.
note: 2020 text confirmed at https://captaincode2020.leviton.com/node/181

group: NEC: general, branch circuits, feeders, services (Art. 100-230)
title: GFCI scope, 125 to 250 V
applies_to: All dwelling receptacles in the listed locations
check: GFCI applies to every 125 V through 250 V receptacle on a single-phase circuit of 150 V or less to ground in the listed locations, regardless of ampere rating. That includes 240 V 30 A dryer and 50 A range receptacles when they fall in a listed location.
edition_difference: Same scope in 2020 (first edition to drop the 15 and 20 A limit).
note: Replaces E-05 (scope part).

group: NEC: general, branch circuits, feeders, services (Art. 100-230)
title: GFCI in bathrooms
applies_to: Every receptacle in a bathroom
check: All bathroom receptacles need GFCI protection.
note: Replaces E-05.

group: NEC: general, branch circuits, feeders, services (Art. 100-230)
title: GFCI in garages, accessory buildings
applies_to: Receptacles in garages and non-habitable accessory buildings
check: All receptacles in garages, and in accessory buildings with a floor at or below grade used for storage or work (not habitable), need GFCI protection. Includes ceiling door-opener and freezer receptacles.

group: NEC: general, branch circuits, feeders, services (Art. 100-230)
title: GFCI outdoors
applies_to: Every outdoor receptacle
check: All outdoor receptacles need GFCI protection.
note: Exception No. 1: a not-readily-accessible receptacle on a dedicated circuit for fixed snow-melting or deicing equipment (irrelevant in Florida).

group: NEC: general, branch circuits, feeders, services (Art. 100-230)
title: GFCI in crawl spaces
applies_to: Receptacles in crawl spaces at or below grade
check: Crawl-space receptacles need GFCI protection.

group: NEC: general, branch circuits, feeders, services (Art. 100-230)
title: GFCI in basements
applies_to: Receptacles in basements
check: All basement receptacles, finished or unfinished, need GFCI protection.
edition_difference: Same in 2020 (2017 covered unfinished portions only).
note: Rare in Florida.

group: NEC: general, branch circuits, feeders, services (Art. 100-230)
title: GFCI in kitchens
applies_to: Every receptacle in a kitchen
check: NEC 2023: every kitchen receptacle needs GFCI protection, including refrigerator, range, microwave, disposal, dishwasher, hood and island receptacles. NEC 2020: only receptacles serving the countertop surfaces (plus anything within 6 ft of the sink).
edition_difference: 2020 (in force with FBC 8th Ed.): countertop-serving receptacles only. 2023: all kitchen receptacles.
note: Replaces E-05. NEC 2020 is the edition in force with FBC 8th Edition until Dec 31, 2026; NEC 2023 applies with FBC 9th Edition.

group: NEC: general, branch circuits, feeders, services (Art. 100-230)
title: GFCI at food/beverage prep sinks
applies_to: Wet bars, butler pantries, beverage stations with a sink
check: NEC 2023: receptacles in any area that has a sink and permanent provisions for food preparation, beverage preparation or cooking need GFCI protection, even if the area is not a kitchen.
edition_difference: New item in 2023; 2020 reaches these receptacles only through the 6 ft sink rule.

group: NEC: general, branch circuits, feeders, services (Art. 100-230)
title: GFCI within 6 ft of sink
applies_to: Any receptacle near any sink (bar, laundry, utility, kitchen)
check: Any receptacle within 6 ft of the top inside edge of a sink bowl needs GFCI protection.
edition_difference: Item number only: (A)(7) in 2020, (A)(8) in 2023.

group: NEC: general, branch circuits, feeders, services (Art. 100-230)
title: GFCI in boathouses
applies_to: Receptacles in a boathouse
check: Boathouse receptacles need GFCI protection.
edition_difference: Item number only.

group: NEC: general, branch circuits, feeders, services (Art. 100-230)
title: GFCI near tub or shower
applies_to: Receptacles within 6 ft of a tub or shower outside a bathroom
check: Any receptacle within 6 ft of the outside edge of a bathtub or shower stall needs GFCI protection (aimed at tubs or showers that open to a bedroom or sit outside a defined bathroom).
edition_difference: Item number; 2023 adds the words 'not installed within a bathroom'.

group: NEC: general, branch circuits, feeders, services (Art. 100-230)
title: GFCI in laundry areas
applies_to: Every receptacle in a laundry area
check: All laundry-area receptacles need GFCI protection, including the washer receptacle and a 240 V dryer receptacle.
edition_difference: Item number only.

group: NEC: general, branch circuits, feeders, services (Art. 100-230)
title: GFCI in damp or wet indoor spots
applies_to: Receptacles in indoor damp or wet locations
check: Receptacles in indoor damp or wet locations (pool-equipment rooms, indoor spa rooms, mud rooms with pet wash, screened lanai treated as damp) need GFCI protection.
edition_difference: Item number only; new in 2020.
needs: Room is a damp or wet location (yes/no)

group: NEC: general, branch circuits, feeders, services (Art. 100-230)
title: GFCI exceptions in dwellings
applies_to: Alarm, ceiling fan/luminaire and exhaust fan receptacles
check: GFCI is not required for: (2023 Ex. 2) a receptacle serving only a permanently installed premises security system; (2023 Ex. 3) a listed weight-supporting ceiling receptacle used only for a ceiling luminaire or fan; (2023 Ex. 4) a receptacle inside a bathroom exhaust fan, unless the fan instructions require GFCI.
edition_difference: 2020: the alarm exception applies only to basements (fire or burglar alarm); the locking-support ceiling receptacle exception exists; no exhaust-fan exception.
note: Exception No. 3 text was not shown in the source; stated from memory.

group: NEC: general, branch circuits, feeders, services (Art. 100-230)
title: GFCI for crawl-space lights
applies_to: 120 V lighting outlets in crawl spaces
check: Crawl-space lighting outlets up to 120 V need GFCI protection.
