group: NEC: general, branch circuits, feeders, services (Art. 100-230)
title: GFCI for specific appliances
applies_to: Dishwasher, electric range, wall oven, cooktop, clothes dryer, microwave, sump pump
check: NEC 2023: provide GFCI protection on the branch circuit or outlet, hardwired or cord-and-plug, for appliances rated 150 V or less to ground and 60 A or less: dishwasher, electric range, wall-mounted oven, counter-mounted cooking unit, clothes dryer, microwave oven, sump pump (plus water coolers/bottle fillers). NEC 2020: dishwasher and sump pump only (through the 422.5(A) list).
edition_difference: 2023 added electric ranges, wall ovens, cooktops, clothes dryers and microwave ovens and wrote the list into 210.8(D). 2020 points to 422.5(A): the dwelling items are dishwashers and sump pumps.
note: Replaces E-05 (appliance part). 2020 text at https://captaincode2020.leviton.com/node/243. NEC 2020 is the edition in force with FBC 8th Edition until Dec 31, 2026; NEC 2023 applies with FBC 9th Edition.

group: NEC: general, branch circuits, feeders, services (Art. 100-230)
title: GFCI for service receptacles
applies_to: Receptacle required near HVAC equipment (210.63)
check: The service receptacle required within 25 ft of heating, air-conditioning and refrigeration equipment needs GFCI protection, indoors or out (attic air handler receptacle included).

group: NEC: general, branch circuits, feeders, services (Art. 100-230)
title: GFCI for outdoor outlets
applies_to: Outdoor hardwired or plug outlets at a dwelling up to 50 A: pool pump, mini-split, landscape transformer, EVSE
check: All outdoor outlets at a dwelling (not only receptacles) on single-phase circuits of 150 V or less to ground and 50 A or less need GFCI protection. Lighting outlets are exempt. In Florida, listed HVAC equipment is exempt by FBC-R E3408.1. NEC 2023 also names outlets in garages with floors at or below grade, accessory buildings and boathouses, and requires GFCI to be added when the supplied equipment is replaced.
edition_difference: 2020: new section; plain outdoor outlets. 2023: adds garages, accessory buildings, boathouses and the replaced-equipment trigger; NEC HVAC exception expires Sept 1, 2026 but Florida's 9th Ed. amendment keeps it permanently.
needs: Outdoor outlet serves listed HVAC equipment (yes/no)
note: Florida amendment read on the ICC viewer (see the E3408.1 rule).

group: NEC: general, branch circuits, feeders, services (Art. 100-230)
title: Number of circuits, balanced load
applies_to: Circuit schedule of a remodel or new panel
check: Provide at least the number of branch circuits the load calculation calls for, and spread the calculated load evenly among the general-purpose circuits. Circuits need only be installed for the connected load.
note: Handled by the load calculator; shown as a note.

group: NEC: general, branch circuits, feeders, services (Art. 100-230)
title: Two small-appliance circuits
applies_to: Kitchen, pantry, breakfast room, dining room
check: Provide at least two 20 A, 120 V small-appliance circuits for the receptacles in the kitchen, pantry, breakfast room and dining room. 12 AWG copper minimum.
note: Replaces E-04. Source article restates the rule without naming the edition; unchanged through 2023 to my knowledge.

group: NEC: general, branch circuits, feeders, services (Art. 100-230)
title: Laundry circuit
applies_to: Laundry area
check: Provide at least one 20 A, 120 V circuit for the laundry receptacle(s). It may serve several receptacles in the laundry area but no other outlets: no laundry lighting, no receptacles elsewhere. Required even where the washer/dryer is a 240 V combination unit.
note: Replaces E-09 (circuit part).

group: NEC: general, branch circuits, feeders, services (Art. 100-230)
title: Bathroom receptacle circuit
applies_to: Bathrooms
check: Provide at least one 20 A, 120 V circuit for bathroom receptacles (the required basin receptacle and any countertop or similar work-surface receptacles). It may serve receptacles in several bathrooms but no other outlets. Exception: a 20 A circuit that serves only ONE bathroom may also feed that bathroom's lights and fan, within the 210.23 limits (fastened-in-place equipment not over 10 A).
edition_difference: Exception cross-reference is 210.23(A)(1),(A)(2) in 2020 and 210.23(B)(1),(B)(2) in 2023.
note: Replaces E-06 (circuit part). The words about countertop and work-surface receptacles are from memory of the 2020 revision.

group: NEC: general, branch circuits, feeders, services (Art. 100-230)
title: Garage receptacle circuit
applies_to: Attached garage, or detached garage with power
check: Provide at least one 20 A, 120 V circuit for the required vehicle-bay receptacles. It may have no other outlets, except outdoor receptacles (2020: readily accessible outdoor receptacles). NEC 2023 adds: in a single-vehicle-bay garage the circuit may also serve other equipment in the garage within the 210.23 limits, and extra garage receptacles beyond the required ones may be on other 15 or 20 A circuits.
edition_difference: 2023 added Exception No. 2 (single-bay garage) and the sentence on additional circuits; dropped 'readily accessible' from the outdoor exception.
note: 2020 text at https://captaincode2020.leviton.com/node/132. Garage lights and door-opener outlets belong on another circuit unless the single-bay exception applies.

group: NEC: general, branch circuits, feeders, services (Art. 100-230)
title: AFCI means of protection
applies_to: Circuits needing AFCI protection
check: Provide AFCI protection by one of the permitted methods: a listed combination-type AFCI breaker (normal method), or the listed combinations of branch/feeder or supplemental breaker with an outlet branch-circuit AFCI at the first outlet under the length and wiring-method limits. The AFCI device must be readily accessible.
edition_difference: 2023 moved the methods list to a new (A) and made the location rules (B) to (E).
needs: Circuit protection type (AFCI / dual-function / none)
note: Method details from memory; source confirms the readily-accessible requirement and the new lettering.

group: NEC: general, branch circuits, feeders, services (Art. 100-230)
title: AFCI rooms in dwellings
applies_to: 120 V, 15 and 20 A circuits serving kitchens, family, dining and living rooms, parlors, libraries, dens, bedrooms, sunrooms, recreation rooms, closets, hallways, laundry areas and similar
check: Every 120 V, single-phase 15 or 20 A (2023: also 10 A) branch circuit supplying outlets or devices (receptacles, lights, switches, smoke alarms, hardwired appliances) in those rooms needs AFCI protection. Not required for circuits serving only bathrooms, garages, outdoors, attics or crawl spaces.
edition_difference: 2020 section is 210.12(A) and covers 15 and 20 A circuits; 2023 is 210.12(B) and adds 10 A circuits.
note: Replaces E-10. Exception (both editions): an individual circuit to a fire alarm system in metal raceway or steel-armored cable. The 10 A wording is described in the source summary but the rule text shown listed 15 and 20 A.

group: NEC: general, branch circuits, feeders, services (Art. 100-230)
title: AFCI when wiring is extended
applies_to: Existing circuits extended, modified or replaced in an AFCI room
check: Where branch-circuit wiring in an AFCI-required room is modified, replaced or extended, protect the circuit with an AFCI breaker or with an outlet branch-circuit AFCI receptacle at the first receptacle outlet of the existing circuit. Exception: extending existing conductors by not more than 6 ft with no added outlets or devices (splices allowed), e.g. a panel relocation.
edition_difference: Section letter: (D) in 2020, (E) in 2023.
needs: Existing circuit is extended or modified (yes/no) and extension length
note: Key remodel trigger. Replacement of a receptacle in an AFCI room also triggers AFCI under 406.4(D)(4) (Chapter 4 rule set).

group: NEC: general, branch circuits, feeders, services (Art. 100-230)
title: Standard circuit ratings
applies_to: Circuit schedule
check: Multi-outlet branch circuits are rated by their breaker: 15, 20, 30, 40 or 50 A (2023 also recognizes 10 A). Flag any other breaker size on a circuit with more than one outlet.
edition_difference: 2023 moved the rating rule from 210.3 to 210.18 and added the 10 A rating.
note: Relocation to 210.18 is from memory; the 10 A circuit is confirmed by Leviton Captain Code 2023 node 313.

group: NEC: general, branch circuits, feeders, services (Art. 100-230)
title: Conductor size for load
applies_to: Every branch circuit
check: Conductor ampacity must be at least the load served: 100 percent of non-continuous load plus 125 percent of continuous load, after any derating. Check wire size against breaker: 14 AWG Cu on 15 A, 12 AWG on 20 A, 10 AWG on 30 A.
edition_difference: 2023 reorganized 210.19 subsections.
note: Small-conductor breaker limits are in 240.4(D) (other rule set).

group: NEC: general, branch circuits, feeders, services (Art. 100-230)
title: Voltage drop recommendation
applies_to: Circuits with long homeruns
check: Recommended (not mandatory): keep voltage drop to 3 percent on the branch circuit and 5 percent on feeder plus branch circuit combined. Flag run lengths that exceed the 3 percent length for the wire size and load as an advisory.
edition_difference: Note numbering differs between editions.
note: Replaces E-17. Advisory only; an informational note is not enforceable. Rough 3 percent lengths at 120 V: 14 AWG at 12 A about 50 ft, 12 AWG at 16 A about 60 ft.

group: NEC: general, branch circuits, feeders, services (Art. 100-230)
title: Wire for multi-receptacle circuits
applies_to: Circuits feeding more than one receptacle
check: Conductors of a circuit supplying more than one receptacle for cord-and-plug loads must have an ampacity at least equal to the circuit rating (no 14 AWG on a 20 A receptacle circuit).

group: NEC: general, branch circuits, feeders, services (Art. 100-230)
title: Range circuit minimum
applies_to: Electric range, cooktop, wall oven circuits
check: A range rated 8.75 kW or more needs a circuit of at least 40 A. Tap conductors from a 50 A circuit to a cooktop or wall oven must be at least 20 A, sized for the load and no longer than needed for servicing. The neutral of a 3-wire range circuit may be reduced to 70 percent of the circuit rating but not below 10 AWG.
edition_difference: Lettering changed in 2023 (from memory).
note: Lettering of this subsection in 2023 not confirmed.

group: NEC: general, branch circuits, feeders, services (Art. 100-230)
title: Minimum branch conductor size
applies_to: All branch circuits
check: Branch-circuit conductors for other loads must be at least 14 AWG copper and sized for the load.
edition_difference: Lettering changed in 2023 (from memory).

group: NEC: general, branch circuits, feeders, services (Art. 100-230)
title: Breaker size for load
applies_to: Every branch circuit
check: The breaker rating must be at least 100 percent of the non-continuous load plus 125 percent of the continuous load, and must protect the conductors (240.4) and the equipment.

group: NEC: general, branch circuits, feeders, services (Art. 100-230)
title: Lampholders over 20 A
applies_to: Lighting on circuits above 20 A
check: Lampholders on circuits rated over 20 A must be heavy-duty type; ordinary dwelling luminaires go on 15 or 20 A circuits only.

group: NEC: general, branch circuits, feeders, services (Art. 100-230)
title: Single receptacle rating
applies_to: A single receptacle on an individual circuit
check: A single (simplex) receptacle on an individual branch circuit must be rated at least the circuit rating: a 20 A dedicated circuit with one simplex needs a 20 A receptacle.
needs: Receptacle is single or duplex; receptacle ampere rating
note: Source is an older EC Magazine article; values unchanged to my knowledge.

group: NEC: general, branch circuits, feeders, services (Art. 100-230)
title: Cord-and-plug load per receptacle
applies_to: Receptacles on multi-outlet circuits
check: Maximum cord-and-plug load on one receptacle of a multi-receptacle circuit: 12 A on a 15 A receptacle, 16 A on a 20 A receptacle, 24 A on a 30 A receptacle.
needs: Appliance nameplate amperes
note: Table 210.21(B)(2). Older source article.

group: NEC: general, branch circuits, feeders, services (Art. 100-230)
title: Receptacle rating versus circuit
applies_to: Receptacles on circuits with two or more receptacles
check: Receptacle rating by circuit: 15 A circuit, 15 A receptacles only; 20 A circuit, 15 or 20 A; 30 A circuit, 30 A; 40 A circuit, 40 or 50 A; 50 A circuit, 50 A. A duplex counts as two receptacles, so 15 A duplexes are fine on 20 A circuits.
note: Table 210.21(B)(3). Older source article.

group: NEC: general, branch circuits, feeders, services (Art. 100-230)
title: Range receptacle rating
applies_to: Range receptacle
check: A range receptacle may be rated on the single-range demand load from Table 220.55 (typically a 50 A receptacle on a 40 or 50 A circuit).

group: NEC: general, branch circuits, feeders, services (Art. 100-230)
title: Individual circuit load
applies_to: Dedicated (individual) appliance circuits
check: An individual branch circuit may supply any load for which it is rated, but never more than its ampere rating.

group: NEC: general, branch circuits, feeders, services (Art. 100-230)
title: 10 A circuits (2023 only)
applies_to: Lighting circuits protected at 10 A
check: NEC 2023 allows a 10 A branch circuit for lighting outlets, bathroom or laundry exhaust fans on the lighting circuit, and a gas fireplace unit on its own circuit. It may NOT supply receptacles, fixed appliances (other than as individual circuits), garage door openers or laundry equipment.
edition_difference: New in 2023. NEC 2020 has no 10 A branch circuit: minimum is 15 A.
note: NEC 2020 is the edition in force with FBC 8th Edition until Dec 31, 2026; NEC 2023 applies with FBC 9th Edition.

group: NEC: general, branch circuits, feeders, services (Art. 100-230)
title: 15 and 20 A circuit loads
applies_to: General-purpose 15 and 20 A circuits
check: A 15 or 20 A circuit may supply lighting, other utilization equipment, or both. The small-appliance, laundry and bathroom circuits may serve only the outlets those rules name.
note: Older source article for the content; 2023 lettering from Leviton node 313.

group: NEC: general, branch circuits, feeders, services (Art. 100-230)
title: 80 percent cord-and-plug limit
applies_to: A plug-in appliance on a shared 15 or 20 A circuit
check: Any one cord-and-plug appliance that is not fastened in place may not exceed 80 percent of the circuit rating: 12 A on a 15 A circuit, 16 A on a 20 A circuit.
edition_difference: Lettering only.
needs: Appliance nameplate amperes

group: NEC: general, branch circuits, feeders, services (Art. 100-230)
title: 50 percent fastened-in-place limit
applies_to: Disposal, dishwasher, hood, microwave, bath heater-fan sharing a circuit with lights or receptacles
check: Fastened-in-place equipment (other than luminaires) on a circuit that also feeds lighting or plug-in loads may total no more than 50 percent of the circuit rating: 7.5 A on 15 A, 10 A on 20 A. Larger equipment needs its own circuit.
edition_difference: Lettering only.
needs: Fastened-in-place appliance amperes and whether the circuit is shared
note: Replaces E-11 (basis for dedicated circuits). Range hoods and over-range microwaves that are cord-and-plug connected need an individual circuit under 422.16(B)(4).

group: NEC: general, branch circuits, feeders, services (Art. 100-230)
title: 30 A circuit loads
applies_to: 30 A circuits (dryer, water heater, A/C)
check: In a dwelling a 30 A circuit may supply utilization equipment only (no general lighting); any one plug-in appliance is limited to 24 A.
edition_difference: Lettering only.

group: NEC: general, branch circuits, feeders, services (Art. 100-230)
title: 40 and 50 A circuit loads
applies_to: 40 and 50 A circuits
check: In a dwelling 40 and 50 A circuits may supply fastened-in-place cooking appliances and other utilization equipment, not lighting.
edition_difference: Lettering only.

group: NEC: general, branch circuits, feeders, services (Art. 100-230)
title: Branch-circuit summary table
applies_to: Circuit schedule
check: Cross-check each multi-outlet circuit against the summary table: 15 A, 14 AWG Cu, 15 A receptacles; 20 A, 12 AWG, 15 or 20 A receptacles; 30 A, 10 AWG, 30 A; 40 A, 8 AWG, 40 or 50 A; 50 A, 6 AWG, 50 A.
edition_difference: 2023 splits it into Table 210.24(1) copper and 210.24(2) aluminum and copper-clad aluminum, and adds the 10 A column.
note: Table values from memory; table split confirmed by the source.

group: NEC: general, branch circuits, feeders, services (Art. 100-230)
title: Circuits stay within the unit
applies_to: Duplexes, townhouses, units with shared areas
check: Branch circuits in a dwelling unit may serve only loads in or associated with that unit. Shared-area loads (common hall or exterior lighting of a two-family building) may not be fed from one unit's panel.

group: NEC: general, branch circuits, feeders, services (Art. 100-230)
title: Appliance receptacle within 6 ft
applies_to: Washer, refrigerator, range, microwave and other plug-in appliance locations
check: A receptacle installed for a specific appliance (washer, gas range, refrigerator) must be within 6 ft of the intended appliance location.

group: NEC: general, branch circuits, feeders, services (Art. 100-230)
title: Receptacles that do not count
applies_to: All required-receptacle checks
check: Required 125 V, 15 or 20 A receptacles are in addition to any receptacle that is part of a luminaire or appliance, is switched as the room's lighting under the 210.70(A)(1) exception, is inside a cabinet or cupboard, or is more than 5 ft 6 in. above the floor. Do not count those toward spacing.
note: A half-switched duplex still counts through its unswitched half (common interpretation). Factory receptacles in permanent electric baseboard heaters may count.

group: NEC: general, branch circuits, feeders, services (Art. 100-230)
title: Wall receptacle spacing
applies_to: Kitchen, family, dining, living room, parlor, library, den, sunroom, bedroom, recreation room and similar rooms
check: No point measured along the floor line of any wall space may be more than 6 ft from a receptacle (so receptacles no more than 12 ft apart, and within 6 ft of each door edge or break).
note: Replaces E-07. In a remodel applies to rooms where walls are opened or the room is new or changes use; untouched rooms are governed by FBC-EB.

group: NEC: general, branch circuits, feeders, services (Art. 100-230)
title: What counts as wall space
applies_to: Rooms under the 6 ft rule
check: Wall space is: (1) any wall 2 ft or more wide, including around corners, unbroken at the floor by doorways, fireplaces, stationary appliances or fixed cabinets that have no countertop or work surface; (2) fixed panels in exterior walls (fixed glass), but not sliding panels; (3) fixed room dividers such as freestanding bar counters or railings.
note: Sliding glass doors are not wall space; the fixed sidelight of a window wall is.

group: NEC: general, branch circuits, feeders, services (Art. 100-230)
title: Floor receptacles
applies_to: Rooms with window walls, railings or open plans
check: A floor receptacle counts toward the wall spacing only if it is within 18 in. of the wall.

group: NEC: general, branch circuits, feeders, services (Art. 100-230)
title: Countertop receptacles don't count
applies_to: Kitchens and dining areas
check: Receptacles installed for countertops and similar work surfaces do not count as the wall receptacles required by the 6 ft rule.

group: NEC: general, branch circuits, feeders, services (Art. 100-230)
title: Receptacles on small-appliance circuits
applies_to: Kitchen, pantry, breakfast room, dining room
check: All wall, floor and countertop receptacles in the kitchen, pantry, breakfast room and dining room, and the refrigerator receptacle, must be on the 20 A small-appliance circuits. Exceptions: a switched receptacle for room lighting may be on a general circuit; a specific appliance such as the refrigerator may be on its own individual circuit of 15 A or more.
note: Replaces E-04.

group: NEC: general, branch circuits, feeders, services (Art. 100-230)
title: Nothing else on small-appliance circuits
applies_to: Small-appliance circuits
check: The small-appliance circuits may have no other outlets: no lighting, no hood, no disposal, no dishwasher, no receptacles in other rooms. Exceptions: a receptacle only for an electric clock, and a receptacle for the igniter, clock or light of a gas range, oven or cooktop.

group: NEC: general, branch circuits, feeders, services (Art. 100-230)
title: Two circuits at the countertop
applies_to: Kitchen countertop receptacles
check: Countertop receptacles in a kitchen must be fed by at least two small-appliance circuits. Those circuits may also feed other receptacles in the same kitchen, pantry, breakfast and dining area, but a small-appliance circuit may not serve more than one kitchen.

group: NEC: general, branch circuits, feeders, services (Art. 100-230)
title: Countertops 12 in. or wider
applies_to: Countertops and work surfaces in kitchens, pantries, breakfast rooms, dining rooms
check: Every countertop or work surface 12 in. or wider gets receptacles under the wall-space, island/peninsula and location rules. Each 12 in. of a multioutlet assembly with two or more receptacles counts as one receptacle.

group: NEC: general, branch circuits, feeders, services (Art. 100-230)
title: Countertop wall spacing
applies_to: Wall countertops and work surfaces
check: No point along the wall line of a countertop may be more than 24 in. from a receptacle (receptacles no more than 4 ft apart, first one within 2 ft of each end and of each break). Sinks, ranges, cooktops and refrigerators break the run into separate spaces.
note: Replaces E-01.

group: NEC: general, branch circuits, feeders, services (Art. 100-230)
title: Behind sink or range
applies_to: Countertop directly behind a sink, range or cooktop
check: No receptacle is required on the wall directly behind a range, counter-mounted cooktop or sink when the depth behind it is less than 12 in. (straight run) or less than 18 in. (corner installation). At or beyond those depths the space behind counts as countertop needing a receptacle. NEC 2023 adds: where a required receptacle cannot go in the wall area, put it as close as practicable to the countertop served.
edition_difference: 2023 added the 'as close as practicable' exception.
note: 12 in. and 18 in. values are from Figure 210.52(C)(1), from memory; the source confirms the exception refers to the figure.

group: NEC: general, branch circuits, feeders, services (Art. 100-230)
title: Island and peninsula receptacles
applies_to: Islands and peninsulas
check: NEC 2020 (FBC 8th Ed., in force now): at least one receptacle for the first 9 sq ft or fraction of island or peninsula top, plus one more for each additional 18 sq ft or fraction; on a peninsula at least one receptacle within 2 ft of the outer end; peninsula measured from the connected perpendicular wall. NEC 2023 (FBC 9th Ed.): no receptacle is required, but if none is installed provide provisions for a future receptacle (e.g. a stubbed raceway or box) at the island or peninsula; any receptacle installed must meet the location rule.
edition_difference: Complete change: 2020 counts by area (9 sq ft / 18 sq ft); 2023 makes the receptacle optional with future provisions.
note: Replaces E-03 (the old one-receptacle-per-island rule is NEC 2017 and earlier). 2020 text at https://captaincode2020.leviton.com/node/150. NEC 2020 is the edition in force with FBC 8th Edition until Dec 31, 2026; NEC 2023 applies with FBC 9th Edition.

group: NEC: general, branch circuits, feeders, services (Art. 100-230)
title: Countertop receptacle location
applies_to: Receptacles serving countertops and work surfaces
check: Locate countertop receptacles on or above the surface but not more than 20 in. above it, or in the surface using a listed countertop (or work-surface) receptacle assembly. NEC 2020 also allows up to 12 in. below the surface where the top does not overhang its base by more than 6 in. NEC 2023 removed the below-counter option: no receptacle on the side of an island or peninsula cabinet may serve the countertop.
edition_difference: 2020 permits not more than 12 in. below the countertop with overhang 6 in. or less; 2023 does not permit below-counter receptacles to serve the countertop.
note: Replaces E-02. Receptacles may not be installed face-up in a countertop unless in a listed assembly (406.5(E)).

group: NEC: general, branch circuits, feeders, services (Art. 100-230)
title: Blocked receptacles don't count
applies_to: Appliance garages, receptacles behind appliances
check: Receptacles made not readily accessible by a fastened-in-place appliance, an appliance garage, a sink or a rangetop, or by an appliance in its dedicated space, do not count toward the required countertop receptacles.

group: NEC: general, branch circuits, feeders, services (Art. 100-230)
title: Bathroom basin receptacle
applies_to: Each lavatory in a bathroom
check: Provide at least one receptacle within 3 ft of the outside edge of each basin, on a wall or partition next to the basin or countertop, in the countertop (listed assembly), or on the side or face of the basin cabinet not more than 12 in. below the top of the basin or countertop. One receptacle between two basins can serve both if within 3 ft of each.
note: Replaces E-06 (receptacle part).

group: NEC: general, branch circuits, feeders, services (Art. 100-230)
title: Outdoor receptacles front and back
applies_to: One- and two-family dwellings, each unit at grade
check: Provide at least one outdoor receptacle at the front and one at the back of the dwelling, readily accessible from grade and not more than 6 ft 6 in. above grade.
note: In an interior remodel this bites only if exterior walls or additions are part of the work. Outdoor receptacles need GFCI and weather-resistant type with in-use covers (406.9, other rule set).

group: NEC: general, branch circuits, feeders, services (Art. 100-230)
title: Balcony, deck, porch receptacle
applies_to: Balconies, decks and porches within 4 in. horizontally of the dwelling
check: Provide at least one receptacle accessible from the balcony, deck or porch, not more than 6 ft 6 in. above its walking surface.
edition_difference: Same in both editions (2020 introduced the 4 in. wording).

group: NEC: general, branch circuits, feeders, services (Art. 100-230)
title: Laundry receptacle
applies_to: Laundry area
check: Provide at least one receptacle in the area where laundry equipment is installed (within 6 ft of the washer location per 210.50(C)).
note: Replaces E-09. Exceptions cover multifamily buildings with shared laundry only.

group: NEC: general, branch circuits, feeders, services (Art. 100-230)
title: Garage, basement, accessory receptacles: general
applies_to: Garages, basements, accessory buildings
check: The receptacles required in garages, unfinished basements and powered accessory buildings are in addition to receptacles for specific equipment (door opener, freezer, water heater). NEC 2023 adds that a receptacle serving only a permanently installed security system does not count.
edition_difference: Security-system sentence is new in 2023.

group: NEC: general, branch circuits, feeders, services (Art. 100-230)
title: Garage bay receptacles
applies_to: Attached garages and detached garages with power
check: Provide at least one receptacle in each vehicle bay, not more than 5 ft 6 in. above the floor.
note: Must be on the 20 A garage circuit (210.11(C)(4)) and GFCI protected.

group: NEC: general, branch circuits, feeders, services (Art. 100-230)
title: Accessory building receptacle
applies_to: Accessory buildings with electric power
check: Provide at least one receptacle in each accessory building that has power.

group: NEC: general, branch circuits, feeders, services (Art. 100-230)
title: Basement receptacle
applies_to: Each separate unfinished portion of a basement
check: Provide at least one receptacle in each separate unfinished portion of a basement.
note: Rare in Florida.

group: NEC: general, branch circuits, feeders, services (Art. 100-230)
title: Hallway receptacle
applies_to: Hallways 10 ft or longer
check: Provide at least one receptacle in each hallway 10 ft or more long, measured along the centerline without passing through a doorway.
note: Replaces E-08.

group: NEC: general, branch circuits, feeders, services (Art. 100-230)
title: Foyer receptacles
applies_to: Foyers larger than 60 sq ft that are not part of a hallway
check: Provide a receptacle in each wall space 3 ft or more wide. Doorways, door-side windows that extend to the floor, and similar openings are not wall space.
note: Replaces E-08.

group: NEC: general, branch circuits, feeders, services (Art. 100-230)
title: Service receptacle at HVAC equipment
applies_to: Air handler, condenser, heat pump, furnace, attic or closet HVAC equipment
check: Provide a 125 V, 15 or 20 A receptacle at an accessible location on the same level as, and within 25 ft of, heating, air-conditioning and refrigeration equipment. It may not be fed from the load side of the equipment's disconnect. It must be GFCI protected (210.8(E)).
note: 25 ft and ratings confirmed in the source; 'same level' and 'not on load side of disconnect' confirmed by a 2026-NEC study guide and from memory. Exception for evaporative coolers at one- and two-family dwellings.

group: NEC: general, branch circuits, feeders, services (Art. 100-230)
title: Service receptacle at service equipment
applies_to: Indoor service equipment in other than one- and two-family dwellings
check: A 125 V receptacle in the same room or area as indoor service equipment is required only in other than one- and two-family dwellings. Not required for a single-family house or duplex; relevant for townhouse or multifamily meter rooms.
note: The one- and two-family exclusion is from memory.

group: NEC: general, branch circuits, feeders, services (Art. 100-230)
title: Battery-only switches
applies_to: Wireless or battery-powered wall controls
check: NEC 2023: a switch or wall control for required lighting may not rely only on a battery unless the lighting turns on automatically when the battery fails.
edition_difference: New sentence in 2023.
needs: Wall control is battery-powered (yes/no)

group: NEC: general, branch circuits, feeders, services (Art. 100-230)
title: Switched light in each room
applies_to: Every habitable room, kitchen, bathroom (2023: and laundry area)
check: Provide at least one lighting outlet controlled by a wall switch (2023: listed wall-mounted control device) located near an entrance to the room, on a wall. NEC 2023 adds laundry areas to the list.
edition_difference: 2020 lists habitable rooms, kitchens and bathrooms and says wall switch; 2023 adds laundry areas, says listed wall-mounted control device, and requires it near an entrance.
note: Replaces E-12. Triggered when a room is created or changes use (garage or den to bedroom).

group: NEC: general, branch circuits, feeders, services (Art. 100-230)
title: Switched receptacle instead of light
applies_to: Habitable rooms other than kitchens and bathrooms (2023: and laundry areas)
check: In rooms other than kitchens, bathrooms (and, in 2023, laundry areas), one or more switch-controlled receptacles may stand in for the ceiling or wall lighting outlet.
edition_difference: 2023 excludes laundry areas from this exception.
note: A fully switched receptacle then does not count toward 210.52 spacing.

group: NEC: general, branch circuits, feeders, services (Art. 100-230)
title: Occupancy sensor control
applies_to: Rooms with sensor-controlled lighting
check: Occupancy sensors may control the required lighting if they are in addition to wall switches, or are at the usual switch location and have a manual override.
needs: Control type (switch / sensor with override)

group: NEC: general, branch circuits, feeders, services (Art. 100-230)
title: Lights in halls, stairs, garages
applies_to: Hallways, stairways, attached garages, detached garages and accessory buildings with power
check: Provide at least one wall-switch-controlled lighting outlet in each hallway, stairway, attached garage, and detached garage with power (2023: also accessory buildings with power).
edition_difference: 2023 added accessory buildings with electric power.
note: Replaces E-12.

group: NEC: general, branch circuits, feeders, services (Art. 100-230)
title: Exterior light at each door
applies_to: Outdoor entrances and exits with grade-level access, including garage man-doors
check: Provide at least one wall-switch-controlled exterior lighting outlet at the outside of each outdoor entrance or exit with grade-level access. A vehicle door is not an entrance for this rule. Remote, central or automatic control is allowed.
edition_difference: 2023 adds an exception for bulkhead (cellar) doors.
note: Bites when a new exterior door is added or relocated.

group: NEC: general, branch circuits, feeders, services (Art. 100-230)
title: Stair switches at each level
applies_to: Interior stairways with six or more risers between levels
check: Where an interior stair has six or more risers between floor levels, provide a wall switch at each floor level and at each landing level that has an entry to the stair. Remote, central or automatic control is allowed in hallways and stairways.
note: Replaces E-12 (stair part).

group: NEC: general, branch circuits, feeders, services (Art. 100-230)
title: Stair and entry dimmers
applies_to: Dimmers controlling stair or entrance lighting
check: Dimmers may control stairway and exterior-entrance lighting only if every control location can bring the stair lighting to full brightness.
needs: Dimmer type at each control point

group: NEC: general, branch circuits, feeders, services (Art. 100-230)
title: Light in attic, underfloor, utility spaces
applies_to: Attics, underfloor spaces, utility rooms and basements used for storage or holding equipment that needs servicing (air handler, water heater)
check: Provide at least one lighting outlet with an integral switch or controlled by a wall switch, with a control point at the usual point of entry to the space, and with the light at or near the equipment requiring servicing. A switched receptacle does not satisfy this.
edition_difference: 2020 has the dwelling rule in 210.70(A)(3); 2023 merged it into 210.70(C) covering all occupancies.
note: Replaces E-12 (attic part). Source article is older; relocation to (C) in 2023 from Mike Holt's 2023 comment and memory. Triggered when an air handler or water heater is placed in the attic or an attic hatch is added for storage.

group: NEC: general, branch circuits, feeders, services (Art. 100-230)
title: Feeder conductor size
applies_to: Feeder to a subpanel
check: Feeder ampacity must be at least 100 percent of the non-continuous load plus 125 percent of the continuous load from the Article 220 calculation, and the feeder breaker must protect it (215.3, 240.4). Check subpanel rating, feeder wire size and feeder breaker agree.
note: Dwelling 83 percent sizing (310.12) applies only to a feeder carrying the entire load of the dwelling.

group: NEC: general, branch circuits, feeders, services (Art. 100-230)
title: Feeder voltage drop
applies_to: Long feeders to subpanels or detached buildings
check: Recommended (not mandatory): limit feeder voltage drop to 3 percent, and feeder plus branch to 5 percent.
note: Advisory. Replaces E-17 (feeder part).

group: NEC: general, branch circuits, feeders, services (Art. 100-230)
title: Feeder equipment ground
applies_to: Feeder to a subpanel
check: A feeder supplying a subpanel must include an equipment grounding conductor (4-wire feeder: two hots, neutral, ground). At the subpanel, neutrals and grounds land on separate bars and the neutral bar is not bonded to the can (250.24(A)(5), 408.40).
needs: Subpanel feeder conductor count; neutral isolated (yes/no)

group: NEC: general, branch circuits, feeders, services (Art. 100-230)
title: GFCI at the feeder
applies_to: Feeders supplying GFCI-required outlets
check: A feeder may be GFCI protected in place of GFCI at the individual branch circuits (2020 removed the 15 and 20 A limit).

group: NEC: general, branch circuits, feeders, services (Art. 100-230)
title: Surge protection at feeder panels
applies_to: Subpanel or feeder-supplied panel serving a dwelling unit, when installed or replaced
check: NEC 2023: where a feeder supplies a dwelling unit, install a Type 1 or Type 2 surge-protective device in or next to the distribution equipment that holds the branch-circuit breakers, with a nominal discharge current rating of at least 10 kA. Applies also when that distribution equipment is replaced.
edition_difference: New in 2023. NEC 2020 requires surge protection only at the service (230.67).
needs: SPD shown at panel (yes/no, type, kA rating)
note: An SPD at the service equipment plus each downstream panel is the conservative reading; whether a house with a service SPD also needs one at every subpanel is interpreted locally.

group: NEC: general, branch circuits, feeders, services (Art. 100-230)
title: No receptacle count limit
applies_to: General-purpose 15 and 20 A receptacle circuits in dwellings
check: In dwellings, general-use receptacles (and the bathroom, outdoor, garage and basement receptacles and lighting outlets) are included in the general lighting load; there is no VA per receptacle and no maximum number of receptacles on a dwelling general-purpose circuit. Do not flag a circuit for receptacle count alone.
edition_difference: 2023 cross-references moved (general lighting load is 220.41 in 2023, 220.12/220.14(J) in 2020).
note: Good practice (not code): about 8 to 10 receptacles per 15 A and 10 to 13 per 20 A circuit.

group: NEC: general, branch circuits, feeders, services (Art. 100-230)
title: Specific appliance outlets
applies_to: Dedicated appliance circuits
check: Size each outlet for a specific appliance or load from the appliance's ampere rating.
needs: Appliance nameplate rating

group: NEC: general, branch circuits, feeders, services (Art. 100-230)
title: Floor area for load calculation
applies_to: Load calculation input
check: Use the outside dimensions of the dwelling for floor area; leave out open porches, garages, and unused or unfinished spaces not adaptable for future use. A garage conversion adds its area to the calculation.
edition_difference: Location of the floor-area rule differs between editions (from memory).
note: Section numbers for both editions are from memory and uncertain. Handled by the load calculator.

group: NEC: general, branch circuits, feeders, services (Art. 100-230)
title: Load calculation reminder
applies_to: Service upgrade, panel change, added large loads (range, EVSE, A/C, tankless heater)
check: Run a dwelling load calculation: general lighting at 3 VA per sq ft, 1500 VA per small-appliance circuit, 1500 VA for the laundry circuit, dryer 5000 VA minimum, range per Table 220.55, optional method 220.82, existing-dwelling method 220.83, measured demand 220.87, and (2023) EVSE at 7200 VA or nameplate under 220.57.
edition_difference: 2023 renumbered much of Article 220 and added 220.57 for EV supply equipment.
note: One-line pointer to the separate load calculator, as the brief asks.

group: NEC: general, branch circuits, feeders, services (Art. 100-230)
title: One supply per building
applies_to: Detached garage or accessory building fed from the house
check: Supply a detached building with only one feeder or one branch circuit (a multiwire circuit counts as one), unless a listed special condition applies.
edition_difference: 2023 added limited allowances for multiple feeders (from memory).
note: Source article is older (2011 NEC era).

group: NEC: general, branch circuits, feeders, services (Art. 100-230)
title: Disconnect at detached building
applies_to: Detached garage or accessory building with power
check: Provide a disconnecting means for all ungrounded conductors supplying the building, located inside or outside at a readily accessible point nearest where the conductors enter.
needs: Disconnect shown at detached building (yes/no, location)

group: NEC: general, branch circuits, feeders, services (Art. 100-230)
title: Number of building disconnects
applies_to: Detached building disconnect
check: Not more than six switches or breakers may serve as the building disconnect, grouped together.
edition_difference: 2023 revised the six-disconnect arrangement to parallel 230.71 (from memory).

group: NEC: general, branch circuits, feeders, services (Art. 100-230)
title: Building disconnect type
applies_to: Detached garage or outbuilding on residential property
check: The building disconnect must be a breaker, molded-case switch or switch suitable for the purpose. For garages and outbuildings on residential property a snap switch (or set of 3-way/4-way switches) is acceptable as the disconnect for a branch circuit.

group: NEC: general, branch circuits, feeders, services (Art. 100-230)
title: Building disconnect rating
applies_to: Detached building disconnect
check: Rating at least the calculated load and not less than: 15 A for one branch circuit, 30 A for two 2-wire circuits, 60 A for other feeder-supplied buildings, 100 A 3-wire where the feeder supplies a one-family dwelling.

group: NEC: general, branch circuits, feeders, services (Art. 100-230)
title: Overhead feeder clearances
applies_to: Overhead span to a detached building
check: Overhead conductors up to 300 V: 10 ft above walkways and at the attachment point, 12 ft over residential driveways, 18 ft over streets; 8 ft above a roof (3 ft where the slope is 4:12 or steeper); 3 ft from windows that open, doors, porches and balconies.
note: Site item; shown only if an overhead feeder is noted.

group: NEC: general, branch circuits, feeders, services (Art. 100-230)
title: Emergency disconnect, feeder-fed dwelling
applies_to: One- or two-family dwelling unit supplied by a feeder (e.g. from a remote meter-main or another building)
check: NEC 2023: provide an emergency disconnect outdoors, readily accessible, on or within sight of the dwelling, with a short-circuit rating at least equal to the available fault current, grouped if more than one, and marked EMERGENCY DISCONNECT in white letters at least 1/2 in. high on a red background on the outside front of the enclosure. Post a directory if other power-source disconnects are elsewhere.
edition_difference: New in 2023.
needs: Dwelling is feeder-supplied; outdoor emergency disconnect shown

group: NEC: general, branch circuits, feeders, services (Art. 100-230)
title: Surge protection, outside feeder
applies_to: Outside feeder supplying a dwelling unit or its distribution equipment
check: NEC 2023: an outside feeder supplying a dwelling needs a Type 1 or Type 2 SPD, 10 kA nominal discharge current minimum, in or next to the distribution equipment; applies on replacement of that equipment.
edition_difference: New in 2023.
needs: SPD shown (yes/no)

group: NEC: general, branch circuits, feeders, services (Art. 100-230)
title: One service per building
applies_to: Service upgrade
check: A building is supplied by only one service unless a listed special condition applies.

group: NEC: general, branch circuits, feeders, services (Art. 100-230)
title: Service conductors near openings
applies_to: Overhead service drop and open service conductors
check: Keep open service conductors at least 3 ft from windows that open, doors, porches, balconies, stairs and similar locations (not required above the top of a window). Do not run them beneath openings through which materials may be moved.
note: Bites when a new window or door is added near the service drop.

group: NEC: general, branch circuits, feeders, services (Art. 100-230)
title: Service drop clearances
applies_to: Overhead service on a service upgrade or roof/addition change
check: Overhead service conductors up to 300 V: 8 ft above a roof, reduced to 3 ft where the roof slope is 4:12 or more, or 18 in. over the overhang for a through-the-roof mast with not more than 6 ft of conductor over 4 ft of roof; 10 ft above grade at the drip loop and walkways; 12 ft over residential property and driveways; 18 ft over public streets.
note: Values match the parallel 225.18/225.19 values confirmed in the secondary source for feeders. Utility (FPL) service standards also apply.

group: NEC: general, branch circuits, feeders, services (Art. 100-230)
title: Point of attachment and mast
applies_to: Overhead service upgrade
check: Service point of attachment at least 10 ft above finished grade and high enough to keep the 230.24 clearances. A service mast used as support must be strong enough or braced; only power service-drop conductors may attach to it (no cable TV or phone).

group: NEC: general, branch circuits, feeders, services (Art. 100-230)
title: Service head and drip loops
applies_to: Overhead service upgrade
check: Use a raintight service head located above the point of attachment (or within 24 in. where that is impracticable), form drip loops, bring conductors of different potential out through separately bushed holes, and arrange so water cannot enter.

group: NEC: general, branch circuits, feeders, services (Art. 100-230)
title: Service equipment marking
applies_to: New or replaced service panel, meter-main
check: Service equipment must be listed or field evaluated and marked as suitable for use as service equipment.

group: NEC: general, branch circuits, feeders, services (Art. 100-230)
title: Surge protection at the service
applies_to: New service or replaced service equipment at a dwelling
check: Every service supplying a dwelling unit needs a Type 1 or Type 2 surge-protective device, integral to or immediately next to the service equipment (or instead at each next-level panel downstream). Required whenever service equipment is replaced. NEC 2023 adds a minimum nominal discharge current rating of 10 kA.
edition_difference: 2020: SPD required, no minimum rating. 2023: adds 10 kA minimum In and extends coverage to dormitories, hotel guest rooms and nursing-home sleeping areas.
needs: SPD shown at service (yes/no, type, kA)
note: 2023 changes at https://captaincode2023.leviton.com/node/318. A panel change-out on a service is the usual trigger in a remodel.

group: NEC: general, branch circuits, feeders, services (Art. 100-230)
title: Service disconnect location
applies_to: Service disconnect / main panel location
check: Locate the service disconnect at a readily accessible place outside the building, or inside nearest the point where the service conductors enter. Long unprotected service runs inside the house are not allowed.
needs: Distance from service entry point to main disconnect
note: Source article is 2017-era; unchanged to my knowledge. Many Florida jurisdictions and FPL limit the interior run to a few feet; check locally.

group: NEC: general, branch circuits, feeders, services (Art. 100-230)
title: No service disconnect in bathroom
applies_to: Service disconnect / main panel location
check: The service disconnect may not be in a bathroom.
note: Companion rules for breakers in bathrooms and clothes closets are 240.24(D),(E) (other rule set). Relates to E-16.

group: NEC: general, branch circuits, feeders, services (Art. 100-230)
title: Mark the service disconnect
applies_to: Service disconnect
check: Permanently mark each service disconnect to identify it as a service disconnect.

group: NEC: general, branch circuits, feeders, services (Art. 100-230)
title: Number of service disconnects
applies_to: Service equipment arrangement
check: Each service has one disconnecting means, or two to six only where each is in its own enclosure, separate panelboard, or separate compartment. A single panel with up to six main breakers and no single main is no longer allowed (since 2020).
edition_difference: Same in 2020 and 2023; the old six-handles-in-one-panel arrangement ended with the 2020 NEC.
needs: Number of service disconnects and enclosures
note: Existing split-bus panels may remain but cannot be replaced in kind.

group: NEC: general, branch circuits, feeders, services (Art. 100-230)
title: Group service disconnects
applies_to: Services with two to six disconnects
check: Group the two to six disconnects together and mark each to show the load it serves.

group: NEC: general, branch circuits, feeders, services (Art. 100-230)
title: Occupant access to disconnect
applies_to: Duplex or multi-occupancy building
check: Each occupant must have access to the service disconnect serving their unit.

group: NEC: general, branch circuits, feeders, services (Art. 100-230)
title: Minimum 100 A service
applies_to: Service disconnect for a one-family dwelling
check: The service disconnect for a one-family dwelling must be rated at least 100 A, 3-wire, and never less than the calculated load.
note: Check: service size field at least 100 A and at least the load-calculator result.

group: NEC: general, branch circuits, feeders, services (Art. 100-230)
title: Equipment ahead of the main
applies_to: Meter disconnects, SPDs, PV or generator taps on the supply side
check: Only the listed items may be connected on the supply side of the service disconnect: meter sockets, meter disconnect switches (with required rating and marking), Type 1 SPDs, and supply-side connections for solar, storage or standby systems, among others.

group: NEC: general, branch circuits, feeders, services (Art. 100-230)
title: Outdoor emergency disconnect
applies_to: One- and two-family dwelling services: new service, or service equipment replaced
check: Provide an emergency disconnect at a readily accessible OUTDOOR location (2023: on or within sight of the dwelling), with a short-circuit rating at least equal to the available fault current, grouped if more than one. It may be the service disconnect, a meter disconnect, or another listed switch or breaker ahead of the service disconnect, marked respectively: EMERGENCY DISCONNECT, SERVICE DISCONNECT / EMERGENCY DISCONNECT, METER DISCONNECT, NOT SERVICE EQUIPMENT / EMERGENCY DISCONNECT, NOT SERVICE EQUIPMENT.
edition_difference: 2020: new rule; markings per 110.21(B) only; no replacement clause in the text shown. 2023: adds 'on or within sight of the dwelling'; applies when service equipment is replaced (not when only the meter socket, service-entrance conductors or raceways are replaced); requires a directory of other energy-source disconnects; marking on the outside front, white on red, letters at least 1/2 in. high.
needs: Outdoor emergency disconnect shown (yes/no) and type
note: 2020 text at https://captaincode2020.leviton.com/node/242. An interior main panel with only a meter outside does not comply; a meter-main outside does. Under NEC 2020 whether a panel change-out triggers this is an AHJ call; under 2023 it explicitly does.

group: NEC: general, branch circuits, feeders, services (Art. 100-230)
title: Service overcurrent protection
applies_to: Service entrance conductors and main breaker
check: Each ungrounded service conductor needs overload protection rated not more than its ampacity (next standard size up allowed up to 800 A). Dwelling service conductors may be sized at 83 percent of the service rating under 310.12.
note: Check main breaker rating against service conductor size, e.g. 200 A main: 2/0 Cu or 4/0 Al (310.12 values from memory).

group: NEC: general, branch circuits, feeders, services (Art. 100-230)
title: Main breaker at the disconnect
applies_to: Service equipment
check: The service overcurrent device must be an integral part of the service disconnect or immediately next to it.

group: NEC: overcurrent, grounding, wiring, devices, panels, lighting (Art. 240-410)
title: Next-size-up breaker
applies_to: Circuits and feeders rated 800 A or less
check: Breaker may be the next standard size above the conductor ampacity only when the ampacity does not match a standard rating, the circuit is not a multi-receptacle branch circuit for cord-and-plug loads, and the rating is 800 A or less.

group: NEC: overcurrent, grounding, wiring, devices, panels, lighting (Art. 240-410)
title: Small conductor breaker limits
applies_to: Every circuit with breaker size and wire size
check: Copper: 14 AWG max 15 A, 12 AWG max 20 A, 10 AWG max 30 A. Aluminum or copper-clad aluminum: 12 AWG max 15 A, 10 AWG max 25 A. Flag any circuit whose breaker exceeds the limit for its wire size.
edition_difference: 2023 adds 14 AWG copper-clad aluminum at 10 A and renumbers the list (14 Cu is (D)(4), 12 Cu (D)(6), 10 Cu (D)(8)); 2020 lists 14 Cu as (D)(3), 12 Cu (D)(5), 10 Cu (D)(7).
note: 2023 10 A branch-circuit change confirmed from the Leviton change index; item numbering from memory. Exceptions exist for motor and HVAC equipment circuits sized per 240.4(E)-(G) (nameplate MOCP).

group: NEC: overcurrent, grounding, wiring, devices, panels, lighting (Art. 240-410)
title: Standard breaker ratings
applies_to: Every circuit breaker and fuse
edition_difference: 2023 adds 10 A as a standard rating.
note: 2023 addition of 10 A from memory, consistent with the 10 A branch-circuit change.

group: NEC: overcurrent, grounding, wiring, devices, panels, lighting (Art. 240-410)
title: Breaker in each hot
applies_to: Every circuit
check: Provide an overcurrent device in series with every ungrounded conductor; none in the grounded (neutral) conductor.

group: NEC: overcurrent, grounding, wiring, devices, panels, lighting (Art. 240-410)
title: Handle ties, multiwire and 240 V
applies_to: Circuits flagged as multiwire (shared neutral) or 240 V
check: 240 V circuits and multiwire branch circuits need a 2-pole breaker or single-pole breakers joined by identified handle ties so all hots open together (see also 210.4(B)).
needs: Circuit is multiwire / shared neutral
note: Handle ties must be identified for the purpose; nails or wire are not acceptable.

group: NEC: overcurrent, grounding, wiring, devices, panels, lighting (Art. 240-410)
title: Overcurrent at supply point
applies_to: Feeders to subpanels
check: Protect each feeder and branch circuit at the point where it receives its supply; tap rules of 240.21(B) are rarely applicable in dwellings and need engineering if used.

group: NEC: overcurrent, grounding, wiring, devices, panels, lighting (Art. 240-410)
title: Breaker height and access
applies_to: Panels and subpanels
check: Overcurrent devices must be readily accessible, with the center of the highest breaker handle (in its top position) no more than 6 ft 7 in. above the floor or working platform.
needs: Height of top breaker handle above floor
note: Same 6 ft 7 in. limit as 404.8(A). Replaces part of E-16.

group: NEC: overcurrent, grounding, wiring, devices, panels, lighting (Art. 240-410)
title: Occupant access to breakers
applies_to: Dwellings and two-family units
check: Each occupant must have ready access to all overcurrent devices protecting conductors supplying that occupancy (panel for a unit may not be located inside the other unit of a duplex).

group: NEC: overcurrent, grounding, wiring, devices, panels, lighting (Art. 240-410)
title: Panel not exposed to damage
applies_to: Panels and subpanels
check: Do not locate overcurrent devices where exposed to physical damage (e.g. unprotected in a garage vehicle path).

group: NEC: overcurrent, grounding, wiring, devices, panels, lighting (Art. 240-410)
title: No panel in clothes closet
applies_to: Panels and subpanels; room type
check: Do not locate overcurrent devices near easily ignitible material: flag any panel or subpanel placed in a room typed as clothes closet.
note: Replaces part of E-16. Applies to relocated or new panels; an existing closet panel may remain but most AHJs require correction on a service or panel change.

group: NEC: overcurrent, grounding, wiring, devices, panels, lighting (Art. 240-410)
title: No panel in bathroom
applies_to: Panels and subpanels; room type
check: Do not locate overcurrent devices (other than supplementary protection) in a dwelling bathroom: flag any panel in a room typed as bathroom.
edition_difference: 2023 extends the prohibition to showering facilities and locker rooms with showers; dwelling bathroom rule is the same in both editions.
note: Replaces part of E-16.

group: NEC: overcurrent, grounding, wiring, devices, panels, lighting (Art. 240-410)
title: No panel over steps
applies_to: Panels and subpanels near stairs
check: Do not locate overcurrent devices over the steps of a stairway.
note: Add to E-16; existing rule cites only (D) and (E).

group: NEC: overcurrent, grounding, wiring, devices, panels, lighting (Art. 240-410)
title: Breaker ON position
applies_to: Panels
check: Breakers must clearly indicate open/closed; where handles operate vertically, up is ON.

group: NEC: overcurrent, grounding, wiring, devices, panels, lighting (Art. 240-410)
title: Breaker markings
applies_to: Panels
check: Breakers must be marked with ampere rating visible after installation and have an interrupting rating not less than the available fault current (110.9); use only breakers listed or classified for the panel.

group: NEC: overcurrent, grounding, wiring, devices, panels, lighting (Art. 240-410)
title: Service neutral grounding
applies_to: Service upgrade or service equipment replacement
check: Connect the grounding electrode conductor to the grounded service conductor at the service (between the service drop/lateral connection and the service disconnect neutral terminal).

group: NEC: overcurrent, grounding, wiring, devices, panels, lighting (Art. 240-410)
title: No neutral-ground bond downstream
applies_to: Subpanels and any panel on the load side of the service disconnect
check: Do not connect the neutral to equipment grounding conductors or enclosures at any point past the service disconnect: subpanel neutral bar isolated, bonding screw/strap removed.
needs: Panel is service equipment or subpanel; neutral isolated yes/no
note: See also 250.142(B) and 408.40. An emergency disconnect or meter-main ahead of the old main panel turns the old panel into a subpanel (230.85 in the 2020/2023 NEC).

group: NEC: overcurrent, grounding, wiring, devices, panels, lighting (Art. 240-410)
title: Main bonding jumper
applies_to: Service equipment
check: Install the main bonding jumper (screw, strap or wire supplied with the equipment) connecting the neutral to the enclosure and equipment grounding bar at the service disconnect only.

group: NEC: overcurrent, grounding, wiring, devices, panels, lighting (Art. 240-410)
title: Detached building feeder
applies_to: Subpanel in a detached garage or accessory building
check: A building supplied by a feeder needs its own grounding electrode system connected to the equipment grounding bar, a feeder with a separate equipment grounding conductor, and neutral isolated from ground. A single branch circuit with an EGC needs no electrode.
needs: Subpanel is in a separate building

group: NEC: overcurrent, grounding, wiring, devices, panels, lighting (Art. 240-410)
title: Bond all electrodes present
applies_to: Service upgrade or panel change
check: Bond together every grounding electrode present at the building: metal underground water pipe, concrete-encased electrode (footing rebar) where accessible, ground rods, etc. Existing buildings need not expose footing steel if doing so would disturb concrete.

group: NEC: overcurrent, grounding, wiring, devices, panels, lighting (Art. 240-410)
title: Electrode types and minimums
applies_to: Service upgrade
check: Water pipe electrode: metal pipe in contact with earth 10 ft or more. Concrete-encased: 20 ft of 1/2 in. rebar or 4 AWG bare copper in footing. Rod: at least 8 ft long, 5/8 in. diameter (listed rods may be 1/2 in.).

group: NEC: overcurrent, grounding, wiring, devices, panels, lighting (Art. 240-410)
title: Two ground rods
applies_to: Service upgrade using rod electrodes
check: A single rod must be supplemented by a second electrode unless it tests 25 ohms or less; rods spaced at least 6 ft apart. Standard practice: drive two rods.

group: NEC: overcurrent, grounding, wiring, devices, panels, lighting (Art. 240-410)
title: Water pipe supplemented
applies_to: Service upgrade where metal water pipe is an electrode
check: A metal underground water pipe electrode must be supplemented by another electrode (rod, concrete-encased, etc.).

group: NEC: overcurrent, grounding, wiring, devices, panels, lighting (Art. 240-410)
title: Electrode conductor installation
applies_to: Service upgrade
check: Run the grounding electrode conductor continuous without splice (except listed irreversible means), securely fastened, protected where exposed to damage; aluminum not within 18 in. of earth.

group: NEC: overcurrent, grounding, wiring, devices, panels, lighting (Art. 240-410)
title: Electrode conductor size
applies_to: Service size
check: Size from Table 250.66 by service conductor size: 100 A (4 Cu / 2 Al service conductors) needs 8 AWG Cu; 200 A (2/0 Cu / 4/0 Al) needs 4 AWG Cu. Portion that only connects to rods need not exceed 6 AWG Cu; to a concrete-encased electrode need not exceed 4 AWG Cu.
note: Show on the riser diagram. Computed from service size entered.

group: NEC: overcurrent, grounding, wiring, devices, panels, lighting (Art. 240-410)
title: Electrode connection accessible
applies_to: Service upgrade
check: Electrode conductor connections must be accessible (except buried or encased ones); where interior metal water pipe is used to connect, the connection must be within 5 ft of where the pipe enters the building.

group: NEC: overcurrent, grounding, wiring, devices, panels, lighting (Art. 240-410)
title: Intersystem bonding termination
applies_to: Service upgrade or service equipment replacement
check: Provide an intersystem bonding termination with at least three terminals, accessible, at the service equipment or meter enclosure, for cable TV, phone and other systems.
note: Existing buildings may use the 250.94 alternative means where already present.

group: NEC: overcurrent, grounding, wiring, devices, panels, lighting (Art. 240-410)
title: Bond metal water piping
applies_to: Service upgrade or panel change in a house with metal water piping
check: Bond the metal water piping system to the service enclosure, neutral at the service, or electrode conductor, with a jumper sized from Table 250.102(C)(1) (200 A service: 4 AWG Cu); connection point accessible.
needs: Water piping material (metal / plastic)

group: NEC: overcurrent, grounding, wiring, devices, panels, lighting (Art. 240-410)
title: Bond gas and other metal piping
applies_to: Gas appliances or metal gas piping present
check: Metal piping likely to become energized, including gas piping, must be bonded; the equipment grounding conductor of the circuit serving the appliance may serve as the bond. CSST needs the manufacturer's direct bond (typically 6 AWG Cu, see fuel gas code).

group: NEC: overcurrent, grounding, wiring, devices, panels, lighting (Art. 240-410)
title: Equipment grounding conductor types
applies_to: Every new circuit
check: Every new circuit needs an equipment grounding conductor of a recognized type: copper or aluminum wire, metal conduit/EMT, listed flexible metal conduit within limits (max 6 ft total, circuit 20 A or less), MC or AC cable armor as listed.

group: NEC: overcurrent, grounding, wiring, devices, panels, lighting (Art. 240-410)
title: Ground wire color
applies_to: New wiring
check: Equipment grounding conductors are bare, green, or green with yellow stripe; green insulation may not be used for hots or neutrals.

group: NEC: overcurrent, grounding, wiring, devices, panels, lighting (Art. 240-410)
title: Equipment ground size
applies_to: Every circuit and feeder with breaker size
check: Minimum copper EGC from Table 250.122 by breaker rating: 15 A = 14 AWG, 20 A = 12, 30 to 60 A = 10, 70 to 100 A = 8, 110 to 200 A = 6. Increase proportionally if hots are upsized (e.g. for voltage drop).
note: Checkable from breaker size where wire size and EGC size are recorded; NM cable has the correct EGC built in up to 10 AWG... verify for larger cables.

group: NEC: overcurrent, grounding, wiring, devices, panels, lighting (Art. 240-410)
title: Grounding for replacement and extension
applies_to: Replacing ungrounded receptacles or extending a circuit with no ground wire
check: Where no ground exists in the box, a separate EGC may be run to the panel ground bar, grounding electrode system, electrode conductor, or (2023) another grounded circuit from the same panel. A circuit extension must have an EGC.
edition_difference: 2023 clarifies/extends application to snap switches and branch-circuit extensions.
note: Change list confirms 250.130(C) retitled in 2023 to cover snap switches and extensions; details from memory.

group: NEC: overcurrent, grounding, wiring, devices, panels, lighting (Art. 240-410)
title: Bond fixed equipment
applies_to: New fixed equipment and metal boxes
check: Connect non-current-carrying metal parts of fixed equipment, metal boxes and raceways to the circuit equipment grounding conductor run with the circuit conductors.

group: NEC: overcurrent, grounding, wiring, devices, panels, lighting (Art. 240-410)
title: Range and dryer 4-wire
applies_to: New or relocated range, cooktop, oven or dryer circuit
check: New circuits must be 4-wire (two hots, neutral, separate equipment ground) with a 4-wire receptacle/cord. Only an existing 3-wire branch circuit may keep the frame bonded to the neutral, under the listed conditions.
edition_difference: 2023 reorganizes into (A) EGC connections and (B) grounded-conductor connections for existing circuits and adds conditions; 2020 states it as a rule with an exception.
needs: Range/dryer circuit is new or existing 3-wire
note: Relocating the appliance outlet = new circuit portion; treat as 4-wire required.

group: NEC: overcurrent, grounding, wiring, devices, panels, lighting (Art. 240-410)
title: No neutral as ground downstream
applies_to: Subpanels, appliances, outlets
check: Do not use the neutral to ground equipment on the load side of the service disconnect (no bootleg grounds; separate neutral and ground bars in subpanels).

group: NEC: overcurrent, grounding, wiring, devices, panels, lighting (Art. 240-410)
title: Receptacle bonding to metal box
applies_to: Receptacles in metal boxes
check: Bond the receptacle grounding terminal to the grounded metal box with a jumper unless the device is self-grounding or the box is surface mounted with direct metal-to-metal contact per (A)-(D).

group: NEC: overcurrent, grounding, wiring, devices, panels, lighting (Art. 240-410)
title: Ground splices in boxes
applies_to: Every box
check: All equipment grounding conductors in a box are spliced together; metal boxes get a grounding screw or listed clip used for no other purpose; removal of a device must not interrupt ground continuity.
edition_difference: 2023 rewords and reorganizes the section.

group: NEC: overcurrent, grounding, wiring, devices, panels, lighting (Art. 240-410)
title: Circuit conductors together
applies_to: New circuits
check: All conductors of a circuit (hots, neutral, ground) run in the same cable or raceway.

group: NEC: overcurrent, grounding, wiring, devices, panels, lighting (Art. 240-410)
title: Bored holes 1-1/4 in.
applies_to: New wiring through wood studs, joists
check: Edge of bored hole at least 1-1/4 in. from the nearest edge of the wood member; otherwise protect with a steel plate at least 1/16 in. thick (or listed plate).
note: Checklist item: nail plates. Framing holes must also meet the building code boring limits.

group: NEC: overcurrent, grounding, wiring, devices, panels, lighting (Art. 240-410)
title: Notches in wood
applies_to: Cables laid in notches
check: Cables in notches need a steel plate at least 1/16 in. thick over the notch before finish is applied.

group: NEC: overcurrent, grounding, wiring, devices, panels, lighting (Art. 240-410)
title: Metal studs
applies_to: NM cable through metal framing
check: NM cable through metal studs needs listed bushings or grommets in every hole, and a steel plate/sleeve where nails or screws are likely to penetrate.
needs: Wall framing is metal stud

group: NEC: overcurrent, grounding, wiring, devices, panels, lighting (Art. 240-410)
title: Cables parallel to framing
applies_to: Cables run along studs, joists, furring
check: Keep cable at least 1-1/4 in. back from the nearest edge of the framing member where nails or screws are likely, or protect with a 1/16 in. steel plate.

group: NEC: overcurrent, grounding, wiring, devices, panels, lighting (Art. 240-410)
title: Wiring under roof decking
applies_to: Cables or boxes under metal-corrugated roof decking
check: Keep cables, raceways and boxes at least 1-1/2 in. below the lowest surface of metal-corrugated sheet roof decking.
edition_difference: 2023 adds exceptions (concrete over the decking; RMC/IMC with listed steel fittings).

group: NEC: overcurrent, grounding, wiring, devices, panels, lighting (Art. 240-410)
title: Cables in shallow grooves
applies_to: Cables in grooves in walls (e.g. furred masonry, foam)
check: Cable in a groove covered by finish needs a 1/16 in. steel plate or at least 1-1/4 in. of free space for its full length.

group: NEC: overcurrent, grounding, wiring, devices, panels, lighting (Art. 240-410)
title: Bushings 4 AWG and larger
applies_to: Feeders in raceway
check: Raceways with 4 AWG or larger insulated conductors entering an enclosure need an insulated bushing or fitting, installed before conductors are pulled.
edition_difference: 2023 adds that the fitting must be in place before pulling.

group: NEC: overcurrent, grounding, wiring, devices, panels, lighting (Art. 240-410)
title: Raceways in wet locations
applies_to: Exterior raceways above grade
check: Interior of raceways in wet locations above grade is a wet location: conductors must be wet-rated (e.g. THWN); NM cable is not permitted inside them.

group: NEC: overcurrent, grounding, wiring, devices, panels, lighting (Art. 240-410)
title: Secure wiring; no ceiling-wire support
applies_to: New wiring; suspended (ACT) ceilings
check: Secure all raceways, cables and boxes in place. Do not support cables or boxes from ceiling grid or its support wires; use independent, identified support wires secured at both ends.
needs: Ceiling is ACT/suspended grid

group: NEC: overcurrent, grounding, wiring, devices, panels, lighting (Art. 240-410)
title: Continuous cable sheath
applies_to: New wiring
check: Cable sheath and raceways run continuous between boxes and enclosures.

group: NEC: overcurrent, grounding, wiring, devices, panels, lighting (Art. 240-410)
title: Pigtail neutrals on multiwire
applies_to: Multiwire branch circuits
check: Neutral continuity must not depend on a device: pigtail the neutral at each receptacle on a multiwire circuit.

group: NEC: overcurrent, grounding, wiring, devices, panels, lighting (Art. 240-410)
title: 6 in. free conductor
applies_to: Every box
check: Leave at least 6 in. of free conductor at each box, measured from where it emerges from the cable sheath or raceway; where the box opening is under 8 in. in any dimension, conductors must reach at least 3 in. outside the opening.
edition_difference: 2023 allows spliced conductors to satisfy the length.

group: NEC: overcurrent, grounding, wiring, devices, panels, lighting (Art. 240-410)
title: Box at every splice and device
applies_to: Every outlet, switch, splice
check: Every splice, outlet, switch point and junction needs a box or listed fitting; no splices buried in walls or flying splices.

group: NEC: overcurrent, grounding, wiring, devices, panels, lighting (Art. 240-410)
title: Firestop penetrations
applies_to: New wiring through rated assemblies, top plates, garage separation
check: Seal electrical penetrations through fire-resistance-rated walls, floors and ceilings with approved firestop methods; maintain the rating. (Fireblocking of plates per FBC-R R302.11.)

group: NEC: overcurrent, grounding, wiring, devices, panels, lighting (Art. 240-410)
title: No NM in ducts or plenums
applies_to: Wiring near returns and air-handling spaces
check: NM cable is not allowed in fabricated ducts or in spaces used for environmental air. Dwelling exception: cable may pass through a joist or stud cavity used as a return only perpendicular to the long dimension of the cavity.

group: NEC: overcurrent, grounding, wiring, devices, panels, lighting (Art. 240-410)
title: Wet-location conductors
applies_to: Conductors in exterior or underground raceways
check: Conductors in wet locations must be listed for wet use (W in the type, e.g. THWN, XHHW).

group: NEC: overcurrent, grounding, wiring, devices, panels, lighting (Art. 240-410)
title: Dwelling service and feeder 83%
applies_to: Service size 100 to 400 A, 120/240 V single-phase; main feeder to a panel carrying the whole dwelling load
check: Service conductors and a feeder supplying the entire dwelling load may be sized at 83% of the service rating: 100 A = 4 Cu or 2 Al; 125 A = 2 Cu or 1/0 Al; 150 A = 1 Cu or 2/0 Al; 200 A = 2/0 Cu or 4/0 Al. Feeders to subpanels carrying part of the load use Table 310.16 instead.
edition_difference: Table is Table 310.12(A) in 2023, Table 310.12 in 2020.
note: Before derating; if adjustment/correction factors apply, they must be applied to the reduced conductor.

group: NEC: overcurrent, grounding, wiring, devices, panels, lighting (Art. 240-410)
title: Ambient temperature correction
applies_to: Circuits routed through attics
check: Correct ampacity for ambient temperature above 86 F (Florida attics: commonly 0.87 to 0.71 factors applied to the 90 C ampacity); result may not be below the breaker rating per 240.4.
needs: Circuit runs through attic; design ambient temperature
note: Rooftop raceway adder is 310.15(B)(2).

group: NEC: overcurrent, grounding, wiring, devices, panels, lighting (Art. 240-410)
title: More than three current-carrying conductors
applies_to: Circuits bundled or sharing a raceway
check: Adjust ampacity when more than three current-carrying conductors share a raceway or are bundled more than 24 in.: 4-6 = 80%, 7-9 = 70%, 10-20 = 50%, starting from the 90 C ampacity.
needs: Number of current-carrying conductors bundled / in same raceway

group: NEC: overcurrent, grounding, wiring, devices, panels, lighting (Art. 240-410)
title: Ampacity table and terminations
applies_to: Every circuit and feeder
check: Copper ampacity at 60 C / 75 C: 14 AWG 15/20, 12 AWG 20/25, 10 AWG 30/35, 8 AWG 40/50, 6 AWG 55/65, 4 AWG 70/85, 2 AWG 95/115. Circuits 100 A or less (14 to 1 AWG) use the 60 C column unless all terminations are rated 75 C; NM cable always 60 C.
note: Feeder to subpanel: check wire size against breaker with these columns.

group: NEC: overcurrent, grounding, wiring, devices, panels, lighting (Art. 240-410)
title: Panels in damp or wet locations
applies_to: Exterior panels, meter-mains
check: Enclosures in damp or wet locations must be weatherproof and mounted with at least 1/4 in. air space from the wall (nonmetallic excepted on masonry).
needs: Panel location is exterior / damp / wet

group: NEC: overcurrent, grounding, wiring, devices, panels, lighting (Art. 240-410)
title: Flush panel setback and gaps
applies_to: Flush-mounted panels in new or patched walls
check: Cabinet front edge set back no more than 1/4 in. in noncombustible finish; flush or projecting in combustible finish. Patch gaps around the cabinet so none exceeds 1/8 in.

group: NEC: overcurrent, grounding, wiring, devices, panels, lighting (Art. 240-410)
title: Cables secured to panel
applies_to: Panel changes and new homeruns
check: Each cable entering the cabinet is secured to it with a connector; no more cables per connector than listed.

group: NEC: overcurrent, grounding, wiring, devices, panels, lighting (Art. 240-410)
title: Splices in panel
applies_to: Panel replacement where conductors are extended
check: Splices are allowed in a panel enclosure only if wiring space is adequate: conductors fill no more than 40% of the gutter cross-section, splices no more than 75%.

group: NEC: overcurrent, grounding, wiring, devices, panels, lighting (Art. 240-410)
title: Screws entering panel
applies_to: Panels and meter sockets
check: Field-installed screws or fasteners entering the wiring space must not damage conductors (use the screws supplied; limited projection).
edition_difference: New in 2023; not in 2020.

group: NEC: overcurrent, grounding, wiring, devices, panels, lighting (Art. 240-410)
title: Box material and grounding
applies_to: New boxes
check: Nonmetallic boxes only with NM cable or nonmetallic raceways (unless internal bonding provided); metal boxes must be grounded and bonded.

group: NEC: overcurrent, grounding, wiring, devices, panels, lighting (Art. 240-410)
title: Screws in boxes
applies_to: New boxes
check: Screws entering the box wiring space must be machine screws or protected so they cannot damage conductors; drywall screws are not acceptable.
edition_difference: New in 2023; not in 2020.

group: NEC: overcurrent, grounding, wiring, devices, panels, lighting (Art. 240-410)
title: Boxes in damp or wet locations
applies_to: Exterior boxes, boxes in showers or wet areas
check: Boxes in damp or wet locations must be listed for wet locations and placed/equipped to keep water out.
needs: Box location is damp or wet

group: NEC: overcurrent, grounding, wiring, devices, panels, lighting (Art. 240-410)
title: Box volume vs fill
applies_to: Every device and junction box
check: Box volume (marked on nonmetallic boxes, or Table 314.16(A) for metal, plus extension rings/domed covers marked with volume) must be at least the calculated fill of 314.16(B).
needs: Box volume in cubic inches; conductors, devices and clamps in the box

group: NEC: overcurrent, grounding, wiring, devices, panels, lighting (Art. 240-410)
title: Volume per conductor
applies_to: Box fill calculation
check: Volume allowance per conductor: 18 AWG 1.5 cu in.; 16 AWG 1.75; 14 AWG 2.0; 12 AWG 2.25; 10 AWG 2.5; 8 AWG 3.0; 6 AWG 5.0.
note: Values from memory; widely published and unchanged for many cycles.

group: NEC: overcurrent, grounding, wiring, devices, panels, lighting (Art. 240-410)
title: Conductor fill count
applies_to: Box fill calculation
check: Count 1 for each conductor that enters and is spliced or terminated, 1 for each conductor passing through unbroken, 2 for an unbroken loop at least 12 in. long; pigtails and jumpers that stay in the box count 0.
needs: Conductor count per box

group: NEC: overcurrent, grounding, wiring, devices, panels, lighting (Art. 240-410)
title: Clamp and fitting fill
applies_to: Box fill calculation
check: Add 1 allowance (largest conductor in the box) if the box has one or more internal cable clamps; add 1 for each type of fixture stud or hickey.
needs: Box has internal clamps

group: NEC: overcurrent, grounding, wiring, devices, panels, lighting (Art. 240-410)
title: Device fill
applies_to: Box fill calculation
check: Add 2 allowances for each device yoke (switch, receptacle), based on the largest conductor connected to that device; a device wider than a single 2 in. gang box (e.g. range receptacle) counts 2 per gang required.
needs: Devices per box

group: NEC: overcurrent, grounding, wiring, devices, panels, lighting (Art. 240-410)
