title: Ground wire fill
applies_to: Box fill calculation
check: Up to four equipment grounding conductors count as 1 allowance of the largest EGC; each additional EGC adds 1/4 allowance.
edition_difference: Same in 2020 and 2023 (changed from the 2017 single allowance). 2023 adds (B)(6) for terminal block assemblies.
needs: Ground wires per box
note: (B)(6) terminal-block item confirmed; (B)(5) quarter-allowance from memory.

group: NEC: overcurrent, grounding, wiring, devices, panels, lighting (Art. 240-410)
title: NM cable entry to box
applies_to: Every nonmetallic box with NM cable
check: Cable sheath must extend at least 1/4 in. inside the box and the cable must be secured to the box. Exception: single-gang nonmetallic box (max 2-1/4 x 4 in.) where cable is stapled within 8 in. of the box. Close unused openings.
edition_difference: 2023 reorganized 314.17 subsections; exact 2023 lettering not confirmed.
note: St. Paul 2023 checklist still cites 314.17(C).

group: NEC: overcurrent, grounding, wiring, devices, panels, lighting (Art. 240-410)
title: Box flush with finish
applies_to: Every flush box; walls with added layers (tile, backsplash, wainscot, shiplap)
check: In noncombustible finish (drywall, tile, plaster) the box front may be set back no more than 1/4 in.; in combustible finish (wood paneling, wood backsplash) box or extension must be flush or project. Use box extenders where tile or new layers are added over existing boxes.
needs: Finish material at device (combustible / noncombustible) and added finish thickness
note: AUTO-flag candidates: existing boxes on walls receiving new tile or an added layer thicker than 1/4 in.

group: NEC: overcurrent, grounding, wiring, devices, panels, lighting (Art. 240-410)
title: Gaps around boxes
applies_to: Flush boxes in drywall or plaster
check: Repair finish so no gap around a flush box with a faceplate exceeds 1/8 in.

group: NEC: overcurrent, grounding, wiring, devices, panels, lighting (Art. 240-410)
title: Surface extensions
applies_to: Extending from an existing flush box
check: A surface extension from a flush box needs an extension ring mounted over the box (or a flexible wiring method from a secured cover per the exception).

group: NEC: overcurrent, grounding, wiring, devices, panels, lighting (Art. 240-410)
title: Box support
applies_to: Every box
check: Boxes rigidly secured: fastened to framing or a brace (wood brace min. nominal 1 x 2), or old-work boxes with listed clamps in the finished surface; boxes in suspended ceilings fastened to framing members or independent support wires.

group: NEC: overcurrent, grounding, wiring, devices, panels, lighting (Art. 240-410)
title: Box depth
applies_to: Boxes for devices and large conductors
check: Boxes must be deep enough for the device without damage to conductors; outlet boxes with no device at least 1/2 in. deep; devices over 1-7/8 in. deep need a box at least 1/4 in. deeper than the device.
note: Depth figures from memory; verify before quoting to a reviewer.

group: NEC: overcurrent, grounding, wiring, devices, panels, lighting (Art. 240-410)
title: Covers on every box
applies_to: Every box incl. abandoned ones
check: Each box needs a cover, faceplate, lampholder or luminaire canopy; metal covers grounded. Blank off abandoned outlets, never bury them.

group: NEC: overcurrent, grounding, wiring, devices, panels, lighting (Art. 240-410)
title: Luminaire boxes
applies_to: Every light location
check: Wall luminaire boxes are marked with max weight if less than 50 lb; a device box may carry a wall luminaire up to 6 lb with two No. 6 screws. Ceiling luminaire boxes must support 50 lb; luminaires over 50 lb need support independent of the box unless the box is listed for the weight.
needs: Luminaire weight

group: NEC: overcurrent, grounding, wiring, devices, panels, lighting (Art. 240-410)
title: Floor boxes
applies_to: Floor receptacles
check: Receptacles in a floor require a box listed specifically for floor use.
note: Flag any receptacle placed in a floor: require listed floor box note.

group: NEC: overcurrent, grounding, wiring, devices, panels, lighting (Art. 240-410)
title: Fan-rated ceiling boxes
applies_to: Ceiling fans; ceiling light outlets in habitable rooms
check: A box used as sole support of a ceiling fan must be listed and marked for fan support, max 70 lb, with the weight marked if rated over 35 lb. In addition, ceiling outlet boxes in habitable rooms of dwellings at a location acceptable for a fan must be fan-rated or give access to structural framing able to carry a fan.
edition_difference: Requirement for all habitable-room ceiling boxes entered in the 2020 NEC (earlier tied to spare switched conductors) and remains in 2023.
note: AUTO: any ceiling light outlet in a bedroom, living, dining, family room or den that is not flagged fan-rated. Florida: 8th Edition uses the 2020 NEC so the rule applies under both editions.

group: NEC: overcurrent, grounding, wiring, devices, panels, lighting (Art. 240-410)
title: Boxes supporting equipment
applies_to: Wall-hung equipment on boxes
check: Boxes supporting utilization equipment other than fans follow the luminaire limits; equipment up to 6 lb may be carried by a device box with two No. 6 screws.

group: NEC: overcurrent, grounding, wiring, devices, panels, lighting (Art. 240-410)
title: Weight-supporting ceiling receptacles
applies_to: Quick-connect ceiling receptacles for lights/fans
check: Listed locking support and mounting receptacles (weight-supporting ceiling receptacles) may be used within their listing and the box weight limits.
edition_difference: 2023 retitles and expands (E) for WSCR/WSAF devices.

group: NEC: overcurrent, grounding, wiring, devices, panels, lighting (Art. 240-410)
title: Pull boxes 4 AWG and larger
applies_to: Feeders spliced or pulled through boxes
check: Boxes with 4 AWG or larger conductors: straight pulls at least 8 times the largest raceway trade size long; angle pulls and splices 6 times plus sum of other raceways.

group: NEC: overcurrent, grounding, wiring, devices, panels, lighting (Art. 240-410)
title: Junction boxes accessible
applies_to: All junction boxes; demolished or relocated devices
check: Boxes must remain accessible without removing any part of the building: no junction boxes buried behind drywall, tile, cabinets fixed over them, or backsplash. Boxes above an ACT or attic space are acceptable.
edition_difference: 2023 splits into (A) in buildings and (B) underground.
needs: Abandoned or relocated outlet: box removed, or left accessible with blank cover
note: Flag: existing device on a wall being covered by new cabinets, tile wainscot or a new wall layer.

group: NEC: overcurrent, grounding, wiring, devices, panels, lighting (Art. 240-410)
title: AC cable basics
applies_to: AC (BX) cable if used
check: Secure within 12 in. of each box and at intervals not over 4.5 ft; install an anti-short bushing at every termination.

group: NEC: overcurrent, grounding, wiring, devices, panels, lighting (Art. 240-410)
title: MC cable basics
applies_to: MC cable if used
check: Secure at intervals not over 6 ft and within 12 in. of each box for cables with four or fewer conductors 10 AWG or smaller; bends not tighter than 7 times cable diameter for interlocked armor.

group: NEC: overcurrent, grounding, wiring, devices, panels, lighting (Art. 240-410)
title: NM cable permitted uses
applies_to: Wiring method = NM (Romex)
check: NM cable is permitted in one- and two-family dwellings and their attached or detached garages and storage buildings, in normally dry locations, exposed or concealed, including air voids of block or tile walls not subject to excessive moisture.
note: Townhouses of Type III, IV, V construction also permitted.

group: NEC: overcurrent, grounding, wiring, devices, panels, lighting (Art. 240-410)
title: NM cable prohibited uses
applies_to: Wiring method = NM; exterior walls, slabs, block walls, wet areas
check: Not as service-entrance cable; not embedded in poured concrete, cement or aggregate; not embedded in masonry, adobe, fill or plaster or in a plastered chase; not in wet or damp locations (including inside exterior or underground conduit).
needs: Wiring method per circuit; wall type CMU/concrete
note: Florida CBS houses: NM on exterior block walls must be in the furred cavity (see 300.4(D),(F)) or use conduit with THWN in direct-embedded runs.

group: NEC: overcurrent, grounding, wiring, devices, panels, lighting (Art. 240-410)
title: Exposed NM cable
applies_to: NM run exposed (garage, utility, unfinished spaces)
check: Exposed cable must closely follow the building surface or running boards and be protected from physical damage where needed by conduit, EMT, guard strips or similar; where passing through a floor, sleeve it at least 6 in. above the floor.
edition_difference: 2023 revises 334.15(B) protection wording.

group: NEC: overcurrent, grounding, wiring, devices, panels, lighting (Art. 240-410)
title: NM in crawl spaces and unfinished basements
applies_to: Crawl space wiring
check: Cables smaller than two 6 AWG or three 8 AWG may not be stapled to the bottom of joists: run through bored holes or on running boards.

group: NEC: overcurrent, grounding, wiring, devices, panels, lighting (Art. 240-410)
title: NM through framing
applies_to: New NM wiring
check: Through studs, joists and rafters, protect per 300.4; grommets required in metal studs.

group: NEC: overcurrent, grounding, wiring, devices, panels, lighting (Art. 240-410)
title: NM in attics
applies_to: New NM wiring in accessible attics
check: Per 320.23: cable run across the top of ceiling joists, or across studs/rafters within 7 ft of the attic floor, needs guard strips at least as high as the cable. Where the attic has no permanent stairs or ladder, protection is needed only within 6 ft of the scuttle hole edge. Cable along the sides of joists/rafters needs no guards.
edition_difference: 2023 320.23(A) says framing members instead of joists.
needs: Attic access type (scuttle / pull-down stair / permanent stair) and hatch location
note: With attic hatch in the model: remind for circuits routed within 6 ft of the hatch.

group: NEC: overcurrent, grounding, wiring, devices, panels, lighting (Art. 240-410)
title: NM bend radius
applies_to: New NM wiring
check: Bends not tighter than 5 times the cable diameter (major dimension for flat cable).

group: NEC: overcurrent, grounding, wiring, devices, panels, lighting (Art. 240-410)
title: NM securing and support
applies_to: New NM wiring
check: Staple or strap at intervals not over 4.5 ft and within 12 in. of every box, cabinet or fitting; cable between the box and the nearest support not longer than 18 in.; flat cable not stapled on edge.
edition_difference: 18 in. slack limit added in 2020; same in 2023.

group: NEC: overcurrent, grounding, wiring, devices, panels, lighting (Art. 240-410)
title: NM support exceptions
applies_to: Horizontal runs; fished cable; luminaire whips
check: Cable through bored holes in framing spaced 4.5 ft or less counts as supported (still secure within 12 in. of boxes). Cable fished in finished walls/ceilings may be unsupported; up to 4.5 ft unsupported from the last support to a luminaire or equipment in an accessible ceiling.

group: NEC: overcurrent, grounding, wiring, devices, panels, lighting (Art. 240-410)
title: Boxless devices
applies_to: Self-contained (boxless) devices
check: Listed self-contained switches/receptacles of insulating material may be used without a box only for exposed work and for rewiring in existing buildings where the cable is concealed and fished.

group: NEC: overcurrent, grounding, wiring, devices, panels, lighting (Art. 240-410)
title: NM ampacity 60 C
applies_to: Every NM circuit
check: NM ampacity is limited to the 60 C column (14 AWG = 15 A, 12 = 20 A, 10 = 30 A, 8 = 40 A, 6 = 55 A); the 90 C rating may be used only as the starting point for derating.
note: E.g. 50 A range circuit on NM needs 6 AWG Cu; 8 AWG NM is limited to 40 A.

group: NEC: overcurrent, grounding, wiring, devices, panels, lighting (Art. 240-410)
title: NM bundling and insulation derating
applies_to: Multiple NM cables through one hole or bundled in insulation
check: Where more than two NM cables with two or more current-carrying conductors pass through the same hole in wood framing that is sealed with caulk/foam/insulation, or are in contact with thermal insulation without spacing, apply the 310.15(C)(1) adjustment (4-6 conductors 80%, 7-9 70%, 10-20 50%).
note: Practical limit: no more than 4 two-wire cables (9 conductors or fewer) per hole for 14 and 12 AWG without downsizing the breaker.

group: NEC: overcurrent, grounding, wiring, devices, panels, lighting (Art. 240-410)
title: NM construction
applies_to: NM cable
check: NM conductors 14 through 2 AWG copper (12 through 2 aluminum), 90 C insulation (NM-B), with an equipment grounding conductor.

group: NEC: overcurrent, grounding, wiring, devices, panels, lighting (Art. 240-410)
title: SE cable for feeders and ranges
applies_to: Subpanel feeders, range/dryer circuits in SE cable
check: Interior SE cable follows the NM installation rules. A feeder to a subpanel or a new range/dryer circuit needs an insulated neutral and separate ground: use SER (4-conductor), not SEU with a bare neutral. Where run in thermal insulation, 10 AWG and smaller use 60 C ampacity; larger sizes use the termination rating (commonly 75 C).
note: Ampacity-in-insulation wording changed across cycles; verify for the edition used.

group: NEC: overcurrent, grounding, wiring, devices, panels, lighting (Art. 240-410)
title: SE cable bends
applies_to: SE cable
check: Bends not tighter than 5 times the cable diameter.

group: NEC: overcurrent, grounding, wiring, devices, panels, lighting (Art. 240-410)
title: Flexible metal conduit
applies_to: FMC whips to luminaires, disposals, equipment
check: 3/8 in. FMC only in lengths up to 6 ft (luminaire whips, equipment). Secure within 12 in. of each box and every 4.5 ft; up to 3 ft unsecured where flexibility is needed at the terminal; up to 6 ft for a luminaire whip in an accessible ceiling.

group: NEC: overcurrent, grounding, wiring, devices, panels, lighting (Art. 240-410)
title: Ground in flex
applies_to: FMC and LFMC
check: FMC serves as the equipment ground only where total length is 6 ft or less, circuit 20 A or less, and listed fittings; otherwise, and wherever installed for flexibility after installation, pull a wire-type EGC.

group: NEC: overcurrent, grounding, wiring, devices, panels, lighting (Art. 240-410)
title: Liquidtight flexible metal conduit
applies_to: Whips to A/C condenser, water heater, exterior equipment
check: Secure within 12 in. of each box and every 4.5 ft; up to 3 ft unsecured at terminals where flexibility is needed.

group: NEC: overcurrent, grounding, wiring, devices, panels, lighting (Art. 240-410)
title: Liquidtight nonmetallic conduit
applies_to: LFNC whips
check: Secure at intervals not over 3 ft and within 12 in. of each box; lengths up to 3 ft at terminals need no securing where flexibility is needed.

group: NEC: overcurrent, grounding, wiring, devices, panels, lighting (Art. 240-410)
title: EMT
applies_to: EMT runs (garage, exposed work, masonry)
check: Secure within 3 ft of each box and at intervals not over 10 ft; no more than 360 degrees of bends between pull points; ream cut ends.
edition_difference: 2023 raises max EMT trade size to 6 (not relevant to dwellings).

group: NEC: overcurrent, grounding, wiring, devices, panels, lighting (Art. 240-410)
title: ENT (smurf tube)
applies_to: ENT in walls or slabs
check: ENT is permitted concealed in walls, floors and ceilings of dwellings and embedded in concrete with listed fittings; not exposed where subject to damage. Secure every 3 ft and within 3 ft of each box.

group: NEC: overcurrent, grounding, wiring, devices, panels, lighting (Art. 240-410)
title: PVC conduit
applies_to: PVC runs (slab, exterior, masonry)
check: Support per table (1/2 to 1 in. every 3 ft) and within 3 ft of each box; expansion fittings where length change is 1/4 in. or more.

group: NEC: overcurrent, grounding, wiring, devices, panels, lighting (Art. 240-410)
title: Flexible cord permitted uses
applies_to: Cord-connected appliances, pendants
check: Flexible cord is permitted for pendants, luminaire wiring, and connection of appliances designed for cord connection (disposal, dishwasher, range hood, range, dryer per Article 422), with a plug into a receptacle.
note: Cord lengths for disposal/dishwasher/hood are in 422.16 (other catalog area).

group: NEC: overcurrent, grounding, wiring, devices, panels, lighting (Art. 240-410)
title: No cord as fixed wiring
applies_to: Appliances, under-cabinet lights, TVs, microwaves, hoods
check: Flexible cord may not substitute for fixed wiring; may not run through holes in walls, ceilings, floors or cabinets-as-structure, through doors or windows, be attached to building surfaces, or be concealed behind walls or ceilings or above suspended ceilings. Receptacle must be in the same space as the appliance.
note: Common remodel hits: wall-mounted TV cord in wall, microwave cord through cabinet into another space, extension-cord wiring for under-cabinet lights.

group: NEC: overcurrent, grounding, wiring, devices, panels, lighting (Art. 240-410)
title: Cord protection
applies_to: Cord-connected appliances
check: Protect cords with bushings where they pass through holes in covers, boxes or enclosures.
note: Section number for this item uncertain between editions.

group: NEC: overcurrent, grounding, wiring, devices, panels, lighting (Art. 240-410)
title: Three-way/four-way switching
applies_to: Three-way and four-way switch groups
check: All switching is done in the ungrounded (hot) conductor; travelers and switched legs in the same cable or raceway.

group: NEC: overcurrent, grounding, wiring, devices, panels, lighting (Art. 240-410)
title: Do not switch the neutral
applies_to: Every switch
check: Switches may not open the grounded (neutral) conductor unless all conductors of the circuit open simultaneously.

group: NEC: overcurrent, grounding, wiring, devices, panels, lighting (Art. 240-410)
title: Neutral at switch boxes
applies_to: New lighting switch locations in bathrooms, hallways, stairways and habitable rooms
check: Provide a neutral conductor at each new lighting switch box. Not required where: raceway allows adding one later; the box is accessible for adding cable without removing finish; a boxless snap switch is used; lighting is automatically controlled (occupancy sensor); the switch controls only a receptacle; or, with multiple switch locations seeing the whole area, at more than one location.
edition_difference: Same substance in 2020 and 2023; exception list reformatted.
note: AUTO: every new switch controlling lighting in the listed rooms gets a neutral-required note (3-wire switch loops). Electronic switches without neutral limited to 5 per branch circuit / 25 per feeder.

group: NEC: overcurrent, grounding, wiring, devices, panels, lighting (Art. 240-410)
title: Switches enclosed
applies_to: Every switch
check: Switches must be in listed enclosures/boxes.

group: NEC: overcurrent, grounding, wiring, devices, panels, lighting (Art. 240-410)
title: Switches in damp or wet locations
applies_to: Exterior switches, switches at pool/patio, near showers
check: Surface-mounted switch in a damp or wet location needs a weatherproof enclosure; flush-mounted needs a weatherproof cover.
needs: Switch location is damp or wet

group: NEC: overcurrent, grounding, wiring, devices, panels, lighting (Art. 240-410)
title: No switch in tub or shower space
applies_to: Switches near tubs and showers
check: No switch within the tub or shower space itself unless part of a listed tub/shower assembly. Flag any switch placed inside the tub or shower footprint.
note: Code does not set a horizontal distance outside the space; good practice is out of reach of a person in the tub/shower.

group: NEC: overcurrent, grounding, wiring, devices, panels, lighting (Art. 240-410)
title: Switch ON/OFF indication
applies_to: Switches and breakers
check: General-use and motor-circuit switches and breakers indicate ON/OFF; vertical handles are ON when up (three-way/four-way exempt).

group: NEC: overcurrent, grounding, wiring, devices, panels, lighting (Art. 240-410)
title: Switch height max 6 ft 7 in.
applies_to: Every switch
check: Switch operable from a readily accessible place, center of the handle grip in its highest position no more than 6 ft 7 in. above the floor or platform. No code minimum height.
edition_difference: 2023 converts the former exceptions into list items.
note: Florida accessibility heights (48 in. max) apply only to covered dwelling types, not to typical single-family remodels.

group: NEC: overcurrent, grounding, wiring, devices, panels, lighting (Art. 240-410)
title: Voltage between adjacent devices
applies_to: Ganged switches/receptacles
check: Snap switches may not be ganged with other switches or receptacles where voltage between adjacent devices exceeds 300 V unless barriers are installed.
note: Rare in dwellings (120/240 V).

group: NEC: overcurrent, grounding, wiring, devices, panels, lighting (Art. 240-410)
title: Switch faceplates
applies_to: Every switch
check: Faceplate fully covers the opening and, for flush boxes, seats against the finished wall surface.

group: NEC: overcurrent, grounding, wiring, devices, panels, lighting (Art. 240-410)
title: Grounding switches
applies_to: Every switch; replacement switches on old 2-wire circuits
check: Switch yokes (incl. dimmers) and metal faceplates connect to the equipment grounding conductor. Replacement where no ground exists: use a nonmetallic faceplate with nonmetallic screws, or provide GFCI protection.

group: NEC: overcurrent, grounding, wiring, devices, panels, lighting (Art. 240-410)
title: Switch mounting
applies_to: Flush switches
check: Switch in a set-back box: mounting ears seated against the finished surface; in a flush box, yoke seated against the box. Mounting screws must be machine screws (32 threads per inch) or the type supplied.

group: NEC: overcurrent, grounding, wiring, devices, panels, lighting (Art. 240-410)
title: Switch enclosure grounding
applies_to: Metal switch boxes
check: Metal switch enclosures connected to the equipment grounding conductor; nonmetallic boxes with metal raceway need bonding provisions.

group: NEC: overcurrent, grounding, wiring, devices, panels, lighting (Art. 240-410)
title: Switch ratings
applies_to: Every switch; switched motor/fan/receptacle loads
check: Use switches within their rating: resistive, inductive and LED/fluorescent loads up to the switch ampere rating at rated voltage; motor loads not over 80% of the switch rating. Aluminum wiring needs CO/ALR switches (20 A or less).
needs: Switched load in amps; switch rating

group: NEC: overcurrent, grounding, wiring, devices, panels, lighting (Art. 240-410)
title: Push-in terminals 14 AWG only
applies_to: Switches wired with push-in (back-stab) terminals
check: Push-in terminations on snap switches only with 14 AWG solid copper on 15 A circuits unless listed otherwise.
edition_difference: New in 2023; not in 2020.

group: NEC: overcurrent, grounding, wiring, devices, panels, lighting (Art. 240-410)
title: Dimmer loads
applies_to: Dimmers
check: General-use dimmers control only permanently installed incandescent luminaires unless listed for the specific load (LED, fan, low-voltage). Do not dim receptacles or use a lamp dimmer on a fan motor.
edition_difference: Subsection letter may be shifted by the new 2023 (D)(3); sources disagree whether dimmers are (E) or (F) in 2023.
needs: Dimmer listed for the connected load type (LED / fan)
note: Flag AUTO: dimmer assigned to a ceiling fan motor or to a receptacle.

group: NEC: overcurrent, grounding, wiring, devices, panels, lighting (Art. 240-410)
title: Switched cord-and-plug loads
applies_to: Switches controlling receptacles
check: A snap switch controlling a receptacle or cord-connected equipment must be rated at least for the receptacle rating or the branch-circuit rating (15 A switch on a 15 A receptacle; 20 A switch where controlling a 20 A receptacle).
edition_difference: 2020 lettering; 2023 letter may be shifted by one.

group: NEC: overcurrent, grounding, wiring, devices, panels, lighting (Art. 240-410)
title: Electronic control switches
applies_to: Smart switches, occupancy sensors, electronic dimmers
check: Electronic control switches must be listed and may not put operating current on the equipment grounding conductor; where the device needs a neutral, connect it.

group: NEC: overcurrent, grounding, wiring, devices, panels, lighting (Art. 240-410)
title: Receptacles listed and rated
applies_to: Every receptacle
check: Receptacles are listed and marked with voltage and ampere rating; rating matches the circuit per 210.21(B) (single receptacle on an individual circuit not less than circuit rating; 15 A or 20 A devices on 20 A multi-outlet circuits).
note: Check: single receptacle on a dedicated 20 A circuit must be a 20 A device.

group: NEC: overcurrent, grounding, wiring, devices, panels, lighting (Art. 240-410)
title: Aluminum and push-in terminations
applies_to: Houses with aluminum branch wiring; back-stabbed devices
check: Receptacles 20 A or less connected directly to aluminum conductors must be marked CO/ALR. Push-in terminals only with 14 AWG solid copper on 15 A circuits.
edition_difference: 2023 adds the push-in limit as 406.3(D)(3) and moves isolated-ground receptacles to (E).
needs: Branch wiring is aluminum (year built approx. 1965-1973)

group: NEC: overcurrent, grounding, wiring, devices, panels, lighting (Art. 240-410)
title: Controlled receptacle marking
applies_to: Receptacles controlled by automation / energy management
check: Automatically controlled receptacles carry the controlled marking; not required for wall-switched lamp receptacles in dwellings.
edition_difference: Renumbered from (E) in 2020 to (F) in 2023.

group: NEC: overcurrent, grounding, wiring, devices, panels, lighting (Art. 240-410)
title: Grounding-type receptacles
applies_to: Every new receptacle
check: Receptacles on 15 and 20 A circuits are grounding type, with the grounding terminal connected to the circuit equipment grounding conductor.

group: NEC: overcurrent, grounding, wiring, devices, panels, lighting (Art. 240-410)
title: Replacement where ground exists
applies_to: Replacing receptacles in existing boxes
check: Where a grounding means exists in the box, or a ground wire is added per 250.130(C), use a grounding-type receptacle connected to it.

group: NEC: overcurrent, grounding, wiring, devices, panels, lighting (Art. 240-410)
title: Replacement where no ground exists
applies_to: Replacing 2-prong receptacles on ungrounded circuits
check: Options: (a) another non-grounding receptacle; (b) a GFCI receptacle marked No Equipment Ground; (c) a grounding receptacle supplied through a GFCI, marked GFCI Protected and No Equipment Ground. Do not connect an equipment ground from the GFCI to downstream outlets.
needs: Existing circuit has equipment ground yes/no (year built is a hint)

group: NEC: overcurrent, grounding, wiring, devices, panels, lighting (Art. 240-410)
title: GFCI at replacement
applies_to: Replacing any receptacle in a location where GFCI is now required
check: A replaced receptacle in a location that now requires GFCI (bathroom, kitchen, laundry, garage, outdoors, within 6 ft of a sink, etc. per 210.8) must be GFCI protected, by device or upstream protection.
edition_difference: 2023 requires the GFCI device to be listed and edits wording.
note: AUTO: existing-status receptacles marked replaced in 210.8 locations without GFCI flag.

group: NEC: overcurrent, grounding, wiring, devices, panels, lighting (Art. 240-410)
title: AFCI at replacement
applies_to: Replacing receptacles in rooms where AFCI is now required
check: A replaced receptacle on a circuit that would need AFCI under 210.12 must be protected by a listed AFCI receptacle, an upstream AFCI receptacle, or an AFCI breaker.
note: Applies to like-for-like device replacement throughout the remodel area (bedrooms, living areas, kitchens, laundry, hallways, closets).

group: NEC: overcurrent, grounding, wiring, devices, panels, lighting (Art. 240-410)
title: Tamper-resistant at replacement
applies_to: Replacing receptacles in a dwelling
check: Replacement receptacles must be tamper-resistant where 406.12 requires TR. Exceptions: non-grounding replaced with non-grounding; (2023) CO/ALR replacement on aluminum conductors.
edition_difference: 2023 adds the aluminum/CO/ALR exception.

group: NEC: overcurrent, grounding, wiring, devices, panels, lighting (Art. 240-410)
title: Weather-resistant at replacement
applies_to: Replacing exterior or damp/wet location receptacles
check: Replacement receptacles in damp or wet locations must be weather-resistant (WR) type.

group: NEC: overcurrent, grounding, wiring, devices, panels, lighting (Art. 240-410)
title: Controlled and GFPE replacements
applies_to: Replacing controlled receptacles
check: Controlled receptacles are replaced in kind; (2023) where GFPE is required elsewhere in the code the replacement must have it.
edition_difference: (D)(8) GFPE is new in 2023.
note: Rare in dwellings.

group: NEC: overcurrent, grounding, wiring, devices, panels, lighting (Art. 240-410)
title: Receptacle mounting
applies_to: Every receptacle
check: Box securely fastened; in set-back boxes the yoke is held rigidly at the finished surface, in flush boxes against the box; receptacle face flush with or projecting from a nonmetallic faceplate (project at least 0.015 in. from metal faceplates).

group: NEC: overcurrent, grounding, wiring, devices, panels, lighting (Art. 240-410)
title: Countertop receptacle assemblies
applies_to: Receptacles mounted in a countertop surface (pop-ups)
check: Receptacle assemblies installed in a countertop must be listed for countertop use (kitchen and bath counters).
needs: Device is a listed countertop pop-up assembly
note: Lettering (E)/(F)/(G) per 2020/2023 from memory; consistent with the task brief.

group: NEC: overcurrent, grounding, wiring, devices, panels, lighting (Art. 240-410)
title: Work surface receptacle assemblies
applies_to: Receptacles in desks, work surfaces, vanities other than countertops
check: Receptacle assemblies in work surfaces must be listed for work-surface or countertop use.
needs: Device is a listed work-surface assembly

group: NEC: overcurrent, grounding, wiring, devices, panels, lighting (Art. 240-410)
title: No face-up receptacles in counters
applies_to: Receptacles on countertops and work surfaces
check: No receptacle installed face-up in or on a countertop or work surface unless listed for that use.
note: Flag any receptacle whose mounting is horizontal face-up on a counter and not flagged as a listed assembly.

group: NEC: overcurrent, grounding, wiring, devices, panels, lighting (Art. 240-410)
title: No face-up receptacle under sink
applies_to: Disposal/dishwasher receptacles in the sink base
check: Receptacles in the area below a sink may not be installed face-up.
edition_difference: New in 2023; not in 2020.

group: NEC: overcurrent, grounding, wiring, devices, panels, lighting (Art. 240-410)
title: Receptacles in seating
applies_to: Built-in seating/benches with receptacles
check: Receptacles in seating areas and similar surfaces must not be face-up unless part of a listed furniture power assembly, listed for countertop/work surface, or in a listed floor box.
needs: Receptacle in built-in bench/banquette is a listed assembly

group: NEC: overcurrent, grounding, wiring, devices, panels, lighting (Art. 240-410)
title: Voltage between ganged devices
applies_to: Ganged receptacles
check: No receptacles ganged with other devices where voltage between adjacent devices exceeds 300 V unless barriered.
note: Rare in dwellings.

group: NEC: overcurrent, grounding, wiring, devices, panels, lighting (Art. 240-410)
title: Receptacle faceplates
applies_to: Every receptacle
check: Faceplate fully covers the opening and seats against the surface; metal faceplates grounded. Faceplates with built-in night light or USB must be listed (2023: 1 W or less, contacts on brass/copper-alloy screws).
edition_difference: 2023 adds 406.6(D) details for night-light/USB faceplates.

group: NEC: overcurrent, grounding, wiring, devices, panels, lighting (Art. 240-410)
title: Damp-location receptacles
applies_to: Receptacles under roofed porches, lanais, canopies
check: Enclosure weatherproof when the plug is removed and cover closed; 15 and 20 A, 125/250 V nonlocking receptacles must be listed weather-resistant (WR).
note: AUTO: exterior/damp receptacle without WR flag. GFCI per 210.8 is a separate rule.

group: NEC: overcurrent, grounding, wiring, devices, panels, lighting (Art. 240-410)
title: Wet-location in-use covers
applies_to: Exterior receptacles exposed to weather
check: 15 and 20 A receptacles in wet locations need an enclosure weatherproof with the plug inserted (in-use cover), with a hood listed extra duty; receptacle listed WR. Hinged covers must open at least 90 degrees or fully.
edition_difference: 2023 adds the 90-degree / full-open hinge requirement.
note: Needs attribute: location wet vs damp; in-use cover flag.

group: NEC: overcurrent, grounding, wiring, devices, panels, lighting (Art. 240-410)
title: No receptacles in tub/shower zone
applies_to: Receptacles near tubs and showers
check: No receptacle inside a tub or shower or within a zone 3 ft horizontally from the tub rim or shower threshold and from the floor to 8 ft above the rim/threshold. Exceptions: bathroom too small for the zone - place the required receptacle on the farthest wall opposite the tub/shower; hydromassage tub equipment receptacle per 680.73; (2023) listed weight-supporting ceiling receptacle for a luminaire or fan per 410.10(D); (2023) one GFCI-protected, readily accessible single receptacle for an electronic toilet/bidet seat, not between the toilet and the tub/shower.
edition_difference: 2020 text has the 3 ft / 8 ft zone and the small-bathroom exception; Exceptions 3 and 4 (WSCR, bidet seat) are new in 2023.
note: Replaces E-14 (receptacle part). The old pre-2020 rule only prohibited receptacles inside the tub/shower space; the 3 ft zone applies under both Florida editions.

group: NEC: overcurrent, grounding, wiring, devices, panels, lighting (Art. 240-410)
title: Flush receptacle faceplate in wet area
applies_to: Flush boxes in damp or wet locations
check: Flush-mounted receptacle boxes in damp/wet locations need a weatherproof faceplate assembly that seals between plate and wall.

group: NEC: overcurrent, grounding, wiring, devices, panels, lighting (Art. 240-410)
title: Receptacle ground connection
applies_to: Every receptacle
check: Connect the grounding terminal to the equipment grounding conductor per 250.146.

group: NEC: overcurrent, grounding, wiring, devices, panels, lighting (Art. 240-410)
title: Tamper-resistant receptacles
applies_to: Every new or replaced 15/20 A, 125 V or 250 V nonlocking receptacle in the dwelling, attached/detached garage and accessory buildings
check: All must be listed tamper-resistant. Exceptions: receptacles more than 5-1/2 ft above the floor; receptacles that are part of a luminaire or appliance; a single (or duplex for two) receptacle in dedicated space for an appliance not easily moved (refrigerator, washer, range hood/microwave in cabinet); non-grounding replacements.
edition_difference: 2023 names mobile/manufactured homes and adds non-dwelling locations; dwelling rule unchanged. Both editions include 250 V and garages/accessory buildings.
note: Replaces E-13.

group: NEC: overcurrent, grounding, wiring, devices, panels, lighting (Art. 240-410)
title: Circuit directory
applies_to: Every panel and subpanel touched by the work
check: Every circuit and modification legibly identified by clear, specific purpose (not by occupant name or transient description), spares marked, directory on or inside the panel door. 2023: explain abbreviations and symbols.
edition_difference: 2023 reformats as a list and adds the abbreviations item.
note: Permit set: provide an updated panel schedule.

group: NEC: overcurrent, grounding, wiring, devices, panels, lighting (Art. 240-410)
title: Source of supply marking
applies_to: Subpanels
check: Panels supplied by a feeder are marked with the source (which panel and location feeds them). The code requirement applies to other than one- and two-family dwellings; treat as recommended practice for houses, required for townhouse/multifamily common equipment.
edition_difference: 2023 adds label durability / not handwritten.

group: NEC: overcurrent, grounding, wiring, devices, panels, lighting (Art. 240-410)
title: Close unused openings
applies_to: Panels
check: Unused breaker openings in the dead front closed with listed filler plates; unused knockouts closed (110.12(A)).

group: NEC: overcurrent, grounding, wiring, devices, panels, lighting (Art. 240-410)
title: Replacement panel interiors
applies_to: Panel change-out using an existing enclosure
check: A replacement panelboard in an existing enclosure must be listed for that enclosure, or, if not, be field labeled when available fault current exceeds 10,000 A and otherwise identified for the application.
edition_difference: New in 2023; not in 2020.

group: NEC: overcurrent, grounding, wiring, devices, panels, lighting (Art. 240-410)
title: Panel main protection
applies_to: Panels and subpanels: bus rating vs feeding breaker
check: Each panelboard protected by an overcurrent device rated not more than the panel bus rating, either a main breaker in the panel or the feeder breaker. Flag subpanel rating less than its feeder breaker, and main panel rating less than the service disconnect.

group: NEC: overcurrent, grounding, wiring, devices, panels, lighting (Art. 240-410)
title: Back-fed breakers secured
applies_to: Back-fed main breakers, generator/PV/interlock back-feeds
check: Plug-in breakers that are back-fed and used to terminate supply conductors need an additional fastener (hold-down kit) so removal requires more than a pull.
needs: Panel main or source breaker is back-fed

group: NEC: overcurrent, grounding, wiring, devices, panels, lighting (Art. 240-410)
title: Panels in damp or wet locations
applies_to: Exterior panels
check: Install per 312.2 (weatherproof, 1/4 in. air space).

group: NEC: overcurrent, grounding, wiring, devices, panels, lighting (Art. 240-410)
title: Ground bar; neutral isolation
applies_to: Panels and subpanels
check: Panel cabinet has a grounding terminal bar bonded to the enclosure for all equipment grounds. Neutrals and grounds may share a bar only at the service disconnect; in subpanels grounds go on a bonded ground bar and neutrals on an isolated bar.
needs: Panel is service equipment or subpanel
note: Service change that adds an exterior disconnect makes the interior panel a subpanel: requires 4-wire feeder and separated bars.

group: NEC: overcurrent, grounding, wiring, devices, panels, lighting (Art. 240-410)
title: One neutral per terminal
applies_to: Panels
check: Each neutral conductor terminates in its own terminal hole; no doubled neutrals, no neutral with a ground under one screw.

group: NEC: overcurrent, grounding, wiring, devices, panels, lighting (Art. 240-410)
title: Panel orientation
applies_to: Panels
check: Panelboards may not be installed face-up or face-down.
edition_difference: 2020 prohibits face-up only; 2023 adds face-down.

group: NEC: overcurrent, grounding, wiring, devices, panels, lighting (Art. 240-410)
title: Maximum number of breakers
applies_to: Panels: circuits vs spaces
check: Do not exceed the number of overcurrent devices the panel is designed, rated and listed for; tandem (twin) breakers only in positions listed for them. Flag circuits needed greater than available spaces.
note: AUTO from panel spaces and circuit count; tandem acceptance is DATA (panel CTL type).

group: NEC: overcurrent, grounding, wiring, devices, panels, lighting (Art. 240-410)
title: No reconditioned panelboards
applies_to: Panel replacement
check: Reconditioned (rebuilt) panelboards are not permitted; damaged panels (water, fire) are replaced.
note: Relevant after flood/water damage: FEMA/NEMA guidance requires replacement of submerged breakers and panel interiors.

group: NEC: overcurrent, grounding, wiring, devices, panels, lighting (Art. 240-410)
title: Luminaires listed
applies_to: Every luminaire, lampholder, retrofit kit
check: All luminaires, lampholders and retrofit kits must be listed and installed per instructions.

group: NEC: overcurrent, grounding, wiring, devices, panels, lighting (Art. 240-410)
title: Wet/damp rated luminaires
applies_to: Lights in showers, exterior, lanais, over tubs
check: Luminaires in wet or damp locations must be marked Suitable for Wet Locations or Suitable for Damp Locations as applicable (wet-rated may be used in damp) and installed so water cannot enter wiring compartments.
needs: Luminaire rating: dry / damp / wet

group: NEC: overcurrent, grounding, wiring, devices, panels, lighting (Art. 240-410)
title: No hanging lights, track or fans over tub/shower
applies_to: Pendants, chandeliers, track lighting, cord-connected lights and ceiling fans near tubs and showers
check: None of these within a zone 3 ft horizontally and 8 ft vertically from the top of the tub rim or shower threshold; the zone includes the space directly over the tub or shower.
edition_difference: 2023 numbers the list and adds ceiling fans with light kits explicitly; 2020 lists paddle fans generally.
note: Replaces E-14 (luminaire part). A chandelier over a freestanding tub needs 8 ft clear above the rim or must be outside the 3 ft zone.

group: NEC: overcurrent, grounding, wiring, devices, panels, lighting (Art. 240-410)
title: Damp/wet rating in tub/shower footprint
applies_to: Any luminaire within the outside dimensions of the tub or shower up to 8 ft above rim/threshold
check: Luminaire must be marked for damp locations, or for wet locations where subject to shower spray.
needs: Luminaire rating: damp / wet
note: AUTO-detect lights inside the shower/tub footprint, then require the rating.

group: NEC: overcurrent, grounding, wiring, devices, panels, lighting (Art. 240-410)
title: Luminaires under roof decking
applies_to: Luminaires installed under roof decking
check: Keep luminaires at least 1-1/2 in. below the lowest surface of roof decking subject to damage from roofing fasteners.
edition_difference: 2020 applies to metal-corrugated sheet roof decking only; 2023 applies to any roof decking and adds a 2 in. concrete exception.
note: Task brief listed (E) as closets and (F) as indoor sports; actual (E) is indoor sports/assembly areas (not dwelling) and (F) is roof decking. Closets are 410.16.

group: NEC: overcurrent, grounding, wiring, devices, panels, lighting (Art. 240-410)
title: Luminaires near combustibles
applies_to: Every luminaire
check: Install so adjacent combustible material is not subjected to temperatures above 90 C (194 F); observe the fixture's marked clearances.

group: NEC: overcurrent, grounding, wiring, devices, panels, lighting (Art. 240-410)
title: Closet luminaire types permitted
applies_to: Lights in rooms typed as clothes closet
check: Only: surface or recessed incandescent or LED luminaires with completely enclosed light source; surface or recessed fluorescent; surface fluorescent or LED identified as suitable for installation within the storage space.
needs: Luminaire type: enclosed / open lamp / pendant; surface or recessed; source type
note: Replaces E-15.

group: NEC: overcurrent, grounding, wiring, devices, panels, lighting (Art. 240-410)
title: Closet luminaire types prohibited
applies_to: Lights in clothes closets
check: No incandescent luminaires with open or partially enclosed lamps, no pendant luminaires, no bare lampholders.
note: AUTO: pendant or open-lamp fixture type in a closet.

group: NEC: overcurrent, grounding, wiring, devices, panels, lighting (Art. 240-410)
title: Closet luminaire clearances
applies_to: Lights in clothes closets
check: Minimum clearance between the luminaire and the nearest point of the storage space: 12 in. for surface-mounted enclosed incandescent or LED on the wall above the door or on the ceiling; 6 in. for surface-mounted fluorescent; 6 in. for recessed enclosed incandescent or LED; 6 in. for recessed fluorescent. Surface fluorescent/LED identified for the purpose may be within the storage space.
edition_difference: 2023 lists four clearances and moves the identified-for-storage-space fixture to an exception; some 2023 summaries cite the clearances as 410.16(D).
note: Replaces E-15. Geometry check needs the storage space below.

group: NEC: overcurrent, grounding, wiring, devices, panels, lighting (Art. 240-410)
title: Closet storage space definition
applies_to: Clothes closets
check: Storage space = volume from the floor up to 6 ft or the highest clothes rod, extending 24 in. from the back and side walls; above that, up to the ceiling, 12 in. deep or the shelf width if greater. In a 24 in. deep reach-in closet this leaves the ceiling area in front of the shelf, typically requiring a recessed or over-the-door fixture.
edition_difference: Definition is in 410.2 in 2020 and moved to Article 100 in 2023.

group: NEC: overcurrent, grounding, wiring, devices, panels, lighting (Art. 240-410)
title: Luminaire outlet boxes
applies_to: Every luminaire
check: Canopy and box provide adequate space; box covered by the canopy; combustible finish exposed between canopy edge and box covered with noncombustible material; surface-mounted linear luminaires over a concealed box must leave access to the box.

group: NEC: overcurrent, grounding, wiring, devices, panels, lighting (Art. 240-410)
title: Luminaire support
applies_to: Every luminaire
check: Luminaires securely supported. A luminaire over 6 lb or over 16 in. in any dimension may not hang from a lampholder screw shell. Box support per 314.27 (50 lb ceiling limit unless listed higher).
needs: Luminaire weight

group: NEC: overcurrent, grounding, wiring, devices, panels, lighting (Art. 240-410)
title: Lights in suspended ceilings
applies_to: Lay-in or surface lights in ACT grid ceilings
check: Ceiling framing members supporting luminaires securely fastened to each other and to the structure; luminaires fastened to the grid with screws, bolts, rivets or listed clips identified for the grid and luminaire.
needs: Ceiling type is ACT grid with luminaires

group: NEC: overcurrent, grounding, wiring, devices, panels, lighting (Art. 240-410)
title: Luminaire grounding
applies_to: Every luminaire; replacement on old ungrounded circuits
check: Luminaires with exposed conductive parts connect to an equipment grounding conductor. Replacement luminaire at an outlet with no ground: add a ground per 250.130(C) or GFCI-protect the luminaire.

group: NEC: overcurrent, grounding, wiring, devices, panels, lighting (Art. 240-410)
title: Lampholder polarity
applies_to: Screw-shell lampholders
check: Connect the neutral to the screw shell of lampholders.

group: NEC: overcurrent, grounding, wiring, devices, panels, lighting (Art. 240-410)
title: Cord-connected luminaires
applies_to: Cord-and-plug connected or pendant luminaires, under-cabinet plug-in lights
check: Cord-connected luminaires only as listed: cord visible for its entire length, not subject to strain or damage, plugged into a receptacle or connected to a box directly; not concealed in walls or cabinets.

group: NEC: overcurrent, grounding, wiring, devices, panels, lighting (Art. 240-410)
title: Wiring through luminaires
applies_to: End-to-end connected luminaires (under-cabinet, strip lights)
check: Do not use luminaires as raceways for circuit conductors unless listed and marked for it; conductors within 3 in. of a ballast or driver rated at least 90 C.

group: NEC: overcurrent, grounding, wiring, devices, panels, lighting (Art. 240-410)
title: Lampholders in wet/damp locations
applies_to: Exterior lampholders
check: Lampholders in wet locations listed for wet locations; in damp locations listed for damp or wet.

group: NEC: overcurrent, grounding, wiring, devices, panels, lighting (Art. 240-410)
title: Recessed luminaire temperature
applies_to: Recessed lights
check: Recessed luminaires installed so adjacent combustible material stays at or below 90 C; recessed incandescent luminaires must have thermal protection and be identified as thermally protected.

group: NEC: overcurrent, grounding, wiring, devices, panels, lighting (Art. 240-410)
title: Non-IC recessed: 1/2 in. from combustibles
applies_to: Recessed lights not rated Type IC
check: Recessed parts of a non-IC luminaire at least 1/2 in. from combustible materials (framing, sheathing), except at support points and the finished trim opening.
needs: Luminaire is Type IC rated yes/no

group: NEC: overcurrent, grounding, wiring, devices, panels, lighting (Art. 240-410)
title: Type IC in contact
applies_to: Recessed lights in insulated ceilings
check: A luminaire identified Type IC may be in contact with combustible material and insulation.
needs: Luminaire is Type IC rated yes/no
note: Energy code (FBC-EC R402.4.5) additionally requires IC-rated and air-tight (labelled max 2.0 cfm leakage) recessed lights in the thermal envelope.

group: NEC: overcurrent, grounding, wiring, devices, panels, lighting (Art. 240-410)
title: Non-IC recessed: 3 in. from insulation
applies_to: Recessed lights in ceilings with insulation above
check: No thermal insulation above a recessed luminaire or within 3 in. of its housing, wiring compartment, ballast, transformer, LED driver or power supply unless it is Type IC. Flag any recessed light in a ceiling below an attic or insulated cavity that is not flagged IC.

group: NEC: overcurrent, grounding, wiring, devices, panels, lighting (Art. 240-410)
title: Recessed luminaire wiring
applies_to: Recessed lights
check: Supply conductors rated for the temperature marked on the luminaire (commonly 90 C). Tap conductors from a remote junction box run in suitable raceway or cable, at least 18 in. and not more than 6 ft long; box at least 1 ft from the luminaire.

group: NEC: overcurrent, grounding, wiring, devices, panels, lighting (Art. 240-410)
title: No access to boxes through luminaire
applies_to: Recessed lights
check: A recessed luminaire may not be the means of access to a separate outlet, pull or junction box unless the box is an integral part of the listed luminaire.

group: NEC: overcurrent, grounding, wiring, devices, panels, lighting (Art. 240-410)
title: Track lighting installation and load
applies_to: Track lighting
check: Track permanently installed and connected to a branch circuit; connected load not over the track rating; track not supplied by a branch circuit rated higher than the track (typically 20 A max).
needs: Track rating and connected load

group: NEC: overcurrent, grounding, wiring, devices, panels, lighting (Art. 240-410)
title: Track lighting prohibited locations
applies_to: Track lighting
check: Not: where subject to physical damage; in wet or damp locations; concealed; extended through walls or partitions; less than 5 ft above the finished floor unless protected from damage or operating under 30 V RMS open-circuit; within the tub/shower zone of 410.10(D) (3 ft horizontal, 8 ft vertical).
note: AUTO: track height under 5 ft; track in bathroom tub/shower zone; track in a damp/wet-typed space (lanai, exterior); track crossing a wall.

group: NEC: overcurrent, grounding, wiring, devices, panels, lighting (Art. 240-410)
title: Track support
applies_to: Track lighting
check: Track securely mounted: a single section 4 ft or shorter gets two supports; each additional section of 4 ft or less gets one more support, unless identified for greater spacing.

group: NEC: overcurrent, grounding, wiring, devices, panels, lighting (Art. 240-410)
title: Decorative lighting listed
applies_to: Decorative lighting strings and similar accessories
check: Decorative lighting and accessories must be listed.

group: NEC: overcurrent, grounding, wiring, devices, panels, lighting (Art. 240-410)
title: No reconditioned luminaires
applies_to: Reused or salvaged light fixtures
check: Luminaires, lampholders, ballasts, LED drivers, lamps and retrofit kits may not be reconditioned; a listed retrofit kit installed per its instructions is acceptable.
edition_difference: New in 2023 (410.2 held the closet storage space definition in 2020).

group: NEC: overcurrent, grounding, wiring, devices, panels, lighting (Art. 240-410)
title: Load calculation reminder
applies_to: Added loads, service or panel change
check: Provide a dwelling load calculation showing the existing service/feeder can carry added loads (handled by the separate calculator).
note: Outside Articles 240-410; one-line reminder as instructed.

group: NEC: appliances, HVAC, EV, tubs and spas, low voltage (Art. 422-820)
title: Lighting demand factors
applies_to: Load calculation (standard method)
check: Dwelling general lighting load demand: first 3,000 VA at 100 percent, 3,001 to 120,000 VA at 35 percent, remainder over 120,000 VA at 25 percent.
edition_difference: Table renumbered from 220.42 (2020) to 220.45 (2023); values unchanged.
note: Verification requested: the 25 percent tier above 120,000 VA is CONFIRMED for Table 220.42 by a study guide (edition not stated) and the 35 percent 3,001-120,000 range by a 2020-based Mike Holt article; the 2023 renumbering to Table 220.45 is from my knowledge. Handled by the separate load calculator.

group: NEC: appliances, HVAC, EV, tubs and spas, low voltage (Art. 422-820)
title: EVSE load in calculation
applies_to: EV charger added to a dwelling
check: In the load calculation count each EVSE at the larger of 7,200 VA or its nameplate rating; EVSE is excluded from the 75 percent fastened-in-place appliance demand factor of 220.53.
edition_difference: Section is new in 2023; under 2020 use the nameplate (continuous load per 625.41/625.42).
note: Handled by the separate load calculator.

group: NEC: appliances, HVAC, EV, tubs and spas, low voltage (Art. 422-820)
title: Appliance demand factor
applies_to: Load calculation with four or more fixed appliances
check: 75 percent demand may be applied to four or more fastened-in-place appliances (each 1/4 hp or 500 W or more) on the same feeder or service; not to cooking equipment, dryers, space heating, air conditioning or EVSE.
edition_difference: 2023 added the 1/4 hp / 500 W threshold wording and the EVSE exclusion.
note: Handled by the separate load calculator.

group: NEC: appliances, HVAC, EV, tubs and spas, low voltage (Art. 422-820)
title: Motor appliances: other articles
applies_to: Motor-operated appliances, refrigeration appliances
check: Motor-operated appliances also follow Article 430; appliances with hermetic refrigerant compressors also follow Article 440 (room air conditioners, refrigerators and freezers are treated as appliances with Article 440 applied as amended by 422).
note: 2017-based article.

group: NEC: appliances, HVAC, EV, tubs and spas, low voltage (Art. 422-820)
title: Appliance GFCI list
applies_to: Dishwasher, sump pump
check: Dishwashers and sump pumps (150 V or less to ground, 60 A or less) need Class A GFCI protection wherever they are, hard-wired or cord-connected.
edition_difference: 2020 lowered the limit from 250 V to 150 V to ground and added sump pumps and dishwashers (dishwasher moved from 210.8(D)). 2023 keeps the list and repeats and enlarges it in 210.8(D).
note: Remaining list items (vacuum machines, drinking water coolers and bottle fill stations, pressure washers, tire inflators, vending machines) are not dwelling items.

group: NEC: appliances, HVAC, EV, tubs and spas, low voltage (Art. 422-820)
title: Where appliance GFCI sits
applies_to: Appliance needing GFCI under 422.5(A)
check: The GFCI must be readily accessible, listed, and one of: GFCI breaker, GFCI device or receptacle, GFCI in the plug, GFCI in the cord within 12 in. of the plug, or factory-installed in the appliance. A dishwasher GFCI therefore cannot be a receptacle hidden behind the dishwasher.
needs: GFCI location for the dishwasher / sump pump (breaker, readily accessible dead-front or receptacle)
note: Wording from a 2017-based article; 2020 Leviton page confirms the 12 in. cord option.

group: NEC: appliances, HVAC, EV, tubs and spas, low voltage (Art. 422-820)
title: Appliances listed
applies_to: All new appliances
check: Appliances supplied at 50 V or more must be listed.

group: NEC: appliances, HVAC, EV, tubs and spas, low voltage (Art. 422-820)
title: Individual appliance circuit rating
applies_to: Appliance on its own branch circuit
check: Branch-circuit rating not less than the appliance marked rating; for a continuously loaded non-motor appliance, not less than 125 percent of the marked rating. Household ranges and cooking appliances may be sized by Table 220.55.
edition_difference: 2023 moved the cooking-appliance conductor reference from 210.19(A)(3) to 210.19(C).
needs: Appliance nameplate amperes or watts
note: The 210.19 renumbering is from my knowledge, not confirmed.

group: NEC: appliances, HVAC, EV, tubs and spas, low voltage (Art. 422-820)
title: Appliance on shared circuit
applies_to: Appliance sharing a circuit with other loads
check: On a 15 or 20 A circuit with other loads: a cord-and-plug appliance not fastened in place may not exceed 80 percent of the circuit rating; fastened-in-place equipment (other than luminaires) may not exceed 50 percent when the circuit also supplies lighting or receptacles (210.23).
edition_difference: 2023 renumbered 210.23(A) to 210.23(B) for 15 and 20 A circuits (210.23(A) now covers 10 A circuits).
needs: Appliance nameplate amperes
note: Drives the dedicated-circuit logic of app rule E-11: a fixed appliance over 7.5 A on a 15 A circuit or over 10 A on a 20 A circuit needs its own circuit.

group: NEC: appliances, HVAC, EV, tubs and spas, low voltage (Art. 422-820)
title: Appliance overcurrent limit
applies_to: Appliance branch circuit
check: Protect the branch circuit per 240.4; if the appliance is marked with a maximum overcurrent device rating, the breaker must not exceed it.
needs: Nameplate maximum breaker size

group: NEC: appliances, HVAC, EV, tubs and spas, low voltage (Art. 422-820)
title: Large cooktops subdivided
applies_to: Household cooking appliance with surface elements over 60 A demand
check: A household appliance with surface heating elements whose maximum demand exceeds 60 A (per Table 220.55) must have its supply subdivided into two or more circuits each protected at 50 A or less.
note: From my knowledge of the section; rare in practice.

group: NEC: appliances, HVAC, EV, tubs and spas, low voltage (Art. 422-820)
title: Breaker for single non-motor appliance
applies_to: Water heater, wall oven, other single non-motor appliance
check: Breaker not larger than the marked maximum; if none is marked: 20 A maximum for an appliance of 13.3 A or less, and 150 percent of rated current for larger appliances (next standard size up allowed).
needs: Appliance rated amperes
note: Example: 4,500 W 240 V water heater = 18.75 A; conductors at 125 percent = 23.4 A (10 AWG, 25 or 30 A breaker).

group: NEC: appliances, HVAC, EV, tubs and spas, low voltage (Art. 422-820)
title: Resistance appliances over 48 A
applies_to: Tankless electric water heater, large resistance heater
check: Resistance-heating appliances rated over 48 A must have the elements subdivided into loads of 48 A or less, each protected at 60 A or less (normally factory-built; tankless heaters need multiple circuits per the nameplate).
note: From my knowledge; listed instantaneous water heaters have their own exception. Use the nameplate circuit count.

group: NEC: appliances, HVAC, EV, tubs and spas, low voltage (Art. 422-820)
title: Central heating own circuit
applies_to: Furnace or air handler (non-electric-strip central heating equipment)
check: Supply central heating equipment (other than fixed electric space heating) from an individual branch circuit. Auxiliary equipment directly associated with it (pump, valve, humidifier, electrostatic air cleaner) and permanently connected air-conditioning equipment may share that circuit.
note: Part of app rule E-11.

group: NEC: appliances, HVAC, EV, tubs and spas, low voltage (Art. 422-820)
title: Storage water heater continuous
applies_to: Storage water heater 120 gal or less
check: Treat a fixed storage-type water heater of 120 gal or less as a continuous load: branch circuit and conductors at 125 percent of the nameplate current.
needs: Water heater watts and voltage

group: NEC: appliances, HVAC, EV, tubs and spas, low voltage (Art. 422-820)
title: Central vacuum
applies_to: Central vacuum unit and inlets
check: A listed central vacuum may be on a general circuit only if its rating is 50 percent or less of the circuit rating; otherwise give it its own circuit (over 7.5 A on 15 A, over 10 A on 20 A). Ground accessible metal parts; the inlet receptacle in a garage needs GFCI under 210.8(A).
needs: Central vacuum amperes

group: NEC: appliances, HVAC, EV, tubs and spas, low voltage (Art. 422-820)
title: Flexible cord allowed when
applies_to: Cord-connected fixed appliance
check: Flexible cord may supply an appliance only (1) for frequent interchange or to stop noise/vibration, or (2) for a fastened-in-place appliance built for ready removal and intended or identified for cord connection. A water heater, range hood without cord kit, or other appliance not identified for cords must be hard-wired.

group: NEC: appliances, HVAC, EV, tubs and spas, low voltage (Art. 422-820)
title: Disposer cord
applies_to: In-sink waste disposer, cord-connected
check: Cord identified for the purpose in the installation instructions, 18 in. minimum and 36 in. maximum, grounding-type plug (unless listed double-insulated), receptacle placed so the cord is not damaged and accessible (normally in the sink base).
edition_difference: 2020 reworded the grounding item (cord must contain an equipment grounding conductor); lengths unchanged.
needs: Disposer is cord-connected; receptacle location
note: Sink-base receptacle also needs GFCI in 2023 (210.8(A)(7) sinks within 6 ft) and must not be face-up (406.5(G)).

group: NEC: appliances, HVAC, EV, tubs and spas, low voltage (Art. 422-820)
title: Dishwasher cord and receptacle
applies_to: Built-in dishwasher, cord-connected
check: Cord identified for the purpose, 3 ft minimum and 6.5 ft maximum measured from the plug face to the plane of the back of the dishwasher. Receptacle must be in the space ADJACENT to the dishwasher space (e.g. sink base), not behind the dishwasher, accessible, with the cord protected from damage; bushing or grommet where the cord passes through the cabinet side. Cord has an equipment grounding conductor and grounding plug.
edition_difference: Dishwasher maximum went from 4 ft to 6.5 ft in 2017; 2020 added the bushing/grommet sentence. 2023 text not opened; no change known.
note: Check: dishwasher receptacle symbol must sit in the neighboring cabinet, never in the dishwasher bay.

group: NEC: appliances, HVAC, EV, tubs and spas, low voltage (Art. 422-820)
title: Trash compactor cord
applies_to: Built-in trash compactor, cord-connected
check: Cord 3 ft minimum and 4 ft maximum (plug face to rear plane of the appliance); receptacle in the compactor space or the adjacent space, accessible, cord protected from damage.
needs: Trash compactor present; receptacle location

group: NEC: appliances, HVAC, EV, tubs and spas, low voltage (Art. 422-820)
title: Wall oven and cooktop connection
applies_to: Wall-mounted oven, counter-mounted cooking unit
check: May be permanently connected or cord-and-plug connected. A separable connector or plug-and-receptacle in the supply must be approved for the temperature of the space where it is located; if used only for ease of servicing it is not the required disconnect unless it meets 422.33.
note: The article read only confirms that cord connection is permitted; the temperature-approval wording is from my knowledge.

group: NEC: appliances, HVAC, EV, tubs and spas, low voltage (Art. 422-820)
title: Range hood / OTR microwave cord and circuit
applies_to: Range hood or over-the-range microwave with integral hood, cord-connected
check: Cord identified for range hoods, 18 in. minimum and 4 ft maximum; receptacle accessible (typically in the cabinet above), placed so the cord is protected; the receptacle must be on an INDIVIDUAL branch circuit; cord has an equipment grounding conductor and grounding plug.
edition_difference: 2020 added the microwave/range-hood combination to the title. 2023 text not opened; no change known.
note: Part of app rule E-11. A hard-wired hood is not required by this section to have its own circuit, but planning one allows a later microwave swap.

group: NEC: appliances, HVAC, EV, tubs and spas, low voltage (Art. 422-820)
title: Ceiling fan support
applies_to: Ceiling (paddle) fan
check: Support the fan independently of the outlet box, or from a listed fan-rated outlet box or box system (marked for fan support, 70 lb maximum; boxes for fans over 35 lb marked with the maximum weight) installed per 314.27(C), or from a listed locking support / weight-supporting ceiling receptacle system per 314.27(E).
edition_difference: 2023 made the old section subsection (A) and added (B) Location.
needs: Ceiling box is fan-rated
note: Related 314.27(C): a ceiling outlet box in a habitable room at a location acceptable for a fan, where spare separately switched conductors are run to it, must itself be fan-rated (that part is in another agent's area and was not opened).

group: NEC: appliances, HVAC, EV, tubs and spas, low voltage (Art. 422-820)
title: Ceiling fan near tub or shower
applies_to: Ceiling (paddle) fan in a bathroom or shower space
check: No metal part of a ceiling-suspended (paddle) fan may be inside the zone 3 ft horizontally and 8 ft vertically measured from the top of the bathtub rim or shower stall threshold; the zone includes the space directly over the tub or shower.
edition_difference: New in 2023; no equivalent in 422 for 2020. Under 2020 the same zone is enforced for paddle fans through 410.10(D).
note: Corrects app rule E-14: 422.18(B) can be cited only for the 2023 NEC (FBC 9th Edition); for permits under the 2020 NEC cite 410.10(D). The 410.10(D) statement is from my knowledge.

group: NEC: appliances, HVAC, EV, tubs and spas, low voltage (Art. 422-820)
title: Fan canopy conductor space
applies_to: Ceiling fan canopy and outlet box
check: The fan canopy and outlet box together must give enough space for the conductors and connections (box fill).
note: Section title and content from my knowledge (sections 422.19-422.21 were added in 2017); could not open the text.

group: NEC: appliances, HVAC, EV, tubs and spas, low voltage (Art. 422-820)
title: Fan outlet box covered
applies_to: Ceiling fan outlet box
check: The outlet box must be fully covered by the fan canopy or a cover; no open gap around the box.
note: From my knowledge; text not opened.

group: NEC: appliances, HVAC, EV, tubs and spas, low voltage (Art. 422-820)
title: Combustible ceiling at fan canopy
applies_to: Ceiling fan on a wood or other combustible ceiling finish
check: Combustible ceiling finish exposed between the edge of the fan canopy and the outlet box must be covered with noncombustible material.
note: From my knowledge; text not opened.

group: NEC: appliances, HVAC, EV, tubs and spas, low voltage (Art. 422-820)
title: Separable attachment fittings
applies_to: Appliance or fan hung from a weight-supporting ceiling receptacle
check: Listed appliances may be supported and connected with listed locking support and mounting receptacles and matching attachment fittings, within their marked weight rating.
edition_difference: Section added in 2020.
note: The task brief described 422.22 as 'appliances over tubs'; I found no such section. To my knowledge 422.22 covers separable attachment fittings; tub/shower location rules are 422.18(B), 410.10(D), 406.9(C), 404.4(C) and 440.8.

group: NEC: appliances, HVAC, EV, tubs and spas, low voltage (Art. 422-820)
title: Appliance disconnect required
applies_to: Every fixed appliance
check: Each appliance needs a means that simultaneously disconnects all ungrounded conductors; appliances fed by more than one circuit need the disconnects grouped and identified.
note: Grouping sentence is from my knowledge.

group: NEC: appliances, HVAC, EV, tubs and spas, low voltage (Art. 422-820)
title: Disconnect: small appliances
applies_to: Permanently connected appliance of 300 VA or less or 1/8 hp or less (e.g. bath fan, small recirculating pump)
check: The branch-circuit breaker may serve as the disconnect if it is within sight of the appliance or lockable in the open position (110.25).
note: 'Within sight' = visible and not more than 50 ft away.

group: NEC: appliances, HVAC, EV, tubs and spas, low voltage (Art. 422-820)
title: Disconnect: appliances over 300 VA
applies_to: Permanently connected water heater, wall oven, cooktop, hard-wired dishwasher, electric heater, etc.
check: A switch or the branch-circuit breaker may be the disconnect only if it is within sight of the appliance (visible, 50 ft or less) or is lockable open with a lock provision that stays in place (110.25). If the panel is out of sight, show a lockable breaker (breaker lock-off) or a local disconnect.
needs: Disconnect method per hard-wired appliance: local switch, in-sight panel, or breaker lock
note: Can be made AUTO for in-sight if the app tests line-of-sight and 50 ft distance from panel to appliance; a unit switch under 422.34 also satisfies it.

group: NEC: appliances, HVAC, EV, tubs and spas, low voltage (Art. 422-820)
title: Disconnect: motor appliances over 1/8 hp
applies_to: Hard-wired disposer, attic fan, well or booster pump, hard-wired compactor
check: Disconnect within sight of the appliance or lockable open per 110.25. Exception: an appliance with a unit switch meeting 422.34 needs no other local disconnect.
needs: Disconnect method (wall switch in sight, cord and plug, or breaker lock)
note: A disposer wall switch in sight of the sink satisfies this.

group: NEC: appliances, HVAC, EV, tubs and spas, low voltage (Art. 422-820)
title: Cord and plug as disconnect
applies_to: Cord-connected dishwasher, disposer, hood, microwave, refrigerator, washer, dryer, range
check: An accessible plug and receptacle (or attachment fitting) may serve as the appliance disconnect; the receptacle must be accessible without removing the appliance (e.g. in the adjacent cabinet).
needs: Receptacle is accessible

group: NEC: appliances, HVAC, EV, tubs and spas, low voltage (Art. 422-820)
title: Range plug behind drawer
applies_to: Cord-connected household electric range
check: A range plug and receptacle that can be reached from the front by removing a drawer counts as the disconnect.
note: Plug and receptacle rating must not be less than the appliance rating (422.33(C), from my knowledge).

group: NEC: appliances, HVAC, EV, tubs and spas, low voltage (Art. 422-820)
title: Unit switch as disconnect
applies_to: Appliance with a built-in on/off switch
check: A unit switch with a marked OFF position that opens all ungrounded conductors may be the appliance disconnect; in a one-family dwelling the service disconnect then serves as the other required disconnect (in a two-family dwelling, the unit's own panel or branch breaker).
note: From my knowledge; only the cross-reference in 422.31(C) was confirmed.

group: NEC: appliances, HVAC, EV, tubs and spas, low voltage (Art. 422-820)
title: Indicating switches
applies_to: Switch or breaker used as appliance disconnect
check: Switches and breakers used as appliance disconnects must show whether they are open or closed.
note: From my knowledge.

group: NEC: appliances, HVAC, EV, tubs and spas, low voltage (Art. 422-820)
title: Appliance nameplate
applies_to: All appliances
check: Size circuits from the appliance nameplate (volts and amperes or watts; for appliances with motors plus other loads, the marked minimum circuit ampacity and maximum overcurrent device). Nameplate must remain visible or accessible after installation.
needs: Nameplate ratings of each appliance
note: From my knowledge; section text not opened.

group: NEC: appliances, HVAC, EV, tubs and spas, low voltage (Art. 422-820)
title: Heating circuit sizes
applies_to: Fixed electric space heaters (baseboard, wall, ceiling, toe-kick)
check: A circuit supplying two or more fixed space-heater outlets in a dwelling may be rated only 15, 20, 25 or 30 A. An individual circuit may supply any size heater.
edition_difference: Numbered 424.3 through the 2017 edition; 424.4 in 2020 and 2023 (to my knowledge).
note: Article read cites the rule as 424.3 (older edition); the 2020/2023 number 424.4 was not confirmed on an opened page.

group: NEC: appliances, HVAC, EV, tubs and spas, low voltage (Art. 422-820)
title: Heating is continuous load
applies_to: Fixed electric space heating and its blower motors
check: Size branch-circuit conductors and breaker at 125 percent of the heater (and motor) load.
needs: Heater watts and voltage
note: Same numbering caveat as 424.4(A).

group: NEC: appliances, HVAC, EV, tubs and spas, low voltage (Art. 422-820)
title: Baseboard heater and receptacles
applies_to: Permanent electric baseboard heater under a wall receptacle location
check: Do not locate a baseboard heater beneath a wall receptacle unless its listing instructions allow it (listing instructions generally prohibit it). A baseboard heater with a factory-installed receptacle may count as the required wall receptacle, but that receptacle may not be fed from the heater circuit.
note: This is not a direct NEC prohibition: it comes from the heater listing (110.3(B)) pointed to by informational notes in 424.9 and 210.52. From my knowledge; text not opened. Flag as a warning.

group: NEC: appliances, HVAC, EV, tubs and spas, low voltage (Art. 422-820)
title: Bathroom and damp-location heaters
applies_to: Wall or ceiling heater in a bathroom, heater near tub or shower
check: Heaters in damp or wet locations must be listed for that location; install per listing clearances to tub, shower, towel bars, doors and combustibles (424.13).
needs: Heater listed for damp/wet location; listed clearances

group: NEC: appliances, HVAC, EV, tubs and spas, low voltage (Art. 422-820)
title: Heater disconnect
applies_to: Fixed electric space heater, air handler with heat strips
check: Provide a means to disconnect the heater, its motor controllers and supplementary overcurrent devices from all ungrounded conductors: within sight of the heater, or a breaker/switch that is lockable open; a unit switch with a marked OFF position that opens all ungrounded conductors is accepted (in a one-family dwelling the service disconnect is the other disconnect).
needs: Disconnect method for each heater
note: 2017-based article; no change known in 2020/2023.

group: NEC: appliances, HVAC, EV, tubs and spas, low voltage (Art. 422-820)
title: Thermostat as disconnect
applies_to: Line-voltage thermostat on a heater
check: A thermostat counts as the disconnect only if it has a marked OFF position, directly opens all ungrounded conductors in OFF, cannot energize automatically in OFF, and is located per 424.19.

group: NEC: appliances, HVAC, EV, tubs and spas, low voltage (Art. 422-820)
title: Heat strips over 48 A
applies_to: Electric furnace / air handler heat strips
check: Resistance elements over 48 A are subdivided into circuits of 48 A or less protected at 60 A or less (factory supplementary overcurrent protection); field conductors sized at 125 percent.

group: NEC: appliances, HVAC, EV, tubs and spas, low voltage (Art. 422-820)
title: Heating cable area limits
applies_to: Ceiling or floor heating cables
check: Heating cables stay within the room where they start; not in closets, not over or under walls or partitions, not under cabinets or fixed built-ins; keep 8 in. from outlet boxes used for surface luminaires and 2 in. from recessed luminaires and ventilating openings.
note: From my knowledge; text not opened.

group: NEC: appliances, HVAC, EV, tubs and spas, low voltage (Art. 422-820)
title: Heated floor GFCI (cables in slab or mortar)
applies_to: Electric floor-heating cables in a bathroom, kitchen or hydromassage tub location
check: GFCI protection is required for electric heating cables embedded in concrete or poured masonry (including tile mortar beds) in bathrooms, kitchens and hydromassage bathtub locations; this is in addition to 210.8.
edition_difference: Was 424.44(G) in older editions; 424.44(E) in 2020. 2023 number not confirmed (no change known).
note: Trigger: room type bath/kitchen + floor heat. Most floor-heat thermostats include the GFCI (Class A 5 mA).

group: NEC: appliances, HVAC, EV, tubs and spas, low voltage (Art. 422-820)
title: Heated floor GFCI (under floor covering)
applies_to: Heating cables installed under floor coverings (not embedded)
check: Heating cables under floor coverings need GFCI protection; cables must be identified for the use, with a grounding sheath or braid, and the floor covering must be one the manufacturer allows.
note: From my knowledge; text not opened.

group: NEC: appliances, HVAC, EV, tubs and spas, low voltage (Art. 422-820)
title: Heated floor label
applies_to: Any floor or ceiling heating cable system
check: Apply the manufacturer's labels at the panelboard identifying which circuits supply heating cables and where they are.
note: From my knowledge.

group: NEC: appliances, HVAC, EV, tubs and spas, low voltage (Art. 422-820)
title: Heating cables in walls
applies_to: Heating cables or mats in, on or behind walls (e.g. heated shower wall or bench)
check: Allowed only if identified for wall installation, GFCI protected, AFCI protected, with a grounding means (braid or sheath), and not higher than 4 ft above the floor.
edition_difference: New in 2023 (the page read shows an effective date of January 1, 2026); not addressed in 2020.

group: NEC: appliances, HVAC, EV, tubs and spas, low voltage (Art. 422-820)
title: Heated floor panels GFCI
applies_to: Radiant heating panels or mats under floor coverings
check: Heating panels and panel sets installed under floor coverings must have GFCI protection (all rooms), be listed for the use, and not be under fixed cabinets or in areas prohibited by the listing.
note: From my knowledge; text not opened. Brief asked for 424.99(B)(5) specifically.

group: NEC: appliances, HVAC, EV, tubs and spas, low voltage (Art. 422-820)
title: Motor disconnect in sight
applies_to: Hard-wired motor: attic fan, well/booster pump, whole-house fan, garage door operator if hard-wired
check: A disconnect must be in sight from the motor and driven machinery (visible and not more than 50 ft). Exceptions exist only where impracticable or in supervised industrial sites. For appliances use 422.31; for A/C use 440.14.
needs: Disconnect location for each hard-wired motor
note: Study-guide source; edition not stated.

group: NEC: appliances, HVAC, EV, tubs and spas, low voltage (Art. 422-820)
title: Motor disconnect rating
applies_to: Hard-wired motor
