check: Disconnect must be horsepower-rated not less than the motor and rated at least 115 percent of full-load current; for stationary motors of 2 hp or less a general-use snap switch (AC, motor load 80 percent or less of switch rating) is allowed.
note: Snap-switch allowance is from my knowledge.

group: NEC: appliances, HVAC, EV, tubs and spas, low voltage (Art. 422-820)
title: Motor branch conductors
applies_to: Single motor circuit
check: Conductors at least 125 percent of the motor full-load current (table value).

group: NEC: appliances, HVAC, EV, tubs and spas, low voltage (Art. 422-820)
title: Feeder with motors
applies_to: Subpanel feeder or service supplying motors plus other loads
check: Feeder ampacity at least 125 percent of the largest motor full-load current plus 100 percent of the other motors plus the other loads (125 percent of continuous non-motor loads). In the dwelling load calculation add 25 percent of the largest motor (220.50).
edition_difference: 2023 moved the dwelling largest-motor rule to 220.50 with a reference to 430.24/440.6.
note: Handled by the load calculator. 220.50 wording from my knowledge.

group: NEC: appliances, HVAC, EV, tubs and spas, low voltage (Art. 422-820)
title: A/C sized from nameplate
applies_to: Condenser, heat pump, package unit, mini-split, air handler
check: Circuit conductors must have ampacity not less than the nameplate minimum circuit ampacity (MCA) and the breaker or fuse must not exceed the nameplate maximum overcurrent device (MOCP); use fuses or HACR-type breaker as the nameplate specifies.
needs: Unit nameplate MCA and MOCP; circuit wire size and breaker
note: AUTO once MCA/MOCP are entered: wire ampacity >= MCA and breaker <= MOCP. NM cable limited to the 60 C column (334.80).

group: NEC: appliances, HVAC, EV, tubs and spas, low voltage (Art. 422-820)
title: A/C equipment not in tub/shower zone
applies_to: Mini-split indoor head, through-wall unit or other A/C equipment in a bathroom
check: Air-conditioning equipment may not be located within 3 ft horizontally and 8 ft vertically of the top of a bathtub rim or shower threshold (equipment, not vents or grilles).
edition_difference: Reported in a January 2025 Mike Holt article that does not name the edition; believed new in 2023. Not in 2020 as far as I know.
note: Edition uncertain: confirm 440.8 in the 2023 text before treating as an error rather than a warning.

group: NEC: appliances, HVAC, EV, tubs and spas, low voltage (Art. 422-820)
title: Wire-type EGC on roofs
applies_to: Outdoor A/C on a roof fed in metal raceway with compression (non-threaded) fittings
check: Install a wire-type equipment grounding conductor in outdoor metal raceway on roofs that uses non-threaded fittings.

group: NEC: appliances, HVAC, EV, tubs and spas, low voltage (Art. 422-820)
title: A/C disconnect enclosure security
applies_to: A/C disconnect readily accessible to unqualified persons
check: Where the disconnect is readily accessible to unqualified persons, any door or hinged cover that exposes energized parts when open must need a tool to open or be lockable.
edition_difference: Sentence added in 2023; not in 2020.
note: Typical pull-out disconnects need a locking provision or tool-secured dead front.

group: NEC: appliances, HVAC, EV, tubs and spas, low voltage (Art. 422-820)
title: A/C disconnect rating
applies_to: A/C disconnect switch
check: Disconnect ampere rating at least 115 percent of the nameplate rated-load current or branch-circuit selection current, whichever is larger (horsepower-rated equivalent for hermetic compressors).
note: From my knowledge; text not opened.

group: NEC: appliances, HVAC, EV, tubs and spas, low voltage (Art. 422-820)
title: Cord-connected refrigeration equipment
applies_to: Room A/C, refrigerator, freezer
check: For cord-connected equipment a separable connector or plug and receptacle may be the disconnect.

group: NEC: appliances, HVAC, EV, tubs and spas, low voltage (Art. 422-820)
title: A/C disconnect location
applies_to: Condenser, heat pump, air handler, mini-split outdoor unit
check: Disconnect must be within sight of (visible, not more than 50 ft) and readily accessible from the equipment, with 110.26(A) working space. It may be on or in the equipment but NOT on panels designed to be removed for access to the equipment and not where it hides the nameplate. A plug and receptacle serves for cord-connected equipment (Exception 2).
note: AUTO test: disconnect symbol within 50 ft and line of sight of each outdoor unit and air handler; working space 30 in. wide by 36 in. deep clear in front. An attic air handler commonly uses a switch or lockable breaker at the unit.

group: NEC: appliances, HVAC, EV, tubs and spas, low voltage (Art. 422-820)
title: A/C breaker maximum
applies_to: Single-compressor equipment without MOCP marking
check: Short-circuit device not over 175 percent of compressor rated-load current (or branch-circuit selection current); up to 225 percent if needed for starting; next standard size up allowed when the value is not standard.
note: Normally superseded by the nameplate MOCP.

group: NEC: appliances, HVAC, EV, tubs and spas, low voltage (Art. 422-820)
title: A/C conductor minimum
applies_to: Compressor circuits
check: Single compressor: conductors at least 125 percent of rated-load or branch-circuit selection current, whichever is larger. Compressor plus other motors: sum of all plus 25 percent of the largest. Multimotor/combination equipment: not less than the nameplate MCA.
note: 440.35 statement from my knowledge.

group: NEC: appliances, HVAC, EV, tubs and spas, low voltage (Art. 422-820)
title: Room A/C on a circuit
applies_to: Window or through-wall room air conditioner (cord-connected, 40 A / 250 V single-phase or less)
check: Marked rating may not exceed 80 percent of the circuit rating when it is the only load, or 50 percent when lighting or other receptacles/appliances share the circuit.
needs: Room A/C nameplate amperes; dedicated circuit or not
note: 2013 article (edition not stated); long-standing values.

group: NEC: appliances, HVAC, EV, tubs and spas, low voltage (Art. 422-820)
title: Room A/C disconnect
applies_to: Room air conditioner
check: The plug and receptacle may be the disconnect if the unit's manual controls are readily accessible and within 6 ft of the floor, or if a readily accessible manual disconnect is within sight of the unit.

group: NEC: appliances, HVAC, EV, tubs and spas, low voltage (Art. 422-820)
title: Room A/C cord length
applies_to: Room air conditioner receptacle placement
check: Supply cord not longer than 10 ft for a 120 V unit or 6 ft for a 208 or 240 V unit; no extension cords; place the receptacle within cord reach of a sleeve or window unit.
note: AUTO if a through-wall A/C sleeve is drawn: receptacle within 6 ft (240 V) or 10 ft (120 V).

group: NEC: appliances, HVAC, EV, tubs and spas, low voltage (Art. 422-820)
title: Room A/C LCDI/AFCI cord
applies_to: Room air conditioner
check: Single-phase cord-and-plug room air conditioners must have a factory-installed LCDI, AFCI or heat-detecting circuit interrupter (HDCI) in the plug or cord within 12 in. of the plug.
edition_difference: HDCI option added in 2017; no 2020/2023 difference known.
note: HDCI and 12 in. detail from my knowledge.

group: NEC: appliances, HVAC, EV, tubs and spas, low voltage (Art. 422-820)
title: Generator emergency shutdown outside
applies_to: Permanently installed standby generator at a one- or two-family dwelling
check: Provide an emergency shutdown device for the generator outside the dwelling unit at a readily accessible location (may be on the exterior of the generator enclosure), marked 'Generator Emergency Shutdown' with a 110.21(B) label. Does not apply to cord-and-plug portable generators.
edition_difference: 2020: 445.18(D) (new in 2020). 2023 moved shutdown rules to 445.19 and added the marking and enclosure-mounted allowance.

group: NEC: appliances, HVAC, EV, tubs and spas, low voltage (Art. 422-820)
title: Generator disconnect
applies_to: Permanently installed generator
check: Generator must have a lockable disconnecting means that disconnects all ungrounded conductors (other than cord-and-plug portable sets).
note: From my knowledge; 2023 Leviton page 445.18(A)(B) exists but was not opened.

group: NEC: appliances, HVAC, EV, tubs and spas, low voltage (Art. 422-820)
title: Standby capacity
applies_to: Generator or battery backup with transfer switch or interlock
check: Manual transfer (interlock kit or manual switch): source sized for the loads the user chooses to run at one time. Automatic transfer: source sized for the full load transferred (Article 220 or other approved calculation), or use a listed energy/load management system that sheds load so the source is never overloaded.
edition_difference: 2020: capacity rule is 702.4(B)(1) manual and (B)(2) automatic, with 702.4(A) covering available fault current; 2023 renumbered capacity to 702.4(A)(1)/(A)(2) and ties load management to 750.30.
needs: Generator kW, transfer type (manual/automatic), transferred load
note: 2023 numbering confirmed by a North Carolina State interpretation; 2020 lettering from a 2017-based article and my knowledge.

group: NEC: appliances, HVAC, EV, tubs and spas, low voltage (Art. 422-820)
title: Transfer equipment required
applies_to: Generator inlet, portable generator connection, standby generator, backup battery
check: Transfer equipment (listed transfer switch, or a listed breaker interlock kit on the panel) is required for every standby source connected to premises wiring and must prevent inadvertent interconnection of normal and standby sources. No backfeeding a dryer or range receptacle. Field-mark the short-circuit current rating on transfer equipment (non-dwelling emphasis).
edition_difference: 2020 added rules for meter-mounted transfer switches (must be listed).
note: Interlock-kit wording from my knowledge; the article read is 2017-based.

group: NEC: appliances, HVAC, EV, tubs and spas, low voltage (Art. 422-820)
title: Standby source sign
applies_to: Permanently installed standby source at a one- or two-family dwelling
check: Place a sign at the 230.85 emergency disconnect showing the location of each permanently installed standby source disconnect or the generator shutdown means.
edition_difference: 2020 introduced the dwelling wording (earlier editions: sign at the service equipment giving type and location of the source). 2023 points to 445.19(C) instead of 445.18(D).

group: NEC: appliances, HVAC, EV, tubs and spas, low voltage (Art. 422-820)
title: Neutral-bonding and inlet signs
applies_to: Portable-generator power inlet with interlock or manual transfer switch
check: At the power inlet post a warning stating which generator type the transfer equipment is built for: bonded-neutral (separately derived, switched neutral) or floating-neutral (non-separately derived, solid neutral). Where removing a neutral bond is needed, sign at the transfer equipment.
note: From my knowledge; not confirmed on an opened page.

group: NEC: appliances, HVAC, EV, tubs and spas, low voltage (Art. 422-820)
title: Portable generator grounding
applies_to: Portable generator connection
check: If the transfer equipment switches the neutral, the generator is a separately derived system grounded per 250.30; if the neutral is not switched, the generator neutral must not be bonded to its frame and its equipment grounding conductor bonds to the building grounding system.
edition_difference: Numbered 702.10 in older editions.
note: Source is a 2002-based article; the principle is unchanged, section number per my knowledge.

group: NEC: appliances, HVAC, EV, tubs and spas, low voltage (Art. 422-820)
title: Outdoor generators and inlets
applies_to: Outdoor generator set or portable generator inlet
check: Portable generator 15 kW or less connected through a flanged inlet (cord and plug): no separate building disconnect needed. Larger or permanently installed outdoor units with a readily accessible disconnect within sight of the building need no additional disconnect. Power inlets must be listed and outdoors/weatherproof; inlets rated 100 A or more must not be capable of being disconnected under load unless rated for it.
edition_difference: 2020 added the power-inlet (100 A or more) item.
note: 100 A inlet item from my knowledge. Also show generator placement away from openings per manufacturer and FBC (CO hazard).

group: NEC: appliances, HVAC, EV, tubs and spas, low voltage (Art. 422-820)
title: PV / battery interconnection
applies_to: Solar or battery inverter connected to the house panel
check: Load-side connection: sum of 125 percent of inverter output current plus the main breaker may not exceed 120 percent of the busbar rating, with the backfed breaker at the opposite end of the bus from the main (or use another permitted method); supply-side connections per 705.11. A panel upgrade or relocated main changes this calculation.
note: From my knowledge; one-line reminder as the brief requested.

group: NEC: appliances, HVAC, EV, tubs and spas, low voltage (Art. 422-820)
title: PV rapid shutdown
applies_to: House with rooftop solar when the service, meter or panel is altered
check: PV systems on buildings need rapid shutdown with an initiation device at a readily accessible outdoor location for one- and two-family dwellings, and the required label at the service; keep or restore both when the service equipment is replaced or moved.
note: From my knowledge; one-line reminder as the brief requested.

group: NEC: appliances, HVAC, EV, tubs and spas, low voltage (Art. 422-820)
title: ESS disconnect and shutdown
applies_to: Home battery (energy storage system over 1 kWh)
check: ESS needs a readily accessible disconnecting means within sight of the ESS (or lockable), and for one- and two-family dwellings an emergency shutdown initiation device at a readily accessible location outside the building.
edition_difference: 2020: 706.15(A) carries the outdoor emergency-disconnect concept for dwellings; 2023 reorganized 706.15 and words it as an emergency shutdown function.
note: Only the existence of the 706.15(A) dwelling rule was seen (cross-reference on the page read); details from my knowledge.

group: NEC: appliances, HVAC, EV, tubs and spas, low voltage (Art. 422-820)
title: ESS location and size limits
applies_to: Home battery drawn in a garage, closet, utility room or on an exterior wall
check: ESS must be listed (UL 9540). Each unit 20 kWh maximum. Aggregate per location: 40 kWh in utility closets and storage/utility spaces, 80 kWh in attached or detached garages, on exterior walls, or outdoors on the ground. Not allowed in sleeping rooms or closets/spaces opening directly into sleeping rooms, nor in habitable space; rooms need finished gypsum walls and ceiling, interconnected smoke alarm (heat detector where a smoke alarm is unsuitable), and vehicle impact protection in garages; outdoors keep 3 ft from doors and windows.
edition_difference: R328 first appears in the FBC Residential 8th Edition (2023); check 9th Edition text for changes.
needs: ESS kWh per unit and per location; room type
note: Capacity limits confirmed from a Florida solar design firm's summary of NFPA 855 Chapter 15 and its statement that FBC-R R328 was added in 2023; the prohibited-location, gypsum, detector and impact-protection items are from my knowledge of IRC R328 and were NOT opened in the Florida text.

group: NEC: appliances, HVAC, EV, tubs and spas, low voltage (Art. 422-820)
title: Battery disconnect
applies_to: Stationary storage batteries over 60 V DC (not listed ESS)
check: Provide a disconnecting means for stationary battery systems; for one- and two-family dwellings a disconnect or its remote control at a readily accessible location outside the building.
edition_difference: Dwelling outdoor-disconnect rule added in 2020.
note: Existence of the 480.7(A) dwelling rule seen as a cross-reference; details from my knowledge.

group: NEC: appliances, HVAC, EV, tubs and spas, low voltage (Art. 422-820)
title: EV charger individual circuit
applies_to: EV charger (EVSE) outlet
check: Each outlet supplying EVSE rated over 16 A or over 120 V must be on an individual branch circuit with no other outlets.
edition_difference: 2020: every outlet installed for EV charging needs an individual branch circuit (no 16 A / 120 V threshold); 2023 adds an exception allowing several EVSE on one circuit when an energy management system or adjustable-setting EVSE under 625.42(A)/(B) limits the load.
note: Part of app rule E-11.

group: NEC: appliances, HVAC, EV, tubs and spas, low voltage (Art. 422-820)
title: EV circuit at 125 percent
applies_to: EV charger branch circuit and feeder
check: Overcurrent protection and conductors for EVSE sized for continuous duty: not less than 125 percent of the EVSE maximum load (48 A charger = 60 A circuit; 40 A charger = 50 A; 32 A = 40 A; 16 A = 20 A).
needs: EVSE output amperes (or adjusted setting)
note: AUTO once amperes are entered: breaker >= 1.25 x EVSE amperes.

group: NEC: appliances, HVAC, EV, tubs and spas, low voltage (Art. 422-820)
title: EV load rating / load management
applies_to: EV charger on a service with little spare capacity
check: EV charging is a continuous load; service and feeder are sized from the EVSE rating unless a listed energy management system (750.30) or an EVSE with access-restricted adjustable current setting limits it, in which case the limited value may be used and the adjusted rating must be durably labeled.
edition_difference: 2020 allowed automatic load management in general terms; 2023 split it into (A) EMS and (B) adjustable settings.
needs: EVSE setting / EMS present

group: NEC: appliances, HVAC, EV, tubs and spas, low voltage (Art. 422-820)
title: EV charger disconnect
applies_to: EVSE rated over 60 A or over 150 V to ground
check: Provide a readily accessible disconnect, lockable open per 110.25; if remote from the EVSE, a plaque on the EVSE gives its location.
edition_difference: Plaque for remote disconnect is 2023 wording.
note: Typical 48 A wall chargers on a 60 A circuit do not trigger it (not over 60 A).

group: NEC: appliances, HVAC, EV, tubs and spas, low voltage (Art. 422-820)
title: EV connection method
applies_to: EV charger: plug-in versus hard-wired
check: Portable and fastened-in-place EVSE may plug into non-locking receptacles of the ratings listed in 625.44 (commonly 125 V 15/20 A, or 250 V 30 or 50 A); all other EVSE must be permanently wired and fastened in place.
needs: EVSE connection type and receptacle rating
note: Exact receptacle rating list was not confirmed.

group: NEC: appliances, HVAC, EV, tubs and spas, low voltage (Art. 422-820)
title: EV charger location and height
applies_to: EV charger in garage or outdoors
check: Locate the EVSE so its cable reaches the vehicle charge port directly. Unless the listing says otherwise, the coupling means (connector storage/holster) is stored at least 18 in. above the floor indoors and at least 24 in. above grade outdoors.
note: Article read is dated November 2023; edition not named.

group: NEC: appliances, HVAC, EV, tubs and spas, low voltage (Art. 422-820)
title: EV charging ventilation
applies_to: EV charger indoors (garage)
check: No mechanical ventilation needed when the EVSE is listed for indoor charging without ventilation (all current residential units); otherwise provide ventilation per 625.52(B).

group: NEC: appliances, HVAC, EV, tubs and spas, low voltage (Art. 422-820)
title: GFCI for EV receptacles
applies_to: Receptacle installed for EV charging (e.g. 14-50 or 6-50 in a garage)
check: Every receptacle installed for connecting EV charging equipment needs GFCI protection, at any voltage and ampere rating and in any location (in addition to 210.8).
edition_difference: New wording in 2020 (all receptacles). Same in 2023.
note: Hard-wired EVSE is not covered by 625.54 (but an outdoor hard-wired outlet 50 A or less falls under 210.8(F)).

group: NEC: appliances, HVAC, EV, tubs and spas, low voltage (Art. 422-820)
title: EV receptacle in wet location
applies_to: Outdoor EV charging receptacle
check: Receptacle in a wet location needs a weatherproof enclosure with the plug inserted or removed (extra-duty in-use cover).
edition_difference: New in 2020.

group: NEC: appliances, HVAC, EV, tubs and spas, low voltage (Art. 422-820)
title: Bidirectional EV / vehicle power export
applies_to: EV used as backup power for the house
check: EVSE that exports power to the premises must be listed and marked for it and installed as a standby source (Article 702) or interconnected source (Article 705) with transfer equipment; vehicle AC receptacles for power export are limited to 50 A 250 V single-phase with GFCI.
edition_difference: 625.60 added in 2020; 2023 added 625.49 island mode.

group: NEC: appliances, HVAC, EV, tubs and spas, low voltage (Art. 422-820)
title: Hydromassage tub: which rules
applies_to: Hydromassage (jetted / whirlpool / air) bathtub
check: A hydromassage bathtub follows only Part VII of Article 680 (not the pool or spa parts); otherwise it is treated as an ordinary bathtub for switch, receptacle and luminaire locations.

group: NEC: appliances, HVAC, EV, tubs and spas, low voltage (Art. 422-820)
title: Jetted tub circuit and GFCI
applies_to: Hydromassage bathtub pump, blower, heater
check: Supply the tub and its associated electrical components from an individual branch circuit protected by a readily accessible GFCI. Follow the listing: many tubs need separate circuits for pump and inline heater.
note: Replaces/confirms the 680.71 part of app rule E-11. 'Readily accessible' means the GFCI device cannot be behind the tub access panel.

group: NEC: appliances, HVAC, EV, tubs and spas, low voltage (Art. 422-820)
title: Receptacles near jetted tub
applies_to: Receptacles within 6 ft of a hydromassage bathtub
check: All 125 V single-phase receptacles rated 30 A or less within 6 ft horizontally of the inside walls of the tub must be GFCI protected.
note: In a bathroom 210.8(A)(1) already requires it; this extends it to tubs in bedrooms or sun rooms.

group: NEC: appliances, HVAC, EV, tubs and spas, low voltage (Art. 422-820)
title: Other equipment at jetted tub
applies_to: Luminaires, switches, receptacles, fans near a hydromassage tub
check: Equipment not associated with the tub follows the ordinary Chapter 1-4 rules for bathtubs (406.9(C) no receptacles in the tub zone, 410.10(D) luminaires, 404.4(C) switches).

group: NEC: appliances, HVAC, EV, tubs and spas, low voltage (Art. 422-820)
title: Jetted tub access
applies_to: Hydromassage bathtub pump, heater, controls
check: Electrical equipment must be accessible without damaging the building structure or finish: show an access panel. If the pump cord-and-plug receptacle is reachable only through a service access opening, the receptacle face must be in direct view and not more than 1 ft from the opening.
note: AUTO: jetted tub requires an access-panel object at the pump end; receptacle within 12 in. of the opening. Plumbing code also sets a minimum access opening (other agent).

group: NEC: appliances, HVAC, EV, tubs and spas, low voltage (Art. 422-820)
title: Jetted tub bonding: what
applies_to: Hydromassage bathtub
check: Bond together: metal fittings in or on the tub structure in contact with the circulating water; metal parts of the circulating equipment including pump and blower motors; metal-sheathed cables, metal raceways and metal piping within 5 ft of the tub inside walls and not separated by a permanent barrier; exposed metal surfaces within 5 ft not separated by a permanent barrier; and electrical devices and controls not associated with the tub within 5 ft. Not required: small conductive surfaces unlikely to be energized (jets, supply valve assemblies, drain fittings not connected to metal piping, towel bars, mirror frames not connected to metal framing) and double-insulated motors and blowers.
edition_difference: 2017 rewrote the section into (A)/(B) and added the 5 ft items; 2020 list has five items. I could not open the 2023 text to confirm whether the double-insulated provisions changed again.
note: Brief asked for the 2020/2023 double-insulated-pump changes: NOT CONFIRMED for 2023. Treat the 2017/2020 content shown here as the rule and verify 2023 wording.

group: NEC: appliances, HVAC, EV, tubs and spas, low voltage (Art. 422-820)
title: Jetted tub bonding: how
applies_to: Hydromassage bathtub
check: Bonding jumper is solid copper, 8 AWG or larger (insulated, covered or bare); it need not run to the panel, service or any electrode. With a double-insulated pump, still leave an 8 AWG jumper long enough to reach a replacement non-double-insulated motor, terminated to the equipment grounding conductor of the motor circuit.

group: NEC: appliances, HVAC, EV, tubs and spas, low voltage (Art. 422-820)
title: Indoor spa: general
applies_to: Indoor spa or hot tub drawn inside the house
check: Indoor spas follow Parts I and II of Article 680 as modified by 680.43; any Chapter 3 wiring method; a listed packaged unit rated 20 A or less may be cord-and-plug connected. Perimeter-surface bonding is not required for a listed self-contained spa above a finished floor.

group: NEC: appliances, HVAC, EV, tubs and spas, low voltage (Art. 422-820)
title: Indoor spa: required receptacle
applies_to: Indoor spa or hot tub
check: At least one 125 V, 15 or 20 A general-purpose receptacle located between 6 ft and 10 ft from the inside wall of the spa.

group: NEC: appliances, HVAC, EV, tubs and spas, low voltage (Art. 422-820)
title: Indoor spa: receptacle distance and GFCI
applies_to: Receptacles near an indoor spa
check: No receptacle closer than 6 ft horizontally from the spa inside walls. Receptacles 125 V, 30 A or less within 10 ft of the inside walls must be GFCI protected, as must any receptacle supplying the spa. Measure along the shortest cord path without passing through a wall, floor, ceiling, hinged or sliding doorway or window.
note: Sub-numbering differs between sources ((A)(1)-(4) versus (B)); numbers confirmed in a 2020-based article.

group: NEC: appliances, HVAC, EV, tubs and spas, low voltage (Art. 422-820)
title: Indoor spa: luminaires and fans
applies_to: Luminaire, lighting outlet or ceiling fan over or within 5 ft of an indoor spa
check: Over the spa or within 5 ft horizontally of its inside walls: mount at least 12 ft above the maximum water level if not GFCI protected, or at least 7.5 ft if GFCI protected. Below 7.5 ft only GFCI-protected damp-location luminaires of the permitted types (recessed with glass/plastic lens and nonmetallic or isolated trim, or surface-mounted with glass/plastic globe and nonmetallic or isolated body).
note: Study guide confirms 7 ft 6 in. with GFCI; the 12 ft non-GFCI value and luminaire types are from my knowledge.

group: NEC: appliances, HVAC, EV, tubs and spas, low voltage (Art. 422-820)
title: Indoor spa: switches
applies_to: Wall switches near an indoor spa
check: Switches at least 5 ft horizontally from the inside walls of the spa.

group: NEC: appliances, HVAC, EV, tubs and spas, low voltage (Art. 422-820)
title: Indoor spa: bonding
applies_to: Indoor spa or hot tub
check: Bond together metal fittings in or attached to the spa, metal parts of circulating equipment (unless part of a listed self-contained unit), and metal surfaces, raceways and piping within 5 ft of the inside walls not separated by a permanent barrier; use threaded metal piping, metal-to-metal mounting on a common frame, or an 8 AWG or larger solid copper jumper. Towel bars and mirror frames not connected to metal piping need no bonding.

group: NEC: appliances, HVAC, EV, tubs and spas, low voltage (Art. 422-820)
title: Spa GFCI
applies_to: Outlet supplying a spa or hot tub
check: The outlet supplying a self-contained, packaged or field-assembled spa needs GFCI protection (hard-wired included) unless the listed unit is marked as having integral GFCI.
needs: Spa has listed integral GFCI

group: NEC: appliances, HVAC, EV, tubs and spas, low voltage (Art. 422-820)
title: Receptacles near a pool
applies_to: House with a pool: receptacles on exterior walls, lanai, pool bath door area
check: At least one 125 V 15/20 A receptacle between 6 ft and 20 ft from the pool inside wall, not more than 6.5 ft above the deck; no receptacle closer than 6 ft; receptacles within 20 ft GFCI protected. Distance is the shortest cord path without passing through a wall, floor, ceiling, hinged or sliding door or window, so interior rooms behind a door are not counted.
edition_difference: 2020: GFCI within 20 ft covers 125 V 15/20 A receptacles; 2023 extends it to all receptacles 125 V through 250 V, 60 A or less (Class A GFCI, or SPGFCI above 150 V to ground per 680.5).
note: Base rule from a 2017-based article; 2023 change from Leviton page https://captaincode2023.leviton.com/node/365.

group: NEC: appliances, HVAC, EV, tubs and spas, low voltage (Art. 422-820)
title: Lights and fans near a pool
applies_to: New luminaire or ceiling fan on a lanai or patio near a pool
check: New luminaires, lighting outlets and ceiling fans over the pool or within 5 ft horizontally of its inside walls must be at least 12 ft above maximum water level; between 5 and 10 ft horizontally they need GFCI unless at least 5 ft above water level and rigidly attached to the structure. Existing luminaires within 5 ft: at least 5 ft above water, rigidly attached, GFCI protected.
note: Indoor pools have a 7.5 ft allowance for enclosed GFCI-protected fixtures (from my knowledge).

group: NEC: appliances, HVAC, EV, tubs and spas, low voltage (Art. 422-820)
title: Switches and other outlets near a pool
applies_to: Switches and other outlets (e.g. remote controls, communications) near a pool
check: Switching devices at least 5 ft horizontally from the pool inside walls unless separated by a solid fence, wall or other permanent barrier (or listed for closer use); other outlets at least 10 ft away.
note: From my knowledge; the article read did not cover (C)/(D).

group: NEC: appliances, HVAC, EV, tubs and spas, low voltage (Art. 422-820)
title: Pool equipotential bonding
applies_to: Remodel that adds metal within 5 ft of a pool (door frames, window frames, railings, fixed metal)
check: Fixed metal parts within 5 ft horizontally of the pool inside walls (and within 12 ft vertically) must be tied to the pool bonding grid with 8 AWG solid copper unless separated by a permanent barrier; replaced metal sliders and window frames at the lanai are a common trigger.
note: 5 ft / 12 ft fixed-metal detail is from my knowledge (680.26(B)(7)); conductor size confirmed.

group: NEC: appliances, HVAC, EV, tubs and spas, low voltage (Art. 422-820)
title: Low-voltage: firestopping and spread of fire
applies_to: Low-voltage cable through rated walls, floors, garage separation
check: Openings for Class 2 cables through fire-resistance-rated walls, floors and ceilings (including the garage-to-house separation and dwelling-unit separations in townhouses and duplexes) must be firestopped with approved methods.
edition_difference: 2023 moved cable provisions for Class 2 into new Article 722; requirement unchanged.
note: From my knowledge. Leviton 2023 page on Articles 722/724/726 exists but was not opened.

group: NEC: appliances, HVAC, EV, tubs and spas, low voltage (Art. 422-820)
title: Class 2 power source
applies_to: Doorbell transformer, thermostat transformer, LED driver, low-voltage lighting supply
check: Class 2 circuits must be supplied by a listed Class 2 transformer or power supply; wiring on the line side follows Chapters 1-4 (in a box, accessible; a doorbell transformer may not be buried in a wall or inside the panel unless listed for it).
edition_difference: 2023 may have renumbered the power-source section during the Article 725 reorganization; not confirmed.
note: From my knowledge. LED drivers and transformers must stay accessible; remote drivers need listed location (attic temperature rating).

group: NEC: appliances, HVAC, EV, tubs and spas, low voltage (Art. 422-820)
title: Low voltage separate from power
applies_to: Low-voltage cable sharing a box, raceway or cable with 120 V wiring
check: Class 2 conductors may not be in the same cable, raceway, enclosure, box or fitting as power and lighting conductors unless separated by a barrier (e.g. listed divided box for a combined power/low-voltage device).
note: Source restates (A) and (B) as 2023 text for cable trays; general wording from my knowledge.

group: NEC: appliances, HVAC, EV, tubs and spas, low voltage (Art. 422-820)
title: Low voltage spacing from power
applies_to: Low-voltage cable run alongside NM cable or entering equipment
check: Inside an enclosure where Class 2 conductors must enter to connect to the same equipment as power conductors: keep 1/4 in. separation. Elsewhere keep Class 2 cables 2 in. from open power conductors unless either is in raceway or the power conductors are in NM, MC, AC or UF cable (so jacketed thermostat or doorbell cable may share framing bays with NM but not the same bored hole bundle tightly, per good practice).
note: From my knowledge; sub-letters and distances not confirmed on an opened page.

group: NEC: appliances, HVAC, EV, tubs and spas, low voltage (Art. 422-820)
title: Low-voltage cable support
applies_to: Thermostat, doorbell, control, LED low-voltage cable
check: Install neatly; support from the building structure with listed straps or staples that do not damage the cable; do not strap to the outside of raceways or lay on ceiling tiles/grid; remove abandoned accessible cable.
edition_difference: 2023: mechanical execution for these cables is in 722.24.
note: From my knowledge.

group: NEC: appliances, HVAC, EV, tubs and spas, low voltage (Art. 422-820)
title: Low-voltage cable type
applies_to: Low-voltage cable in a return-air plenum, air handler closet used as plenum, or riser
check: Use CL2P/CL3P plenum cable in ducts and other air-handling spaces, CL2R in risers between floors, CL2/CL2X in ordinary dwelling spaces (one- and two-family dwellings may use CL2X under 0.25 in. diameter).
edition_difference: 2023 moved cable listing and application tables to Article 722 (722.135).
note: From my knowledge; section numbers approximate.

group: NEC: appliances, HVAC, EV, tubs and spas, low voltage (Art. 422-820)
title: Smoke alarm power source
applies_to: Smoke alarms where the remodel triggers R314 (new bedrooms, permits for alterations/additions)
check: Smoke alarms take primary power from the building wiring with battery backup, with no disconnecting switch other than the overcurrent device. Florida: in one- and two-family dwellings and townhouses undergoing repair or Level 1 alteration, 10-year nonremovable, nonreplaceable battery alarms are permitted instead of hard-wiring.
edition_difference: Check the 9th Edition text for changes.
needs: Each smoke alarm: hard-wired with battery backup, or 10-year sealed battery
note: Complements app rule B-19. Source is a Florida Home Builders Association summary that does not name the edition. The NEC has no rule requiring a dedicated or a shared circuit for smoke alarms; either is allowed (a lighting circuit is common so that a tripped breaker is noticed).

group: NEC: appliances, HVAC, EV, tubs and spas, low voltage (Art. 422-820)
title: Smoke alarm interconnection
applies_to: More than one smoke alarm required
check: Interconnect the alarms (wired or listed wireless) so one sounds all; in alterations interconnection is not required where the work does not expose the structure or provide access (attic, crawl space).
note: Complements app rule B-19.

group: NEC: appliances, HVAC, EV, tubs and spas, low voltage (Art. 422-820)
title: Smoke alarm placement clearances
applies_to: Smoke alarm near bathroom door, supply register or ceiling fan
check: Keep smoke alarms at least 36 in. horizontally from a door to a bathroom with a tub or shower, from forced-air supply registers, and from the tip of a ceiling (paddle) fan blade; other placement per NFPA 72 Chapter 29 (distance from cooking appliances, peaks of sloped and tray ceilings).
note: AUTO test on the three 36 in. distances. Section sub-number for the 36 in. items not confirmed (source gives only the R314 heading).

group: NEC: appliances, HVAC, EV, tubs and spas, low voltage (Art. 422-820)
title: Fire alarm panel circuit
applies_to: Household fire alarm system (control panel) used in place of smoke alarms
check: The branch circuit to a fire alarm control unit must be an individual circuit, not GFCI or AFCI protected, with the breaker identified (red marking) and its location recorded at the panel.
note: Only the AFCI/GFCI exemption was confirmed on the page read; the individual-circuit and marking items are from my knowledge. Applies only to systems with a control unit, not to 120 V smoke alarms.

group: NEC: appliances, HVAC, EV, tubs and spas, low voltage (Art. 422-820)
title: Communications outlet
applies_to: New dwelling unit
check: A newly constructed dwelling unit needs at least one communications outlet in a readily accessible area, cabled to the service provider demarcation point. Not triggered by an interior remodel of an existing house; an addition creating a new dwelling unit (ADU, duplex conversion) would trigger it.
note: Corrects the brief's '800.156': current number is 805.156.

group: NEC: appliances, HVAC, EV, tubs and spas, low voltage (Art. 422-820)
title: Communications cable workmanship
applies_to: Data, phone, coax cable in the remodel
check: Install neatly; support from the structure so cable is not damaged; not strapped to the outside of raceways or pipes; plenum-rated cable in air-handling spaces; remove abandoned accessible cable (800.25) and firestop penetrations of rated assemblies (800.26).
edition_difference: 2020 consolidated these general rules for all Chapter 8 articles into Article 800.
note: 800.25/800.26 from my knowledge.

group: NEC: appliances, HVAC, EV, tubs and spas, low voltage (Art. 422-820)
title: Communications separation from power
applies_to: Data, phone, coax cable near 120 V wiring
check: No communications cable in the same box, raceway or enclosure as power conductors unless separated by a permanent barrier or listed divider; keep 2 in. from open power conductors unless the power wiring is in raceway or NM/MC/AC/UF cable or the communications cable is in raceway.
edition_difference: Section may be numbered 805.133 for telephone/data circuits and 820.133 for coax in 2020/2023; not confirmed.

group: NEC: appliances, HVAC, EV, tubs and spas, low voltage (Art. 422-820)
title: Communications bonding / intersystem bonding
applies_to: Service upgrade or relocated service equipment; cable, phone, satellite entrance
check: At service equipment provide an intersystem bonding termination (at least three terminals, accessible, outside or at the meter/service). Communications and coax bonding conductors: 14 AWG copper minimum, as short and straight as practicable, not over 20 ft in one- and two-family dwellings; a separate communications ground rod must be bonded to the power grounding electrode system with 6 AWG copper.
note: 250.94 terminal details from my knowledge.

group: NEC: appliances, HVAC, EV, tubs and spas, low voltage (Art. 422-820)
title: Coax shield bonding
applies_to: Coax (cable TV, satellite) entering the house
check: Bond the coax outer shield at the building entrance to the intersystem bonding termination with 14 AWG or larger.

group: NEC: appliances, HVAC, EV, tubs and spas, low voltage (Art. 422-820)
title: Optical fiber cable
applies_to: Fiber-to-the-home cable inside the dwelling
check: Same workmanship, support, plenum/riser listing and firestopping rules as other communications cable; conductive fiber cables need bonding of metallic members.
note: From my knowledge; Leviton 2020 page on 770.24 not opened.

group: NEC: appliances, HVAC, EV, tubs and spas, low voltage (Art. 422-820)
title: Conduit fill
applies_to: Circuits drawn in conduit (garage, exterior, slab, service/feeder raceways)
check: Conductor fill of a raceway: 53 percent for one conductor, 31 percent for two, 40 percent for more than two; nipples 24 in. or shorter may be filled to 60 percent. Use Tables 4 and 5 or Annex C for conductor counts.
note: Values from my knowledge (long-standing); not confirmed on an opened page.

group: NEC: appliances, HVAC, EV, tubs and spas, low voltage (Art. 422-820)
title: Conductor area (circular mils) for voltage drop
applies_to: Voltage-drop calculator
check: Circular mil area, same for copper and aluminum: 14 AWG 4,110; 12 AWG 6,530; 10 AWG 10,380; 8 AWG 16,510; 6 AWG 26,240; 4 AWG 41,740; 3 AWG 52,620; 2 AWG 66,360; 1 AWG 83,690; 1/0 105,600; 2/0 133,100; 3/0 167,800; 4/0 211,600. Formula: VD = 2 x K x I x L / cmil (single-phase), K about 12.9 ohm-cmil/ft copper and 21.2 aluminum at 75 C.
note: Verified against two independent sources: a study guide reprinting Table 8 and Southwire bare-copper spec 10080 (https://cabletechsupport.southwire.com/tile/1/spec/10080/?country=US), which give identical circular mil values for all thirteen sizes. Feeds app rule E-17.

group: NEC: appliances, HVAC, EV, tubs and spas, low voltage (Art. 422-820)
title: Conductor DC resistance for voltage drop
applies_to: Voltage-drop calculator
note: From one study-guide reprint of Table 8 (edition not stated); 6 AWG 0.491 and 8 AWG 0.778 cross-checked on other pages. For AC circuits Table 9 gives effective impedance (slightly different for large conductors in steel conduit).

group: NEC: appliances, HVAC, EV, tubs and spas, low voltage (Art. 422-820)
section_now: 210.19(A) Informational Note No. 4, 215.2(A)(1) Informational Note No. 2
title: Voltage drop recommendation
applies_to: Long branch circuits and feeders (run length in the model)
